children.text: yasmin sarvaṃ yataḥ sarvaṃ yaḥ sarvaṃ sarvataśca yaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to him in whom everything exists, from whom everything comes, who is everything, and who is in every way everything,

children.text: yaśca sarvamayo nityaṃ tasmai sarvātmane namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: who is always made of all things: homage to that self of all.
On the lovely summit of <s>Kailāsa</s>, adorned with many jewels,
covered with many trees and creepers, and free from concealed connections,
the god of gods, sitting at ease, the blue-throated three-eyed one,
the goddess <s>Pārvatī</s>, bowing with her head, asks him:
The blessed Goddess said:
O god of gods, great god, O Time, burner of the body of <s>Kāma</s>,
destroyer of <s>kula</s>, <s>kaula</s>, <s>mahākaula</s>, <s>siddhakaula</s>, and the rest,
by your favor I have heard everything and understood it completely.

children.text: yadi te 'ham anugrāhyā yadyahaṃ tava vallabhā ||
children.translated_text: If I am to be favored by you, if I am beloved to you,
please tell me, Lord, what this <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living) is like,
which is indicated in all the tantras, yet is not openly revealed.
The blessed <s>Bhairava</s> said:
Good, good, greatly fortunate one; good, daughter of the mountain.

children.text: sādhu pṛṣṭaṃ tvayā devi bhaktānāṃ hitakāmyayā ||
children.translated_text: You have asked well, goddess, out of a desire for the welfare of devotees.
The knowledge of identity with <s>Śiva</s> in an undecaying, immortal body,
O great goddess, is <s>jīvanmukti</s>, difficult even for the gods to obtain.

children.text: piṇḍapāte ca yo mokṣaḥ sa ca mokṣo nirarthakaḥ
children.translated_text: The liberation that occurs when the body falls is a pointless liberation,

children.text: piṇḍe tu patite devi gardabho'pi vimucyate ||
children.translated_text: for when the body has fallen, goddess, even a donkey is liberated.

children.text: yadi muktirbhagakṣobhe kiṃ na muñcanti gardabhāḥ
children.translated_text: If liberation came from the agitation of the vulva, why are donkeys not liberated?
And goats and bulls too, O mother of the hosts, why are they not liberated?
Therefore one should preserve the body by means of <s>rasa</s> (mercurial elixir) and <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenating alchemy).
If liberation came from consuming semen, urine, and feces,
why, O great goddess, are the species of dogs and pigs not liberated?
Even in the six systems, liberation is taught as occurring when the body falls,
but even that is not directly perceived like a myrobalan fruit in the palm.
O mistress of the gods, I shall tell you the true reality, though it should not be spoken.

children.text: śūnyapāpo mantrayājī na piṇḍaṃ dhārayet kvacit
children.translated_text: One who is free of empty sin and performs mantra-sacrifice should never abandon the body.
O mistress of the gods, even for the gods the holding of the body is hard to obtain.
How much more, then, for human beings living on the surface of the earth?

children.text: dharme naṣṭe kuto dharmaḥ dharme naṣṭe kutaḥ kriyā ||
children.translated_text: When <s>dharma</s> is destroyed, whence comes <s>dharma</s>? When <s>dharma</s> is destroyed, whence comes ritual action?

children.text: kriyānaṣṭe kuto yogaḥ yoge naṣṭe kuto gatiḥ
children.translated_text: When ritual action is destroyed, whence comes yoga? When yoga is destroyed, whence comes the path?

children.text: gatinaṣṭe kuto mokṣo mokṣe naṣṭe na kiṃcana ||
children.translated_text: When the path is destroyed, whence comes liberation? When liberation is destroyed, nothing remains.
The blessed Goddess said:
O god of gods, I have heard the nature of <s>jīvanmukti</s>.

children.text: tatpratyupāyaṃ me brūhi yadyasti karuṇā mayi ||
children.translated_text: Tell me the means to attain it, if there is compassion in you for me.
The blessed <s>Bhairava</s> said:
O mistress of the gods, preservation of the body is obtained through <s>karmayoga</s> (the discipline of practice).
<s>Karmayoga</s> is considered twofold: <s>rasa</s> and breath.

children.text: mūrchito harati vyādhiṃ mṛto jīvayati svayam
children.translated_text: When stupefied, it removes disease; when killed, it itself gives life.

children.text: baddhaḥ khecaratāṃ kuryāt raso vāyuśca bhairavi ||
children.translated_text: When bound, O <s>Bhairavī</s>, <s>rasa</s> and wind produce the state of moving in the sky.
O mistress of the gods, liberation comes from knowledge, and knowledge from holding the breath.

children.text: tatra devi sthiraṃ piṇḍaṃ yatra sthairye rasaḥ prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, goddess, the body is firm where, in firmness, <s>rasa</s> is the lord.
Before long, goddess, the body becomes undecaying and immortal.
And just as meditation belongs to the mind, it is obtained through the yoga of <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: satyaṃ sa labhate devi jñānaṃ vijñānapūrvakam
children.translated_text: Truly, goddess, he obtains knowledge preceded by discriminating realization.
The mantras of one who consumes dead <s>sūtaka</s> (processed mercury) become successful.
As long as the descent of power has not occurred, and as long as the cutting of bonds has not taken place,
how can understanding arise in him with respect to dead <s>sūtaka</s>?
Those who are always devoted to wine and meat, who delight in vulvas and phalluses,
for them, whose intellects are ruined, knowledge of <s>rasa</s> is very hard to obtain.
For those bereft of the discipline of the <s>kula</s>, who desire the true vision,

children.text: na sidhyati raso devi pibanti mṛgatṛṣṇikām ||
children.translated_text: <s>rasa</s> is not accomplished, goddess; they drink a mirage.
One who eats cow's flesh and drinks immortal liquor,
him I regard as noble and a knower of <s>rasa</s>; the others are low.

children.text: na garbhaḥ sampradāyārthe raso garbho vidhīyate
children.translated_text: For the purpose of the tradition, <s>garbha</s> is not an embryo; <s>rasa</s> is prescribed as the <s>garbha</s>.

children.text: tenāyaṃ labhate siddhiṃ na siddhiḥ sūtakaṃ vinā ||
children.translated_text: By that one attains accomplishment; there is no accomplishment without <s>sūtaka</s>.

children.text: yāvanna harabījaṃ tu bhakṣayet pāradaṃ rasam
children.translated_text: As long as one does not consume the seed of <s>Hara</s>, the <s>pārada</s> mercury,

children.text: tāvattasya kuto muktiḥ kutaḥ piṇḍasya dhāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: how can he have liberation, and how can the body be preserved?
Those whose judgment is attached to wine and meat are deluded by the magic power of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: jalpanti ca vayaṃ muktā yāsyāmaḥ śivamandiram ||
children.translated_text: They chatter, 'We are liberated; we shall go to the abode of <s>Śiva</s>.'
The dull-minded are indifferent to the yoga of preserving the body.
O mistress of the gods, the whole moving and unmoving world is colored by fragmentary knowledge.

children.text: svadehe khecaratvaṃ ca śivatvaṃ yena labhyate
children.translated_text: By such knowledge of <s>rasa</s>, through which one obtains sky-going power and <s>Śiva</s>-hood in one's own body,

children.text: tādṛśe tu rasajñāne nityābhyāsaṃ kuru priye ||
children.translated_text: practice constantly, dear one.
The blessed Goddess said:
O lord of the gods, I wish to hear the descent and greatness of the lord of <s>rasa</s>.
O lord of the gods, you ought to speak of it truthfully.
The blessed <s>Bhairava</s> said:
You have asked well, greatly fortunate one, about what is more secret than the secret.
It is a meditation that brings favor and benefits the worlds.

children.text: tvaṃ mātā sarvabhūtānāṃ pitā cāhaṃ sanātanaḥ
children.translated_text: You are the mother of all beings, and I am the eternal father.
The <s>rasa</s>, goddess, that belongs to the two of us arises from the great sexual union.
Because it arose spontaneously, goddess, <s>pārada</s> is proclaimed as a great radiance.
And what is called <s>pārada</s> has been explained by the best practitioners for the sake of others.
This <s>sūta</s> is equal to me, goddess, born from each limb of mine.
Because it is the fluid of my body, it is therefore called <s>rasa</s>.
From seeing it, touching it, eating it, or even remembering it,
and from worshiping it and giving it, a sixfold result is seen.

children.text: kedārādīni liṅgāni pṛthivyāṃ yāni kāni ca
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>liṅgas</s> such as <s>Kedāra</s> exist on the earth,

children.text: tāni dṛṣṭvā tu yatpuṇyaṃ tatpuṇyaṃ rasadarśanāt ||
children.translated_text: the merit gained by seeing them is the same merit gained from seeing <s>rasa</s>.
The <s>rasa</s> (mercury), placed amid sandalwood, aloe, camphor, and saffron,
is swooned in the worship of <s>Śiva</s>, for the attainment of <s>Śiva</s>'s presence.
When eaten, O <s>Parameśāni</s>, the <s>rasa</s> destroys the threefold sin;
likewise it destroys the threefold affliction and the diseases born from the three <s>doṣas</s>.
The supreme state, hard to obtain even by those immersed in <s>Brahman</s>, is attained,
O <s>Maheśvarī</s>, through <s>Rasendra</s> abiding within the pericarp of the sky of the heart.
By remembering him one is immediately freed from sins accumulated in other births.
The fruit that comes from properly worshipping thousands of self-born <s>liṅgas</s>,
that fruit, multiplied ten million times, arises from worship of the <s>rasa-liṅga</s>.
The doctrine of <s>khaga</s> is inferior; the doctrine of <s>bila</s> is middling.
The doctrine of mantra is superior, but the doctrine of <s>rasa</s> is highest of all.
Those who, while knowing mantra and tantra, disparage <s>rasayoga</s>,
all go to hell after cutting away their accumulated merit.
<s>Rasavidyā</s> is the highest knowledge, very hard to obtain even in the three worlds.
Since it grants enjoyment and liberation, it should therefore be given by those endowed with virtue.
Someone says, 'It exists'; someone says, 'It does not exist.'

children.text: āstike tu bhavetsiddhiḥ tasya sidhyati bhūtale ||
children.translated_text: But for one who has faith there is accomplishment; his practice succeeds on earth.
Whoever, with the attitude of a denier, says, 'It does not exist, it does not exist,'
for him, dear one, there is no accomplishment even through hundreds of crores of births.
As for the sinner who reviles <s>rasa</s>, though he may be freed by knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>,
I will not become his savior even through hundreds of crores of births.
O <s>Devi</s>, he is born as a dog for a thousand births;
because of <s>rasa</s> he is born as a cat for three crores and lakhs of births.
He becomes a donkey for a hundred thousand births, and a crow for a hundred thousand births.
He is a worm for a hundred thousand births and a rooster for a hundred thousand births;
the sinner who reviles <s>rasa</s> is a vulture for a hundred thousand births.
Whoever holds conversation or bodily contact with revilers of <s>rasa</s>,
he will be afflicted with suffering for a thousand births.
In taste, potency, and post-digestive effect, <s>sūtaka</s> is like nectar.
By it, dear one, <s>sūtaka</s> removes birth, old age, and disease.
First one should worship the guru with an inward self made pure.
When the guru is pleased, the rays grant the tradition.

children.text: gurusevāṃ vinā karma yaḥ kuryān mūḍhacetanaḥ
children.translated_text: The foolish-minded person who performs an operation without service to the guru

children.text: sa yāti niṣphalaṃ karma svapnalabdhaṃ dhanaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: goes to fruitless action, like wealth obtained in a dream.

children.text: yaḥ karma kurute dṛṣṭaṃ tasya lābhaḥ pade pade
children.translated_text: For one who performs the operation that has been shown, gain comes at every step.

children.text: kārayed rasavādaṃ tu tuṣṭena guruṇā priye ||
children.translated_text: One should have <s>rasavāda</s> performed by a pleased guru, dear one.
This is instruction in the means of accomplishment, granting both enjoyment and liberation.
This great tantra, the <s>Rasārṇava</s>, is exceedingly rare.
It is secret; by the guru's grace it may be obtained for the success of the fruit.
Having obtained the operations of <s>rasa</s> here, one should not act with arrogance.
Authorized by the guru, and having received the command called the <s>rasāṅkuśī</s>,
one should take refuge in the <s>Bhairavī</s> body and accomplish <s>Rasabhairava</s>.
Thus the origin of <s>rasa</s> and its greatness have been stated, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>.
Tell me that, O <s>Deveśī</s>: what else do you wish to hear?
The blessed <s>Devī</s> said:

children.text: rasopadeśadātā ca kathaṃ syādvada me prabho
children.translated_text: Tell me, lord, what sort of person should be a giver of instruction in <s>rasa</s>?
And what sort of disciple, O god, is devoted to the practice of <s>rasa</s>?
The blessed <s>Bhairava</s> said:
One who is free from longing, free from ego, devoid of greed and illusion,
always devoted to the <s>kula</s> path and devoted to worship of the guru;
self-controlled, knowing how to instruct disciples, powerful, free from envy,

children.text: dharmajñaḥ satyavāk dakṣaḥ śīlavān guṇavān śuciḥ ||
children.translated_text: knowing <s>dharma</s>, truthful in speech, skillful, virtuous, endowed with qualities, and pure;
versed in many <s>rasaśāstras</s> and skilled in the <s>rasa</s> pavilion;
knowing the procedure of <s>rasadīkṣā</s>, the apparatus, medicines, and great minerals;
the number of colors, seed-calculations, the combining of pairs, and <s>viḍa</s>;

children.text: rañjanaṃ sāraṇaṃ tailaṃ dalāni krāmaṇāni ca ||
children.translated_text: coloring, conveying, oils, leaves, and the <s>krāmaṇas</s>;
heightening of color, softness, digestion, and the immature and bound states;

children.text: khecarīṃ bhūcarīṃ caiva yo vetti sa gururmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: one who knows <s>khecarī</s> and <s>bhūcarī</s> is regarded as a guru.
He knows place, time, and procedure, and is endowed with compassion and generosity.
Free from greed and illusion, he is devoted to the performance of mantras.
He possesses auspicious bodily marks, is deep, and is affectionate toward the guru.
He is always devoted to worship of the gods, fire, the circle of yoginīs, and the <s>kula</s>.
The disciple is humble, versed in tantra, truthful, and firm in his vow.
Men whose hands are marked with signs such as a pot, hoe, banner, and conch,
O <s>Devi</s>, are to be appointed to the accomplishment of treasures.
Those who are strong, of great vitality, with black and red eyes,
crooked-nosed and always fierce, are praised for <s>bila-sādhana</s>.
Those with fleshless head-lumps, red-haired, free from laziness,
hard, and hot-footed should be assigned to <s>dhātuvāda</s>.
At the beginning, O <s>Devi</s>, he should examine practitioners who are well composed:
<s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and <s>Śūdras</s>, in due order.
Practitioners who have conquered their senses, endure hardship, and are always energetic,
and who are brave and learned, are praised, dear one.
Those who lack <s>rasadīkṣā</s> and are devoid of the qualities that have been stated,
being disruptive and devoted to sin, one should carefully avoid.
A woman who is ill-conducted, badly behaved, harsh, fond of quarrels,

children.text: bahvāśinī ca duścittā koṭarākṣī ca nirdayā
children.translated_text: gluttonous, evil-minded, hollow-eyed, and merciless,

children.text: rasanindākarī yā ca tāṃ nārīṃ parivarjayet ||
children.translated_text: and one who reviles <s>rasa</s>: such a woman one should avoid.
With women of this sort, O fair-hipped one, the circle of the earth is filled.
There would be no woman like one who binds <s>rasa</s>.
<s>Kākiṇī</s>, <s>kīkaṇī</s>, a woman, and likewise <s>kāñcikācinī</s>:

children.text: kṛṣṇapakṣe ṛtumatī sā nārī kākiṇī smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: a woman who menstruates in the dark fortnight is remembered as a <s>kākiṇī</s>.

children.text: ubhayapakṣe ṛtumatī sā nārī kīkaṇī matā ||
children.translated_text: A woman who menstruates in both fortnights is regarded as a <s>kīkaṇī</s>.
A woman who menstruates in the bright fortnight is a <s>kāñcikācinī</s>.
A woman endowed with fresh youth, beautiful in form and charming in smile,

children.text: sūkṣmakeśā tu yā nārī kṣīrāhārapriyā sadā ||
children.translated_text: with fine hair, and always fond of a diet of milk,
who constantly speaks affectionately and delights in discourse on the <s>Śivaśāstra</s>,
whose face is lotus-shaped and whose glance has the form of a blue lotus,
whose teeth are like diamonds and whose lower lip is like coral,

children.text: yasyāḥ payodharau devi tuṅgapīnau samāv ubhau ||
children.translated_text: whose two breasts, O goddess, are high, full, and equal,
whose yoni is like the leaf of the aśvattha tree and whose vulva is even,
whose two feet are fleshy, smooth, round, and have curling hair,

children.text: śyāmā ca madhye kṣāmā ca tanvī bhaktiparā śive
children.translated_text: who is dark, slender at the waist, delicate, and devoted to worship, O <s>Śivā</s>,

children.text: padminī sā tu vijñeyā prasannā mṛgalocanā ||
children.translated_text: she should be known as a <s>padminī</s>, gracious and deer-eyed.
Menstruating at the full moon or at the new moon, in each fortnight,
the sixfold one previously named <s>kākiṇī</s> is said to grant rasa.
For the one with whom <s>Mahādeva</s> is pleased, she becomes successful in <s>rasāyana</s>.
With her alone, O queen of the gods, he should cause the operations of rasa to be performed.
For his intellect is pure and fixed upon the accomplishment of rasa.
Therefore both guru and disciple, as previously described, become sharers in success.
<s>Śrīdevī</s> said:
Where can a practitioner obtain a woman with such characteristics?

children.text: yatra rūpaṃ mahādeva lakṣaṇaṃ nātra vidyate ||
children.translated_text: Where there is beauty, O <s>Mahādeva</s>, such a characteristic is not found.

children.text: lakṣaṇaṃ vidyate yatra bhāvanā nātra vidyate
children.translated_text: Where the characteristic is found, inner cultivation is not found there.
Or, in one devoid of beauty, by what means does beauty arise?
Where have you seen the triad of characteristics, O <s>Maheśvara</s>?
Tell me, lord, the means by which this comes about.
<s>Śrībhairava</s> said:

children.text: śṛṇu devi paraṃ guhyaṃ yatsurairapi durlabham
children.translated_text: Listen, goddess, to the supreme secret, which is hard even for the gods to obtain:
birth from the father <s>Sadāśiva</s>, and birth in the womb of <s>Caṇḍikā</s>.
Their intellect, O goddess, should become pure in the practice of rasa.
He should give her the <s>Tvaritā</s> mantra, and she should recite it free from arrogance.

children.text: lakṣamantraṃ japedyā tu jāyate sā sulakṣaṇā
children.translated_text: The woman who recites the mantra one hundred thousand times becomes one of good characteristics.

children.text: baddhvā tu khecarīṃ mudrāṃ japet pheṭkārabhairavīm ||
children.translated_text: Having bound the <s>khecarī</s> mudrā, she should recite the <s>Pheṭkārabhairavī</s>.

children.text: mameyaṃ caṇḍikā mātā janma ca tripurāntakāt
children.translated_text: "This <s>Caṇḍikā</s> is my mother, and my birth is from <s>Tripurāntaka</s>;
I have arisen as <s>Kālikā</s>." Thus should she remember.

children.text: bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ ca trailokye kathayettu sā
children.translated_text: She should speak of the past, the future, and what is to come in the three worlds.
His assistants will be such as his destiny is to be.
<s>Śrīdevī</s> said:
O god of gods, <s>Mahādeva</s>, vessel of all knowledge,

children.text: rasadīkṣāṃ tu pṛcchāmi sādhakānāṃ hitāya vai ||
children.translated_text: I ask about <s>rasadīkṣā</s>, for the benefit of practitioners.
<s>Śrībhairava</s> said:

children.text: śṛṇu bhairavi yadbhāvam apūrvaṃ varṇayāmi te
children.translated_text: Listen, O <s>Bhairavī</s>; I shall describe to you an unprecedented disposition.
Therefore hear the prescribed procedure of <s>rasadīkṣā</s> as it is set forth.
Where the king is devoted to policy, powerful, and intent on dharma,
and where the minister knows the truth of dharma and is endowed with devotion and faith,
there one should have this rite performed, the binding of rasa, the <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: janā māheśvarā yatra tatra sthāne tu kārayet ||
children.translated_text: Where the people are <s>Māheśvaras</s>, one should have it performed in that place.
One should have it performed in a solitary place, where there is no beast,
in a well-hidden, level place, free from all disturbances,
furnished with a rampart and moat, protected by doors and bars,
secluded, pure, pleasant, and furnished with various flowering trees,
filled with geese and kāraṇḍava ducks, adorned with cakravāka birds,
endowed with groups of divine herbs, with water, dark with green turf,
adorned with clusters of kumuda, utpala, kahlāra lotuses, and plantains,
in a decorated palace garden one should have it made, O <s>Parameśvarī</s>.
In the middle of that, O queen of the gods, there should be a pavilion with rutting elephants,
provided with windows and with smoke issuing upward,
joined with red banners and likewise furnished with prepared implements,
with separate stores for medicines, husks, wood, forest products, and lotuses,
with the deities of the directions drawn upon it and <s>Vināyaka</s> worshiped,
established by <s>Umā</s> and <s>Īśa</s> and protected by the guardians of the worlds.
He should have a one-storied or two-storied pavilion constructed.
Then, O goddess, in the bright fortnight, when the moon and stars are strong,

children.text: puṇye tithau muhūrte ca lagne saumyagrahekṣite
children.translated_text: on an auspicious lunar day, at an auspicious moment, under an ascendant aspected by benefic planets,
having bathed, wearing white garments, with white garlands and unguents,
he should worship maidens with honey, ghee, curds, milk, and sesame.
In a place smeared with the dung of a tawny cow and surrounded by golden pitchers,
strewn with barley and white mustard seeds and adorned with perfumes and garlands,
there, on a hand-platform made with bricks, O queen of the gods,
having incised a stone slab and a stone-slab bolt, O beloved,
having performed nyāsa with the <s>rasāṅkuśa</s> on the fingers, heart, and other places,

children.text: rasaliṅgaṃ nyasettatra hemnā ca sahitaṃ priye
children.translated_text: he should install the <s>rasaliṅga</s> there together with gold, O beloved.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ sūtarājasya mūlamantra udāhṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ": this is declared to be the root mantra of the king of mercury.
With that root mantra he should invoke the goddess <s>Rasāṅkuśī</s> there, O beloved.

children.text: caturasre tu dikpālān pūjayitvā bahiḥ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: Having worshiped the guardians of the directions in order outside the square,
he should worship <s>Nandin</s>, <s>Mahākāla</s>, <s>Bhṛṅgirīṭa</s> the very strong,

children.text: kumbhakarṇaṃ ca sugrīvaṃ bhṛṅgīkaṃ ca dṛḍhāyudham ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, <s>Sugrīva</s>, <s>Bhṛṅgīka</s>, and <s>Dṛḍhāyudha</s>.
Having placed them fourfold at the door, he should worship them on the right and left.
Having first worshiped <s>Śukra</s> in the east, and <s>Skanda</s> in the southeast quarter,

children.text: dakṣiṇasyāṃ tato rudraṃ pavanaṃ nairṛte tathā
children.translated_text: then <s>Rudra</s> in the south and <s>Pavana</s> in the southwest,

children.text: śivaṃ paścimabhāge tu pāvakaṃ vāyave nyaset
children.translated_text: he should place <s>Śiva</s> in the western part and <s>Pāvaka</s> in the northwest.
But <s>Umā</s> is in the upper part, and the all-pervading one is in the domain of <s>Īśa</s>.

children.text: lepikā kṣepikā caiva kṣārikā rañjikā tathā
children.translated_text: The applicator, the thrower, the caustic one, and likewise the dyer,
the iron-working one, the binder, the earth-moving one, and the destroyer of death,

children.text: vibhūtiḥ khecarī caiva daśa dūtyaḥ krameṇa ca
children.translated_text: <s>Vibhūti</s> and <s>Khecarī</s>: these are the ten female messengers in order.
They are to be worshipped on the eight-petaled lotus, in the petals above and below.
<s>Mākṣika</s>, <s>Vimala</s>, <s>Śaila</s>, <s>Capala</s>, and <s>Rasaka</s>,
<s>Sasyaka</s>, sulfur, and orpiment are placed in order beginning with the east.
The <s>Rudras</s> have eighteen arms, five faces, and three eyes;
their crowns are adorned with a half-moon, their throats are blue, and their banner is the bull.
All bear their own colors; so too are the eight lords of knowledge.
They are to be worshipped, O <s>Maheśānī</s>, in the second eight-petaled lotus.
In the pericarp, beginning from the east in due order, are four powers:
<s>Mālinī</s>, the golden power, the supreme power, and the power called <s>Balā</s>;
the lower power, the adamantine power, and <s>Kānti</s> are known as the supreme-and-lower.

children.text: madhye tāsāṃ ca śaktīnāṃ sarvajñaṃ rasabhairavam
children.translated_text: In the midst of those powers is omniscient <s>Rasabhairava</s>,
shining like pure crystal, five-faced and three-eyed,
with fierce blazing tawny eyes and a mouth with a blazing tongue,
with blazing brows and blazing hair, hard to behold, seated on a corpse,
joined with a crown of matted hair and bearing the half-moon as his crest,
wearing a tiger skin, with a serpent as his sacred thread, and having the bull as his banner.
He is a god with eighteen arms and a face slightly smiling.
With the thirty-two-syllabled mantra one should worship <s>Śiva</s> in his entirety.

children.text: raseśvarasya mantraṃ ca kathyamānaṃ nibodha me ||
children.translated_text: Now listen to me as the mantra of <s>Raseśvara</s> is being taught.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ krīṃ raseśvarāya mahākālāya mahābalāyāghorabhairavāya vajravīra krodhakaṅkāla kṣlauḥ kṣlaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ hrīṃ krīṃ raseśvarāya mahākālāya mahābalāyāghorabhairavāya vajravīra krodhakaṅkāla kṣlauḥ kṣlaḥ.
On his lap is the great goddess, adorned with jeweled ornaments,
beautiful with the luster of heated gold, clothed in yellow garments, and three-eyed.
She shines between two white yak-tail fans and beneath a pearl parasol,
holding a goad and a rosary in her right hands,
and a noose and the gesture of fearlessness in her left hands, with the half-moon as her crest.
One should worship the great goddess <s>Rasāṅkuśī</s>, blue-throated and full of compassion,
for the sake of success in <s>rasa</s>, by means of the five-seed vidyā.

children.text: vāgbhavaṃ bhuvaneśīṃ ca śrībījaṃ ca sureśvari ||
children.translated_text: It consists of <s>Vāgbhava</s>, <s>Bhuvaneśī</s>, the seed of <s>Śrī</s>, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>,
the erotic seed, and the seed of power; this vidyā is exceedingly difficult to obtain.
With incense, lamps, offerings of food, flowers, betel, and sandalwood,
with the loud recitations of the peace rite and the auspicious sounds of hymns,
accompanied by the ringing of bells, one should perform the worship according to rule.
With the Aghora mantra one should offer bali for the pacification of all obstacles,
carefully to the spirits, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rakṣases</s>, and <s>piśācas</s>.
It is joined with the Aghora mantra, begins with oṃ, and ends with namaḥ;
O <s>Devi</s>, it accomplishes every rite and destroys obstacles and afflictions.
Having recited the vidyā of <s>Rasāṅkuśī</s> according to his ability,
he should prepare a fire-pit, O <s>Deveśī</s>, with a yonicakra and a surrounding belt.
There he should perform the oblation in sequence, using ghee mixed with sesame.
He should set up a water-pot, O <s>Devi</s>, filled with milk and furnished with fruits,
provided with the five jewels and wrapped with cloths.
Having empowered it there separately with the eighteen vidyās,
filled with perfumes, flowers, and the like, and made beautiful with shoots,
he should worship the vessel for arghya and sprinkle the practitioner with the vardhanī.
One hundred and eight times, with the water from the arghya-vessel,
the knower of mantra should bathe him according to rule with the water of the pot.
He should teach the vidyā, O <s>Devi</s>, and cause the practitioner of <s>rasa</s> to recite it.
He should honor maidens, yoginīs, yogins, and practitioners as is proper,
with food and drink, and he should cause a night vigil to be held there.
A practitioner initiated in this manner, O queen of the gods,
should then, through the thread of breath-control and self, recite the vidyā
which consists of the great elements, is joined with the five colors,
and has the five seeds as its essence; having formed the <s>Rasāṅkuśī</s> mudrā, he should recite it one hundred thousand times, O dear one.
For him, O <s>Deveśī</s>, <s>Rasabhairava</s> is accomplished without obstruction.
The highest recitation, after the tarpaṇa, begins with the praṇava and ends with namaḥ.
Nonviolence is the sandalwood; truth is the flower; non-stealing is the incense;
celibacy is the great lamp, and non-acceptance is the little bell.
The rice cooked in milk, O <s>Maheśānī</s>, is the compassion whose nature is kindness toward all beings.
Having worshipped the goddess inwardly and secretly, he becomes a vessel of siddhi.

children.text: sahasraṃ vā śataṃ vāpi trisaṃdhyaṃ saṃjapedimām ||
children.translated_text: He should recite this a thousand times, or even a hundred times, at the three junctions of the day.
By the favor of her command, the <s>rasa</s> becomes sky-moving,
and divine herbs also become effective for him, O you honored by the gods.
Just as, in a forest, one mounts a rutting elephant without a goad,
so one who is not skilled in <s>Rasāṅkuśī</s>, having obtained <s>Rasendra</s>, comes to grief.
The procedures involving <s>rasa</s> should be considered together with the vidyā
by one who desires success in every way, from a guru of a true lineage.
Now, for the introduction of the questions, he should meditate with concentrated mind
on the previously described <s>Rasabhairava</s>, and should act while absorbed in him.
Having placed the mind in the stainless <s>anāhata</s> and <s>brahmarandhra</s>,
having first performed the hand-nyāsa and then the limb-nyāsa,
he should recite the mantra of <s>Rasendra</s>, concentrated, according to his ability.
Then, having made a square, he should make a six-cornered maṇḍala in the middle.
One should draw it one hasta or two hastas in size with spotless rice grains.
In a place smeared with fragrant substances, he should worship it with sandalwood and the like.
In the pericarp, O <s>Devi</s>, he should place the previously described <s>Rasabhairava</s>.
In the six-pointed figure he should arrange the group of six deities, beginning with <s>Mahākāla</s>.
He should place <s>Mahākāla</s>, <s>Mahābala</s>, <s>Aghora</s>, and <s>Vajravīraka</s>,

children.text: nyaset krodhaṃ ca kaṅkālaṃ mālāmantraiḥ samarcayet ||
children.translated_text: and also <s>Krodha</s> and <s>Kaṅkāla</s>; he should honor them with the garland-mantras.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ krauṃ kṣlaiṃ kṣlaṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ hrūḥ huṃ phaṭ raseśvarāya mahākālabhairavāya raudrarūpāya kṛṣṇapiṅgalalocanāya
children.translated_text: Oṃ hrīṃ krauṃ kṣlaiṃ kṣlaṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ hrūḥ huṃ phaṭ: to <s>Raseśvara Mahākālabhairava</s>, of fierce form, with dark tawny eyes,

children.text: avatara 2 avatāraya 2 jalpaya 2 śubhāśubhaṃ kathaya 2 kathāpaya 2 mahārakṣāṃ rasasiddhiṃ dehi
children.translated_text: descend, descend; cause descent, cause descent; speak, speak; tell the auspicious and inauspicious, tell it; cause it to be told; grant great protection and success in <s>rasa</s>.
These are the garland-mantras.
Oṃ, obeisance to <s>Mahākālabhairava</s> for the heart.
Oṃ, svāhā to <s>Mahābalabhairava</s> for the head.
Oṃ, vauṣaṭ to <s>Aghorabhairava</s> for the topknot.
Oṃ, huṃ to <s>Vajravīrabhairava</s> for the armor.
Oṃ, vauṣaṭ to <s>Krodhabhairava</s> for the eyes.
Oṃ, phaṭ to <s>Kaṅkālabhairava</s> for the missile.
Everywhere it ends with svāhā.
Thus are the installations on the limbs.
In this same way he should first perform the installations on the fingers.
These are the root-mantras in the worship of the six limbs.
Thus, with the syllables of installation arranged in groups, he should worship with perfumes and flowers.
He should set a full water jar in the middle and a bowl together with rice grains.
On top of it he should place a ghee lamp and consecrate the wick with mantras.

children.text: samānīya kumārīṃ tu kumāraṃ vā suśobhanam
children.translated_text: He should bring a beautiful maiden, or else a beautiful boy,
one, two, three, four, or five, bringing them according to availability.
He should worship them with perfumes, flowers, incense, lamps, and a food offering.
For each one he should install the mantra and the deities beginning with the heart.
Then, after they have gazed at that lamp, all the maidens there
see the deity in the lamp, and the boys see the auspicious and inauspicious.
The maidens tell of success or, alternatively, failure.
Having thus understood the descent of the answer, he should proceed in the <s>rasa</s>-operation.
He who formerly, O <s>Devadeveśī</s>, had his mind intent on lordly mercury,

children.text: saptajanma mṛto jāto na tyajed rasabhāvanam ||
children.translated_text: though dead and born through seven births, would not abandon the cultivation of <s>rasa</s>.
Having thus learned the auspicious and inauspicious, and being endowed with the deity's favor,
after worshipping the goddess <s>Rasāṅkuśī</s> in the pavilion as before,
and after fully honoring the ācārya with incense, garlands, sandalwood, and the like,

children.text: aghoreṇa baliṃ dattvā tataḥ karma samācaret ||
children.translated_text: having offered a bali with the Aghora mantra, he should then undertake the work.
The herbs are in the eastern part of the pavilion; the heating of <s>rasa</s> is in the region of fire.
The killing of metals is in the southern quarter, and grinding and the like in the southwest.

children.text: drutikriyā tu vāruṇyāṃ vāyavye dhamanaṃ priye
children.translated_text: The liquefaction procedure is in the western quarter, O beloved, and blowing with bellows is in the northwest.
Improvement of color is in the northern quarter, and piercing by <s>rasa</s> is in the northeast.
Having placed the guru's seat in the middle, O leader of the gods,
the operations beginning with regulation and ending with penetration, O fair-faced one,
are to be performed by the sādhaka with the <s>rasāṅkuśa</s> mantra.
The <s>Rasabhairava</s> who was formerly described, O <s>Devadeveśī</s>,

children.text: sadyojātaṃ tasya jānu vāmadevaṃ tu guhyakam ||
children.translated_text: has <s>Sadyojāta</s> as his knee and <s>Vāmadeva</s> as his private part.

children.text: aghoraṃ hṛdayaṃ tasya vaktraṃ tatpuruṣaṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: His heart is <s>Aghora</s>; his mouth is remembered as <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>.
Up to the space between the brows is <s>Īśāna</s>; the half-moon is the forehead.

children.text: bindur deveśi tasyordhve bindorūrdhve sthito nadaḥ
children.translated_text: Above that, O <s>Deveśī</s>, is the bindu; above the bindu stands the nāda.
Between the forehead and the head, <s>Śakti</s> is established just there.
The all-pervading one is situated at the brahmarandhra; above that is unmanā.
<s>Unmanā</s> is the state beyond mind, the imperishable station of unmanā.
Above that is the supreme truth, abiding in space, higher than the highest,

children.text: śūnyaṃ śūnyaṃ punaḥ śūnyaṃ triśūnyaṃ ca nirāmayam ||
children.translated_text: void, void, again void, the triple void, stainless and free from affliction.

children.text: nabhaśca gaganaṃ vyoma khamākāśaṃ ca kevalam
children.translated_text: It is sky, firmament, ether, space, and mere expanse,
without parts, stainless, eternal, waveless, and free from affliction;
without phenomenal expansion, unsupported, without qualities, yet within the range of qualities.
One should always meditate on <s>Rasabhairava</s> in one's own body in this form.

children.text: yadā ca niścalaṃ dhyāyet yadā ca niścalaṃ manaḥ
children.translated_text: When he meditates steadily, and when the mind is steady,
then mercury is bound in the midst of fire, likewise motionless.

children.text: yadā ca calati dhyānaṃ raso vahnau na tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: But when the meditation wavers, the <s>rasa</s> does not remain in the fire.
At night, outside the maṇḍala, with liquor, fish, meat, and the like,
he should worship yakṣas, gandharvas, piśācas, and rākṣasas.
Obstacles to the performance of the rite and obstacles to its fruit
arise by the tens of millions; therefore, for the pacification of each of them,
he should worship <s>Vaṭukeśvara</s> and the sixfold favorable worship at the beginning, and then proceed.

children.text: karmānte ca punar bālam aṣṭāṣṭakam anugraham
children.translated_text: At the end of the work, again, having honored the child and the sixty-fourfold favoring rite,

children.text: sampūjya viniyuñjyāt tat siddhadravyaṃ tu siddhidam ||
children.translated_text: after worshipping, he should employ that perfected substance, which grants success.
When he has become perfected, he should put an end to disputation and abandon that region.
When the great <s>rasa</s> is well perfected, he should wander for alms in the manner of a bee.
If, through negligence, an obstacle arises after the binding of mercury has been performed,
pacification of the <s>rasa</s> must be carried out; he should not cause agitation of the <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: rasaṃ na darśayeddevi nārīhaste na pātayet
children.translated_text: He should not show the <s>rasa</s>, O <s>Devi</s>, nor place it in a woman's hand.

children.text: nāryai guhyaṃ na vaktavyaṃ dravyaṃ tābhyo hi gopayet ||
children.translated_text: The secret should not be told to a woman; the substance should indeed be concealed from them.
It should not be done with another's property; he should not touch another's wife.

children.text: parānnaṃ naiva bhuñjīta parāṃścaiva na viśvaset ||
children.translated_text: He should certainly not eat another's food, nor should he trust others.
It is not to be given to evil-minded men who ask in the guise of an assembly.
On the eighth lunar day, on the full-moon day, on the new-moon day, and at the beginnings of yugas...
At the solstice and at the equinox, and especially on the fourteenth lunar day,
one should perform the <s>rasotsava</s> according to the extent of one's wealth.
O <s>Devi</s>, whoever performs the <s>rasotsava</s> in this way, endowed with devotion,
his various sins, including the killing of a brahmin, are destroyed.

children.text: anena vidhinā yatra pūjāṃ kurvanti sādhakāḥ
children.translated_text: Where practitioners perform worship by this procedure,

children.text: na tatra rogadaurgatyaṃ netayaḥ prabhavanti ca ||
children.translated_text: there disease, misfortune, and calamities do not prevail.
Having established such worship in <s>rasa</s> according to rule,
afterwards the rite should be carried out by those who desire their own good fortune.

children.text: anyathā kurute yastu tasya siddhirna jāyate
children.translated_text: But the man who performs it otherwise does not attain success;

children.text: apāyaḥ pāpaśaṅkā ca buddhibhaṅgo hi jāyate ||
children.translated_text: danger, fear of sin, and the breaking of understanding arise for him.

children.text: avajñā rogajātaṃ ca saṃdehaśca pade pade
children.translated_text: Disregard, a mass of diseases, and doubt at every step arise.
Through laziness, through greed toward the guru, and through another's instruction,
the <s>kulakas</s>, dear one, take away even knowledge that has arisen.
An initiated man should perform the <s>rasa</s>-rites with knowledge of mantra-nyāsa.
Tell me that, O queen of gods; what else do you wish to hear?
The blessed <s>Devi</s> said:
Blessed lord, lord of gods, master of the world, ruler of the universe,
explain the mantra-nyāsa that assists the <s>rasa</s>-rite.
The blessed <s>Bhairava</s> said:
Again I shall teach another mantra-embodiment, <s>Rasāṅkuśī</s>,

children.text: pañcamaṃ tu gṛhaṃ devi durlabhaṃ devadānavaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the fifth house, O <s>Devi</s>, which is hard for gods and demons to obtain.
There are four principal houses; the <s>Haṃsa</s>-house is the fifth.

children.text: yatra siddhir makārādiḥ tiṣṭhate pañcame gṛhe ||
children.translated_text: There success beginning with the syllable <s>ma</s> abides in the fifth house.

children.text: liṅgāśrayaṃ yathā rūpaṃ liṅgimāyā tu liṅginī
children.translated_text: As form rests on the <s>liṅga</s>, the <s>māyā</s> of the bearer of the <s>liṅga</s> is <s>Liṅginī</s>.

children.text: gaganena tu sā jñeyā bhagarekhā tu pañcame ||
children.translated_text: She is to be known through <s>gagana</s>; the <s>bhagarekhā</s> is in the fifth.
Having first uttered the <s>praṇava</s>, then the seed, the unsurpassed sound,
and the syllable <s>hrīṃ</s>, the syllable <s>krīṃ</s>, and then the <s>haṃsa</s>-awareness,
the lord of practitioners should take up <s>Kālapāśa</s>, the great mantra.
At the great commencement, that mantra, the <s>pratīhāra</s>, is <s>Rasāṅkuśī</s>.
If he recites it one hundred thousand times, great accomplishment begins for him.
Then he should have the dung of a young calf procured by that very means.
By that same means he should have ash from a funeral fire procured, O supreme lady.
That field is the highest place; <s>Rasendra</s> abides there.
He should sweep the place with a broom; the <s>khecarī</s> called <s>Kubjikā</s>
has thirty-two syllables, O <s>Devi</s>, and is established in the five sounds.
Then four accomplished beings and eighteen men are remembered.
It is joined with the five objects, and the meditation is again fivefold.
It is joined with the six yoginīs and endowed with the twenty-sevenfold sequence;
it has eighty-one words and is furnished with five enclosures.
By this ordered method he should fully worship the broom.

children.text: anena mārjayet kṣetraṃ rasendro yatra tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: By this he should sweep the field where <s>Rasendra</s> abides.

children.text: upalepaṃ tu tatraiva caṇḍaghaṇṭāṃ tu kārayet
children.translated_text: There he should perform the smearing, and he should invoke <s>Caṇḍaghaṇṭā</s>.

children.text: pūrve gṛhe tu sā devī caṇḍaghaṇṭā vyavasthitā ||
children.translated_text: That goddess <s>Caṇḍaghaṇṭā</s> is established in the eastern house.
The goddess <s>Caṇḍabhairavikā</s> is established in the southern house.
By her he should take cow-dung for the sake of smearing, O lovely-faced one.
The goddess <s>Caṇḍakāpālinī</s> is established in the northern house.
Taking water by her, he should smear the ground-maṇḍala.
He should place the seventeen-syllabled <s>Kālī</s> on the mortar-stone.
He should assign the terrible thirty-two-syllabled mantra to the pestle.
O <s>Devi</s>, he should take <s>kāñjika</s> consecrated with <s>Kālapāśa</s>.
Thus the clan of <s>khecarīs</s> brings about the conjunction with a good rite.
The eighty-eight thousand divine <s>khecarīs</s> who are present,

children.text: tāḥ sarvāḥ kiṃkarāstasya auṣadhaṃ peṣayanti tāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all of them become his servants; they grind the medicine.
For all of them there is a single mantra, furnished with four syllables:

children.text: so 'haṃ haṃsaḥ sā vidyā khecarīṇāṃ tu nāmnāṃ tu kulakhecarī ||
children.translated_text: <s>So 'haṃ haṃsaḥ</s>; that vidyā of the <s>khecarīs</s>, among their names, is <s>Kulakhecarī</s>.

children.text: rājikāṃ saindhavaṃ nyasya sā vidyā kulakhecarī
children.translated_text: Having placed mustard seed and rock salt, that vidyā is <s>Kulakhecarī</s>.
There he should consecrate the <s>kāñjika</s> with mantra; the mantra-king is <s>Rasāṅkuśī</s>.
There he should recite the weapon-vidyā that is known in the former <s>Bhārgava</s> teaching.

children.text: guḍeṣṭakāṃ tu saṃmardya priye tanmarditaṃ rasam ||
children.translated_text: Having crushed the brick of jaggery, dear one, he should use the <s>rasa</s> crushed with it.

children.text: kā kathā mantrarājasya na vākyaṃ triśirasya ca
children.translated_text: What need is there to speak of the mantra-king, or of the utterance of <s>Triśiras</s>?

children.text: ṣaḍaṅgaṃ yojayet tāṃ tu tvaritaṃ dhārayet tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: He should apply its six limbs and then quickly retain it.
He should assign the great mantra called <s>Ḍāmara</s> to the channels.
He should assign the great vidyā <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> to the protective armors.

children.text: caṇḍikāyā mahāmantraṃ taṃ tu pātre niyojayet
children.translated_text: He should assign the great mantra of <s>Caṇḍikā</s> to the vessel.
O lovely-hipped one, he should place <s>Navavidyā</s> in the husk and cow-dung mixture.
He should place the goddess <s>Tripurābhairavī</s> in the mustard seed and <s>kāñjika</s>.
O honored by heroes, <s>Kālarātrī</s> should be placed in the jaggery.

children.text: trikūṭākṣaṃ trinetraṃ tu analasya tu vinyaset
children.translated_text: He should place <s>Trikūṭākṣa</s> and <s>Trinetra</s> in the fire.
O <s>Devi</s>, he should place the eighty-four <s>Caṇḍikās</s> in the water.
Dear one, <s>Kṣetrapāla</s> and the <s>Aghorāstra</s> should be placed in the furnace chamber.
The <s>Mahāpāśupatāstra</s> should be assigned to the crucible.
O <s>Devi</s>, he should assign this group of mantras to the place of <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: tadā tu sidhyate tasya sādhakasya phalaṃ priye ||
children.translated_text: Then the fruit of that practitioner is accomplished, dear one.
He should recite the great <s>Rasāṅkuśa</s> mantra within the heart.
As for the other yoginī-mantras, he should cause all the women to recite them.
He should keep that mantra-king <s>Rasāṅkuśa</s> concealed.
He should keep it concealed from women too, and likewise guard the <s>praṇava</s>.
For women this is like a breach of the great covenant in the heart.

children.text: kubjikādyāstu ye mantrā mayā te saṃprakāśitāḥ
children.translated_text: The mantras beginning with <s>Kubjikā</s> have thus been revealed by me to you.

children.text: trailokyaṃ kṣobhitāste tu na manyante mama priye ||
children.translated_text: But when the three worlds are agitated, my dear, they pay me no heed.
By the knowledge that is the goad of <s>rasa</s> (alchemy), one should bring the three worlds under control.
Knowing the installation of mantras, and understanding the measures of apparatus, crucible, and fire,
the practitioner who performs alchemical operations obtains accomplishment.
<s>Śrī Devī</s> said:
Even if he knows the mantras, if he does not know the apparatuses, crucibles, fires, and measures,

children.text: kiṃ karoti mahādeva tāni me vaktumarhasi ||
children.translated_text: what can he do, <s>Mahādeva</s>? You should tell me those things.
<s>Śrī Bhairava</s> said:
<s>rasa</s> substances, secondary minerals, metals, cloth, sour gruel, and <s>viḍa</s> (alkaline flux),
blowpipes, iron implements, devices, mortars, stone grinders,
furnaces, bent tubes, cow dung, good fuel,
earthen apparatuses, pestles and mortars,
tongs, plates, pincers, earthen vessels, and iron bowls,
weights, balances, cutting tools, and touchstones,
bamboo tubes, metal tubes, crucibles, charcoal, and also herbs,
oils, acids, salts, alkalis, poisons, and secondary poisons:
having gathered such equipment, one should undertake the discipline of the operation.
When a vessel is half filled in its belly with a liquid substance,

children.text: mukhe tiryakkṛte bhāṇḍe rasaṃ sūtreṇa lambitam
children.translated_text: and when the mouth of the vessel is set crosswise, the <s>rasa</s> is suspended by a cord,
and one should steam it below; this is remembered as the <s>dolāyantra</s>.
Having made two iron crucibles, each measuring twelve finger-breadths,
one of them should have slight holes and be furnished with sulfur.
That one should be inserted into the other crucible, which contains <s>rasa</s>;
water should be below the mercury, and fire should be kindled above and below.
Dear one, the juice of garlic, carefully filtered through cloth,
should be applied abundantly with effort, flooding the <s>rasa</s> and sulfur.

children.text: sthālikāyāṃ nidhāyordhvaṃ sthālīm anyāṃ dṛḍhāṃ kuru
children.translated_text: Having placed it upward in a cooking pot, set another strong pot over it,

children.text: saṃdhiṃ vilepayedyatnāt mṛdā vastreṇa caiva hi ||
children.translated_text: and carefully smear the joint with clay and also with cloth.
In another pot, a heating called 'pigeon' should always be made with fire of karṣa fuel;
below the apparatus one should apply cow-dung fire, or else a very fierce fire.

children.text: evaṃ tu tridinaṃ kuryāt tato yantraṃ vimocayet
children.translated_text: One should do this for three days; then one should release the apparatus.
The operation should be done in hot water and on a hot hearth, not when it is cold.

children.text: na tatra kṣīyate sūto na ca gacchati kutracit
children.translated_text: There the mercury is not diminished, nor does it go anywhere.
By this procedural sequence one should perform the digestion of sulfur.
Fire is above, water below, and the collection of <s>rasa</s> is in the middle:
this, <s>Devī</s>, is the crucible-apparatus; it digests mica and the like.
I shall explain the womb-apparatus, which is for making paste and ash.
One should make a firm earthen crucible four finger-breadths long,
three finger-breadths across in the middle, with a round mouth.
There should be twenty parts of iron and one part of guggul.

children.text: suślakṣṇaṃ peṣayitvā tu toyaṃ dadyāt punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: After grinding it very finely, one should add water again and again.

children.text: mūṣālepaṃ tataḥ kuryāt tale piṣṭīṃ ca nikṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Then one should make a coating for the crucible and place the paste at the bottom.
With fire from husk and cow dung, one should produce a gentle steaming in the ground.

children.text: ahorātraṃ trirātraṃ vā rasendro bhasmatāṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: In one day and night, or in three nights, the lord of <s>rasa</s> becomes ash.
In the digestion, killing, and coloring of the king of <s>rasa</s>,
the apparatus alone is the supreme secret, where the medicines have great power.
This mercury, even without medicines, is bound by force through the apparatus.
Everywhere mercury escapes, except when it has the characteristic of a mountain-holder.
Drawn away by deities, it goes off even when it is standing in a clod of earth.
Therefore one who knows should not transgress the single power of the apparatus.
Through the combination of mantra and medicines, this indeed makes it perfectly accomplished.
The <s>Aghora</s> mantra is to be recited here; at the end of the recitation one should worship the <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: ekānte tu kriyā kāryā dṛṣṭānyairviphalā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: The operation should be performed in solitude; if it is seen by others, it will be fruitless.

children.text: gandhakasya kṣayo nāsti na rasasya kṣayo bhavet
children.translated_text: There is no loss of sulfur, and there should be no loss of <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: kṣayo yantrasya vijñeyaḥ yantre vikriyate kriyā
children.translated_text: Loss should be understood as belonging to the apparatus; the operation changes in the apparatus.
If magnetic iron is not available, one should make the apparatus from ordinary iron.
If one does not know the sign of the fire, half of the <s>rasa</s> may be lost.
For one who knows the rule of loss in the apparatus, a quarter may be lost.
In two months a second portion is lost; in three months a third may be lost.

children.text: mahāgniṃ sahate hy eṣa sārito yatra tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: This one, when discharged and remaining there, indeed withstands a great fire.
Having made a potsherd filled with sand, one should place it on top of that;

children.text: aparaṃ kharparaṃ tatra śanair mṛdvagninā pacet ||
children.translated_text: then another potsherd there should be cooked slowly with a gentle fire.
With the five alkalis, with urines, and with salts, then the <s>viḍa</s> is prepared.
That is known as the swan-cooking by those skilled in the meaning of apparatus and procedure.

children.text: kṛṣṇā raktā ca pītā ca śuklavarṇā ca mṛttikā
children.translated_text: Clay may be black, red, yellow, or white in color.

children.text: ādyā śreṣṭhā kaniṣṭhāntyā madhyamā madhyamā matā ||
children.translated_text: The first is best, the last is inferior, and the middle two are regarded as middling.
Clay mixed with burnt grain-husk is recommended for the method of the furnace,
or else clay prepared with a bent tube is praised, beautiful goddess.

children.text: gārā dagdhā tuṣā dagdhā dagdhā valmīkamṛttikā
children.translated_text: Burnt mortar, burnt husk, and burnt anthill clay,

children.text: ajāśvānāṃ malaṃ dagdhaṃ yāvattat kṛṣṇatāṃ gatam ||
children.translated_text: and the burnt dung of goats and horses, until it has become black:

children.text: vāsakasya ca pattrāṇi valmīkasya mṛdā saha
children.translated_text: the leaves of <s>vāsaka</s> too, together with anthill clay,
should be ground with fire-water until it has become smooth.
One should knead with that and bind the bent tube and the furnace.

children.text: gārā dagdhā tuṣā dagdhā dagdhā valmīkamṛttikā
children.translated_text: Burnt mortar, burnt husk, and burnt anthill clay,
with old charcoal and dross, cannot be split even by a diamond.
Six parts of burnt charcoal and one part of black clay,
with old charcoal and dross, are called the diamond-crucible.
Burnt husk equal to cloth, and clay in four parts,
combined with kupī-stone, is proclaimed to be an excellent crucible.

children.text: prakāśā cāndhamūṣā ca mūṣā tu dvividhā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: The crucible is remembered as of two kinds: open and closed.
The open crucible, O <s>Deveśī</s>, has the form of a shallow dish;
for the draining off of substances it is highly praised by the alchemical practitioners.
But the closed crucible should be made resembling a cow's teat,
fitted with a lid and with its top somewhat raised.
For coating leaves, for coloring, and also for combining pairs of substances,
that same one, furnished with holes, slow and deep, is suitable for sāraṇa (transmission).
Sesame ash, two parts, together with one part brick,
should be known as an ash-crucible, useful for purifying silver.
Two parts of mokṣa-alkali, together with one part brick,
and portions of clay are best for the purification of silver, O fair one.
Mixed with the red group, drenched in the red group,
and coated with the red group, it is excellent for all purifications.
Mixed with the white group, drenched in the white group,
and coated with the white group, it is excellent for purifications of white metals.
Mixed with the viḍa group, it seeks firmness in jāraṇa (digestion/assimilation);
one should carry out nirvāhaṇa (draining) with one smeared with the red group.
One should make a crucible coating with poison, borax, and guñjā seeds;
or else one should apply an aṅgāra coating on the open crucible.

children.text: tasyāṃ vinyasya mūṣāyāṃ dravyam āvartayed budhaḥ
children.translated_text: Having placed the substance in that crucible, the wise person should heat it to fusion.
The coating is a color-puṭa, O <s>Devi</s>, made with red clay, sindhu, earth, and khaga.

children.text: āvartamāne kanake pītā tāre sitā prabhā
children.translated_text: When gold is being fused, its flame is yellow; in silver, the radiance is white;
in copper it is like blue; in tīkṣṇa (iron/steel), it is black-colored, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>.
In tin the flame is dove-colored; in lead it is soiled and smoky;

children.text: śaile tu dhūsarā devi āyase kapilaprabhā ||
children.translated_text: in śaila it is grey, O <s>Devi</s>; in iron it has a tawny radiance.
In lodestone it is smoke-colored; in sasyaka it should be red;
in diamond the flame is of many kinds, and in kha-sattva it has a pale radiance.

children.text: na visphuliṅgo na ca budbudaśca yadā na rekhāpaṭalaṃ na śabdaḥ
children.translated_text: When there is no spark, no bubble, no streaked layer, and no sound,

children.text: mūṣāgataṃ ratnasamaṃ sthiraṃ ca tadā viśuddhaṃ pravadanti loham ||
children.translated_text: and the metal in the crucible is steady like a jewel, then they declare the metal purified.
Pratīvāpa (covering addition) should first be applied; niṣeka (quenching) comes immediately after.

children.text: chādanaṃ tu pratīvāpaḥ niṣekaṃ majjanaṃ viduḥ
children.translated_text: They know pratīvāpa as covering, and niṣeka as immersion.

children.text: abhiṣekaṃ tadicchanti snapanaṃ kriyate tu yat ||
children.translated_text: They understand abhiṣeka as the sprinkling that is performed as bathing.

children.text: vāpo niṣekaḥ snapanaṃ drute nirmalatāṃ gate
children.translated_text: Vāpa, niṣeka, and bathing are done when the molten metal has become clear.

children.text: uṣṇenaiva hi vāñchanti śītalaṃ na ca vāñchati ||
children.translated_text: Indeed they desire it while it is still hot; they do not desire it cold.
When the fire is bright white and accompanied by sound,

children.text: lohāvartaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ sattvaṃ patati nirmalam ||
children.translated_text: that should be known as the fusion of metal; the pure sattva falls down.
For the settling out of metallic sattva, O fair one,
the auspicious furnace should be sixteen fingers broad and one hasta long.
With firm charcoal produced from bamboo, khadira, madhūka, and badarī wood,
one should fill the furnace and blow it with air;
with bellows, through the flame-channel, one should kindle the fire.
The furnace should have a broad mouth, its inner region closed in, and a long intervening grating constructed on the ground.

children.text: bakagalasamamānaṃ vaṅkanālaṃ vidheyaṃ śuṣiranalinikā syānmṛnmayī dīrghavṛttā ||
children.translated_text: A curved tube equal to a crane's neck should be made; the hollow pipe should be earthen, long, and round.
In an earthen vessel, or in an iron vessel, or else in one made of lodestone,
or in stone, crystal, or one made of pearl-rock,
a very firm mardaka (grinding pestle) should be made, four fingers high.

children.text: sa ca lohamayaḥ śailo hy ayaskāntamayo'thavā ||
children.translated_text: And it may be made of metal, stone, or else lodestone.
By means of the mantra called <s>Aghorāstra</s>, or by the great <s>Pāśupata</s> mantra,
one should perform purification, and with that same mantra purify the ground.

children.text: indhanāni ca sarvāṇi dravyāṇi ca viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: All the fuels, and especially the substances,
one should set the burner aflame with it, and with it also purify the mortar.
With it one should purify mercury, and set it down on an auspicious day.
Having placed it upon the mortar, one should call to mind the form of <s>Śiva</s>.
Having obtained the favor of the deity, one who knows the measures of apparatus, crucibles, and fire,
O <s>Deveśī</s>, should also know the herbs for the sake of success with mercury.
The apparatus, crucibles, and measures of fire have been described, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>.
Tell that to me, O <s>Deveśī</s>; what else do you wish to hear?
<s>Śrīdevī</s> said:
O <s>Sureśvara</s>, please tell the herb by means of which
the operations beginning with niyāmana and ending with krāmaṇa are accomplished for these substances.
<s>Śrībhairava</s> said:
Sarpākṣī, vahnikarkoṭī, kañcukī, jalabindujā,
śatāvarī, bhṛṅgarāja, śarapuṅkhā, and punarnavā;
maṇḍūkaparṇī, matsyākṣī, brahmadaṇḍī, and śikhaṇḍinī;
anantā, kākajaṅghā, kākamācī, and kapotikā;
viṣṇukrāntā, sahacarā, sahādevī, and mahābalā;
balā, nāgabalā, kṛṣṇā, cakramarda, and kuruṅgiṇī;
pāṭhā, āmalakī, nīlī, jvālinī, and padmacāriṇī;
phaṇitrijihvā, gojihvā, kokilākṣa, and ghanadhvani;
ākhuparṇī, triparṇī, dviparṇī, and ekaparṇikā;

children.text: tittiḍī kṣīriṇī rāsnā meṣaśṛṅgī ca kukkuṭī ||
children.translated_text: tittiḍī, kṣīriṇī, rāsnā, meṣaśṛṅgī, and kukkuṭī;

children.text: kṛṣṇaparṇī ca tulasī śvetā ca girikarṇikā
children.translated_text: kṛṣṇaparṇī, tulasī, śvetā, and girikarṇikā:
these are the regulating herbs, furnished with flowers, roots, and leaves.
Dolāsveda (swing-steaming) should be performed with this root, O virtuous one.
Caṇḍālī, rākṣasī, vyāghrī, khaḍgārī, and gajakarṇikā,
śaṅkhapuṣpī, agnidhamanī, lāṅgalī, and bālamocakā.
<s>Raktasnuhī</s>, <s>raktaśṛṅgī</s>, <s>raktikā</s>, and <s>nīlacitraka</s>;

children.text: śṛgālajihvā bṛhatī vajrā cakrī ca rājikā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śṛgālajihvā</s>, <s>bṛhatī</s>, <s>vajrā</s>, <s>cakrī</s>, and <s>rājikā</s>;
<s>Ekavīrā</s>, <s>narakasā</s>, <s>rudantī</s>, and <s>brahmacāriṇī</s>;
<s>Uccaṭā</s>, <s>māninīkandā</s>, <s>kumārī</s>, and <s>raktacitraka</s>;
<s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>śākhoṭaka</s>, <s>kañcukī</s>, and <s>meṣaśṛṅgikā</s>;
<s>Himāvatī</s>, <s>somalatā</s>, <s>modā</s>, <s>vyāghranakhī</s>, and <s>śamī</s>;

children.text: kāñcanī vanarājī ca kākamācī ca keśinī
children.translated_text: <s>Kāñcanī</s>, <s>vanarājī</s>, <s>kākamācī</s>, and <s>keśinī</s>;
<s>Ajamārī</s>, <s>koṭarākṣī</s>, <s>hanūmatī</s>, and <s>aṅganāyikā</s>;
<s>Narajīvā</s>, <s>hemapuṣpī</s>, <s>kākamuṇḍī</s>, and <s>kālikā</s>;
<s>Toyavallī</s>, <s>gajārī</s>, <s>haṃsāṅghrī</s>, and <s>kuhukaṃvikā</s>;
<s>Tāmbūlī</s>, <s>sūryabhaktā</s>, and the substances that make mercury lifeless;
<s>Kaṭutumbī</s>, <s>gosandhī</s>, <s>devadālī</s>, and <s>indravāruṇī</s>;
<s>Vākucī</s>, <s>brahmabīja</s> seeds, cotton, and black cumin;
<s>Kaṅgunī</s>, <s>kṛṣṇakanaka</s>, white <s>arka</s>, and what is produced by ants;
<s>Dantinī</s>, <s>yavaciñcā</s>, <s>karkoṭī</s>, and <s>kāravallikā</s>;

children.text: gojihvā kākajaṅghā ca mahākālī ca śambarī
children.translated_text: <s>Gojihvā</s>, <s>kākajaṅghā</s>, <s>mahākālī</s>, and <s>śambarī</s>;
white <s>guñjā</s>, white <s>aṅkola</s>, <s>paṭolī</s>, and also <s>bilva</s>;
the seed of each single herb calcines <s>Rasabhairava</s> (mercury as Bhairava).
<s>Raktasnuhī</s>, <s>somalatā</s>, <s>rudantī</s>, and <s>raktacitraka</s>;
<s>Śākhoṭakī</s>, <s>dagdharuhā</s>, <s>modinī</s>, and <s>vṛddhadāruka</s>;
<s>Triśūlī</s>, <s>kṛṣṇamārjārī</s>, <s>cakrikā</s>, and <s>kṣīrakukkuṭī</s>;
<s>Devadālī</s>, <s>śaṅkhapuṣpī</s>, <s>kākamācī</s>, and <s>hanūmatī</s>;
<s>Nīlajyotis</s>, <s>tṛṇajyotis</s>, <s>utkaṭā</s>, and <s>hemavallarī</s>;
<s>Tridaṇḍī</s>, <s>brahmadaṇḍī</s>, <s>cakrāṅkī</s>, and <s>sthalapadminī</s>;
<s>Nāgajihvā</s>, <s>nāgakarṇī</s>, <s>vīrā</s>, and <s>vartulaparṇikā</s>;
<s>Arkapattrī</s>, <s>vaṃśapattrī</s>, <s>tāmraparṇī</s>, and likewise <s>īśvarī</s>;
<s>Indurī</s>, O goddess of gods: these are makers of mercury-binding, my dear.
By substances, fixed and moving, whose smell, taste, and touch are sharp,
mercury is calcined and also bound through steaming and rubbing.
<s>Sūryāvarta</s>, banana, <s>vandhyā</s>, and likewise <s>kośātakī</s>;
<s>Vajrakanda</s>, <s>udakakaṇā</s>, <s>kākamācī</s>, and <s>śigruka</s>;
and <s>devadālī</s>, O goddess of gods, are proclaimed to be liquefying agents.

children.text: doṣān haranti yogena dhātūnāṃ pāradasya ca ||
children.translated_text: Through their combination they remove the defects of metals and of mercury.
<s>Kākamācī</s>, <s>ghanarava</s>, <s>kāsamarda</s>, and <s>kṛtāñjali</s>;
<s>Varāhakarṇī</s>, <s>saṭirī</s>, <s>haṃsadāvī</s>, and <s>śatāvarī</s>;

children.text: tāmbūlī nāginī brahmī haṃsapādī ca lakṣaṇā
children.translated_text: <s>Tāmbūlī</s>, <s>nāginī</s>, <s>brahmī</s>, <s>haṃsapādī</s>, and <s>lakṣaṇā</s>;
<s>Arjunī</s>, <s>kṣīranālī</s>, <s>kāravella</s>, and <s>arkapattrikā</s>;
<s>Vyāghrī</s>, <s>cavī</s>, <s>kuravaka</s>: these are the creeping substances, O <s>Suravanditā</s>.
<s>Brahmadaṇḍa</s>, <s>sudaṇḍa</s>, and <s>lohadaṇḍa</s> as the third:
these three are fit for <s>rasāyana</s> and are <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: bhūpāṭalī ca kaumārī siṃhavallī ca śūkarī
children.translated_text: <s>Bhūpāṭalī</s>, <s>kaumārī</s>, <s>siṃhavallī</s>, and <s>śūkarī</s>;

children.text: hemaparṇī paṭolī ca nāgavallī ca bhṛṅgarāṭ
children.translated_text: <s>Hemaparṇī</s>, <s>paṭolī</s>, <s>nāgavallī</s>, and <s>bhṛṅgarāṭ</s>;

children.text: ityaṣṭa mūlikāḥ proktāḥ pañcaratnaṃ śṛṇu priye ||
children.translated_text: these are declared to be the eight roots; now hear of the five jewels, my dear.
<s>Mantrasiddhāsanā</s> and the goddess <s>kaṅkālakhecarī</s>,

children.text: indirā ca kṣamāpālī pañcamī tu niśācarī
children.translated_text: <s>Indirā</s>, <s>kṣamāpālī</s>, and as the fifth <s>niśācarī</s>:
this is the five-jewel group, O goddess, for the purification and digestion of mercury.
Each one is praised for the binding of mercury, O <s>Suravanditā</s>.
One should take the five jewels with the <s>rasāṅkuśa</s>, O woman of good vows.
In union with <s>Rasabhairava</s>, it gives the <s>khecarī</s> perfection.
The three alkalis are <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> alkali, barley alkali, and <s>sarjikā</s>.
Those born from sesame, <s>apāmārga</s>, banana, <s>palāśa</s>, <s>śigru</s>, and <s>mocikā</s>,
and from radish, ginger, and tamarind are proclaimed to be plant-alkalis.
Sour sorrel, citron, lime, sour <s>caṇaka</s>,
orange, tamarind, and <s>cāṅgerī</s> are the best group of acids.
Sea salt, rock salt, and likewise <s>cūlikā</s> salt,

children.text: sauvarcalaṃ ca kācaṃ ca lavaṇāḥ pañca kīrtitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: together with <s>sauvarcala</s> and <s>kāca</s>: these are called the five salts.

children.text: saktukaṃ kālakūṭaṃ ca sitamustā tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Saktuka</s>, <s>kālakūṭa</s>, and likewise white <s>mustā</s>,

children.text: śṛṅgī kṛṣṇaviṣaṃ caiva pañcaite tu mahāviṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śṛṅgī</s> and black poison: these five are the great poisons.
<s>Snuhī</s>, <s>arka</s>, <s>unmattaka</s>, <s>karavīra</s>, and <s>lāṅgalī</s>:

children.text: pañcaivopaviṣā mukhyāḥ tailāni hy uttamāni vai
children.translated_text: these five are the chief minor poisons; the best oils indeed
are those born from safflower, <s>kaṅguṇī</s>, <s>naktā</s>, sesame, and mustard.
The urines are those of elephant, horse, goat, and woman, with cow's urine as the fifth.
Bile is fivefold: that born from fish, cow, horse, human, and peacock.
Fat is fivefold: that of fish, ram, snake, human, and peacock.
The feces are of pigeon, blue jay, and vulture, and of peacock and cock.
<s>Mañjiṣṭhā</s>, saffron, lac, <s>khadira</s>, and likewise <s>āsana</s>
are the red group, O goddess of gods; now hear the yellow group.
Safflower, <s>kiṃśuka</s>, turmeric, <s>pataṅga</s>, and <s>madayantikā</s>;
the white group consists of lime, tortoise, conch, oyster shell, and cowrie shell.
<s>Guñjā</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, honey, ghee, and jaggery are the five liquefiers.
<s>Kāca</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, and <s>sauvīra</s> are the triad of purifiers, my dear.

children.text: sarve malaharāḥ kṣārāḥ sarve cāmlāḥ prabodhakāḥ
children.translated_text: All alkalis remove impurities, and all acids awaken it.
Poisons destroy dullness, and unctuous substances produce softness.
Thus the groups of herbs have been declared; they give accomplishment in union with mercury.
Through combination with them, the śaktis and the great minerals perform the operation.
Tell me that, O goddess of gods; what else do you wish to hear?
The blessed Goddess said:
O god of gods, O <s>Mahādeva</s>, what are the characteristics of the śaktis?
Please tell their preparation for being fit in mercurial work.
The blessed <s>Bhairava</s> said:
Once the goddess <s>Girijā</s>, seeing charming <s>Hara</s>,
released semen; what was then born from that is the auspicious mica.

children.text: pītaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ tathā śuklaṃ raktaṃ bhūmeśca saṃgamāt ||
children.translated_text: There are yellow, black, white, and red varieties, according to their conjunction with the earth.
Now hear about abhraka (mica), magnet-stone, diamond, and vaikrāntaka.

children.text: pinākaṃ darduraṃ nāgaṃ vajraṃ cābhraṃ caturvidham
children.translated_text: Pināka, dardura, nāga, and vajra: abhra (mica) is of four kinds.

children.text: pināke'gniṃ praviṣṭe tu śabdaś ciṭiciṭir bhavet ||
children.translated_text: When pināka enters the fire, it makes a crackling sound.
When dardura enters the fire, its sound is like that of a cock.

children.text: agniṃ praviṣṭaṃ nāgaṃ tu phūtkāraṃ devi muñcati ||
children.translated_text: But nāga, when it has entered the fire, O <s>Devi</s>, emits a hissing sound.

children.text: agniṃ praviṣṭaṃ vajraṃ tu vajravattiṣṭhati priye ||
children.translated_text: And vajra, when it has entered the fire, remains like a diamond, dear one.
Pināka mica causes skin disease; dardura causes death.

children.text: nāgaṃ dehagataṃ nityaṃ vyādhiṃ kuryād bhagaṃdaram ||
children.translated_text: Nāga, when constantly present in the body, would produce the disease called fistula.

children.text: rase rasāyane caiva yojyaṃ vajrābhrakaṃ priye
children.translated_text: Vajra-abhraka, dear one, is to be used in mercury and in rasāyana (rejuvenating alchemy).
Because of the difference of its many colors, that abhraka is fourfold.

children.text: raktaṃ pītaṃ ca hemārthe kṛṣṇaṃ hemaśarīrayoḥ
children.translated_text: Red and yellow are for the purpose of gold; black is for gold and for the body.

children.text: tārakarmaṇi śuklaṃ ca kācakiṭṭaṃ sadā tyajet ||
children.translated_text: White is for work with silver, but glassy slag should always be rejected.
First make the abhraka into single sheets, O leader of the gods.
With water of <s>Agastya</s> flowers and with the juice of kumuda lilies,
with kapitinduka, jambīra, meghanāda, and punarnavā,
with barley, tamarind, sour gruel, karavīra, and red lotus,
with wild sūraṇa, bhūdhātrī, the root of bhiṇḍī, and sour vetasa,
with meṣaśṛṅgī, hare fat, horn-oil, and juice of śamī,
with vajravallī, milky tubers, pepper, and sumukha,
one should steam it for three days, O <s>Devi</s>; it becomes free from defects.
Having first made dhānyābhraka, very smooth like fresh butter,
take thirty palas of mica-powder and two palas of small fish,
one pala of sesame powder, three palas of guñjā, and a quarter pala of borax.
That lump, bound with wheat and steeped in pañcagavya,
when blown in a koṣṭhikā apparatus with a fierce fire from two bellows,
yields the essence of abhraka, and indeed all essences fall out.
Stirred with the extracts of steaming herbs and repeatedly subjected to puṭa-firing,
it is killed by five nicula-puṭas and becomes deeply yellow.

children.text: piṇḍitaṃ vyoma niṣkledaṃ dattvā sattvaṃ nirañjanam
children.translated_text: Having made the dry mica into a lump and added the stainless essence,
with umā fruits and flowers soaked in sour ṣaṣṭika liquid,
through pounding with aumadaṇḍa, the gagana (mica) clearly liquefies.
Having placed the fire-digested material in a new pot with an earthen cover,
the gagana (mica) quickly liquefies, with a radiance like pearl-fruit.
Powder kañcukī a hundred times and soak it in kañcukī juice.
It will liquefy gagana (mica), O <s>Devi</s>, and all metals as well.
When it has stayed in sour grain-water, in nicula-alkali water,
that becomes liquid, resembling mercury without adhesion.
After grinding it with water of <s>Agastya</s> flowers in a sūraṇa tuber,
and keeping it for a month in a pit in the floor, it becomes like mercury.
Sprinkled with goat's urine and with dust of kapitinduka,
the abhraka, when quenched, O <s>Devi</s>, becomes like water.
The dust produced from abhraka, rubbed with powder of kākinī seeds

children.text: snuhikṣīreṇa saptāhaṃ siktaṃ dhmātaṃ drutaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: and sprinkled for seven days with snuhī latex, when blown, becomes molten.
The five parts of apāmārga and abhraka, very well ground,
should be placed in an earthen vessel; it becomes like water.
Powder of abhraka, rubbed together with kapālī and pepper,
and again quenched with śilā, mixed with <s>Agastya</s> juice,
pounded with the expressed juice of mārjārapādī and sour fruit and root,
placed in a citron fruit and deposited amid rice,
liquefies in only a fortnight when joined with rock-salt and śilā.
Mica made into single sheets should be put for seven days into muni-juice,
mixed with dārvī and pepper and drenched with maurvī juice.
The megha (mica), joined with sauvarcala salt and drenched with vajravallī juice,
when blown in a closed pair of dishes, becomes like water.
The dust produced from abhraka, equal to powder of vegā fruit,
steeped in kuliśa latex and blown, liquefies at once.
Having ground vyoma (mica) with vajravallī juices and mixed it with sauvarcala salt,
and cooked it in a covered pair of dishes, it liquefies like water.
With cow-flesh, rock-salt, and arka, and again with muni-water,
placed inside a plantain tuber, it liquefies in cow-dung fire in three days.
Taking a sheet of black abhra, one should smear it with pīlu oil.
Heated for seven days in the sun and put into sour liquid for three days,
vajra, arka, citraka-alkali, tumbī-alkali, and likewise arjuna,
sarja-alkali, barley-alkali, and borax should be the eighth.
And also juice of kṣīrakanda and likewise juice of vajrakanda,
combined with the three bṛhatīs: one should smear it with this group of alkalis.
That sheet-mica, smeared with this paste, is to be placed in a bronze vessel.
By blowing, and from the heat of the sun, it becomes molten in three days.
Or else the mica sheet, placed in the milk of kañcukī,

children.text: bhāvayecca tathā tena yāvaccūrṇaṃ tato bhavet ||
children.translated_text: should be steeped with that until it has become powder.
One should take the mica sheets and, after placing them in sour liquid for three days,
smear them with that paste and set them in a bronze vessel.
By the heat of the sun for seven days, druti (liquefaction) arises immediately.
With powder of kākāṇḍī fruit and likewise with the five liquefying agents,

children.text: abhrakasya yutaṃ cūrṇaṃ dhmātaṃ mūṣāgataṃ dravet ||
children.translated_text: powder mixed with abhraka, when blown in a crucible, liquefies.

children.text: bhrāmakaṃ cumbakaṃ caiva karṣakaṃ drāvakaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Bhrāmaka, cumbaka, karṣaka, and drāvaka likewise

children.text: evaṃ caturvidhaṃ kāntaṃ romakāntaṃ ca pañcamam ||
children.translated_text: Thus <s>kānta</s> is fourfold, and <s>romakānta</s> is the fifth.
It is respectively one-faced, two-faced, three-faced, four-faced, five-faced, and all-faced.

children.text: pītaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ tathā raktaṃ trivarṇaṃ syāt pṛthak pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: It may be yellow, black, red, and three-colored, each separately.
There, in order, the deities are <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: sparśavedhi bhavet pītaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ rasāyane
children.translated_text: The yellow one should be a piercer by touch; the black one is best in <s>rasāyana</s> (alchemy/rejuvenation).
The red-colored one, O greatly fortunate one, is praised for binding mercury.

children.text: bhrāmakaṃ tu kaniṣṭhaṃ syāt cumbakaṃ madhyamaṃ priye
children.translated_text: The <s>bhrāmaka</s> is inferior, the <s>cumbaka</s> is middling, dear one.
The <s>karṣaka</s>, O goddess, is superior, and the <s>drāvaka</s> is best of all.
That which makes kinds of metal revolve is the <s>bhrāmaka kānta</s>, dear one.
The <s>cumbaka kānta</s> attracts; the <s>karṣaka</s> draws, dear one.
That <s>kānta</s> which directly melts metal is the <s>drāvaka</s>.
That is <s>romakānta</s> from which, when split open, a hair-like sprouting appears.
The one-faced is inferior; the two- or three-faced is middling.
The four- or five-faced is excellent; the all-faced is superior.
The <s>bhrāmaka</s> and the <s>cumbaka</s> are praised for the destruction of disease.

children.text: rase rasāyane caiva karṣakaṃ drāvakaṃ hitam ||
children.translated_text: For mercury and for <s>rasāyana</s>, the <s>karṣaka</s> and <s>drāvaka</s> are beneficial.
Mercury is a rut-maddened elephant; <s>kānta</s> is called its goad.
Having dug up the ground, it should be obtained with great effort.
One should avoid what has been scattered by wind and sun, O lovely goddess.
A piece of lodestone lying outside should be treated with goat's blood.
It should be wrapped in a cloth smeared with goat's blood.
Wrapping it in goat-skin, one should place it in the ground as before.
After seven months it should be dug up and put into a water jar.
It should always be worshiped with red flowers, red garlands, and unguents.
Having also been worshiped with wine and meat, it should be applied in mercury and <s>rasāyana</s>.
When prepared with goat's blood, the <s>bhrāmaka</s> becomes a <s>cumbaka</s>.
By this methodical procedure, dear one, it becomes a <s>drāvaka</s>.
I shall explain the preparation of mercury-metal, which gives very great ease.
And when it enters the living body, it grants bodily comfort and strength.

children.text: kāntalohaṃ vinā sūto dehe na krāmati kvacit
children.translated_text: Without <s>kānta</s> metal, mercury never enters the body at all.
It should pierce and spread quickly, like a drop of oil in water.

children.text: na sūtena vinā kānto na kāntaḥ sūtavarjitaḥ
children.translated_text: There is no <s>kānta</s> without mercury, nor <s>kānta</s> apart from mercury.
The operation in which <s>kānta</s> and mercury are joined sustains the body.
One should take barley-alkali and place it in a greased vessel.
With powdered pepper and mica, one should make it into a compact lump.
When heated by blowing, <s>kānta</s> metal will melt; there is no need for deliberation about this.
Having pounded thirty measures of <s>cumbaka kānta</s> with water of <s>triphala</s>,

children.text: tenaiva kṣālanaṃ kāryaṃ pañcaniṣkaṃ tu ṭaṅkaṇam ||
children.translated_text: washing should be done with that same liquid; five <s>niṣkas</s> of borax should be used.
Placing it in an old cloth, mixed with honey and ghee, one should subject it to a closed heating.
After keeping it for a full month, purification takes place there, dear one.
The root of <s>sināḍikā</s>, in the amount of ten <s>niṣkas</s>, should be added.
It should be thoroughly rubbed in a mortar with a decoction of the three fruits.
It should be placed equally in three crucibles measuring eight fingers each.
For coating the crucible, that root should be used in the measure of one <s>niṣka</s>.
Then a five-faced crucible of <s>Śiva</s> should be made, equal for each crucible.
After fastening it well in the hand of the apparatus, with the ingot on a stone slab,
having mixed it with oil, one then obtains <s>kānta-nāga</s>.
By the procedure used for mica, one should accomplish the dropping of the molten essence.
When the ocean of milk was being churned by the gods and anti-gods with Mount <s>Mandara</s>,
the gods drank that nectar and attained immortality.
As they drank, O goddess, drops fell upon the surface of the earth.
When dried, they became diamonds of various colors and great power.
Some drops became grains, and also spotless ones.
They became <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>kṣatriya</s>, <s>vaiśya</s>, and <s>śūdra</s>, thus in many forms.
They are fourfold: white, red, yellow, and black.
They are male, female, and neuter, respectively.
Those that are round, filled out like plates, brilliant, and large
should be understood as male, lacking lines and spots.
Those furnished with lines and spots, and broken, are female.
Those triangular, thin, and long should be known as neuter.
Possessing essence and endowed with power, apt to penetrate metal,
male diamonds quickly bring about the binding of mercury, O praised by the gods.
Female diamonds generate bodily luster but have little power.
