children.text: napuṃsakāḥ sattvahīnāḥ kaṣṭaṃ lohe kramanti ca ||
children.translated_text: Neuter diamonds lack essence and penetrate metal only with difficulty.
<s>Kṣatriya</s> diamonds should be avoided in all operations and in mercury work.
They are described as superior, middling, and inferior.
Some are coarse, very coarse, and middling; others are fine and very fine, dear one.
By the distinctions of bursting, burning, and splitting, they are flawless and free of defects.
Those that are potent, spotless, and very strong are the eldest or best.
In <s>rasāyana</s>, the <s>vipra</s> type grants powers such as minuteness.
The <s>kṣatriya</s> type serves to destroy death and removes wrinkles, greying hair, and disease.

children.text: dravyakārī tathā vaiśyaḥ śarīraṃ dṛḍhatāṃ nayet
children.translated_text: The <s>vaiśya</s> type produces wealth and brings firmness to the body.
The <s>śūdra</s> type pacifies disease and produces arrest of age.

children.text: klībe klībāḥ striyaḥ strīṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ puruṣā hitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Neuter ones are beneficial for neuters, female ones for women, and male ones for all.

children.text: yathā jātistathotsāhaṃ yathā sattvaṃ tathā guṇān
children.translated_text: As is the birth, so is the exertion; as is the essence, so are the qualities.

children.text: yathā rucistathā śīlaṃ yathā śīlaṃ tathā varam
children.translated_text: As is the inclination, so is the character; as is the character, so is the excellence.

children.text: yathā varastathā varṇaṃ kurvanti kuliśāḥ priye ||
children.translated_text: O beloved, diamonds produce color according to the excellence of the material.
<s>śyāmā</s>, <s>śamī</s>, <s>ghanarava</s>, <s>varṣābhū</s>, and intoxicated <s>kodrava</s>,
<s>ākhukarṇī</s>, <s>munitaru</s>, horse gram, and sour <s>vetasa</s>,
<s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, and also the juice of these, especially of the <s>sūraṇa</s> tuber,
should purify diamond for three days; it becomes purified, O queen of the gods.
Ram's horn, serpent bone, tortoise shell, and <s>śilājatu</s>,
the sap of the <s>snuhī</s> stalk, breast milk, and magnet-stone too,

children.text: vajrakaṃ cāpi vaikrāntaṃ tanmadhye prakṣipet priye
children.translated_text: and also diamond and <s>vaikrānta</s> should be placed in the middle of that, O beloved.
After applying a <s>puṭa</s> (sealed heating) over an intense fire, until the heating is complete,
one should grind horse gram and <s>kodrava</s> with horse urine,
and quench the heated diamond on the slab until it has become ash.
This is the <s>kāpālika</s> procedure, the excellent killing of diamond.
<s>mākṣika</s>, ram's horn, <s>śilā</s>, sulfur, and borax,
<s>vaikrānta</s> and <s>tālaka</s> as well, soaked in the milk of <s>vajrī</s>,

children.text: lepaṃ mūṣodare dattvā samāvarttaṃ tu kārayet
children.translated_text: should be applied as a coating inside the crucible, and one should perform the <s>samāvarta</s> heating.
Diamonds die there, and they combine properly in union.

children.text: gandhakaṃ ca śilādhātuṃ bhrāmakasya mukhaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Sulfur, <s>śilādhātu</s>, and the mouth of <s>bhrāmaka</s>,
and the teeth of a hare should be ground with sour <s>vetasa</s>.
With this perfected paste one should make the coating of the crucible.

children.text: andhamūṣāgataṃ dhmātaṃ vajraṃ tu mriyate kṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: Diamond placed in a closed crucible and blown with heat dies in an instant.

children.text: tenaiva militaṃ vajraṃ tārahemni na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By that very means diamond, once fused, combines with silver and gold; there is no doubt.
<s>tālaka</s>, sulfur, magnetite, <s>tāpya</s>, camphor, and borax,
tamarind seed and ram's horn, ground with menstrual blood,

children.text: mūṣālepagataṃ dhmātaṃ vajraṃ tu mriyate kṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: when heated in the coating of a crucible, cause diamond to die in an instant.
The five parts of <s>śarapuṅkha</s> should then be ground with menstrual blood,
or <s>peṭārī</s> seed may be well ground with rice-water.
Or cotton root of three <s>karṣas</s> should be ground with rice-water,
or the root of red <s>rākā</s>, ground with a woman's breast milk.
Or one should grind <s>vajrakanda</s> with the milk of <s>vajrī</s>, O virtuous one.

children.text: tatkalkapuṭitaṃ dhmātaṃ vajraṃ caiva mṛtaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Heated after being enclosed in that paste, the diamond becomes dead.
It may be soaked for one day in a white shell from a great river,
with the milk of <s>uttaravāruṇī</s> and with this paste, O virtuous one.

children.text: tālena meṣaśṛṅgyā ca vajravallyā ca veṣṭitam
children.translated_text: Wrapped with <s>tāla</s>, <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, and <s>vajravallī</s>,

children.text: andhamūṣāgataṃ dhmātaṃ vajraṃ tu mriyate kṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: and heated by blowing in a closed crucible, diamond dies in an instant.
One should place the diamond, O goddess, in the paste of magnetite,
and grind it with fragrant oil; the diamond dies, O sovereign lady.
In horse-gram water, combined with green vitriol, <s>saurāṣṭrī</s>, and <s>tālaka</s>,
and joined with <s>apāmārga</s> alkali, diamond when quenched becomes dead.
Wrapped with <s>amṛtā</s> tuber, <s>timira</s> seed, bark, and latex,
and placed in a ram's horn and coated with clay, diamond dies by <s>puṭas</s>.

children.text: peṭārī haṃsapādī ca vajravallī ca sūraṇam
children.translated_text: <s>peṭārī</s>, <s>haṃsapādī</s>, <s>vajravallī</s>, and <s>sūraṇa</s>,
and shoots of the aśvattha tree, O goddess, all ground with a woman's breast milk,
with this perfected paste wrapped inside a fruit of <s>bṛhatī</s>,

children.text: kṣiptaṃ bahirmṛdā liptaṃ mriyate saptabhiḥ puṭaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: placed there and coated outside with clay, it dies with seven <s>puṭas</s>.
Wrapped with water of white <s>indurekhā</s> flowers, sulfur, the triad, and <s>mākṣika</s>,

children.text: veṣṭitaṃ kuliśaṃ devi puṭapākāt mṛtaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: the <s>kuliśa</s> (diamond), O goddess, becomes dead through <s>puṭa</s>-cooking.
Aśvattha, jujube, okra, <s>mākṣika</s>, and crab bone,
ground with the milk of <s>snuhī</s>: by a <s>puṭa</s>, the brāhmaṇa type is killed.
With the milk of oleander and arka, ram's horn together with cinnabar,
and mixed with udumbara: by a <s>puṭa</s>, this is the killing of the kṣatriya type.

children.text: bālā cātibalā caiva gandhakaṃ karkaṭāsthi ca
children.translated_text: <s>bālā</s> and <s>atibalā</s>, sulfur, and crab bone,
with the milk of <s>uttaravāruṇī</s>: by heating, this is the killing of the vaiśya type.
With <s>kaṇḍūla</s> and <s>sūraṇa</s>, with <s>śilā</s> and garlic,
and with the latex of banyan and conch preparation, the śūdra type too dies at once.
Large ones and the like, such as slabs, are destroyed by many large <s>puṭas</s>.
They become as if well boiled, and softness arises.
Having ground the five parts of <s>āmalaka</s> and the pale <s>indravāruṇī</s>,

children.text: anena veṣṭitaṃ vajraṃ mriyate saptabhiḥ puṭaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: diamond wrapped with this dies with seven <s>puṭas</s>.
One should place diamond in the middle of a living <s>mātṛvāhaka</s>,
and, in swing-steaming for three days, O goddess, it becomes like <s>guṇapattra</s>.
One should place diamond, O goddess, in the middle of a castor tree.
After one month has passed, O goddess, it becomes like <s>guṇapattra</s>.
One should place diamond, O goddess, in the paste of magnetite.
Cotton leaf, neem leaf, and jujube leaf should be added,
and all that should be ground together, wrapped in a ball of magnetite,
covered outside with a betel leaf, and kept between the knees.
In two <s>yāmas</s>, that diamond certainly becomes soft.

children.text: tatkṣaṇānmriyate vajraṃ tāre hemni na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Immediately the diamond dies in silver or gold; there is no doubt.
Placed in the middle of a citron fruit and put into a cloth pouch,
one should boil it in a decoction of <s>kodrava</s>, by this sequence, for three days.

children.text: tadvajraṃ jāyate khoṭaṃ hemnā milati tatkṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: That diamond becomes <s>khoṭa</s> and immediately combines with gold.
Smeared with <s>nāgavallī</s> and wrapped in that very leaf,

children.text: jānumadhye sthitaṃ yāmaṃ mṛdu saṃjāyate dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: kept between the knees for a <s>yāma</s>, it surely becomes soft.
At the root of <s>vajralatā</s>, one should place the softened diamond.
One should carefully give a <s>puṭa</s>; it becomes ash at once.

children.text: sukhād bandhakaraṃ hy āśu sattvaṃ muñcati tatkṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: It quickly becomes easy to bind, and the <s>sattva</s> (essence) is released at once.
These procedures pacify every death and bring about all attainments.
Having placed the perforated diamond within a chain of bones,

children.text: jalabhāṇḍe tu tat svinnaṃ saptāhaṃ dravatāṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: and cooked it in a water-vessel for seven days, it becomes liquid.
The three alkalis, <s>rāmaṭha</s>, chickpea, sour <s>vetasa</s>,
having added the milk of <s>jvālāmukhī</s> and the juice of <s>sthalakumbhī</s>,
with these the diamond is ground, and likewise with the milks of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>;
one should cook it in a swing-apparatus, O <s>Devi</s>; it becomes like <s>rasa</s>.
Or else mica, when cooked, and pearl and coral,

children.text: mākṣikaṃ nīlapuṣpaṃ ca pītaṃ marakataṃ mahat
children.translated_text: <s>mākṣika</s>, <s>nīlapuṣpa</s>, the yellow mineral, and the great emerald,
cat's-eye, crystal, and the like melt just like water.

children.text: lohajātaṃ tathā dhmātam agnivarṇaṃ tu dṛśyate
children.translated_text: So too every kind of metal, when blown upon, is seen to be fire-colored;

children.text: vāpitaṃ sakṛd ekena mṛtaṃ jalasamaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: quenched once with this one substance, it becomes dead and like water.
A pearl, steeped for seven days in the sour juice of <s>vetasa</s>,
should be placed inside the belly of a citron and buried in a heap of grain;
by baking in a covered heating it becomes powder, like water.
Listen, O highly fortunate <s>Devi</s>, to the great <s>rasa</s> called <s>vaikrānta</s>.
The lord of demons, <s>Mahiṣa</s>, a perfected being born from the body of <s>Hara</s>,

children.text: durgā bhagavatī devī taṃ śūlena vyamardayat ||
children.translated_text: was crushed with a spear by the blessed goddess <s>Durgā</s>.

children.text: tasya raktaṃ tu patitaṃ yatra yatra sthitaṃ bhuvi
children.translated_text: Wherever his blood fell and remained upon the earth,

children.text: tatra tatra tu vaikrānto vajrākāro mahārasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there in each place arose <s>vaikrānta</s>, a great <s>rasa</s> shaped like diamond.

children.text: vindhyasya dakṣiṇe cāsti uttare nāsti sarvathā
children.translated_text: It exists south of the <s>Vindhya</s>; north of it, it does not exist at all.
Because it cuts metals, it is remembered as <s>vaikrāntaka</s>.
It is white, yellow, red, blue, dove-colored,
one variety resembling a peacock's tail, and another having the luster of emerald.

children.text: dehasiddhikaraḥ kṛṣṇaḥ pīte pītaḥ site sitaḥ
children.translated_text: The black one brings perfection of the body; the yellow is for yellow, the white for white;
the red grants every desired success, and so does the emerald-colored one.

children.text: śeṣe dve niṣphale varjye vaikrāntamiti saptadhā ||
children.translated_text: The remaining two are fruitless and should be rejected: thus <s>vaikrānta</s> is sevenfold.

children.text: yatra kṣetre sthitaṃ devi vaikrāntaṃ tatra bhairavam
children.translated_text: In whatever field <s>vaikrānta</s> is found, O <s>Devi</s>, there
the foremost practitioner should worship <s>Bhairava</s> and <s>Vināyaka</s>, and then take it.
<s>Vaikrānta</s>, finely powdered and honored by gods and demons,
should be placed inside a tiger-plant tuber and heated by blowing in a covered firing.
With horse urine, over a gentle fire, one should cook it for seven days;
then one should dry it in the shade: this is the excellent <s>vaikrānta</s>.
Or with salt, alkali, urine, sour liquid, and black oils,
one should cook it for seven days in decoctions of horse gram and <s>kodrava</s>.

children.text: vandhyācūrṇaṃ tu vaikrāntaṃ samāṃśena tu cūrṇayet
children.translated_text: One should powder the infertile powder and <s>vaikrānta</s> in equal parts;
after impregnating it with goat's urine, one should dry it in the shade.

children.text: andhanāle dhamitvā tu mūṣāsattvaṃ tu jāyate ||
children.translated_text: When it has been blown in a blind tube, crucible-essence is produced.
Impregnated with <s>mokṣa</s>, <s>moraṭa</s>, <s>palāśa</s> alkali, and cow urine,
combined with paste of diamond-tuber root, lac, and borax,
the powder arising from <s>vaikrānta</s>, mixed with the liquid of <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>,
formed into a lump in a sealed crucible and heated, releases its essence.
One should grind <s>vaikrānta</s> and diamond-tuber with diamond-water;

children.text: māhiṣe navanīte ca sakṣaudraṃ piṇḍitaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: then, in buffalo butter and together with honey, it should be made into a lump.
After purifying it, one should heat it; the essence falls like an <s>indragopa</s> insect.
The fresh juice of <s>ketakī</s>, <s>kāṅkṣī</s>, <s>maṇimattha</s>, and <s>khecara</s>:
through cooking with these, O <s>Devi</s>, <s>vaikrānta</s> becomes like <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ tāmraṃ kāntalohasya vā rajaḥ
children.translated_text: Gold, silver, copper, or the dust of magnetic iron
melt like water by this procedure of cooking.
Thus have been stated the characteristics and related procedures of the four beginning with mica.
Tell me, O mistress of the gods, what else do you wish to hear?

children.text: iti śrīpārvatīparameśvarasaṃvāde rasārṇave rasasaṃhitāyām abhrakādilakṣaṇasaṃskāranirṇayo nāma ṣaṣṭhaḥ paṭalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Rasārṇava</s>, in the <s>Rasasaṃhitā</s>, in the dialogue of glorious <s>Pārvatī</s> and <s>Parameśvara</s>, the sixth chapter, named 'Determination of the Characteristics and Processing of Mica and the Others,' is complete.
The glorious goddess said:
Together with their characteristics and processing, command me concerning the great <s>rasas</s>,
and anything else of that kind, O god, that is useful for the science of <s>rasa</s>.
Glorious <s>Bhairava</s> said:
<s>Mākṣika</s>, <s>vimala</s>, <s>śaila</s>, <s>capala</s>, and <s>rasaka</s>,
<s>sasyaka</s>, <s>darada</s>, and <s>srotoñjana</s> are the eight.
Thus there are eight great <s>rasas</s>; hear these first.
When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, after hearing the <s>Bhārata</s>, had entered yogic sleep,
the sole of his foot was pierced by a hunter, who mistook him for a deer.
The drops of blood from the wound that fell there upon the earth
became stones of <s>mākṣika</s>, shaped like neem fruits.
There <s>mākṣika</s> is twofold, divided into yellow and white;
<s>vimala</s>, O <s>Devi</s>, is threefold: white, yellow, and red.
In oil, sour gruel, and buttermilk, in cow urine and banana juice,
with decoctions of horse gram and <s>kodrava</s>, <s>mākṣika</s> and likewise <s>vimala</s>
should repeatedly be cooked while placed in an elephant-foot yam tuber, O fair one.
Combined with alkali, sour liquid, salt, castor oil, and ghee,
three covered heatings should be given; those two then become purified.
Powdered <s>mākṣika</s>, impregnated with breast milk and the milks of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>,
releases its essence when well heated and treated with borax and <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
Soaked in banana tuber, basil, and sour orange juice,
provided with seven times seven covered heatings and combined with the five solvents,
<s>mākṣika</s>, treated with breast milk and heated, releases its essence.
With honey and <s>gandharva</s> oil, with cow urine and with ghee,
<s>mākṣika</s>, repeatedly impregnated with the essence of banana tuber,

children.text: mūṣāyāṃ muñcati dhmātaṃ sattvaṃ śulvanibhaṃ mṛdu ||
children.translated_text: When heated by blowing in a crucible, it releases a soft essence resembling copper.
Having added the juice of <s>devadālī</s>, mixed with one-quarter part of borax,

children.text: prakaṭāṃ mūṣikāṃ kṛtvā dhamet sattvam apekṣitam ||
children.translated_text: one should make an open small crucible and blow it; the desired essence is obtained.
What wonder is there in this? When well cooked with plantain juice inside a casing of elephant-foot yam tuber,

children.text: vātāritailena puṭena tāpyaṃ puṭena dagdhaṃ varaśuddhim eti ||
children.translated_text: and heated with a closed heating using <s>vātāri</s> oil, when burnt by that heating it attains excellent purity.
It should be impregnated with cow urine, with the latex of <s>snuhī</s>, and with castor oil.

children.text: mākṣikaṃ dinam ekaṃ tu marditaṃ vaṭakīkṛtam
children.translated_text: <s>Mākṣika</s>, rubbed for one day and made into pellets,
should be blown like mica; this is also the method for the essence of <s>sasyaka</s>.
<s>Tāpya</s>, <s>āvartaka</s>, <s>dhātumākṣika</s>, and <s>madhudhātuka</s>
are names of <s>mākṣika</s>. It is bitter and sweet, and removes urinary disease, piles, consumption, and skin disease.
It removes phlegm and bile, gives strength, acts as a carrier for compounds, and is a <s>rasāyana</s>.
Fevers, complex fevers, and even poverty vanish merely at the utterance of its name
within a hundred yojanas; what, then, is a better agent for piercing metals than it?
<s>Vimala</s>, with water of <s>śigru</s>, with alum, green vitriol, and borax,
joined with <s>vajrakanda</s> and impregnated with plantain juices,
combined with the alkali of <s>mokṣaka</s> and blown in a sealed crucible,
gives an essence shining like the moon and sun; there is no doubt.
O <s>Īśvarī</s>, <s>śaila</s> is of two kinds, fallen and not fallen.
It is proclaimed in another treatise too, and has been praised by many gods.
In the hot season, when scorched by heat, the mountains that bear the essence of metals
give forth an exudation; that is called <s>śilājatu</s>.
It is called <s>śilāvad dhātuka</s>, <s>śailaja</s>, <s>girisānuja</s>,
<s>jatvadrija</s>; mountain and <s>śaila</s> are terms that have been stated and recounted by you.
<s>Śilājatu</s> is purified when heated with alkalis, acids, and cow's liquid,
or also with cow's ghee, and with the juices of <s>triphala</s> and fresh ginger.
Having placed it in an iron vessel, one should carefully purify it.
Having powdered <s>śaila</s>, with grain-sour gruel, minor poisons, and poisons,

children.text: piṇḍaṃ baddhvā tu vidhivat pātayeccapalaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: one should bind it into a lump according to rule and make <s>capala</s> fall, as prescribed.
<s>Capala</s> may be pale, white, red, or black; it is praised.
When it has the appearance of gold or the appearance of silver, it is especially a binder of mercury.

children.text: śeṣau madhyau ca lākṣāvat śīghradrāvau tu niṣphalau
children.translated_text: The remaining two are middling; like lac, they melt quickly but are fruitless.
Because <s>capala</s> melts in fire like tin, it is so called.
If, after binding <s>capala</s> in cloth, one were to make it cross the ocean,

children.text: vastraṃ ca veṣṭayet sadyaḥ tenāsau capalaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the cloth at once wrapped itself around it, then that is remembered as <s>capala</s>.
One should extract <s>capala</s> by closed heating on the summit of a mountain.
It certainly produces fixation of the body, and especially binding of mercury.
<s>Capala</s>, active like solid mica, effects the penetration called <s>capalāvedha</s>.
<s>Capala</s> is regarded as scraping, unctuous, and productive of body and metal.
<s>Rasaka</s> is threefold, according to its distinction as clay, jaggery, or stone.
The yellow one, with the form of clay, is the best, the clay-like <s>rasaka</s>.
The one resembling jaggery is to be known as middling; the one resembling stone is inferior.
One should stir <s>rasaka</s> with the exudation of bitter bottle-gourd and cook it.
Purified and freed from defects, it becomes yellow in color.

children.text: kimatra citraṃ rasakaṃ rasena rajasvalāyāḥ kusumena bhāvitam
children.translated_text: What wonder is there in this? <s>Rasaka</s>, impregnated with the menstrual flower of a menstruating woman,

children.text: krameṇa kṛtvā uragena rañjitaṃ karoti śulbaṃ tripuṭena kāñcanam ||
children.translated_text: then colored in sequence with <s>uraga</s>, turns copper into gold by three closed heatings.
Placed in fire, it does not waste away; in the form of essence it is very powerful.

children.text: rasakaṃ cūrṇayitvā tu baddhvā vastre vicakṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Having powdered <s>rasaka</s>, a skilled man should bind it in cloth
and place it in women's urine for seven nights, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>.
He should impregnate it with the juices and leaves of red and yellow flowers.

children.text: kṣāraiḥ snehaistathā cāmlaiḥ bhāvitaṃ rasakaṃ muhuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rasaka</s>, repeatedly impregnated with alkalis, oils, and acids,
and combined with wool, lac, turmeric, <s>pathyā</s>, <s>bhūlatā</s>, and soot,
when placed in a sealed crucible, blown, and combined with borax,
certainly releases an essence resembling <s>kuṭila</s>; there is no doubt.
<s>Gobhadda</s>, <s>rasaka</s>, <s>tuttha</s>, earth-scoria, and mercury-born,
<s>kharpara</s>, enemy of eye diseases, maker of brass, and colorer of copper are its names.
<s>Rasaka</s> is coloring, dry, productive of wind, and destructive of phlegm.
But its essence destroys all three humors and removes defects of the eyes.
Having drunk the <s>kālakūṭa</s> poison, <s>Garuḍa</s> was unable to endure it.
Likewise he vomited forth nectar, after consuming the poison and nectar of venomous serpents.

children.text: svayaṃ vinirgate cañcvoḥ sasyako'bhūt sa kālikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When it came out from his beak by itself, that black <s>sasyaka</s> arose.
First, one should impregnate the powder of that <s>sasyaka</s> in women's urine,
or else place it for one day amid hare's blood.
Its powder, O <s>Maheśānī</s>, mixed with a quarter part of <s>saubhāgya</s>,
should be placed for one day in the midst of <s>karañja</s> oil.
Set in the middle of a blind crucible, it should be blown with three <s>kokila</s> heatings.
A fine essence falls, resembling the <s>indragopaka</s> insect.

children.text: ekadhā sasyakas tasmāt dhmāto nipatito bhavet
children.translated_text: From that, when <s>sasyaka</s> is blown once, it becomes fallen down,
red, free from blackness, and having the appearance of a peacock's neck.
<s>Sasya</s> is peacock-<s>tuttha</s>; it is fire-made and a destroyer of blackness.

children.text: rasāyane tu yogyaḥ syād vayaḥstambhakaro bhavet ||
children.translated_text: It is fit for <s>rasāyana</s> and brings about the arrest of age.
<s>Sasyaka</s> obtains purity when impregnated with the red group of substances.
<s>Darada</s> is said to be threefold: <s>carmāra</s>, <s>śukatuṇḍaka</s>,
and the third is <s>haṃsapāda</s>; each succeeding one is more excellent in qualities.
Again, <s>darada</s> is twofold by the distinction of powdered and mercurial forms.
In cow's flesh, in buffalo urine, and in curd, sour gruel, and sesame oil...
Having cooked each one for three days, one should impregnate it with peacock bile.
One should make <s>darada</s> (cinnabar ore) fall in a distillation apparatus into a water receptacle.

children.text: sattvaṃ tu sūtasaṃkāśaṃ jāyate nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then an essence resembling <s>sūta</s> (mercury) is produced; there is no doubt about this.
<s>Laghukandarasa</s>, <s>mleccha</s>, <s>hiṅgula</s>, and powdered mercury,
and that born from jewel-red color: these are the names of this <s>carmāragandhika</s>.
<s>Hiṅgula</s> is bitter, hot, divine, and born from <s>rasa</s> and <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur).
It removes disorders of metals and skin diseases, and kindles divine strength, intelligence, and digestive fire.

children.text: kimatra citraṃ daradaḥ subhāvitaḥ kṣīreṇa meṣyā bahuśo 'mlavargaiḥ
children.translated_text: What is surprising here? <s>Darada</s>, well impregnated many times with ewe's milk and groups of sour substances,
makes white gold, heated with much warmth, appear directly like excellent saffron.
Born from channels, it has the form of an anthill peak, and when broken it has the splendor of a blue lotus.
When rubbed, it has the hue of red ocher, O one honored by the gods.
When that is impregnated many times in cow dung, cow urine, ghee, honey, and fat,
it quickly binds <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury).
Thus the <s>mahārasas</s> have been taught. Listen now, beloved, to the <s>uparasas</s>.
<s>Gandhaka</s>, <s>tālaka</s>, <s>śilā</s>, <s>saurāṣṭrī</s>, bird-<s>gairika</s>,
<s>rājāvarta</s>, and <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s> are remembered as the eight <s>uparasas</s>.
Long ago, O <s>Devi</s>, on <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>, adorned with every jewel,
beautiful and filled with every desire, on the shore of the ocean of milk,
with foremost <s>Vidyādharī</s> women and other women,
with radiant perfected women and likewise with hosts of <s>Apsarases</s>,
and with other divine women at play, beloved,
with varied songs and dances and many kinds of instruments,
as you were thus sporting, your menstrual fluid flowed forth.
That menstrual fluid, O fair-hipped one, was extremely fragrant and very lovely.
Because of the great abundance of the menstrual fluid, your garment became red.

children.text: tatra tyaktvā tu tadvāsaḥ susnātā kṣīrasāgare ||
children.translated_text: Leaving that garment there, you bathed well in the ocean of milk.
Surrounded by divine women and by the gods also, you went to the city.
Your menstrual garment was carried by the waves into the midst of the ocean.

children.text: evaṃ te śoṇitaṃ bhadre praviṣṭaṃ kṣīrasāgare
children.translated_text: In this way your blood, O blessed one, entered the ocean of milk.
At the churning of the milk-ocean, this arose together with the nectar,
delighting all the gods and demons with its own fragrance.
Then it was said by the hosts of gods: 'Let this be called <s>gandhaka</s>.'
'Let this serve for binding <s>rasa</s> (mercury) and for digesting it.

children.text: ye guṇāḥ pārade proktāste caivātra bhavantviti ||
children.translated_text: Whatever qualities are declared in mercury, let those also be present here.'

children.text: iti devagaṇaiḥ prītaiḥ purā proktaṃ sureśvari
children.translated_text: So, O queen of the gods, it was formerly proclaimed by the delighted hosts of gods.
Therefore this is famous on the earth's surface by the name <s>gandhaka</s>.

children.text: sa cāpi trividho devi śukacañcunibho varaḥ
children.translated_text: And that too, O <s>Devi</s>, is threefold: the best resembles a parrot's beak.
The middling kind is yellow in color; the inferior, beloved, is white in color.
After melting it with <s>karañja</s> and castor oil in goat's milk,
one should pour it into the exudation of <s>unmattā</s> three times, separately each time.
One should impregnate it with powder of <s>jvālinī</s> seeds and with fish bile.
Or, when it has been impregnated for seven days with water of <s>bhṛṅga</s>, it is washed with water.
Heated with jujube embers in an iron vessel smeared with ghee,
and turned over a gentle fire upon cloth smeared with ghee,

children.text: kṣipraṃ bhṛṅgasya niryāse kṣālito gandhako hitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then quickly washed in the exudation of <s>bhṛṅga</s>, the <s>gandhaka</s> is beneficial.
<s>Gandhaka</s>, by its own nature, is in essence of the form of <s>rasa</s>.
One should purify <s>gandhaka</s> in milk and also in ginger juice,

children.text: rase ca bhṛṅgarājasya nimbukasya rase tathā
children.translated_text: in the juice of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> and likewise in the juice of citron.
Purified seven times, <s>gandhaka</s> becomes stainless.

children.text: tālakaḥ paṭalaḥ piṇḍo dvidhā tatrādya uttamaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tālaka</s> is of two kinds, leaf-like and lump-like; of these the first is superior.

children.text: kuṣmāṇḍe tu śataṃ vārān tālakaṃ svedayedbudhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The wise man should steam <s>tālaka</s> one hundred times in ash gourd.
Separately, seven times, in the latex of <s>snuk</s> and the juice of bitter bottle-gourd,
with sesame, mustard, <s>śigru</s>, lac, salt, jaggery,

children.text: ṭaṅkaṇaṃ ca yutairhyetaiḥ tālakaṃ bhūdhare dravet ||
children.translated_text: and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> joined with these, <s>tālaka</s> melts in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus.
The wise man should grind it for seven days with liquids produced from <s>punarnavā</s>,
together with alkali from the fruit of <s>vyādhighāta</s> and sweet ash gourd.
Having added a quarter part of everything, then in the distillation apparatus

children.text: dadyāt puṭaṃ gajākāraṃ patet sattvaṃ sutālakāt ||
children.translated_text: one should apply a heating the size of an elephant; the essence falls from good <s>tālaka</s>.

children.text: raktā śilā tu gomāṃse luṅgāmlena vipācitā
children.translated_text: Red <s>śilā</s>, cooked in beef with citron acid,
should be impregnated with the juices of red and yellow flowers and with biles.

children.text: sitā kṛṣṇā ca saurāṣṭrī cūrṇakhaṇḍātmikā ca sā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Saurāṣṭrī</s> is white and black, and it has the nature of powder and lumps.
Then one should impregnate <s>saurāṣṭrī</s> one hundred times with cow bile.
After blowing it, one should make its essence fall; the penetrating agent is extremely secret.

children.text: kāsīsaṃ trividhaṃ śuklaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ pītamiti priye ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kāsīsa</s> is threefold: white, black, and yellow, beloved.
Having powdered <s>kāsīsa</s>, one should impregnate it
with the juice of <s>kāsamarda</s>, the waters of <s>rājakośātakī</s>, and biles.
<s>Gairika</s> is threefold, divided into red, golden, and plain kinds.
One should impregnate each separately with juices and decoctions of the red group and with biles.
By this procedural sequence one should blow purified <s>gairika</s>.

children.text: kramāt sitaṃ ca raktaṃ ca sattvaṃ patati śobhanam ||
children.translated_text: In order, a fine white and red essence falls.
<s>Rājāvarta</s> is twofold, O <s>Devi</s>, divided into pill and powder forms.
Its powder, O mistress of the lord of gods, combined with buffalo milk,
should be cooked in an iron vessel mixed with cow ghee.
That, powdered, O queen of the gods, and mixed with <s>kunaṭī</s> ghee,
should be made into lumps with auspicious <s>pañcagavya</s>.
When blown with khadira charcoal, it releases a fine essence.
<s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, coral-colored, is made of essence, O beloved.
With drops of <s>sūryāvarta</s> water, fire, and the juices of <s>śigru</s> root,
with the pith of the plantain bulb and with the juices of sterile <s>kośātakī</s>,
and likewise with the juices of <s>kākamācī</s>, <s>devadālī</s>, and <s>vajrakanda</s>,
by these, separately or all together, along with alkalis, acids, fats, and salts,
the <s>mahārasas</s> (great minerals) and <s>uparasas</s> (secondary minerals), when impregnated, attain purification.
Lac, salt, <s>saubhāgya</s>, soot-essence, and the three pungents,
<s>śigru</s> root, beeswax, <s>pathyā</s>, <s>guggulu</s>, and metals,
together with <s>sarjikā</s>, <s>sarja</s> resin, oil-cake, and wool,
pigeon dung, <s>kṣudra</s>, fish, and the five melting agents,
sesame, mustard, wheat, black gram, field bean, and husk,
combined with goat's milk: this is called <s>vajrapiṇḍī</s> (the adamantine lump).
With this <s>vajrapiṇḍī</s>, combined with the five products of the buffalo,
the <s>mahārasas</s>, prepared and impregnated with <s>pañcagavya</s> (the five cow products),

children.text: koṣṭhe kharāgninā dhmātāḥ sattvaṃ muñcanti suvrate
children.translated_text: when blown in a furnace with fierce fire, release their essence, O virtuous one.

children.text: evaṃ śilābhyo jīvebhyo mṛdbhyaḥ sattvaṃ prajāyate ||
children.translated_text: In this way essence is produced from stones, living substances, and earths.

children.text: evaṃ coparasāḥ proktāḥ śṛṇu lohānyataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>uparasas</s> have been stated; now listen further to the metals.

children.text: suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ tāmraṃ tīkṣṇaṃ vaṅgaṃ bhujaṃgamam
children.translated_text: Gold, silver, copper, sharp iron, tin, and lead:

children.text: lohaṃ tu ṣaḍvidhaṃ tacca yathā pūrvaṃ tadakṣayam ||
children.translated_text: metal is sixfold, and each of these, as taught before, is imperishable.
Among them, first, O <s>Sureśānī</s>, the pair of noble metals is remembered as excellent.
In the ordinary group are sharp iron and copper, while tin and lead are base metals.
Gold arises in three forms: born from <s>rasa</s>, born from the field, and born from a mixture of metals;
a fourth kind is not found.

children.text: raktābhaṃ pītavarṇaṃ ca dvividhaṃ devi kāñcanam
children.translated_text: Gold is of two kinds, O goddess: red in appearance and yellow in color.

children.text: dāhe raktaṃ sitaṃ chede nikaṣe kuṅkumaprabham ||
children.translated_text: It is red when heated, white when cut, and on the touchstone has the luster of saffron.
Heavy, soft, and unctuous, free from silver and copper,
gold endowed with sixteenfold purity is praised for the body and for metals.
Clay, impregnated for five days with the sour juice of citron,
together with ash and salt, purifies gold by closed-heating.

children.text: śuklaṃ ca tārakṛṣṇaṃ ca dvividhaṃ rajataṃ priye
children.translated_text: Silver is of two kinds, O beloved: white and blackish silver.
The best silver is considered heavy, unctuous, soft, and white.
Melted with lead and the king of alkalis, it requires purification.
Silver should be thrown three times into the midst of <s>piśācī</s> oil.

children.text: tāmraṃ ca dvividhaṃ proktaṃ raktaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ sureśvari
children.translated_text: Copper too is said to be of two kinds, red and black, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>.
That which withstands heavy blows, is unctuous, red-sheeted, and soft is best.
Smeared with the latex of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>, salt, alkali, and acid,
a copper sheet should be quenched in the juice of <s>nirguṇḍī</s>.

children.text: rohaṇaṃ vājaraṃ caiva tṛtīyaṃ ca paḍālakam
children.translated_text: <s>Rohaṇa</s>, <s>vājara</s>, and the third, <s>paḍālaka</s>:

children.text: iti tīkṣṇaṃ tridhā tacca kāntalohamiti smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: thus sharp iron is threefold, and it is known as magnetic iron.
Blue or black, unctuous, made with a fine edge, the iron is good.
<s>Guḍūcī</s>, <s>haṃsapādī</s>, <s>naktamāla</s>, and the three fruits,
<s>gopālakī</s>, cow's <s>rasona</s>, <s>tumburu</s>, and <s>lohanighnaka</s>:
in the juice of these one should quench it, in order to remove the defects of the ore.
Tin should be known as twofold, divided into white and black.
White, light, soft, and unctuous tin is called the best <s>vaṅga</s>.
Lead is of one kind, O goddess: quickly melting, soft, and heavy.
By a casting-addition with powdered buffalo bone and sprinkling with its urine,
tin becomes purified; likewise lead, through <s>nāga</s>-bone and urine.
Fruits of <s>gaurī</s>, <s>kṣuraka</s>, turmeric, and <s>tumburu</s>,
the seeds of <s>kuberākṣa</s>, and jasmine, O beautiful one,
together with dried <s>palāśa</s>, <s>apāmārga</s> alkali, and <s>snuhī</s> latex,
purify lead by sevenfold casting-addition.
Then one should also cast tin with a combination of <s>snuhī</s> latex.
With <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s> latex, <s>halinī</s>, <s>kañcukī</s> bulb, and <s>citraka</s>,
with <s>guñjā</s>, <s>karañja</s>, <s>dhuttūra</s>, <s>hayagandhā</s>, <s>aṅghri</s>, and <s>tālaka</s>,
and with the roots of <s>naktamāla</s>, <s>iṅgudī</s>, <s>śakra</s>, and <s>vāruṇī</s>,
all ground in buffalo buttermilk and kept for seven nights,

children.text: niṣekaḥ sarvalohānāṃ malaṃ hanti na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the quenching of all metals destroys impurity, without doubt.
Powder of <s>devadālī</s> fruit, repeatedly impregnated with its fresh juice,

children.text: drāvayet kanakaṃ vāpāt bhūyo na kaṭhinaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: will melt gold when added; afterward it does not become hard again.
By its power it liquefies all essences as well.
The powder of <s>suragopa</s> and of <s>suradālī</s>, in equal parts,
when added, O goddess, makes gold resemble water.
With frog bone, fat, <s>ṭaṅka</s>, <s>hayalāla</s>, and <s>indragopaka</s>,
through repeated additions, gold remains molten for a very long time.
Ash of <s>jvālinī</s>, strained in cow urine twenty-one times,
should be dried; by adding it, sharp iron placed in a crucible melts.
Likewise, by ash of <s>nicula</s> impregnated twenty-one times,
through additions with the juices of <s>ketakī</s>, sharp iron becomes fluid.
When it has been impregnated for seven days in a conch with the juice of ripe <s>dhātrī</s> fruit,
and again impregnated for seven days with the water of <s>kañcukī</s>,
placed inside a pair of earthen dishes and very firmly heated all around,
that powder of sharp iron, O queen of gods, becomes mercury-like in form.
<s>Tālaka</s>, sulfur-stone, <s>śilā</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, and red ocher,
<s>kāsīsa</s>, <s>khaṇḍa</s>, <s>saurāṣṭrī</s>, <s>tuttha</s>, and mica as well,
the dung of dog, jackal, and hyena, and likewise that of a cock,
and the excrement of peacock, vulture, and cat, in equal parts:
one should impregnate this three times with <s>snuhī</s> latex and with the juice of <s>devadālī</s>.
With its paste, in an eighth part, one should smear the sheets of iron.
One should blow it; the iron will become molten, and with these same substances one should quench it.
One should grind the roots of <s>aṅkola</s> with sour gruel.

children.text: lohalepaṃ tato dadyāt agnisthaṃ dhārayet priye ||
children.translated_text: Then one should apply a coating to the iron and hold it in the fire, dear one.
Then again one should apply a coating with the juice of <s>paricchinna</s>.
With fish bile, O <s>Deveśī</s>, one should hold it in the fire, dear one.
Again one should make a coating produced from the tuber of <s>lāṅgalī</s>.
By three coatings the iron becomes molten, stainless, and clear like pure water.
O <s>Devi</s>, powdered tortoise bone, ram's horn, and <s>śilājatu</s>
make it, at each casting-in, powerful and firm, as if like solid water.
<s>Arka</s>, <s>apāmārga</s>, <s>musalī</s>, <s>nicula</s>, and also <s>citraka</s>,

children.text: kadalī potakī dālī kṣārameṣāṃ tu sādhayet ||
children.translated_text: <s>kadalī</s>, <s>potakī</s>, and <s>dālī</s>: one should prepare the alkali of these.
One should filter it six times in buffalo urine, O you honored by the gods.
By casting it in, this melts powder produced from the essence of mica and the like.
The tooth of <s>dantī</s> especially melts it like water.
Powder produced from <s>vaikrānta</s>, soaked with the juice of <s>uttaravāruṇī</s>,
melts metals by casting-in, making them like water.

children.text: ratnānāṃ drāvaṇaṃ vakṣye gaganasya drutiṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: I shall explain the liquefaction of jewels, and also the melting of mica.
<s>Triphala</s>, <s>trikaṭuka</s>, the three alkalis, the five salts,

children.text: balā cātibalā caiva tṛtīyā ca mahābalā ||
children.translated_text: <s>balā</s>, <s>atibalā</s>, and the third, <s>mahābalā</s>,
<s>aśvagandhā</s>, <s>cavī</s>, <s>nārī</s>, <s>bhūlatā</s>, and <s>mātṛvāhaka</s>,
also <s>gopendramaṇḍalī</s>, <s>ṣaḍbindu</s>, and <s>dvimukhī</s>,
<s>dhīrā</s>, the tuber of <s>sūraṇa</s>, <s>kañcukī</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>,
<s>snuhī</s>, <s>arka</s>, <s>unmatta</s>, <s>halinī</s>, <s>pāṭhā</s>, and <s>uttaravāruṇī</s>,
lodestone, <s>gokṣura</s>, tender <s>dūrvā</s>, and sour <s>vetasa</s>,
<s>śilājatu</s>, <s>sauvīra</s>, poison, sulfur, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>:
of each of all these one should take ten palas and make a fine powder.
With two kumbhas of horse gram and with wood of <s>tiniśa</s>,
one should boil it over a gentle heat until one kumbha remains.
With that decoction one should impregnate that powder twenty-one times.

children.text: ratnāni tena liptāni tatkvāthasthaṃ dhamet punaḥ
children.translated_text: Gems smeared with it should again be blown while standing in that decoction.
Within a day and night they quickly melt like water.
Mica and the other metals melt without doubt,
and they become stainless and like the seed of <s>Hara</s>.
They quickly unite with mercury and remain imperishable while in the fire.

children.text: tair drutaiḥ sparśamātreṇa kṣaṇād badhyeta sūtakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By those molten substances, through mere contact, <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury) is fixed in an instant.
I shall explain the calcination of metals; listen with attentive mind.
With the milk of <s>snuhī</s>, one should treat <s>sindūra</s>, gold, and then silver.
With that same substance one should treat <s>mākṣika</s> and copper; with goat's milk, sulfur.
With breast milk one should treat <s>hiṅgula</s>, sharp iron, tin, <s>tāla</s>, and <s>palāśaka</s>.
Lead, made into clean sheets, should be treated with <s>śilā</s> and the milk of <s>arka</s>, dear one.
One should calcine it by enclosed heating; an unrevivable ash is produced.

children.text: na so 'sti lohamātaṃgo yaṃ na gandhakakesarī
children.translated_text: There is no metal-elephant
that the sulfur-lion, or the <s>mākṣika</s>-lion, would not kill by mere smell.
Dead metals become rasa-like, O you honored by the gods.

children.text: haranti rogān sakalān rasayuktāni kiṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Joined with mercury, they remove all diseases; how much more so, then?
Through regular use they indeed destroy wrinkles, gray hair, disease, and old age.
Diamond, <s>mākṣika</s>, sharp iron, and mica are praised for operations on the body.

children.text: nāgaṃ vaṅgaṃ suvīraṃ ca dravyakarmaṇi yojayet ||
children.translated_text: Lead, tin, and <s>suvīra</s> should be employed for operations on substances.

children.text: paribālaṃ tu yallohaṃ tathā ca malayodbhavam
children.translated_text: The iron called <s>paribāla</s>, and also that which arises from <s>Malaya</s>,
these two kinds of iron, O <s>Devi</s>, are especially protective of the body.
Having understood the <s>rāga</s> (coloring potency) of the great minerals and the rest, one should prepare the seeds.
Tell that to me, O <s>Deveśī</s>; what else do you wish to hear?
<s>Śrīdevī</s> said:
O lord of the gods, tell the count of the <s>rāga</s> of the great minerals, metals,

children.text: rāgasaṃkhyāṃ tathā bījasādhanaṃ ca vada prabho ||
children.translated_text: and jewels, and also the preparation of the seed, O lord.
<s>Śrībhairava</s> said:
Among the great minerals, the copper <s>rāga</s> is doubled, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>.

children.text: giridoṣe kṣayaṃ nīte sūtakaṃ rañjayanti te ||
children.translated_text: When the mountain-defect has been brought to destruction, they color the <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury).
<s>Sasyaka</s>, <s>capala</s>, <s>rājāvarta</s>, and <s>mākṣika</s>,
<s>vimala</s> and <s>gairika</s>: of these, each one should be double.
In the attractive stones beginning with <s>bhrāmaka</s>, too, it is onefold, twofold, and threefold.
And in mica, for each one, there are white, yellow, red, and bright varieties.
Eighteen thousand <s>rāgas</s> are established in sulfur.
There are ten thousand in <s>darada</s>, O <s>Devi</s>, and two thousand in <s>śilā</s>.
In <s>rasaka</s> there are seven thousand; in <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, four.
They become manifest in the womb of mercury, if digestion is performed.

children.text: dvādaśāgraṃ śataṃ pañca nāge rāgā vyavasthitāḥ
children.translated_text: In lead, five hundred and twelve <s>rāgas</s> are established.

children.text: śatahīnaṃ sahasraṃ tu vaṅge rāgā vyavasthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In tin, one thousand less one hundred <s>rāgas</s> are established.
One hundred and fifty <s>rāgas</s> are established within copper.
There are red, yellow, and white ones; in gold there are sixteen <s>rāgas</s>.
Sixty thousand <s>rāgas</s> are established in <s>śakranīla</s>.

children.text: mahānīle ca deveśi te rāgā dviguṇāḥ sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In <s>mahānīla</s>, O <s>Deveśī</s>, those <s>rāgas</s> are established as double.
In ruby, O queen of the gods, the <s>rāgas</s> are thirteen lakhs.
A gem produced from an elephant or from water is known as a pearl.
There are three thousand in the elephant-born one and six thousand in the water-born one.
Nine lakhs of <s>rāgas</s> are established in <s>padmarāga</s>.

children.text: bhedayet sarvalohāni yacca kena na bhidyate
children.translated_text: That which splits all metals and is not split by anything

children.text: tadvajraṃ tasya deveśi rāgaṃ lakṣadvayaṃ viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: is diamond; its <s>rāga</s>, O <s>Deveśī</s>, is known as two lakhs.
Sixteen thousand are established in <s>puṣparāga</s>.
The colorings, short of a quarter-lakṣa, are taught for <s>marakata</s>, O beloved.

children.text: rāgasaṃkhyāṃ na jānāti saṃkrāntasya rasasya tu
children.translated_text: But he does not know the number of colorings of the transmuted <s>rasa</s>.
If there is excess he may kill the metal; if there is deficiency he will merely make it show.

children.text: mānavendraḥ prakurvīta yo hi jānāti pārvati
children.translated_text: The lord among men who knows this, O <s>Pārvatī</s>, should undertake it.
He should determine the number of colorings by a measure of a hundred crores.
And by thus observing the touch and appearance, a hundred crores is accomplished.

children.text: ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi bījānāṃ sādhanaṃ priye
children.translated_text: After this I shall explain the preparation of the bījas, O beloved.
Because of gold and silver, the bīja is first twofold, O <s>Īśvarī</s>.
The gold-bīja comes from yellow and reddish materials; the silver-bīja comes from white ones.
It is further threefold: prepared, colored, and cooked.
That prepared bīja is twofold, by the distinction of pure and mixed.
The preparation of the bījas of <s>rasa</s>, subsidiary minerals, and metals is separate.

children.text: śuddhaṃ miśraṃ tu saṃyogāt yathālābhaṃ sureśvari ||
children.translated_text: The pure is by itself, but the mixed is from combination, according to what is available, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>.
The essence extracted from <s>vyoma</s>, purified with glass and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,
by sprinklings with a paste of sour tamarind fruit and <s>nirguṇḍī</s> leaves,
becomes cooked and compacted, O <s>Devi</s>, fit for a mercury paste.
With the oily, alkaline, and sour groups, and with three calcinations of <s>śilā</s>,
in the fumigation apparatus, with fumigating substances and anointing when it has been killed,
also by the procedure for tin, or for killed <s>tālaka</s>,
or for <s>tāpya</s> and <s>hiṅgula</s>, or for killed <s>rasaka</s>,
the black sheet of gold and silver melts in the womb of <s>rasa</s>.
The so-called mixture is hard to combine, O beloved, being called soft and hard.
Then, when it is thoroughly ground, O <s>Devi</s>, the pairing of opposites is quickly accomplished.

children.text: bhavet samarasaṃ garbhe rasarājasya ca dravet ||
children.translated_text: It becomes homogeneous in the womb and melts in the king of <s>rasa</s>.
After this I shall explain the pairing of opposites; listen.
<s>Varṣābhū</s>, plantain bulb, <s>kākamācī</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>,
powdered human skull, together with <s>guñjā</s> and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,
well blown with milk and oil: <s>hemābhra</s> combines, O beloved.
By this same procedure one should also combine <s>tārābhra</s>.
Having melted tin, O <s>Deveśī</s>, and then joined it with mercury,
one should grind it with plantain-bulb water, mixed with <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>.
When it is placed in a blind crucible and blown, <s>vaṅgābhra</s> combines at once.
Powder of human skull, women's milk, and wild <s>śigru</s>,
combined with <s>guñjā</s> and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>: <s>vaṅgābhra</s> combines at once.
Having powdered mica, soaked with the juice of <s>kākamācī</s>,
touched with wood-apple water and joined with <s>rasa</s> and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,
placed between tin sheets and blown, <s>vaṅgābhraka</s> will combine.
Having melted it with pungent oil, one should add ash produced from <s>apāmārga</s>.

children.text: vaṅgābhraṃ haritālaṃ ca nāgābhre tu manaḥśilāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For <s>vaṅgābhra</s> there is <s>haritāla</s>; for <s>nāgābhra</s> there are <s>manaḥśilā</s> substances.
<s>Hemābhra</s> is made with lead and <s>tāpya</s>; <s>tārābhra</s> from tin and <s>tālaka</s>.
<s>Śulvābhra</s> is made with sulfur; <s>tīkṣṇābhra</s> from <s>sindhu</s> and <s>hiṅgula</s>.
<s>Vaṅgābhra</s> combines with <s>haritāla</s>, and <s>nāgābhra</s> with <s>śilā</s>.
<s>Lāṅgalī</s>, <s>cāmarīkeśa</s>, cotton seed, and horse gram,
<s>bhūlatā</s>, <s>aśmadalanī</s>, women's milk, and <s>suragopaka</s>:
when a crucible is smeared with these and well blown with fierce fire,
<s>kānta</s>, mica, <s>śaila</s>, and <s>vimala</s> all combine at once.
Meat of <s>latāchuchundarī</s>, combined with poison and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,
when used as a crucible-smear, produces combination in all paired substances.

children.text: abhrakaṃ surasā śṛṅgaṃ maṇḍūkasya vasā viṣam
children.translated_text: Mica, <s>surasā</s>, horn, frog fat, and poison,
with the conjunction of <s>guñjā</s> and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, cause combination in all essences.
With <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, wool, mountain resin, <s>karṇākhya</s>, <s>āmala</s>, and crab,
all paired substances combine when ground with women's milk.
With <s>dhātakī</s>, <s>guggulu</s>, jaggery, <s>sarja</s>, barley, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,
ground with women's milk, every product of pairing in <s>rasāyana</s> combines.
The essence of <s>kha</s>, as a fine powder, joined with the preceding paste,
placed in a blind crucible and blown, combines with the mixture at once.
When quenched with <s>tāpya</s>, <s>rasaka</s>, <s>sasyaka</s>, and <s>darada</s>,

children.text: khasattvaṃ syānnibaddhaṃ ca dṛḍhaṃ dhmātaṃ milettataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the essence of <s>kha</s> becomes bound; when firmly blown, it then combines.
One should smelt all the <s>rasas</s>, subsidiary minerals, and metals together in one place.

children.text: anyonyaṃ dvaṃdvatāṃ yānti dravanti salilaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: They attain mutual pairing and liquefy like water.
Thus the bījas have been prepared. Now listen to the colored ones.
Mica, colored with powder of <s>mākṣika</s> and powder of copper,
paired with the essence of <s>tāpya</s>, is the coloring of the king of <s>rasa</s>.
Repeatedly impregnated many times with <s>āraktavallī</s> and cow urine,
with <s>kunaṭī</s>, sulfur-stones, gold, <s>mākṣika</s>, and <s>hiṅgula</s>,
quenched and treated with substances of the red class and oily substances, then killed,
it is a coloring for the king of <s>rasa</s>, especially in sharp iron and copper.

children.text: kevalaṃ vimalaṃ tāmraṃ vāpitaṃ daradena ca
children.translated_text: Pure <s>vimala</s> and copper alone, quenched with <s>darada</s>,

children.text: kurute triguṇaṃ jīrṇaṃ lākṣābhaṃ nirmalaṃ rasam ||
children.translated_text: make the mercury threefold digested, lac-colored, and spotless.

children.text: rasakaṃ dviguṇaṃ dattvā tāmraṃ sudhmātam īśvari
children.translated_text: Having added twice as much <s>rasaka</s> and well-blown copper, O <s>Īśvarī</s>,

children.text: kṛṣṇābhrakasya cūrṇaṃ ca raktavargair muhuḥ puṭaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and powder of black mica, with repeated calcinations by substances of the red class,

children.text: tāpyena vā mṛtaṃ hema triguṇena nivāpitam
children.translated_text: or gold killed with <s>tāpya</s> and quenched with three times as much,
and <s>rasaka</s> in a vessel, joined with <s>tāpya</s> and rock salt,
until it is like an <s>indragopa</s> insect, through double digestion of all,

children.text: drutaṃ hemanibhaṃ sūtaṃ kurute nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: it quickly makes mercury like gold; there is no doubt about this.

children.text: abhrakaṃ hema tāmraṃ ca śilayā mākṣikeṇa ca
children.translated_text: Mica, gold, and copper, together with <s>śilā</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>,

children.text: gairikeṇa ca mukhyena rasakena ca rañjayet ||
children.translated_text: and with excellent <s>gairika</s> and <s>rasaka</s>, should be used for coloring.
Thus the seed-materials have been colored; now listen to the ripened seed-materials.
One should add the great minerals, the secondary minerals, and the sharp metals,
in equal portions, together with an equal amount of <s>mākṣika</s>, by means of a pouring of sulfur.
One should pour this in a hundred times; undiminished and with some residue remaining,
it certainly melts in the womb of an equal portion of the king of <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
This, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>, is commended in digestion, in the arresting of the paste,
in the coloring of the king of <s>rasa</s>, and also in the operation of <s>sāraṇā</s> (transmission).
That same material, sprinkled a hundred times with oils from the red group,
is praised as superior among them, producing penetration by a thousandth part.
When extracted with lead and tin in the operation concerning gold and silver,
the essence of <s>kha</s> is to be joined with copper; paired in this way it is fit for <s>rasāyana</s>.
With oily substances, alkalis, the five acids, those juices, and minerals such as <s>tālaka</s>,
one should make tin and lead enter copper in equal, double, and triple quantities.
When it has been sprinkled with red oils, that is remembered as the attraction of <s>rasa</s>.
<s>Mākṣika</s>, sulfur-stone, yellow orpiment, and realgar,
<s>vaikrāntaka</s>, chiefly lodestone, <s>sasyaka</s>, purified antimony,
and <s>rasaka</s>, repeatedly poured in and powdered, should be made to enter gold.
By means of iron flakes, <s>tāpya</s>, <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, <s>vimala</s>, and mica,
with dead copper, mineral essence, the latex of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>, and cinnabar,

children.text: nāgo nirjīvatāṃ yāti puṭayogaiḥ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: lead becomes lifeless through repeated applications of closed heating.
Likewise tin, with <s>rasa</s>, <s>tālaka</s>, conch, mica, and tamarind alkalis,

children.text: mṛtaṃ nāgaṃ mṛtaṃ vaṅgaṃ śulvaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca vā mṛtam
children.translated_text: or dead lead, dead tin, copper, and sharp iron that has been killed,
each one should be made to enter the finest gold, O one honored by the gods.

children.text: nirutthe pannage hemni nirvyūḍhe śataśo gaṇe
children.translated_text: When lead is no longer able to rise in gold, and the group has been extracted a hundred times,
the brilliance in copper is like <s>gorocanā</s>, and in the sun-metal it resembles silver.
Sharp mica equal to copper, and likewise twice as much <s>mākṣika</s>,

children.text: āvartitaṃ cūrṇitaṃ ca māritaṃ saptabhiḥ puṭaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be melted, powdered, and killed by seven closed heatings.

children.text: vyūḍhe śataguṇe hemni tadbījaṃ jārayet samam
children.translated_text: When gold has been extended a hundredfold, one should digest that seed-material in an equal amount.
With a coating on leaves of moon-metal and sun-metal, it should penetrate by a hundredth part.

children.text: ūrdhvādho mākṣikaṃ dattvā śulvaṃ hemasamaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: With <s>mākṣika</s> placed above and below, copper becomes equal to gold.
Thus the seed-material, extended tenfold, is like the operative cause.
One should then blow <s>rasaka</s>-mica into lodestone-copper according to the increase of parts.

children.text: mākṣikeṇa hataṃ tacca bīje nirvāhayet priye ||
children.translated_text: That, killed with <s>mākṣika</s>, should be made to enter the seed-material, my dear.

children.text: dvātriṃśadguṇitaṃ hemni nāgaṃ tāpyaṃ hataṃ vahet
children.translated_text: Lead and <s>tāpya</s>, killed, should be made to enter gold increased thirty-two times.
With a thirtyfold pouring of realgar, this is called lead-seed.
Through a pouring of <s>tāpya</s> and <s>tālaka</s>, the essence of yellow mica
should be made to enter the seed-material; this is the penetrator of what has been thoroughly rubbed by women.

children.text: nāgaḥ karoti mṛdutāṃ nirvyūḍhastāṃ ca raktatām
children.translated_text: Lead produces softness, and when extracted it produces that redness.

children.text: vāpitaṃ pītatāṃ tīkṣṇaṃ kāntasthāṃ kālikāṃ viṣam ||
children.translated_text: Sharp iron, when poured in, gives yellowness; it is the hostile blackness residing in lodestone.
The gold-seed has thus been explained; now listen to the silver-seed.
Sharp iron, mica, <s>tāpya</s>, <s>vimala</s>, and <s>rasaka</s> in equal parts,
and four parts of tin: all of this should be blown and finely powdered.

children.text: puṭena nihataṃ kāryaṃ vyūḍhaṃ tāraṃ tu vedhayet
children.translated_text: It should be killed by closed heating; when extended, it should penetrate silver.

children.text: dvātriṃśatsadguṇaṃ tāre vaṅge tāpyaṃ hataṃ vahet
children.translated_text: In silver increased thirty-twofold, killed <s>tāpya</s> should be made to enter tin.
From a thirtyfold pouring of <s>tāla</s>, this is called tin-seed.

children.text: kuṭilaṃ vimalaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ khasattvaṃ cāpi vāhayet
children.translated_text: One should also make <s>kuṭila</s>, <s>vimala</s>, sharp iron, and the essence of <s>kha</s> enter,
or tin-mica or the essence of <s>tāpya</s>, through a pouring of <s>tāla</s> and <s>mākṣika</s>.
One should perform sprinkling with groups of white flowers combined with oils.
The silver-seeds have been stated; listen to the coloring of the seed-materials.
Sharp iron, <s>mākṣika</s>, copper, lead, and calcined <s>capala</s>
should be made like vermilion; with that one should color the seed-materials.
Having placed lead in an earthen pan together with leaves of <s>brahmabīja</s>,
one should burn it, applying fire below, until it becomes fire-colored.
With <s>vāsaka</s>, <s>vibhīta</s>, pot-herbs, <s>kiṃśuka</s>, and <s>śigru</s>,
with the flowers of <s>koraṇḍaka</s>, <s>bakula</s>, and <s>arjuna</s>,
with <s>ahimāra</s>, <s>nāginī</s>, <s>kumārī</s>, and <s>nāgakanyā</s>,
and with a triple portion of realgar boiled in goat-water,

children.text: bhāvitaṃ kharparasthaṃ ca plāvayitvā punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: it should be impregnated while in the earthen pan and repeatedly flooded.
In only seven days it is killed, O one honored by the gods.
One should heat it first with sulfur and afterward with acids.
This is to be used in the coloring of foils, seed-materials, and the king of <s>rasa</s>,
in opening and in <s>krāmaṇa</s> (sequential penetration), especially in the arresting of paste.
In the juice of madder and <s>kiṃśuka</s>, with catechu, red sandalwood,
oleander, deodar, pine, and the two kinds of turmeric,
and other red flowers ground with lac-resin,
one should cook oil, O <s>Devi</s>; with that one should color the seed-materials.
In a decoction containing twice as much of the red flowers and of the red-yellow group,
with four times as much milk and one part oil, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>,
arising from <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>, <s>karañja</s>, and the bitter gourd,
and mixed with the juices of <s>pāṭalī</s>, long pepper, <s>kāmaka</s>, and <s>kākatuṇḍī</s>,
with the fat of frogs, boars, rams, snakes, fish, tortoises, and leeches,
and joined with one fat, all well ground in sixteenth parts,
with the herbs that unite <s>bhūlatā</s>, <s>amala</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, and the paired compound,
cooked and filtered, this is called the oil for <s>sāraṇā</s> (transmission).

children.text: rasatulyaṃ yathā bījaṃ gataṃ garbhadrutiṃ priye
children.translated_text: Just as the seed-material, equal to the <s>rasa</s>, has entered womb-melting, my dear,
so, because of its pervasiveness, all are likewise desired in equal parts.

children.text: pakvaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ samaṃ garbhe yaddravedrañjayecca tam ||
children.translated_text: What is cooked, excellent, and equal in the womb, and what should melt and color, is that.
Thus the seed-materials have been explained; one should digest them through the use of <s>viḍa</s> (flux).
Tell me that, O <s>Deveśi</s>; what else do you wish to hear?
<s>Śrīdevī</s> said:

children.text: bījānāṃ kalpanaṃ proktaṃ viśeṣeṇa ca sādhanam
children.translated_text: The preparation of the seeds has been taught, and especially their accomplishment.

children.text: jāryante tāni yaiḥ sūte tān viḍān vaktumarhasi ||
children.translated_text: Please tell me the <s>viḍa</s> substances by which those are digested in mercury.
<s>Śrībhairava</s> said:
<s>Kāsīsa</s>, rock-salt, <s>kāṅkṣī</s>, <s>sauvīra</s>, <s>vyoṣa</s>, and sulphur,
<s>sauvarcala</s>, <s>sarjikā</s>, and what is produced from the sap of <s>mālatī</s>,
sprinkled with the juices of <s>śigru</s> root: this is the all-digesting <s>viḍa</s>.
Burnt conch-shell powder, soaked a hundred times in the milk of <s>ravi</s>,
and repeatedly heated in a sealed firing, O goddess, is praised as a <s>viḍa</s> for digestion.

children.text: śataśo vā plutaṃ cūrṇaṃ gandhakasya gavāṃ jalaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or sulphur powder may be soaked a hundred times in the waters of cows.
Burnt conch-shell powder, treated with water from <s>śigru</s> root,
and combined a hundred times with what arises from poison and salt, is <s>Vaḍavāmukha</s>.
Borax, O goddess, should be treated a hundred times with the juices of <s>kiṃśuka</s>.
This <s>viḍa</s>, called <s>Vahnimukha</s>, is for the digestion of metals, O beloved.

children.text: cūlikā gandhapāṣāṇaḥ kāntasya ca mukhaṃ priye
children.translated_text: <s>Cūlikā</s>, sulphur-stone, and the mouth of the magnet, O beloved,
each one by itself is sufficient for digesting iron powder.
Sulphur, orpiment, what arises from salt, <s>cūlī</s>, borax, and mica,
should be cooked with alkalis and urines; this is the <s>Jvālāmukha</s> <s>viḍa</s>.
<s>Nicula</s> alkali, treated twenty-one times with the juices of <s>devadālī</s> leaves,
will digest all mineral essences.
<s>Vāstuka</s>, castor, plantain, <s>devadālī</s>, <s>punarnavā</s>,
<s>vāsā</s>, <s>palāśa</s>, <s>nicula</s>, sesame, and golden pyrite,
cut in pieces in every part on a stone slab, not over-dried,

children.text: dagdhakāṇḍais tilānāṃ tu pañcāṅgaṃ mūlakasya ca ||
children.translated_text: with burnt sesame stalks and the five parts of radish,
should be flooded with the group of urines; the liquid filtered from that
should be cooked in an iron vessel in an apparatus, with a controlled fire at <s>haṃsapāka</s> heat.
When many vapors and bubbles arise,
then <s>kāsīsa</s>, <s>saurāṣṭrī</s>, the three alkalis, and the three pungents,

children.text: gandhakaṃ ca sitaṃ hiṅgulavaṇāni ca ṣaṭ tathā
children.translated_text: sulphur, sugar, cinnabar, and the six salts as well:
one should add the powder of these. This, placed inside an iron crucible,
buried in the earth for seven days and afterward placed in grain, is an excellent <s>viḍa</s>.
Cooking with the sour juice of citron and with the liquid of <s>śigru</s> root,
and the two <s>viḍa</s>s sprinkled with <s>cūlikā</s> and sulphur, should each be done a hundred times in sequence.
With juices of <s>koṣātakī</s> leaves, or with alkalis produced from <s>nicula</s>,
<s>devadālī</s>, <s>śivā</s> seed, <s>guñjā</s>, rock-salt, and borax
should be treated with the group of sour liquids; this <s>viḍa</s> digests gold.
Sulphur should be treated a hundred times with the alkalis of radish, ginger, and <s>citraka</s>, filtered through cow urine.
This <s>viḍa</s> is for the digestion of gold.
Orpiment, stone-alkali, salt, conch shell, and oyster shell,
cooked by the <s>haṃsapāka</s> method, become a <s>viḍa</s> for the digestion of gold.
Having gathered the materials in this way, one should undertake the work of <s>rasa</s>.
Tell me that, O <s>Deveśi</s>; what else do you wish to hear?
<s>Śrīdevī</s> said:

children.text: rasasya lakṣaṇaṃ kiṃvā rasakarma ca kīdṛśam
children.translated_text: What is the characteristic of <s>rasa</s>, and what is the work of <s>rasa</s> like?
I do not know that, O lord of gods; please explain it truly.
<s>Śrībhairava</s> said:
The origin of <s>rasa</s> has already been stated; now hear its characteristic.
Its names are thousands, tens of thousands, and hundreds of millions.

children.text: śakyate na mayā vaktuṃ saṃkṣepāt kathyate śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: I cannot state them all; hear, for it is being told in brief.
<s>Rasa</s>, <s>Rasendra</s>, <s>Sūta</s>, <s>Pārada</s>, and also <s>Miśraka</s>:
one should know <s>rasa</s> as accomplished <s>rasa</s>, dwelling in an accomplished field.
It destroys all diseases, and also wrinkles and gray hair.
Now hear of purified <s>Rasendra</s>, which acts on the body and on metals.

children.text: śarīre hemni kartā ca jāraṇe sāraṇāsu ca ||
children.translated_text: It is the agent in the body and in gold, and in digestion and transference.
That which is white externally and internally, heavily covered with a sheath,

children.text: taṃ vidyāt pāradaṃ devi tārakarmaṇi yojayet
children.translated_text: know that to be <s>Pārada</s>, O goddess; it should be applied in the work of silver.
Just as a milk-vessel is spoiled by contact with sour gruel,

children.text: tathā hema śarīraṃ ca pāradena vinaśyati ||
children.translated_text: so too gold and the body are destroyed by <s>Pārada</s>.
The wise know <s>Miśraka</s> as having the appearance of a peacock feather.
When one sees smoky-colored <s>rasa</s>, it is recognized especially
as <s>Miśraka</s>, and should be known as effecting the elevating operation.
Thus, O goddess, the five kinds of <s>rasa</s> have been explained.

children.text: svedanaṃ mardanaṃ caiva cāraṇaṃ jāraṇaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Steaming, grinding, consuming, and digestion,

children.text: drāvaṇaṃ rañjanaṃ caiva sāraṇaṃ krāmaṇaṃ kramāt
children.translated_text: liquefaction and coloring, transference and penetration, in order:

children.text: iti yo vetti tattvena tasya sidhyati sūtakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for one who knows these in truth, mercury becomes perfected.

children.text: tīvratvaṃ jāyate svedāt amalatvaṃ ca mardanāt
children.translated_text: Intensity arises from steaming, and stainlessness from grinding.
By consuming it produces strength; from digestion, binding comes about.
Its unity comes from liquefaction, and redness from reddening.
Its pervasiveness comes from transference, and its penetrative power from penetration.
Going into water, it becomes water-formed; when swift, it becomes <s>Haṃsaga</s>.
Going into impurity, it assumes the form of impurity; smoky, it becomes smoke-going.
Another movement is life-going, O goddess; the living principle comes forth as from an egg.

children.text: sa tāvajjīvayejjīvaṃ tena jīvo rasaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: So long as it gives life to a living being, by that it is remembered as living <s>rasa</s>.
Its fourfold movement is obtained by a skilled practitioner.

children.text: catasro gatayo dṛśyā adṛśyā pañcamī gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Four movements are visible; the fifth movement is invisible.
Through mantra, meditation, and the like, its fifth movement is diminished.
Smoke, crackling, and the frog-leap,
non-trembling and trembling: these are the five states of <s>rasa</s>.
When it is being churned with a paste, three movements arise:
movement in water, movement in impurity, and then the <s>haṃsa</s>-movement.

children.text: hema dattvā tataḥ śuddhaṃ tattu stambhen niyāmake
children.translated_text: Having then given purified gold, it should be stopped by the regulating agent.
After adding <s>rasa</s> (mercury) with the group of regulating herbs, one should cook it thoroughly.

children.text: niyamito na prayāti tathā dhūmagatiṃ śive ||
children.translated_text: When regulated, O <s>Śive</s>, it does not go into the condition of smoke.
Motionless as to particles and free from bubbles,
this becomes regulated, and it also withstands the hearth-fire.
When one digests unregulated <s>sūta</s> (mercury) in a vessel of sour gruel,

children.text: jāyate niścitaṃ bhadre tadā tasya gatitrayam ||
children.translated_text: then, O good lady, three courses of movement certainly arise for it.
It must indeed be sweated by swing-sudation for three days.
O <s>Devi</s>, by means of vasubhaṇṭa and the rest the king of <s>rasa</s> does not diminish.

children.text: akṣīṇaṃ tu rasaṃ dṛṣṭvā dadyādvyomādikaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that the <s>rasa</s> has not been depleted, one should then add mica and the rest.

children.text: svedanaṃ ca tataḥ karma dīyamānasya mardanam ||
children.translated_text: Then comes the operation of sweating, and grinding of what is being added.
The food embraced by <s>rasa</s> is called <s>piṣṭikā</s> (amalgam).
When that has liquefied in the womb of <s>rasa</s>, it is called digestion.
That is termed digestion, and it is recognized in this way.
At the end of digestion, coloring should be done with the group of red substances.

children.text: jīrṇaṃ jīrṇaṃ tu saṃraktaṃ samahemnā tu sārayet
children.translated_text: When it is digested and well reddened, one should make it flow with an equal quantity of gold.
By the application of the flowing apparatus, the mercury that has been made to flow is bound.
When <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury) has been made to flow again and again,

children.text: krāmaṇena samāyuktaṃ taṃ ca vedhe niyojayet ||
children.translated_text: one should join it with penetration and apply it to transmutation.
Fluid mercury is <s>Brahmā</s>; when swooned it is <s>Janārdana</s>.
When bound, <s>rasa</s> becomes <s>Rudra</s> in form, through the power of the operative procedure.
Listen, O <s>Devi</s>; I shall explain in detail the operative procedure.

children.text: pāradasya trayo doṣā viṣaṃ vahnirmalas tathā
children.translated_text: Mercury has three defects: poison, fire, and impurity.

children.text: viṣeṇa saviṣaṃ vidyāt vahnau kuṣṭhī bhavennaraḥ
children.translated_text: By poison it should be known to be poisonous; through fire a man becomes afflicted with skin disease.
Through impurity he becomes diseased in the belly and dies in the elixir-treatment.

children.text: ṣaṭ truṭyaś caikalikṣā syāt ṣaḍlikṣā yūka eva ca
children.translated_text: Six <s>truṭis</s> make one <s>likṣā</s>, and six <s>likṣās</s> make one louse-measure.
Six louse-measures are called <s>rajas</s>, as has been told to you, O fair-vowed one.

children.text: ṣaḍrajaḥ sarṣapaḥ sākṣāt siddhārthaḥ sa ca kīrtitaḥ
children.translated_text: Six <s>rajas</s> make exactly one mustard seed; that is called <s>siddhārtha</s>.
Six <s>siddhārthas</s>, O <s>Deveśi</s>, are said to make one barley grain.
Six barley grains make one <s>guñjā</s>, and six <s>guñjās</s> make one <s>māṣaka</s>.

children.text: māṣā dvādaśa tolaḥ syāt aṣṭau tolāḥ palaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Twelve <s>māṣas</s> make a <s>tola</s>, and eight <s>tolas</s> make a <s>pala</s>.
Thirty-two <s>palas</s>, O <s>Devi</s>, are called one <s>śubha</s>.

children.text: śubhasya tu sahasre dve bhāra ekaḥ prakīrtitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Two thousand <s>śubhas</s> are said to make one <s>bhāra</s>.

children.text: dve sahasre palānāṃ tu sahasraṃ śatameva vā
children.translated_text: Two thousand <s>palas</s>, or else one thousand and one hundred,

children.text: aṣṭāviṃśat palānāṃ tu daśa pañcakameva vā ||
children.translated_text: or twenty-eight <s>palas</s>, or fifteen,
with half a <s>pala</s> only the processing of mercury should be performed.
With <s>mahābalā</s>, <s>nāgabalā</s>, <s>meghanādā</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>,
and <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, together with their essences and with <s>navasāra</s>,
one should sweat mercury for three days, O queen of the gods.
With <s>girikarṇī</s>, <s>mīnākṣī</s>, <s>sahadevī</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>,
<s>uragā</s>, <s>triphalā</s>, <s>kāntā</s>, <s>laghuparṇī</s>, and <s>śatāvarī</s>,

children.text: tuṣavarje tu dhānyāmle sarvaṃ saṃkṣubhya nikṣipet
children.translated_text: one should stir everything together and place it in grain-acid from which the chaff has been removed.
In this sour liquid of elevenfold quantity, it should be ground with sixteenth-parts.
With <s>āsurī</s>, salt, the three pungents, <s>citraka</s>, fresh ginger, and roots,
one should sweat it in a swing apparatus for three days over a gentle fire, O <s>Devi</s>.
<s>Aṅkola</s> destroys poison, O beloved, and <s>āragvadha</s> destroys fire.
<s>Citraka</s> destroys impurity, and <s>kumārī</s> removes the seven sheaths.
Therefore the wise man should grind and distill it, furnished with these in equal measure.
With the <s>Vidyādhara</s> apparatus he should impregnate it after its defects have been removed.
Then, O <s>Devi</s>, that <s>rasa</s>, placed in three layers of cloth, should be filtered.
Since <s>triphalā</s> and fire-root are present, it should be joined with the juice of house-aloe.

children.text: nirudgāre tu pāṣāṇe mardayet pātayet punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: On a stone without exhalation he should grind it and distill it again.
With soot, jaggery, the three pungents, turmeric, sugar, and mustard seeds,
with brick, sour gruel, and spider-web, he should then grind it for three days.
The <s>sūta</s> becomes stainless and reveals my power.
He should grind it with <s>vāsaka</s> and <s>vibhīta</s>, and distill it again.
Defects arising from admixtures such as lead and tin go to destruction.
Seven times he should grind the defect-free mercury with <s>kākamācī</s>.
He should distill it seven times, and <s>rasa</s> abandons its mountain-defect.
O <s>Devi</s>, when swooned with the juice of <s>gokarṇa</s>, it abandons the field-defect.
Sweated in the exudation of cotton leaves, together with the three pungents,
within seven days <s>rasa</s> becomes freed from its seven sheaths.
<s>Kākamācī</s>, <s>jayā</s>, <s>brāhmī</s>, <s>gāṅgerī</s>, red <s>citraka</s>,
<s>maṇḍūkī</s>, <s>mudgaparṇī</s>, dry ginger, and <s>rasāṅkuśa</s>,
<s>devadālī</s>, <s>śaṅkhapuṣpī</s>, <s>kākajaṅghā</s>, and <s>śatāvarī</s>,
<s>kumārī</s>, <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>, <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, and <s>grīṣmasundara</s>,
<s>śūlinī</s>, <s>śūrpaparṇī</s>, <s>gojihvā</s>, and <s>kṣīrakañcuka</s>:
ground with their juices and distilled seven times, it becomes stainless.
Having made an amalgam with copper, one should distill it by upward sublimation.
Having abandoned tin and lead, <s>sūtaka</s> becomes purified.
Ground with <s>triphalā</s>, <s>śigru</s>, mustard, salt, and <s>citraka</s>,
it should be cooked in the upper vessel with blazing cow-dung cakes below.
By blocking the lotus of creation, <s>rasa</s> becomes almost recovered.
Joined with <s>karkoṭī</s>, <s>kañcukī</s>, <s>bimbī</s>, <s>sarpākṣī</s>, and <s>ambuja</s>,

children.text: rasaṃ niyāmake dadyāt tejasvī nirmalo bhavet
children.translated_text: one should place the <s>rasa</s> in the regulating agent; it becomes powerful and stainless.
Thus purified, <s>sūta</s>, dried with one eighth of <s>bhadrā</s>,
with small sour substances, salt, alkali, <s>bhūkhaga</s>, <s>uṣaṇa</s>, and <s>śigru</s>,
together with mustard and borax, should remain in sour gruel for three days.
By steaming, O <s>Devi</s>, <s>rasa</s> (mercury) is kindled and becomes eager for a morsel.
The seeds beginning with the essence of <s>vyoma</s> are used in the digestion and purification of mercury;
tell me that, O <s>Deveśi</s>. What else do you wish to hear?
The blessed <s>Devī</s> said:

children.text: lakṣaṇaṃ śodhanaṃ caiva pāradasya śrutaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: I have heard the marks and the purification of mercury,
and I wish to hear of <s>cāraṇa</s> and <s>jāraṇa</s>, O <s>Bhairava</s>.
The blessed <s>Bhairava</s> said:
When the destruction of all sins has come about, the digestion of mercury is obtained;
when that is obtained, knowledge itself, the cause of liberation, is as good as obtained.
For the practitioner, O <s>Devi</s>, <s>jāraṇa</s> is the revealer of liberation;

children.text: yāvanna jāryate sūtaḥ tāvattu na ca nirvṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: so long as <s>sūta</s> (mercury) has not been digested, there is no release.
The mortar, O <s>Devi</s>, is the pedestal; <s>rasendra</s> (lord mercury) is called the liṅga.

children.text: mardanaṃ vandanaṃ tasya grāsaḥ pūjā vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: Its rubbing is homage; the morsel is prescribed as worship.
For as many days mercury is digested and maintained while placed in the fire,
for that many thousands of ages he is honored in <s>Śivaloka</s>.
He who gives fire to <s>Rasendra</s> for a single day

children.text: dravanti tasya pāpāni kurvannapi na lipyate ||
children.translated_text: has his sins melt away; even while acting, he is not tainted.
<s>Jāraṇā</s> is twofold: preliminary digestion and bound digestion.
Of these, first, O <s>Parameśānī</s>, preliminary digestion will be explained.
First one should digest <s>gagana</s> (mica); after that, all the essences,
then purified <s>mākṣika</s>, and gold thereafter.

children.text: garbhasthaṃ drāvayitvā tu tato bāhyadrutiṃ dravet
children.translated_text: Having melted what is in the womb, one should then bring about the external liquefaction.

children.text: sitaṃ sitena dravyeṇa raktaṃ raktena rañjayet ||
children.translated_text: One should color white with a white substance and red with a red one.

children.text: sāraṇaṃ krāmaṇaṃ jñātvā tato vedhaṃ prayojayet ||
children.translated_text: Having learned <s>sāraṇa</s> and <s>krāmaṇa</s>, one should then apply <s>vedha</s>.
Oṃ, homage to the immortal metal, born from the supreme ambrosial <s>rasa</s>: huṃ svāhā.
For the benefit of all beings, O Blessed One, with your permission,

children.text: jāraṇaṃ kartumicchāmi grāsaṃ gṛhṇa mama prabho ||
children.translated_text: I wish to perform digestion; accept the morsel, my lord.
Saying, "Do it," as taught by <s>Śiva</s>, it is indeed to be accepted by the intelligent man.
Listen, O <s>Devi</s>; I shall explain the excellent digestion of <s>vyoma</s>.
It is twofold: digestion of leaf-mica and digestion of essence.
Without a mouth, with a mouth, and also with a mouth produced by perfuming:

children.text: ekaikaṃ trividhaṃ tacca tad vakṣyāmy ānupūrvaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: each of these is threefold, and I shall explain it in order.
Through contact with <s>vaikrānta</s> and diamond, or by the power of divine herbs,
mouthless mercury consumes <s>gagana</s> in an instant, O <s>Devi</s>.

children.text: hemakarmaṇi hemaiva tāre tāro mukhaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: In work with gold, gold itself is the mouth; in work with silver, silver becomes the mouth.
A paste made in a heated mortar, very smooth, with mica added little by little,
and triturated with sour <s>vetasa</s>, <s>jambīra</s>, <s>bījapūra</s>, sour substances, and <s>bhūkhaga</s>,
makes it move, O <s>Devi</s>; this is digestion with a mouth.
The three alkalis, the five salts, <s>kākṣī</s>, <s>kāsīsa</s>, and sulfur,
with <s>mākṣika</s> and sour substances, should be digested in a copper vessel.
Having made this divine fermented preparation, the discerning man

children.text: jāraṇārthaṃ ca bījānāṃ vajrāṇāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: uses it for the digestion of seeds, and especially of diamonds.
In that, O worshiped by the gods, he should quench molten lead or tin
a hundred times, though not in the operation of <s>rasāyana</s>.
By this, O <s>Devi</s>, he should impregnate the whole substance used for <s>cāraṇa</s>.

children.text: kṣārāmle bhāvitaṃ vyoma rajasā prathamena ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vyoma</s>, impregnated with alkali and acid and with the first powder,
is triturated with <s>sṛṣṭitrayodaka</s>, <s>kaṇā</s>, and the liquid of <s>tumburu</s>.
