When heated in a sealed crucible, it moves or digests with the juice of <s>yavaciñcā</s>.
<s>Śatāvarī</s>, <s>gadā</s>, <s>rambhā</s>, <s>meghanādā</s>, <s>punarnavā</s>,

children.text: śigruko yavaciñcā ca bhāvitaṃ tadrasaiḥ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: <s>śigruka</s>, and <s>yavaciñcā</s>: it is impregnated successively with their juices.
The root of <s>hilamucā</s> and the root of <s>kauverī</s>,
<s>kadalī</s>, <s>musalī</s>, <s>śigru</s>, <s>tāmbūlī</s>, <s>vāṇa</s>, and <s>pīluka</s>,
<s>alambuṣā</s>, <s>balā</s>, <s>kola</s>, <s>āsphoṭa</s>, and <s>kharamañjarī</s>,
<s>tumburu</s>, or else bitter greens: with the single juice of one of these,
mica, mixed with <s>rājikā</s> and <s>vyoṣa</s>, is steamed for three days.
Joined with <s>kāsīsa</s>, <s>tuvarī</s>, <s>sindhu</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, and alkali,
by the earlier fermented preparation, mercury moves in an instant.
It quickly becomes a pellet that grants all accomplishments.
Taking grain-sour liquid, O <s>Devi</s>, joined with the acid group,
one should decoct that mica and triturate it with the milk of <s>snuhī</s>.
Then, with forest cow-dung, one should give the heating called <s>kapota</s>.
With exudates of banana rhizome and with the juice of radish tuber,
<s>kākamācī</s>, <s>mīnākṣī</s>, <s>apāmārga</s>, and also <s>muni</s>,
<s>eraṇḍa</s>, fresh ginger, <s>meghanādā</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>,
one should give one heating with the liquid of each in turn.
Combined with the milk of <s>vajrī</s>, one should cook it in a swing-apparatus;
then, having dried it in the shade, and combined it with chickpea-sour liquid,

children.text: navasāraṃ ca kāsīsaṃ vacāṃ nimbaṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: <s>navasāra</s>, <s>kāsīsa</s>, <s>vacā</s>, and <s>nimba</s> as well,
one should put each of these there in the proportion of one sixteenth of the mica.
Having placed it in a copper vessel, O virtuous woman, one should rub it;

children.text: navavāraṃ tato devi lohapātre tu jārayet ||
children.translated_text: then, O <s>Devi</s>, one should digest it nine times in an iron vessel.
Together with mercury, O <s>Deveśi</s>, the sour gruel with chickpea-sour liquid
should be boiled on a gentle fire; it is ready within half a watch.
Having ground <s>vyoma</s> with the juices of <s>somavallī</s>, mixed with <s>sauvarcala</s>,
one should slowly, slowly give three heatings with <s>haṃsapādī</s>.
One should give it seven times with the juice of <s>somavallī</s> alone;
one should cast it into an earthen vessel, together with mercury.
One should rub the root of white <s>iṣupuṅkhā</s> with cow's milk;

children.text: kalkena lepayet sūtaṃ gaganaṃ ca tadūrdhvagam ||
children.translated_text: with the paste one should smear mercury and the upward-going <s>gagana</s>.
One should heat it with the heat of the sun; mouthless mercury consumes it in an instant.

children.text: jāyate piṣṭikā śīghraṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: A <s>piṣṭikā</s> (paste-amalgam) is quickly produced; no deliberation is to be made here.
With the juice of <s>tilaparṇī</s> alone, one should impregnate mica, O dear one.
From grinding, a paste is produced; no deliberation is to be made here.
One should repeatedly quench lead in the exudation of <s>muṇḍī</s>.

children.text: tenābhrakaṃ tu saṃplāvya bhūyobhūyaḥ puṭe dahet ||
children.translated_text: Then, having drenched mica with that again and again, one should burn it in a <s>puṭa</s> (closed heating).
With each of the roots of <s>citraka</s> and fresh ginger, seven times,
the powder of sulfur and mica should be carefully drenched.
It is to be impregnated with the juice of <s>nāgaśuṇḍī</s>, breast milk, menstrual blood, and the acid of citron.
With a sixteenth part, likewise, mercury should be made to circulate in the swing-apparatus.
Sixty-four times, O <s>Devi</s>, or thirty-two times,
or else sixteen times, and likewise eight times,

children.text: caturguṇaṃ vā dviguṇaṃ samaṃ vā cārayet priye ||
children.translated_text: or four times, two times, or an equal amount, one should make it consume, O dear one.
Now hear, O <s>Pārvatī</s>, the supreme digestion of the essence of mica.
The essence of mica, combined in equal portion with the essence of <s>tāpya</s>,
when mercury consumes it in this way, O <s>Devi</s>, becomes one that liquefies in the womb.
Lead-mica, O <s>Devi</s>, tin-mica, iron-mica, copper-mica,
silver-mica, O <s>Devi</s>, and gold-mica should be digested by the womb of mercury.
By the previous consecration procedure it melts in the womb through grinding.
The first is a sixty-fourth part; the second is a thirty-second part.
The third is a sixteenth part, and the fourth is an eighth part.
The fifth is declared to be a fourth part, and the sixth a half part.
The <s>grāsa</s> (morsel-dose) of mica possessing essence is to be given to the mercury.
At the sixty-fourth-part dose, mercury becomes staff-bearing.
At the second dose-combination it is like a leech, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>.
With the third dose it becomes like crow-dung.
With the fourth dose it becomes like the whey of curds.
When the fifth dose has been processed, it becomes like fresh butter.
At the sixth it is globular; these are the signs of what is digested in sequence.
Red mica, quenched with sour gruel and washed a hundred times,
should be made to consume inside the mortar, together with the conditioning of copper.

children.text: hema tāraṃ ca saṃghṛṣya khalle tatra rasaṃ nyaset
children.translated_text: Having rubbed gold and silver in the mortar, one should place mercury there.
Mercury consumes <s>kāsīsa</s> with sour gruel, by means of salt.

children.text: hema sīsaṃ tu saṃghṛṣya rasaṃ tatra pradāpayet
children.translated_text: Having rubbed gold and lead, one should add mercury there.
Mica joined with lead and gold, equally digested, becomes liquid.
This one quickly consumes mica and secondary minerals by its mouth alone.

children.text: tāraṃ vaṅgaṃ ca saṃghṛṣya rasaṃ tatra pradāpayet
children.translated_text: Having rubbed silver and tin, one should add mercury there.
Mica joined with lead and gold, equally digested, becomes liquid.
It consumes mica by mouth, and is praised for work with silver.
Whether with a mouth or without a mouth, one should carefully make it consume mica.
Having thus performed the threefold feeding and the inner liquefaction in mercury,
one should digest it, steam it, and form the lump by the three stages of maturation.
It is smeared with pungent, sour, and alkaline substances, cow urine, and the milk of <s>snuhī</s>.

children.text: bahiśca baddhaṃ vastreṇa bhūyo grāsaṃ niveditam
children.translated_text: Bound on the outside with cloth, the dose is again presented.
One should steam it in alkalis, <s>aranāla</s>, and oils with a gentle fire.
By this sequence, O <s>Deveśī</s>, it is digested in three days.

children.text: yantrād uddhṛtamātraṃ tu lohapātre sthitaṃ rasam ||
children.translated_text: As soon as the mercury is taken from the apparatus and placed in an iron vessel,
it should first be washed with lukewarm sour gruel and filtered through cloth.
In a vessel, with a comfortably warm hand, one should rub it as long as any residue remains.
Pressed through fourfold cloth, it becomes clear and pure.
Through the filtering process, when the dose has come out by crushing,
that mercury becomes staff-bearing, and the dose has then been digested.
If it is undigested, one should cook the paste, steam it, and grind it likewise.
When it is digested through the application of <s>vetasa</s> acid, one should give the dose.
With substances born from burnt brick, jaggery, burnt wool, mustard, rock salt, and soot,

children.text: ṣoḍaśāṃśaiḥ sa dhānyāmlaiḥ mardyaḥ svedyaśca pāradaḥ ||
children.translated_text: each in a sixteenth part, with grain-sour gruels, mercury should be ground and steamed.

children.text: nirmalīkaraṇārthaṃ tu grāse grāse punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: For the sake of purification, with each dose again and again,
when its mica and seed are digested, it, being stainless, takes on colors.
In this sequence, four doses should be processed in the swing-apparatus.
After that, by means of the tortoise-apparatus, ignition and fixation are done in order.
Having given <s>viḍa</s> above and below in an eighth part, one should digest it.
Mercury whose mica has been equally digested becomes capable of hundredfold penetration, O dear one.
With double, it penetrates a thousand; with triple, it penetrates ten thousand.

children.text: caturguṇe lakṣavedhī sa bhaved bhūcaro rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With quadruple, it penetrates a hundred thousand; that mercury becomes earth-moving.
When fivefold is digested, O <s>Devi</s>, mercury obtains the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>.
With sixfold, its lifespan is that of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; mercury becomes capable of ten-millionfold penetration.
All the defects of mercury, through sixfold mica
when it has been digested, go to destruction; no deliberation is to be made here.

children.text: rasarāje yadā jīrṇaṃ ṣaḍguṇaṃ gaganaṃ priye
children.translated_text: When sixfold mica has been digested in the king of mercury, O dear one,
then it devours metals and abandons its own motion.
Smoke, crackling, and frog-like leaping,
trembling and violent trembling: these are the five states of mercury.
It becomes tawny, then ceases belching and spattering.
It stands in fire without trembling: this is the sign of mica that has been digested.
When equally digested it is a child; with fourfold digestion it is in youth.

children.text: vṛddhastu ṣaḍguṇaṃ jīrṇaḥ kuryāt karma pṛthak pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: With sixfold digested it is old; it performs each operation separately.
The child works by coating sheets; the youth works by application of a paste.
The old one pierces metals, whether digested or made to flow.

children.text: kumārastu raso devi na samartho rasāyane
children.translated_text: But immature <s>rasa</s> (mercury), O <s>Devi</s>, is not capable in <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: yauvanastho raso devi kṣamo dehasya rakṣaṇe ||
children.translated_text: A youthful <s>rasa</s>, O <s>Devi</s>, is capable of protecting the body.

children.text: jarāvastho raso yaśca dehe lohena saṃkramet
children.translated_text: And aged <s>rasa</s>, when in the body, should pass through with metal.
In the absence of mica essence, one should cause magnetic-iron essence to be added.

children.text: kāntasya cāpyabhāve tu tīkṣṇalohaṃ tu dāpayet
children.translated_text: And if magnetic iron is also absent, then one should have sharp iron added.
By this ordered procedure one should digest all the essences.
Even a single one, combined with gold, makes gold at once.
Beyond sulfur there is nothing higher among the <s>rasas</s> or the secondary <s>rasas</s>.
By means of the apparatus procedure described before, one should digest sulfur sixteenfold,
or else twelvefold, or even sixfold.
Having taken the essence of <s>mākṣika</s>, one should digest it with a quarter portion.
After that, one should melt all the essences from within mercury.
There is friendship between gold and fire, and likewise between gold and mercury.
There is enmity between fire and mercury; through the friend of those two, there is friendship.
<s>Agnika</s>, <s>yavaciñcā</s>, <s>vasuhaṭṭa</s>, and <s>rāgiṇī</s>
when cooked by swing-steaming, make the best digestion of gold.
Ash of <s>palāśa</s>, <s>apāmārga</s>, barley-alkali, and sour gruel,

children.text: sauvarcalaṃ ca kāsīsaṃ sāmudraṃ saindhavaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>sauvarcala</s> salt, <s>kāsīsa</s>, sea salt, and rock salt,
<s>āsurī</s>, borax, and likewise sal ammoniac,
camphor and <s>mākṣika</s>: one should make them in equal parts.
With the milks of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>, O <s>Deveśī</s>, one should make a coating for the crucible.

children.text: viḍacūrṇaṃ tato dattvā kanakaṃ jārayet priye ||
children.translated_text: Then, having added the powdered flux, one should digest the gold, O beloved.

children.text: śṛṇu devi pravakṣyāmi bhūcarākhyaṃ tu jāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: Listen, O <s>Devi</s>; I shall explain the digestion called <s>bhūcara</s>.

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ pītaṃ raktamabhraṃ śulve tīkṣṇe ca melayet ||
children.translated_text: One should mix black, yellow, and red mica with copper and sharp iron.

children.text: śulve tīkṣṇaṃ yadā cūrṇaṃ dvāviṃśatiguṇaṃ priye
children.translated_text: When the sharp iron in the copper is powdered twenty-twofold, O beloved,

children.text: gandhanāgaṃ tato'rdhaṃ tu krameṇaiva tu melayet ||
children.translated_text: then sulfur and lead, half as much, should be mixed in proper sequence.

children.text: hemnā tu saha dātavyaṃ sūtakaikena ṣoḍaśa
children.translated_text: It should be given together with gold: sixteen parts with one part of mercury.

children.text: gandhanāgaṃ yadā jīrṇaṃ tadā baddho bhavedrasaḥ
children.translated_text: When the sulfur and lead are digested, then the <s>rasa</s> becomes bound.
When the gold is digested, one should then color it with half as much dead metal.
Copper killed with sulfur, <s>mākṣika</s>, <s>darada</s>, and iron

children.text: puṭena mārayecchuddhaṃ hema dadyāt tu ṣaḍguṇam ||
children.translated_text: should be calcined by a closed heating, purified, and then gold should be added sixfold.

children.text: sūtake hemabījaṃ ca yadā jīrṇaṃ caturguṇam
children.translated_text: When the gold-seed in mercury has been digested fourfold,
one should know it as fixed in color; the <s>rasa</s> becomes gold-like.
Set in the middle of the <s>sāraṇā</s> apparatus, one should make it pass through together with that very substance.
Having made it pass through in three parts, one should again digest it there itself.
Digested and passed through, and again digested and passed through,
by the procedure of seven chains the <s>rasa</s> becomes capable of ten-millionfold penetration.

children.text: bhūcarī jāraṇā proktā khecarīṃ jāraṇāṃ śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: The <s>bhūcarī</s> digestion has been stated; hear the <s>khecarī</s> digestion.
One should make the chief jewels, beginning with diamond, into residues of <s>rasa</s>.
The seeds of bitter bottle-gourd should be added in half that amount.
This is called the great digestion; the skilled man should make it into a paste.
At the mouth of a diamond crucible he should place the <s>rasa</s> in its middle.

children.text: katakaṃ kanakaṃ caivam ekīkṛtya ca mardayet
children.translated_text: Combining <s>kaṭaka</s> and gold in this way, he should grind them together.

children.text: padmarāgaṃ prayatnena rase grāsaṃ tu dāpayet ||
children.translated_text: With care he should feed a morsel of ruby to the <s>rasa</s>.
Up to eleven times the amount of ruby should be given to the mercury.
When the color has been digested, O <s>Deveśī</s>, the <s>rasa</s> becomes shaped like a liṅga.
It should be carefully guarded by the eight guardians of the world.
A sixfold portion of the lordly mercury should be given among all of them.
It should be eaten carefully, after bowing to the guru and the gods,
and after honoring all the siddhas and especially the deities.
Then fainting and burning of the limbs arise; there is no doubt about this.
One sees oneself risen up, with divine splendor and great strength.
Amid the sounds of conches and kettle-drums, together with siddhas and vidyādharas,
one roams the worlds at will, assuming whatever form one desires and traveling by aerial vehicle.
Where the gods dissolve away, the siddha dissolves there itself.
Again I shall explain another excellent procedure of digestion.
Mercury, well rubbed and cooked, then freed from all defects,
with the essence of vegetable sprouts and with the juice of <s>viṣṇukrāntā</s>,
and sulfur in equal amount, impregnated with water of <s>palāśa</s> flowers,

children.text: samaṃ kṛṣṇābhrasattvaṃ ca rasakaṃ cāṣṭakaṃ guṇam ||
children.translated_text: together with an equal amount of black mica essence and eight times as much <s>rasaka</s>,
should digest sharp iron, copper, and lead by means of the tortoise apparatus.
Afterward one should digest gold by the flux procedure, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.

children.text: tataḥ siddhaṃ vijānīyāt dvaidhaṃ śulvasya dāpayet
children.translated_text: Then one should know it to be perfected; one should add twice the amount of copper.
According to the number and measure of the operations, lead becomes gold.
After this I shall explain the best sequence of digestion.
Having impregnated the seed powders again and again with oil,
one should slowly rub that morsel with a finger in a sixteenth part.
Then, by a compound beginning with ginger, it should be added in a sixteenth part.

children.text: bhūrje dattvā tato deyaṃ dolāyantre vinikṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Having placed it in birch bark, it should then be put into the swing apparatus.
In a day and night, O beloved, the mercury devours that seed.
Having taken up that <s>rasa</s>, O <s>Devi</s>, one should then grind it in a mortar.
Then, placing it in the apparatus, one should heat it with a strong fire for a day and night.
Once heated and removed from the apparatus, it should be ground in a heated mortar.

children.text: mardayitvābhrake piṇḍaṃ kṣiptvā tatra puṭaṃ dadet
children.translated_text: After grinding it, one should put the lump in mica and there apply a closed heating.

children.text: tato garbhe patatyāśu jārayet tat sukhena tu ||
children.translated_text: Then it quickly falls into the womb, and one should digest it with ease.
Then, placing it in the swing apparatus together with a moist lump,

children.text: tṛtīye divase sūto jarate grasate tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: on the third day the mercury digests it and then devours it.
The skilled man should keep it in the swing apparatus until it is evenly digested.
Afterward, by means of the tortoise apparatus, when it is evenly digested, O <s>Pārvatī</s>,
he should digest it with the tortoise method by a morsel equal to a twelfth part.
As before, there is the ginger compound and the liquefaction of the womb;
then, O <s>Devi</s>, having deposited it, the skilled man should apply a closed heating.

children.text: aṣṭāṃśena tato grāsaṃ garbhadrāvaṃ ca pūrvavat
children.translated_text: Then an eighth part is the morsel, and the womb-liquefaction is as before;
having placed that mercury in the belly of a <s>sūraṇa</s> tuber,

children.text: puṭettu jāritastāvat yāvat kando na dahyate ||
children.translated_text: he should heat it. It is digested until the tuber is not burnt.

children.text: pādāṃśena tu mūṣāyā grāsaḥ sūte vidhīyate
children.translated_text: A morsel for the mercury is prescribed in the crucible by a quarter portion;
and, as before, he should add the <s>viḍa</s> (alkaline flux) and the womb-liquefaction.

children.text: evaṃ caturguṇe jīrṇe sūtako balavān bhavet
children.translated_text: When in this way fourfold has been digested, the mercury becomes powerful;

children.text: tataḥ śalākayā grāsān agnistho grasate rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then, while standing in the fire, the <s>rasa</s> devours morsels by means of a rod.
Then the jewels are to be digested according to the sequence about to be stated.

children.text: abhrakaṃ bhrāmakaṃ caiva śaṅkhanābhiṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: Mica, <s>bhrāmaka</s>, and likewise <s>śaṅkhanābhi</s>,
having added <s>rasa</s>s and <s>uparasa</s>s, combined with the great digestion,
<s>Vajrakanda</s>, <s>vajralatā</s>, <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, <s>amṛtā</s>, and iron,
the seeds of bitter bottle-gourd and dead metals he should cook.
All are in equal parts, measured with peacock blood;

children.text: tāvattaṃ mardayet prājño yāvat karma dṛḍhaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: the wise man should grind it so long as the operation becomes firm.
The crucible should be made in the shape of a lute, together with coverings;
he should place the mercury in its middle and blow it with a downward current.
At first, in that very place, diamond smeared with medicinal substances should be given.

children.text: gṛhyate ko 'tra saṃdeho yathā tīvre hutāśane ||
children.translated_text: It is taken up; what doubt is there here, as in a fierce fire?

children.text: kuliśena puṭe dagdhe karṣvagnau tena mardayet
children.translated_text: When the diamond has been burnt in a closed heating, he should grind it with that in a <s>karṣa</s>-fire,
until he again digests diamond up to eleven times the amount.
And well-burnt <s>śaṅkhanābhi</s>, soaked in citron juice,

children.text: muktāphalaṃ tato deyaṃ vajrajīrṇe tu sūtake ||
children.translated_text: then pearl should be given when diamond has been digested in the mercury.
By this sequential procedure it becomes elevenfold.
Only peacock bile, mixed with the exudation of <s>nīlī</s>,
blue lotuses smeared with it and thrown into the mercury,
should produce deep colors in the <s>rasa</s>; he should reject inferior colors.
Red substances, peacock bile, and what is furnished with great jewels,
with that he should smear the excellent jewel; it melts within the <s>rasa</s>.
Turmeric and <s>kuṣṭha</s>, impregnated with the exudation of <s>brahma</s>,
with that same mixture he should cause the digestion of topaz.
When many jewels have been digested among the <s>bhṛṅgarāga</s>s, O faithful one,
the lord of mercury is seen, O <s>Devi</s>, with blue, yellow, and red luster.
Pure gold leaves should be smeared with a hundredth part;
he should kill it with a closed heating; it will become like an <s>indragopa</s> insect.
By contact this dead gold penetrates everything, O beloved;
he should cause three parts of the lordly mercury to pass through together with that same substance.
When that is situated in the middle of the crucible, he should again digest it with that same substance;
it becomes smoke-penetrating, O <s>Devi</s>, once again passed through and digested.
If by this sequential procedure the three-chain process has been digested,
it will penetrate, there is no doubt, mountain, netherworld, and earth.

children.text: pārśvajyotiḥ pradṛśyeta cordhvaṃ naiva tu dṛśyate
children.translated_text: A side-light is seen, but it is not seen upward;

children.text: bhūcaraṃ taṃ vijānīyāt rasendraṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should know that lord of mercury to be earth-roving; there is no doubt.
By means of that, O <s>Devi</s>, one whose movement is tireless would go a hundred <s>yojana</s>s,
with divine radiance, great body, divine sight, and great strength.
Freed from all diseases, he would live as long as the moon and stars;
his urine and feces penetrate all metals.

children.text: samajīrṇena vajreṇa hemnā ca sahitena ca
children.translated_text: With diamond evenly digested and together with gold,
when set in fire it should digest the metals; the mercury attains fixation.
He should cause it to pass through with that seed; it would penetrate even a thousandfold.

children.text: sāritaṃ jārayet paścāt lepyaṃ kṣepyaṃ sahasraśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Afterward he should digest what has been passed through; smearing and throwing are to be done thousands of times.
He should cause it to pass through with that seed; he obtains hundred-thousandfold penetration.
By this sequential procedure the <s>rasa</s> becomes capable of ten-millionfold penetration.

children.text: kevalaṃ tu yadā vajraṃ samajīrṇaṃ tu jārayet
children.translated_text: But when only diamond is evenly digested and then further digested,
then the fixed mercury should be known as unmoving and free from disturbance.

children.text: agnistho jāyate sūtaḥ śalākāṃ grasate kṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: When set in fire, the mercury arises; it devours the rod in an instant.
Blown with forced fire, it devours everything eagerly.
The mercury moves and digests, granting life and wealth;

children.text: mūṣāsthaṃ dhamayet sūtaṃ haṭhāgnau naiva kampate ||
children.translated_text: one should blow the mercury placed in the crucible; in forced fire it does not tremble.
It should digest all jewels; when fixed it leads to <s>khecaratā</s> (sky-moving power).
Thus, when iron has been digested eightfold, there is binding of mercury.

children.text: lohāni sattvaṃ triguṇaṃ dviguṇaṃ kanakaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Metals, essence threefold, and gold twofold likewise:
it becomes smoke-sight-penetrating; the <s>rasa</s> becomes one that bestows liberation.
At first the great <s>rasa</s>, mica essence, should be digested eightfold;
with an equal amount of gold, he should digest diamonds and jewels in a tenth part.

children.text: sarvaṃ ca jārayedvajraṃ tadāsau khecaro rasaḥ
children.translated_text: And when it has digested all the diamond, then that <s>rasa</s> is sky-roving;
it revolves clockwise and becomes capable of ten-millionfold penetration.

children.text: same tu pannage jīrṇe daśavedhī bhavedrasaḥ
children.translated_text: When lead is digested in equal amount, the <s>rasa</s> becomes tenfold-penetrating;

children.text: dviguṇe śatavedhī syāt triguṇe tu sahasrakam ||
children.translated_text: when twofold, it is hundredfold-penetrating; when threefold, it reaches a thousandfold.
When fourfold, it reaches ten-thousandfold, O <s>Devi</s>; by this sequence he should increase it.
By successive increase he should digest the lead there.

children.text: kuṭilaṃ pannagaṃ jāryaṃ tatra saṃkhyākrameṇa tu
children.translated_text: Crooked lead should be digested there according to the numerical sequence;
it reaches that doctrine, O <s>Deveśī</s>; the <s>rasa</s> becomes capable of ten-millionfold penetration.
The ash-mercury eaten by <s>Ruru</s>, lord of demons,
where sharp iron is digested twelvefold, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>.
After eating one pala, the demon, proud of his strength,
uprooted the world, and even <s>Kailāsa</s> was crushed by him.

children.text: tatra mayā kṣaṇaṃ dhyātvā dṛṣṭvā tanmāyayā kṛtam
children.translated_text: There, after meditating for a moment and seeing that this had been done by his magic,

children.text: jāritaṃ pannage sūtaṃ samāṃśaṃ śilayā hatam ||
children.translated_text: I used <s>sūta</s> (mercury) digested in <s>pannaga</s> (lead), struck with an equal part of <s>śilā</s> (realgar).
With that mercury the trident was smeared, O <s>Himaśailajā</s>,
and with that spear the demon, proud of his strength, was slain.

children.text: hema śulvaṃ tathā tīkṣṇaṃ vājaraṃ paḍālakam
children.translated_text: Gold, copper, likewise sharp iron, <s>vājara</s>, and <s>paḍālaka</s>,
<s>rohaṇa</s> and magnetic iron should be digested according to the count of the principles.
This king of <s>rasa</s> (mercury), fixed in each single one, brings about the state of moving through the sky.

children.text: gandhanāge drute devi jāraṇāṃ sukarāṃ śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: In molten <s>gandhanāga</s>, O <s>Devi</s>, hear an easy digestion procedure.
First, purified mercury, mixed with powder of <s>rajanī</s> (turmeric),
should be ground until it becomes black, then washed with hot sour gruel.
When rubbed again and again in this way, <s>gandhanāga</s> undergoes melting.

children.text: nāgasya mūtre deveśi vatsasya mahiṣasya vā
children.translated_text: In the urine of an elephant, O <s>Deveśi</s>, or of a calf or buffalo,
one should heat and reheat the <s>bhujaga</s> (lead) and quench it seven times.
Having made its sheets pierceable by thorns, O <s>Sundarī</s>,
one should add sulfur in the measure of one quarter.
One should spread a layer of lac, and then hair after that,

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ gandhakacūrṇaṃ ca tato nāgadalaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: with powdered sulfur above, and then a sheet of lead in the same way.
Sulfur, human hair, and a layer of lac should be set out above in sequence,

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ prasārya saṃsthāpya sūtrairvartiṃ tu kārayet ||
children.translated_text: spread and arranged, and one should make it into a wick with threads.
It should be placed in karanja oil for ten nights,

children.text: dīptāgrabhāgāṃ tāṃ vartiṃ saṃḍaśyā tu vidhārayet ||
children.translated_text: and that wick, with its tip lit, should be held with tongs.
One should make that melt fall into a vessel containing <s>sauvīra</s> and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax).

children.text: kācakūpyāśca madhye tu tattailaṃ sthāpayet priye ||
children.translated_text: In the middle of a glass bottle, O beloved, one should place that oil.
Putting the mercury in a cow-teat crucible smeared with <s>śilā</s>,
in portions beginning with one sixty-fourth, O <s>Devi</s>, one should judge its strength and weakness.
Having added the melt of <s>gandhanāga</s> to that crucible, O one honored by the gods,
one should place it in a pit filled with cow dung and cook it by the closed-heating method.
One should apply two handful-measures of dung and husks.
If there is a suspicion that it is undigested, then of the juice of <s>siṃhavallī</s>
one should add four drops in the closed heating, as before; this should be done each day.
By a threefold digestion the mercury becomes like the fruit of the rose-apple.
The essence of <s>mākṣika</s>, little by little, combined with dead lead,
should remain in the crucible until, with glass placed below and above,
it has been well blown in this way twelve times and becomes colored.
Seed-powder cooked by that, in a quarter part in mercury,
when ground with sour chickpea liquid, becomes a womb-melt in an instant.
If the womb-melt does not occur, O <s>Devi</s>, then from two colorants and sulfur,
from red <s>sindhu</s>, <s>alarka</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, and <s>āśugapuṅkha</s>,

children.text: kalkena liptaṃ puṭitaṃ bījaṃ garbhe drutaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: the seed, smeared with a paste and calcined, becomes molten in the womb.

children.text: bīje pādārdhatulyāṃśe jīrṇe vedhaṃ karoti saḥ
children.translated_text: When the seed, in a quarter or half-equal portion, has been digested, it performs penetration,
successively in a tenth, sixteenth, and twenty-second part.
Combining a threefold <s>rīti</s> (brass alloy) with silver, together with residues of silver,

children.text: tārāriṣṭam idaṃ liptvā tena sūtena vedhayet ||
children.translated_text: one should smear on this silver preparation and penetrate it with that mercury.

children.text: ataḥ paraṃ tu saṃskāraṃ vakṣye nāgābhrajāraṇam
children.translated_text: After this I shall explain the next operation, the digestion of lead and mica.
Having powdered <s>manaḥśilā</s> red as oleander, O <s>Devi</s>,
one should impregnate it twenty times with the juice of barley-tamarind.
With that paste one should carefully smear a sheet of lead,
and cook it with a karṣa-fire until it becomes powdered.

children.text: rasakasya ca bhāgāṃs trīn bhāgaikaṃ daradasya ca
children.translated_text: One should grind three parts of <s>rasaka</s> and one part of <s>darada</s>
with citron, together with a quarter part sulfur and <s>śilāviṣa</s>.
When it is cooked by closed heating in a crucible smeared with this paste,
one should blow that lead in this way seven times; it becomes like gold.

children.text: pītābhrakaṃ tv ekadalaṃ liptāyāṃ maricena tu
children.translated_text: A single sheet of yellow mica, smeared with pepper,
should be blown in a crucible until it is fire-colored, then thrown into the juice of <s>saubhāñjana</s>.
One should extract its essence by the former method; that essence shines like gold.
A sheet of colored lead and the essence of yellow mica,
with women’s milk, soot from glass, <s>guñjā</s>, lodestone, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,
combined with <s>tuttha</s>, becomes this paired compound of lead and mica.
With stalk of <s>kiṃvāra</s>, mustard, soot, brick, and jaggery,
one should grind the mercury for three days and steam it in a swing apparatus for three days.
Mixed with a paste of <s>punarnavā</s>, <s>meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, and <s>sarpākṣī</s>,
and then with <s>āsurī</s>, <s>sindhuviṣa</s>, and peppers thoroughly ground,
one should again steam it in the swing apparatus for three days.
Having made it consume <s>nāgābhra</s> in an eighth part, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>,
there should be two parts of <s>śilā</s> and one part of <s>sindhu</s> and <s>sauvarcala</s>.
There should be half as much <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> and a quarter part poison; the flux is one eighth of the lump.

children.text: tridine kacchape jāryamevaṃ jāryaṃ tu ṣaḍguṇam ||
children.translated_text: It is to be digested for three days in the tortoise apparatus; thus it should be digested sixfold.
Rock-mineral, <s>tuttha</s>, lead, copper, sharp iron, <s>ghoṣāra</s>, and gold:
this <s>tuttha</s> is increased in sequence through the deposition of the essence of <s>tāpya</s>.
That seed, with gold remaining, in a quarter part, with citron water,
one should feed to the king of <s>rasa</s> and digest it with gold-containing substances.
With <s>tāpya</s>, <s>sauvarcala</s>, <s>śilā</s>, sulfur, <s>kāsīsa</s>, and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,
having placed it in the lotus apparatus and inserted a plug, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>,
one should blow it gently for three days, until the seed becomes molten.

children.text: tameva samajīrṇaṃ tu vahnau niṣkampanaṃ rasam ||
children.translated_text: That very mercury, evenly digested and unmoving in the fire...
Then, by means of the sixfold seed, <s>sāraṇā</s> should be performed according to the proper sequence;
it should penetrate silver, <s>ariṣṭa</s>, lead, and copper with a thousandth part.
Poison, sulfur, <s>tāpya</s>, mica, crow-dung, and <s>ghanadhvani</s>,
with a paste of <s>sahadevī</s> and <s>vahniśikhā</s>, make the mercury advance step by step.
Swooned mercury, dead mercury, and the leech-binding,
the fourth is the embodied binding, and the fifth is the sheet-binding;
ash-mercury and <s>khoṭa</s>: through processing, mercury is sevenfold.
When the <s>sūta</s> becomes lead-colored, abandoning dense mobility,

children.text: lakṣaṇaṃ dṛśyate yasya mūrchitaṃ taṃ vadanti hi ||
children.translated_text: and when this sign is seen in it, they call that mercury swooned.
Moistness, density, brilliance, heaviness, and mobility:
when these are not seen in it, one should know it as dead mercury.

children.text: nānāvarṇaṃ tathā svacchaṃ drutaṃ yonau jalūkavat
children.translated_text: When mercury, multicolored, clear, and melted, in the matrix like a leech,
is bound, that is the characteristic of the leech-binding of mercury.
Heaviness and redness, with brilliance like the sun,
and remaining when held in the midst of fire: this is the sign of embodied binding.
Or embodied binding is accepted when it has been digested by means of a rod.

children.text: śvetaṃ pītaṃ guru tathā mṛdu sikthakasaṃnibham
children.translated_text: White, yellow, heavy, and also soft, resembling wax:
when it remains in the midst of fire, this is the sign of sheet-binding.

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ śvetaṃ tathā pītaṃ nīlaṃ bhasmanibhaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Black, white, yellow, blue, and also resembling ash:
when mobility has disappeared, this is the sign of ash-mercury.
When the mercury is like a hen's egg and also breaks salt,
and the <s>rasa</s> turns in that way, this is the sign of <s>khoṭaka</s>.

children.text: athavā chedane snigdhaṃ raśminā mṛdunā dravet
children.translated_text: Or, when on being cut it is unctuous and melts with a soft ray,
imperishable, hard, and white: this is the sign of <s>khoṭa</s>-binding.
But the five beginning with <s>khoṭa</s>, apart from the leech-form,

children.text: haṭhāgnau dhāmitāḥ santi na tiṣṭhatyeva mūrchitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: remain when blown in forced fire; the swooned form alone does not remain.
Like the newly risen sun, multicolored, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>,
the colored <s>Rasabhairava</s> penetrates bodies and metals.
First comes the purification of mercury; after that, the measure of its food;
then the digestion of mica-essence and the digestion of every essence;
afterward internal and external liquefaction, and the digestion of gold;
then the sealed heating with divine herbs, and after that the jewel-binding;

children.text: rañjanaṃ ca tato devi jāraṇā cānusāraṇā
children.translated_text: then coloring, O <s>Devi</s>, and digestion together with <s>anusāraṇā</s>;

children.text: krāmaṇaṃ ca tato deyaṃ sūtakasya vicakṣaṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: after that <s>krāmaṇa</s> is to be applied to mercury by the discerning.

children.text: evaṃ kramaṃ tu yo vetti tasya siddhirna saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One who knows this sequence obtains success; there is no doubt.

children.text: vedhakaṃ yastu jānāti dehe lohe rasāyane
children.translated_text: Whoever knows the penetrating agent in body, metal, and <s>rasāyana</s>,

children.text: tasya janma jarā vyādhirnaśyatyeva na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for him birth, old age, and disease are destroyed; there is no doubt.

children.text: dehe tu pañcaratnāni nāgaṃ vaṅgaṃ tathāyasam
children.translated_text: For the body there are the five jewels, lead, tin, and also iron;
the <s>krāmaṇa</s> of the king of mercury is the medicine that destroys disease.
The <s>sūta</s> advances through medicines by the sequence of the power of the formula;
it advances against masses of disease and devours the corrupt illness.

children.text: tasya tu krāmaṇaṃ jñātvā tato vaidyairupācaret
children.translated_text: After knowing its <s>krāmaṇa</s>, physicians should then treat with it.

children.text: krāmaṇena vinā sūto na kramet na ca vedhayet
children.translated_text: Without <s>krāmaṇa</s>, mercury does not advance and does not penetrate

children.text: dehalohāmayān sarvān vṛthā syāt kevalaṃ śramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: all bodily and metallic diseases; mere labor would be in vain.

children.text: yasya rogasya yo yogastenaiva saha yojayet
children.translated_text: The formula appropriate to whatever disease there is should be joined with that very disease;
<s>Rasendra</s> removes the diseases of men, elephants, and horses.
<s>Āroṭa</s> imparts strength; the swooned form destroys disease;
by the bound form there is <s>khecarī</s>-siddhi, and by the killed form one becomes ageless and deathless.
It is especially disease-pacifying when swooned with sulfur;

children.text: oṣadhyā ghātitaḥ sūto yathā bhūyo na jīvati ||
children.translated_text: mercury killed by an herb does not come back to life again.

children.text: sa hi krāmati loheṣu tena kuryādrasāyanam
children.translated_text: For it advances among metals; by means of it one should make a <s>rasāyana</s>.
Tell me, O <s>Deveśī</s>, what else do you wish to hear?
The blessed <s>Devī</s> said:
What sort of auspicious herb, O lord, produces swooning of the <s>rasa</s>?

children.text: kena vā bhasmasūtaḥ syāt kena vā khoṭabandhanam ||
children.translated_text: By what does ash-mercury arise, and by what does <s>khoṭa</s>-binding arise?
The blessed <s>Bhairava</s> said:
Listen carefully, O <s>Bhairavī</s>, to the secret binding of mercury,
not known even by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Surendra</s>, and the rest, O you who are honored by heroes.
Between the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the <s>Yamunā</s> there is a <s>rākṣasa</s> named <s>Prayoga</s>;
near it, O fair-hipped one, mercury is bound in an instant.
The best practitioner should take the leaves of the night-roamer,

children.text: adho niṣpīḍitaṃ devi raso bhavati cottamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: pressed downward, O <s>Devi</s>; the <s>rasa</s> becomes excellent.

children.text: rasaṃ saṃmardya tenaiva dināni trīṇi vārttikaḥ
children.translated_text: Having triturated the mercury with that for three days, the technician

children.text: āroṭaṃ bandhayet kṣipraṃ gaganaṃ tatra jārayet ||
children.translated_text: should quickly bind <s>āroṭa</s>; he should digest mica there.
With that very leaf-juice he should again process the mica;
impregnated seven times with it, together in one mass with the three pungents,

children.text: yantre vidyādhare devi gaganaṃ tatra jārayet ||
children.translated_text: in the <s>vidyādhara</s> apparatus, O <s>Devi</s>, he should digest the mica there.

children.text: māsamātreṇa deveśi jīryate tat samaṃ same
children.translated_text: In just a month, O <s>Deveśī</s>, it is digested, equal with equal;
when it is equally digested in the mercury, O <s>Devi</s>, the <s>rasa</s> becomes hundred-penetrating.
Then, O <s>Devi</s>, he should impregnate sulfur in the juice of the night-roamer;

children.text: bhāvayet saptavāraṃ tu dvipadyāśca rasena tu ||
children.translated_text: he should impregnate it seven times with the juice of <s>dvipadī</s> too.
With a leaf-coating of silver, and with excellent gold half and half,
when the sulfur has been equally digested in this, the <s>rasa</s> becomes hundred-penetrating.

children.text: punastaṃ gandhakaṃ dattvā pattralepe raviṃ haret
children.translated_text: Again, having given that sulfur, he should remove the copper with the leaf-coating;

children.text: taṃ raviṃ tāramadhye tu triguṇaṃ vāhayettataḥ ||
children.translated_text: then he should carry that copper threefold into the silver.
Gold, joined with half as much gold, reaches equality with the matrix;
again, melting that sulfur directly, he should make it molten.
He should triturate <s>Rasendra</s> with it and make it lose its body.
By merely applying that very paste, O beloved, the eighteen kinds of <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin disease)
and piles, fistula-in-ano, spider-poison, and diseases of the head are destroyed.
<s>Tālaka</s> should be impregnated seven times in the juice of <s>niśācara</s>.

children.text: tenaiva ghātayedvaṅgaṃ vaṅgaṃ tāre tu nirvahet ||
children.translated_text: With that very substance one should kill tin, and the tin should be carried through in silver.

children.text: taṃ tāraṃ jārayet sūte tatsūtaṃ bandhanaṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: One should digest that silver in mercury; that mercury will proceed to fixation.
By merely applying it, it becomes the sixty-fourth part.
In the sixty-fourth part, one should cause penetration of copper.

children.text: śulvaṃ tu dāpayettāre tattāraṃ kāñcanaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: One should apply the copper to silver; that silver becomes gold.
That silver becomes excellent, granting <s>dharma</s>, desire, wealth, and liberation.
One should make the flowers of <s>niśācara</s> into a fine powder.
Ten <s>palas</s> of the powder should be impregnated with the juices of <s>dhātrī</s>.
Having stirred it with ghee and honey, one should place it in a new vessel.
It should be deposited in a heap of grain for three weeks, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>.
By merely eating it, one becomes free from wrinkles and gray hair.

children.text: valkalaṃ sūkṣmacūrṇaṃ tu madhunā sahitaṃ lihet
children.translated_text: One should lick the fine powder of the bark together with honey.
By using it for half a month, this becomes directly effective, O beloved.
By his urine and feces, copper becomes gold.
By using it for only a month, <s>pannaga</s> becomes gold.
Or one should take the oil of that fruit in the apparatus called <s>pātāla</s>.

children.text: tena tailena deveśi rasaṃ saṃkocayed budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With that oil, O <s>Deveśi</s>, the wise man should contract mercury.
At that very moment, O <s>Devi</s>, the great <s>rasa</s> becomes bound into a pellet.
A pungent ring should be made on the mercury-linga, O fair-faced one.
Having contracted it, one should perform killing with it, a most wondrous operation.
Copper should be placed seven times in the juice of <s>niśācara</s>.
By that means, free from blackness, it becomes gold-colored.

children.text: tattāreṇa samaṃ vāhyaṃ tena siktaṃ tu vāpitam
children.translated_text: It should be combined with an equal amount of that silver; when sprinkled and sown with that,

children.text: daśāṃśaṃ vedhayet sūtaṃ daśa pītaṃ śatena ca ||
children.translated_text: it penetrates mercury by a tenth part; with ten parts it becomes yellow, and with a hundred
it penetrates a hundred, a lakh, a thousand, and a crore.

children.text: daśāṃśaṃ koṭivedhi syāt koṭivedhi samena ca ||
children.translated_text: With a tenth part it becomes crore-penetrating, and with an equal part it is crore-penetrating.
Again I shall explain another very rare binding of mercury.
There is a herb, the mother of the three worlds, without a female companion.
By mere contact with it, mercury stands fixed.
When it has been triturated for seven days with the juice of that great herb,
by penetration with only a hundredth part it makes divine gold.
By trituration in its juice for two weeks, O beautiful one,
the mercury is visibly lakh-penetrating, and turns the eight metals into gold.
In three weeks, O <s>Deveśi</s>, it penetrates ten lakhs.
And in the fourth week the great <s>rasa</s> becomes crore-penetrating.
Sweated, heated, and rubbed with the juice of the great herb,
he gains the <s>khecarī</s> siddhi, moving in an unrestricted sphere.
Within a day he may enjoy a thousand desirable women.

children.text: naṣṭacchāyo hy adṛśyaśca trailokyaṃ ca bhramedrasaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having lost his shadow and become invisible, he roams the three worlds by means of the elixirs.
By the very juice of the great herb, reviving the dead becomes possible.

children.text: anena ghātayet sūtaṃ pañcāvasthaṃ kuru priye ||
children.translated_text: With this one should kill mercury; make it into five states, O beloved.
One should administer it as nasal medicine to the dead person and rub the hands and feet.
Then life enters him, even though he is dead, O fair-faced one.
Again I shall explain another very rare binding of mercury.
By the juice of <s>narasāra</s> alone, mercury is fixed in an instant.
Having added the juice of <s>narasāra</s> together with the dust of the two-footed woman,
by the end of the day it comes to fixation and tinges all metals.
When sixfold <s>pannaga</s> has been digested by the juice of <s>narasāra</s>,

children.text: tāre tāmre'pi vā devi bhāvayettaṃ manaḥśilām ||
children.translated_text: in silver or even copper, O <s>Devi</s>, one should impregnate that <s>manaḥśilā</s>.
It becomes odorless, and it kills that elixir.
Together with the dust of the two-footed woman, <s>pannaga</s> becomes without metallic essence.
When sixfold <s>pannaga</s> has been digested by the juice of <s>narasāra</s>,

children.text: tāre tāmre'pi vā devi koṭivedhī bhavedrasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in silver or even copper, O <s>Devi</s>, the mercury becomes crore-penetrating.
In the milk joined with the juice of <s>narasāra</s>, seven separate impregnations are to be made.
One should make <s>Rasendra</s> take a morsel in the apparatus called <s>Vidyādhara</s>.

children.text: jīryate gaganaṃ devi nirmukhaṃ ca varānane
children.translated_text: Mica is digested, O <s>Devi</s>, without an opening, O fair-faced one.
With the juice of <s>narasāra</s> alone and with the juice of <s>kīṭamārī</s>,

children.text: drāvayedgaganaṃ devi tīkṣṇaṃ lohaṃ ca pannagam ||
children.translated_text: one should melt mica, O <s>Devi</s>, as well as sharp iron and <s>pannaga</s>.
With the juice of <s>narasāra</s> alone and with the juice of <s>Hanūmatī</s>,
divine gold is produced by sprinkling, O beloved of the sun.
Having added madder and red sandalwood to the juice of <s>narasāra</s>,

children.text: svarase mardayet paścāt pannagaṃ devi secayet ||
children.translated_text: one should afterwards triturate it in its own juice and sprinkle <s>pannaga</s>, O <s>Devi</s>.
At that instant divine gold is produced, when it has been sprinkled seven times.

children.text: ravighṛṣṭaṃ tu taṃ devi pannagaṃ triguṇaṃ priye ||
children.translated_text: Then, O <s>Devi</s>, rub that threefold <s>pannaga</s> with the sun, O beloved.
That copper, having the appearance of gold and joined with a fifth part of silver,
and gold joined with an eighth part, is the reagent for making gold.
Cinnabar should be impregnated seven times in the juice of <s>narasāra</s>.
With that very substance one should kill sharp iron and declare that it has become ash.

children.text: tadbhasma tāmrapiṣṭaṃ tu triguṇaṃ tena nirvahet ||
children.translated_text: That ash, made into a paste with copper, should be carried through with three times that amount.
That copper, having the appearance of gold and joined with an eighth part of silver,

children.text: tārahema samāṃśaṃ tu dviguṇaṃ pittalaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: with equal parts of silver and gold, becomes twice as much brass.
<s>Rasaka</s> should be impregnated seven times in the juice of <s>narasāra</s>.

children.text: taṃ rasaṃ rasakaṃ caiva tīkṣṇaṃ lohaṃ ca pannagam
children.translated_text: That mercury and <s>rasaka</s>, sharp iron, and <s>pannaga</s>,
should be triturated together with the juice of <s>narasāra</s> alone, with that very substance.
At that instant the fixation of both mercury and <s>rasaka</s> takes place.

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ nāgaṃ tathā śulvaṃ rasakena tu rañjayet
children.translated_text: One should color tīkṣṇa iron, lead, and likewise copper with rasaka;
the whole becomes gold, shining like a pumpkin flower.
Again I shall explain another very rare binding of <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
There is an herb named <s>Kaṅkālakhecarī</s>, O supreme goddess.
Having collected its oil, together with <s>Māghakhecarī</s>,
one should steep it for one day in a vessel made of solar metal.

children.text: dvitīye vāsare prāpte vajraratnaṃ tu ghātayet
children.translated_text: When the second day has arrived, one should strike the diamond jewel,
and blow it in the fire until it is like blazing, well-heated flame.
One should quench the diamond jewel in the oil of <s>Kaṅkālakhecarī</s>;

children.text: daśavāraṃ niṣiktaṃ tu bhasmākāraṃ hi jāyate ||
children.translated_text: when it has been quenched ten times, it indeed becomes ash-like.
Take that gold-ripened seed and make it equal in ash with that;
having added three parts borax and put it into a sealed crucible, one should blow it.
At that very moment the pair, the diamond jewel and gold, combines.
O fair-hipped one, if it digests silver and gold equally,

children.text: koṭivedhī raso devi lohānyaṣṭau ca vidhyati ||
children.translated_text: the <s>rasa</s>, O goddess, penetrates ten millionfold and pierces the eight metals.
Again I shall explain another very rare binding of <s>rasa</s> (mercury).

children.text: sabījā cauṣadhī grāhyā kācid gulmalatā priye
children.translated_text: A certain shrub-creeper herb with seed is to be taken, O beloved;
the second, O goddess, is the khecarī named <s>Mantrasiṃhāsanī</s>.
In a subterranean apparatus one should collect its oil in a copper vessel.

children.text: tasya tailasya madhye tu prakṣipet khecarīrasam
children.translated_text: Into the midst of that oil one should cast the sap of khecarī,
and place it inside the earth-apparatus, O lovely-faced one.
By the former herb, O goddess, mica is brought down upon the earth;
then, having given it a morsel of mercury, make a ball by grinding.

children.text: baddhvā poṭalikāṃ tena gaganaṃ tena jārayate
children.translated_text: Having bound it into a packet, one digests mica with it;

children.text: same tu gagane jīrṇe baddhastiṣṭhati sūtakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: when an equal amount of mica has been digested, the mercury remains bound.
When it is blown with a bellows and heated, it is destroyed,
and the form of what is equally digested becomes like crow-droppings.

children.text: dviguṇe gagane jīrṇe aṣṭau lohāni saṃharet ||
children.translated_text: When twice as much mica has been digested, it subdues the eight metals.
Again I shall explain another very rare binding of <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
There is an herb called <s>Turasiṃhanī</s>, arisen from the body of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: jārayedgandhakaṃ sā tu jārayet sāpi tālakam ||
children.translated_text: It digests sulfur, and it also digests orpiment.

children.text: kāñcanaṃ jārayet sāpi rasendraṃ sā ca baddhayet
children.translated_text: It also digests gold, and it binds <s>rasendra</s> (lord mercury).

children.text: pravālaṃ jārayet sā tu gaganaṃ drāvayet tathā
children.translated_text: It digests coral and likewise liquefies mica.

children.text: vajraṃ ca ghātayet sā tu sarvasattvaṃ ca pātayet ||
children.translated_text: It also strikes diamond and precipitates every metallic essence.
It digests all metals and also cooks their essences.
Having placed it in <s>Harīṃdarī</s> sap, in a cow's horn, O lovely-faced one,
it should be deposited in a heap of grain; the mercury remains dead there.
By the very sap of a divine herb, O worshiped by the gods, <s>rasendra</s>

children.text: same tu kanake jīrṇe daśakoṭīstu vedhayet ||
children.translated_text: when digested with an equal amount of gold, penetrates ten crores.
At the fifth stage it reaches a lakh of crores; at the sixth it becomes a touch-transmuter.

children.text: saptame dhūmavedhī syāt aṣṭame tv avalokataḥ
children.translated_text: At the seventh it becomes a smoke-transmuter; at the eighth, one that works by sight.

children.text: navame śabdavedhī syādata ūrdhvaṃ na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: At the ninth it becomes a sound-transmuter; beyond that there is nothing.
Foolish beasts wander about, bereft of the family herb.
From the saps of common grass-herbs no accomplishment at all arises.
Therefore by every effort the family herb must be known.
Sixty-four divine herbs are established within the family tradition;
those fools do not know them, deluded by the delusion of the gods.
The non-divine grass-herbs grow in mountain caves.

children.text: tṛṇauṣadhyā rase sūtaṃ naiva baddhaṃ kadācana
children.translated_text: Mercury is never bound by the sap of a grass-herb,

children.text: akṣayaṃ ca varārohe vahnimadhye na tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: and, O fair-hipped one, it is imperishable and does not stay in the midst of fire.

children.text: na khoṭo naiva vāhastu naiva dravyaṃ karoti saḥ
children.translated_text: It makes neither a khoṭa nor a vāha, nor does it make the substance;

children.text: kiṃ tat dravyaṃ prakurvīta dhāmyamāno na tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: what substance could it make, when it does not remain while being blown?

children.text: pattre pāke kaṭe chede naiva tiṣṭhati kāñcane
children.translated_text: In leafing, cooking, assay, and cutting it does not remain in gold,

children.text: na vedhaṃ ca śatād ūrdhvaṃ karoti sa rasaḥ priye ||
children.translated_text: and that <s>rasa</s>, O beloved, does not make penetration beyond a hundredfold.

children.text: yāvanna baddhamekaṃ tu vikrītaṃ tattu kāñcanam
children.translated_text: As long as one thing is not bound, that gold is as good as sold away;
for the sake of <s>dharma</s>, wealth, desire, and liberation, O beloved, one should not give it.
The blessed <s>Devi</s> said:

children.text: nirjīvatvaṃ gataḥ sūtaḥ kathaṃ jīvaṃ dadāti ca
children.translated_text: When mercury has become lifeless, how can it give life?

children.text: nirjīvena tu nirjīvaḥ kathaṃ jīvati śaṃkara ||
children.translated_text: How can the lifeless live by means of what is lifeless, O <s>Śaṃkara</s>?
The blessed <s>Bhairava</s> said:

children.text: divyauṣadhyā yadā devi rasendro mūrchito bhavet
children.translated_text: When, O goddess, <s>rasendra</s> is made swooned by a divine herb,
then, O <s>Pārvatī</s>, mercury becomes devoid of kālikā.
The <s>rasa</s> without kālikā takes away another's time of death,

children.text: aṣṭānāṃ caiva lohānāṃ malaṃ śamayati kṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: and instantly quiets the impurity of the eight metals.
Who, then, would call mercury that has entered great swooning dead?
By the very sap of a divine herb it becomes one whose consciousness is lost.
Mercury, consisting of the five elements, always remains <s>Sadāśiva</s> himself.
Again I shall explain the binding of <s>rasa</s>, O mistress.
Diamond killed by kṣmāpāla, and gold by this very means,
diamond ash and gold ash: one should bind these together in one place.
It is to be digested in the sap of <s>Niśācara</s>; one should digest it with <s>Narajīva</s>.
The divine elephant-enemy herb, O gracious one, should kill that mercury.

children.text: bhakṣitaḥ sa raso yena so 'pi sākṣāt sadāśivaḥ
children.translated_text: He by whom that <s>rasa</s> has been eaten is himself directly <s>Sadāśiva</s>.
When one tolaka has been eaten, the man becomes a touch-transmuter.
From the sweat of his body, even the king of <s>rasa</s> is made penetrating;
from the sweat, and even by his urine, the eight metals become gold.
That supreme practitioner lives for hundreds of thousands of lakhs of years;
the dark-radiant <s>Prajāpati</s> binds mercury in an instant.
By contact with <s>gajāri</s>, O <s>Devi</s>, and with <s>kṣmāpāla</s>, it is bound.
Mica, dear one, processed with the juice of <s>vajravallī</s>,
should be digested in a sand-apparatus; it becomes a <s>khoṭa</s> at once.
One <s>māṣa</s> of a killed pellet and one <s>māṣa</s> of a gold pellet
should be combined and then triturated with citron acid for three days.
One <s>karṣa</s> of lead sheets should be coated with the mercury paste.
Then one should wrap that lump with <s>vṛścikālī</s> and coat it.
One should kill the lead, O <s>Devi</s>; it becomes like an <s>indragopa</s> insect.
One <s>karṣa</s> of silver sheets should be coated with killed lead.
Then that coated sheet should be wrapped with <s>vṛścikālī</s>.
That silver dies, O <s>Devi</s>, becoming like vermilion-red color.
With that very substance, in a thousandth part, one should cause penetration of copper.
Divine gold is produced, fit to adorn the ornaments of the gods.
It has latex, many fruits, and knots, O <s>Pārvatī</s>;
called <s>Caṭulaparṇī</s> by name, it is praised for binding mercury.
Mercury placed in a sealed crucible in the juice of the tuber of <s>ekavīrā</s>
should be blown with mouth-air; when bound, it is praised for consumption.
The tuber of <s>raktakañcukī</s>, ground with a woman's breast milk,
causes binding of mercury in the crucible by the previous procedure.
The seed of <s>vṛścikāpattrikā</s>, joined with woman's milk,
should be blown with mercury as before by the practitioner, for the sake of consumption.
Having taken the <s>vajrakanda</s>, one should place it in the midst of mercury.

children.text: gajendrākhyaṃ puṭaṃ dattvā saptadhā baddhatāṃ nayet ||
children.translated_text: Having given a heating called <s>gajendra</s>, one should bring it to boundness seven times.

children.text: bhakṣayet taṃ rasaṃ prājñaḥ ṣaṇmāsādamaro bhavet ||
children.translated_text: A wise man should consume that mercury; after six months he becomes deathless.
Having taken the tuber of <s>lāṅgalī</s> and also the tuber of <s>karkoṭī</s>,
one should place mercury inside them, steam it, and triturate it again.
It dies, there is no doubt, when blown with a fierce fire.
Mercury placed in <s>śukacañcu</s> should be heated in a sealed fire and then blown.
This makes penetration in a hundredth part and produces bodily accomplishment.
One should put mercury with the juice of <s>haṃsapādī</s> inside the tuber of <s>śūka</s>.
One should give a <s>gajendra</s>-heating; it dies, there is no doubt.

children.text: haṃsāṅghriṃ śukatuṇḍīṃ ca gṛhītvā mardayed rasam
children.translated_text: Taking <s>haṃsāṅghri</s> and <s>śukatuṇḍī</s>, one should triturate the mercury.
Having put it inside <s>krauñcapāda</s>, one should then give three heatings.
It dies, there is no doubt; the great mercury becomes hundred-thousand-penetrating.
Known as <s>tṛṇajyotis</s>, listen, dear one, to this divine herb:
it always blazes at night, O <s>Pārvatī</s>, but it does not blaze by day.

children.text: tasyā mūle tu nikṣiptaṃ kṣīraṃ raktaṃ bhavet priye ||
children.translated_text: Milk placed at its root becomes red, dear one.
With the juice of its root, sulfur, and mica, ground with citron acid,
a coated copper sheet becomes gold after three heatings.
The king of mercury, combined with the powder of its root, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>,
causes mica rubbed with citron juice to be consumed at once.
Now I shall teach <s>uccaṭī</s>, dear one, which binds mercury.

children.text: ekameva bhavennālaṃ tasya roma tu veṣṭanam ||
children.translated_text: It has just one stalk, and its hairs serve as the wrapping.

children.text: tasyāgre ca bhavet puṣpaṃ śukatuṇḍasya saṃnibham
children.translated_text: At its tip there is a flower resembling a parrot's beak.
Its leaves, O <s>Deveśī</s>, are like parrot feathers.
Its tuber has the form of <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and its latex is like vermilion.
A fluid like beeswax exudes; taking that, O <s>Pārvatī</s>,
one should penetrate all metals, and they become gold.
Mercury, orpiment, and copper sulfate should be triturated with the juices of <s>uccaṭī</s>.
Heated in the sun, the mercury dies through the power of the divine herb.
It should penetrate the seven metals with one hundred-thousandth part, O fair-faced one.
Now I shall explain the procedure of red <s>snuhī</s>, O beautiful goddess.
One should have a leaf-coating of copper made with the latex of <s>snuhī</s>.
One should heat it again with the latex seven times, O fair-faced one,
until, when melted repeatedly, it has the luster of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold.
After that one should cook it with sesame oil for three days.

children.text: tathā śulvasya pattrāṇi vedhyaṃ jāmbunadaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Then the sheets of copper, once penetrated, become <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold.
Mercury, red <s>snuhī</s> latex, <s>kunaṭī</s>, sulfur, mica,
and <s>darada</s> should penetrate metals with a thousandth part.
Having taken <s>snuhī</s> latex, <s>niśārdha</s>, gold, and both substances,
also <s>kunaṭī</s> and sulfur powder, one should triturate everything together.
By this very method one should purify <s>niśārdha</s> and gold.
Having made it into a pill, by that very substance it penetrates lead at once.
Now listen to the procedure of the divine herb <s>sthalapadminī</s>.
It is like a lotus in its leaves, and likewise in its flowers.

children.text: bhaṅge caiva bhavet kṣīraṃ raktavarṇaṃ suśobhanam ||
children.translated_text: When broken it has beautiful red-colored latex.
Stepping on it with the left foot, one should look at the vault of the sky.
One sees it furnished with stars, the circle of planets and lunar mansions.
From a hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>, O <s>Devi</s>, it is to be known as <s>sthalapadminī</s>.
Having taken its five parts, together with <s>Haragaurī</s>,
with realgar and orpiment, and together with pyrite,

children.text: mardayet saptarātraṃ tu tena śulvaṃ ca vedhayet
children.translated_text: one should triturate it for seven nights, and with it penetrate copper.
When penetrated with a thousandth part, O <s>Deveśī</s>, it becomes gold.
Having taken its five parts by the procedure stated before, dear one,
one should make the king of mercury consume them and blow it in a sealed crucible.
It dies within the crucible by contraction; there is no doubt.
With that very substance one should penetrate all metals with a thousandth part.
Now therefore, dear one, I shall fully explain the procedure of <s>kumudinī</s>.
Having split the <s>kāśmīri</s> stone, he should perform the operation on the full-moon day.
Taking its five parts, he should impregnate realgar.

children.text: kharpare dhārayitvā tu bhāvayettu punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Keeping it in a potsherd, he should impregnate it again and again.

children.text: kharpare drāvitaṃ nāgaṃ tatkalkena yutaṃ kuru
children.translated_text: Put lead melted in a potsherd together with that paste.
Gold is certainly produced, equal to the fluid of <s>kāśmīra</s>.
I shall tell briefly how <s>citraka</s> is to be gathered.
<s>Citraka</s> should be known as threefold: red and black for <s>rasāyana</s> (alchemy and rejuvenation),
and white for pacifying disease; they are superior, middling, and inferior.

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ raktaṃ sitaṃ vāpi hemante noddhared budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A wise man should not pull up black, red, or white <s>citraka</s> in the cold season.
Having uprooted black <s>citraka</s>, not smelled by cows, O <s>Īśvarī</s>,
milk placed in its midst becomes black in color at once.
With the powder of its five parts he should triturate mercury.
He should heat it by blowing in a sealed crucible; a <s>khoṭa</s> (solid pellet) is produced at once.
Having put on red garments, with red garlands and ointment,
on the fifth day of the dark fortnight, with cooked red <s>śāli</s> rice,
having given an offering, O <s>Mahādevi</s>, he should uproot the red <s>citraka</s>.
With powder of red <s>citraka</s>, tin, through three successive heatings,
freed from all defects, immediately comes to <s>stambha</s> (fixation).
With its root and <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury) in sour liquid, through the use of <s>kaṅguṇī</s> oil,
by twenty-one repetitions copper will become purified.
Smeared with oil of red <s>citraka</s> and <s>bhallāta</s> and heated with a <s>puṭa</s> (sealed firing),
the foils of moon and sun, O <s>Deveśi</s>, become beautiful gold.
<s>Nāginī</s> tuber and lordly <s>sūta</s> (mercury), joined with red <s>citraka</s>,
in the measure of a leaf-coating, make moon and sun into gold.
Mercury too, when joined with red <s>citraka</s>, becomes effective for every purpose.
I shall explain the procedure for <s>jyotiṣmatī</s> oil; listen, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.

children.text: jyotiṣmatī nāma latā yā ca kāñcanasaṃnibhā
children.translated_text: There is a vine named <s>jyotiṣmatī</s>, resembling gold,
with abundant spreading tendrils, auspicious, and with gold-colored fruit.
In the bright fortnight of <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, having taken the excellent seed,

children.text: tilavat kvāthayitvā tu hastaiḥ pādairathāpi vā
children.translated_text: and having boiled it like sesame, whether by hand or even by foot,

children.text: tasya tailaṃ samādāya kumbhe tāmramaye kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: he should collect its oil and place it in a copper pot.
He should heat the pot buried in the ground, gradually upward, with a chaff-fire.

children.text: ṣaṇmāse tu vyatikrānte sa ghaṭaḥ kāñcanaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: When six months have passed, that pot becomes gold.
Having made it golden, he should take the oil mixed with <s>mākṣika</s> (pyrite),

children.text: prativāpe niṣiñcet tat hema tāmrasamaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: and pour that in at each casting; the gold becomes equal to copper.
Thus it becomes hundred-penetrating, an unsurpassed jewel of knowledge.
I shall proclaim <s>dagdhārohā</s>, dear one, which effects the binding of mercury.
It should be known for contact-transmutation, accomplishing every desired purpose.

children.text: śastracchinnā mahādevi dagdhā vā pāvakena tu
children.translated_text: Cut by a knife, O <s>Mahādevi</s>, or burned by fire,
that divine great herb, burned or cut, sprouts again in an instant.

children.text: raktaṃ pītaṃ sitaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ tasyāḥ puṣpaṃ prajāyate
children.translated_text: Its flowers arise red, yellow, white, and black;
one should observe its well-grown leaves as being like those of chickpea.

children.text: sā sthitā gomatītīre gaṅgāyām arbude girau
children.translated_text: It grows on the bank of the <s>Gomatī</s>, on the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and on <s>Arbuda</s> mountain,
and it is seen south of <s>Ujjayinī</s> and in forest regions.
Its divine bulb-juice, marked with black streaks,

children.text: tāmbūlena samaṃ kṛtvā guṭikāṃ kārayed budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be made equal with betel, and the wise man should make a pill.
Of all metals melted in the midst of fire,

children.text: sahasraṃ vedhayitvā tu kāñcanaṃ kurute kṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: after penetrating a thousand, it makes gold in an instant.
Likewise <s>sūta</s> (mercury), joined with magnetite, gold, and mica, is killed,
and it makes divine gold, an ornament for the adornment of the gods.
Hear, O <s>Devi</s>, of the divine herb renowned as <s>kaṭutumbī</s>.
Having gathered its seeds, he should make them into a fine powder.
It should be impregnated twenty-one times with juice of <s>dhātrī</s>,
together with milk and combined with <s>viśvabheṣaja</s> (ginger).

children.text: bījaṃ yantre vinikṣipya tailaṃ saṃgṛhya paṇḍitaḥ
children.translated_text: Putting the seed in an apparatus and collecting the oil, the learned man
should make mercury swoon with it, triturating it with <s>cakramarda</s>.
Cow's bile and peacock's bile, joined with alum and green vitriol,
these are equal to silver, and mercury is equal to them all.
It should be placed in a ram's horn continuously for one month.
Applied with an iron rod, it penetrates all metals.
Sulfur, impregnated twenty-one times with an iron rod,
joined with this very metal and combined with citron juice,
together with seed and <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury), placed in a blind crucible,

children.text: bhūgataṃ māsamekaṃ tu tāraṃ kāñcanatāṃ nayet ||
children.translated_text: and buried in the ground for one month, brings silver to the state of gold.
One part of foil and five parts of silver,

children.text: śulvasya pañcabhāgaṃ ca bījasyaikaṃ ca yojayet ||
children.translated_text: five parts of copper and one part of seed should be combined.

children.text: ete dvādaśa bhāgāḥ syuḥ sarvaṃ taddhārayet kṣitau
children.translated_text: These become twelve parts; he should keep all that in the earth.

children.text: sthānasyāsya niṣekaṃ tu bhūdaṇḍena tu kārayet ||
children.translated_text: He should perform the sprinkling of this place with an earth-rod.
After twenty-five days, the finest gold is produced.
I shall explain the procedure for <s>kṣīrakanda</s>, the supreme means that grants all accomplishments.
It is of four colors there; the red tuber is praised.
When broken, this exudes milk, red in color and very beautiful.
Born with the rumbling of clouds and adorned with handsome
unctuous leaves like <s>snuhī</s>, seven in number, shining splendidly like gold,
it is a binding of the king of mercury, bringing all essences under control.

children.text: tasya kṣīraṃ tu saṃgṛhya tāraṃ nirvāpayed budhaḥ
children.translated_text: Having collected its milk, the wise man should quench silver.
And by a blazing fire that burns fiercely, beautiful gold is produced.
With exudations from tamarind leaves, mixed with a little copper powder,
the wise man should triturate mercury; binding of the <s>rasa</s> will occur.
When it is thrown into water, the pill becomes like a diamond.
O <s>Deveśi</s>, having pressed out the excellent sap of the śāka tree,
combined with red sandalwood, it digests all metals.
He should apply it to iron with the odor of sulfur-stone;
all metals unite and melt like water.
Sulfur, <s>rasaka</s>, <s>tāpya</s>, mercury, and red sandalwood,
joined with the sap of <s>rudantī</s>, make silver come to gold.

children.text: śākavṛkṣasya niryāsaṃ pattre tasya ca gālayet
children.translated_text: He should filter the exudation of the śāka tree through its leaf,
and he should triturate powder of the śigru root with that sap.
Having smeared copper leaves, placed them in a sealed heating, and cooked them,
that, when melted, becomes divine gold, furnished with the proper marks.
One should collect the fully ripened fruits of the śāka tree;

children.text: tadrasena yutaṃ prājñaḥ saptarātraṃ tu bhāvayet ||
children.translated_text: the wise man should moisten it with that sap for seven nights.
Joined with that sap and likewise mixed with madder,
he should smear silver leaves; when heated, it becomes gold.
Now I shall explain the further procedure for the great herb <s>devadālī</s>.

children.text: sā śvetā vyādhināśe ca kṛṣṇā pītā rasāyane ||
children.translated_text: Its white form is for destroying disease, while the black and yellow forms are for <s>rasāyana</s>.
On a full-moon day or on the thirteenth lunar day, when the sun is eclipsed by <s>Rāhu</s>,
or else on the fifth day of the dark fortnight, one should uproot this plant according to rule.
O <s>Devi</s>, <s>devadālī</s> fruit, <s>viṣṇukrāntā</s>, and mercury

children.text: mūrchayed bandhayet kṣipraṃ śulvaṃ hema karoti ca ||
children.translated_text: quickly swoon it and bind it, and it turns copper into gold.
<s>Devadālī</s> fruit and root, together with the sap of <s>īśvarī</s>,

children.text: toyena marditaṃ kṛtvā vaṅgaṃ stambhayati kṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: when triturated with water, fix tin at once.
After this, O beloved, I shall explain the procedure for white <s>guñjā</s>.
On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, or on the eighth day, O worshiped by the gods,

children.text: kapāle mṛttikāṃ nyasya secayet salilena tu ||
children.translated_text: one should place clay in a skull-bowl and sprinkle it with water.
He should sow the seeds of white <s>guñjā</s> with the proper flower-rite,
and should also perform the taking-up with the mantra about to be stated.

children.text: namo bhagavati śvetavalli śvetaparvatavāsini sarvakāryāṇi kuru kuru apratihate namo namaḥ svāhā
children.translated_text: Homage to the blessed white creeper, dweller on the white mountain; accomplish, accomplish all tasks, O unobstructed one; homage, homage, svāhā.
By this mantra, as taught, success comes about and not otherwise.
For six months one should guard the creeper, purified by mantra.

children.text: śuddhaśulvaṃ tu saṃgṛhya mūṣāmadhye tu saṃsthitam
children.translated_text: Having taken purified copper and placed it inside a crucible,
in the amount of fifteen palas, together with half a karṣa of white <s>guñjā</s>,
it becomes silver in a single mass, without its odor.
Together with <s>brahmarīti</s> and with <s>guñjā</s> powder in one place,

children.text: devānāṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ devi jāyate hema śobhanam ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Devi</s>, beautiful gold is produced, an ornament for the gods.
O <s>Deveśi</s>, I shall explain the binding of mercury by means of <s>candrodaka</s>.
On the full moon of the bright fortnight, when the full disk of the moon has been seen,
many kinds of moon-water break through the earth and emerge.
Some are clay-colored and salty in taste;
some are like the moon, and some shine like the sky.
They increase with the moon's waxing and diminish with its waning.
The mantra-knower should look for <s>candrodaka</s>, especially on the full-moon day;
it emerges, breaking through the earth, and increases with the moon's growth.
Having first enclosed the field and worshiped the god <s>Śaṃkara</s>,
the discerning man should worship that field on the fourteenth day,
remain fasting there for a day and night, and present an offering there.

children.text: pūrṇamāsyāṃ ca rātrau ca gatvā tasya samīpataḥ
children.translated_text: On the full-moon night, having gone near it,
he should collect the <s>candrodaka</s>, joined with mantra and well consecrated by mantra.
Having stirred it with honey and ghee, he should drink it with concentrated mind.
By the very act of drinking it, swooning occurs at that moment.

children.text: candrodaye tato dṛṣṭe kṣīraṃ tasya tu dāpayet
children.translated_text: Then, when moonrise is seen, milk should be given to him.
By using it for seven nights, he becomes stainless like the moon.
By twenty-one nights he lives for three days of <s>Brahmā</s>.
By using it for one month, the man comes to have the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: candrodakena gaganaṃ rasaṃ hema ca mardayet
children.translated_text: With <s>candrodaka</s> he should triturate mica, mercury, and gold.
Heated inside a crucible, it becomes a pill at once.

children.text: ayaṃ ca sparśamātreṇa lohānyaṣṭau ca vedhayet ||
children.translated_text: And this, by mere touch, penetrates the eight metals.
Mercury should be impregnated with that sap, evenly digested with diamond.
In a lump containing a sixty-fourth part, with twice as much, it becomes a thousandfold.
A man, having bound a guñjā-measure of mercury in ten chains,
and having placed it in his mouth, enclosed in the three metals, becomes invisible.

children.text: oṃ namo rudrāya daṃṣṭrotkaṭāya vighnanāśāya diśāṃ rakṣa rakṣa vidiśāṃ rakṣa rakṣa rudro vijñāpayati huṃ phaṭ svāhā
children.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to <s>Rudra</s>, terrible with fangs, destroyer of obstacles; protect, protect the directions; protect, protect the intermediate directions; <s>Rudra</s> makes this known: huṃ phaṭ svāhā.

children.text: oṃ namo bhagavate rudrāya triśūlahastāya amṛtodbhavāya rakṣa rakṣa phaṭ svāhā
children.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to the blessed <s>Rudra</s>, holding the trident, born from nectar; protect, protect; phaṭ svāhā.
Now therefore I shall fully explain the binding of <s>rasa</s> with the scissors-plant.
When the demons were joined in battle, with his mind filled with anger,
the great discus <s>Sudarśana</s> was hurled by the enemy of <s>Mura</s>.
Then from the plate of his forehead fell drops of sweat;

children.text: te bhūmau patitā divyāḥ saṃjātāḥ kartarīrasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: those divine drops, fallen on the earth, became <s>kartarīrasa</s>.

children.text: rakṣārthaṃ sthāpitaṃ tatra viṣṇunā ca sudarśanam
children.translated_text: For protection, <s>Viṣṇu</s> established <s>Sudarśana</s> there.
This spins like a discus and cuts down weapons.

children.text: kurute garjitaṃ nādaṃ dhūmaṃ jvālāṃ vimuñcati
children.translated_text: It makes a roaring sound and sends forth smoke and flame.
There is a <s>kartarī</s> (cutting power) by sight alone, and likewise another, the sound-<s>kartarī</s>.
That one is the touch-<s>kartarī</s>, the shadow-<s>kartarī</s>, and the smoke-<s>kartarī</s>.
And it is also the flame-<s>kartarī</s>, the <s>kartarī</s> of the terrible <s>śakti</s>.
For the welfare of beings, the terrible <s>śakti</s> has been established.
She is in the form of <s>rasa</s> (mercury), very terrible, and a cutter of those who are not accomplished.

children.text: tasyāḥ kṣetraṃ yadā gacchet aghorāstraṃ japettadā
children.translated_text: When one goes to her field, one should then recite the <s>Aghora</s> weapon.
Again he should install <s>Ghora</s> there; then the wise man should set down the weapon.
Forward and backward, having established the <s>kartarī</s> upon the body,
he should seal it with the mudrā, joined with the <s>Aghora</s> weapon.
He should worship her with a lamp and immobilize her with incense.
With the <s>viṣṭarā</s>-mudrā he should assign her connection with the place.

children.text: kañcukī tu śilā krāntā kumārī vajrakandakam
children.translated_text: <s>Kañcukī</s>, stone, <s>krāntā</s>, <s>kumārī</s>, and <s>vajrakandaka</s>,
women's blood, cow's urine: this tilaka brings all under control.
Now therefore I shall explain the binding of <s>rasa</s> by means of <s>viṣodara</s>.
<s>Viṣodaka</s> is equal to poison, and ghee-water is like ghee;
it is rich in colors such as white and yellow, and that, O <s>Devi</s>, is the best <s>rasa</s>.
Having gone there, to a region of forest, one should remember the thousand names of <s>Ghora</s>.

children.text: keśāḥ kṣiptāḥ sphuṭantyasmin ātmacchāyā na dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: Hairs thrown into it burst apart; one's own shadow is not seen.

children.text: tailaṃ ca golakākāraṃ ghṛtaṃ caiva visarpati
children.translated_text: Oil becomes globular there, and ghee spreads out.
It removes the odor of sulphur, and a salty-sour taste arises.
Having obtained it with a palāśa leaf, he should put it into a bitter gourd.

children.text: viṣodakaṃ gandhakaṃ ca harabījaṃ ca tatsamam ||
children.translated_text: He should add <s>viṣodaka</s>, sulphur, and <s>harabīja</s> in equal amount.
Having ground them with goat's milk, he should smear copper leaves.
By that heating, O <s>Deveśi</s>, it becomes like vermilion-red.
With only a hundredth part of it, O <s>Deveśi</s>, he should pierce all metals.

children.text: anena vidhinā devi nāgaḥ sindūratāṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: By this method, O <s>Devi</s>, lead becomes vermilion.
With a thousandth part of that very substance, he should make it give penetration to silver.
Red, yellow, and then black are successively effective for the intended work.
