Taking three palas in a magnetic vessel, or even in a vessel made of gourd,
he should wrap it outside with palāśa leaves, as before.
He should place it in a heap of grain for twenty-one days.
Then he should prepare one drop in buffalo's milk.
Whoever eats milk-rice combined with honey and ghee,
O <s>Devi</s>, lives according to the number of those drops, as long as there is a pala of powder.
<s>Lāṅgalī</s>, household soot, vermilion, the two kinds of turmeric,

children.text: meṣaśṛṅgīṃ ca śṛṅgīṃ ca kṛṣṇonmattaṃ ca mārakam
children.translated_text: <s>Meṣaśṛṅgī</s>, <s>śṛṅgī</s>, black <s>unmatta</s>, and <s>māraka</s>,
together with seed and mercury, should be triturated with poison-water.
The intelligent man should impregnate it seven times with poison-water.
Or else he should impregnate it until it becomes a powder.
With that, having added a sixteenth part to lead, success is obtained.
In the bamboo apparatus called a crucible, he should impregnate it even three times.
He should avoid its smoke, for it is extremely productive of disease in the limbs.
Then he should place the lead-vermilion in a vessel made of gourd.
With a hundredth part of that powder he should pierce silver leaves.
Having taken poison-water and a good paste made with barley-gruel,

children.text: niṣiktaṃ tacca varte 'yaṃ tāraṃ bhavati śobhanam ||
children.translated_text: when that is sprinkled, this becomes excellent silver.
Having taken poison-water, he should throw it into the best <s>rasa</s>.
<s>Kunaṭī</s>, sulphur-stone, poison, borax, and <s>lāṅgalī</s>
should be reduced to a lost paste in the mortar, and he should smear silver leaves with it.
Heated in a closed crucible, it becomes seedless gold.
Oṃ, to blessed <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s>: ṭha ṭhaḥ.
One should recite this ten thousand times.
I shall explain the procedure with poison-grass; listen with concentrated mind.
Fragrant pyrite and realgar, combined with the juice of <s>kunaṭī</s>,
mixed with poison-grass and triturated with citron acid:

children.text: etat kalkaṃ palamātraṃ cauṣadhyā lepanaṃ kuru
children.translated_text: make this paste, a pala in measure, as a coating with the plant.

children.text: niryāse tu puṭaṃ kuryāt trivāraṃ hema śobhanam ||
children.translated_text: He should perform three heatings in its exudation; the gold becomes excellent.
Now, O <s>Pārvatī</s>, I shall explain the procedure for the water of <s>Saṃjīvanī</s>.
O <s>Devi</s>, O you honored by the gods, in former times I was worshiped by <s>Śukra</s>,
for the welfare of the demons who had died in battle with the gods.
I gave the <s>Saṃjīvanī</s> science, having the form of water.

children.text: tayā saṃjīvitā daityā ye mṛtā devasaṃgare ||
children.translated_text: By it the Daityas who had died in battle with the gods were brought back to life.

children.text: nikṣiptā martyaloke sā samyak te kathayāmyaham ||
children.translated_text: It was deposited in the mortal world; I shall tell you about it correctly.
In the mortal world, in the southern country, there is a very holy and purifying

children.text: nadī godāvarī nāma prasiddhā jāhnavī yathā ||
children.translated_text: river named <s>Godāvarī</s>, renowned like the <s>Jāhnavī</s>.

children.text: dakṣiṇe ca taṭe tasyāḥ kadalīnagaraṃ param
children.translated_text: On its southern bank is the excellent city of <s>Kadalī</s>.
To its south is a mountain renowned in all the worlds.
It is seen, O all-auspicious one, by the name <s>Kṛṣṇagiri</s>.
Near it there is a village named <s>Suprasiddhāmbikā</s>.
There too, O you worshiped by the gods, the water should be examined after looking at it.
Having taken a dry bamboo, he should throw it into the middle of the water.
Within a day and night it certainly becomes green and glossy.
It sends forth sprouts and leaves, and appears delightful.
Then he should worship the goddess with offerings of bali and flowers,
and also the lord of the field, <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, and <s>Caṇḍayonīśvara</s>.

children.text: tasya mantraṃ pravakṣyāmi triṣu lokeṣu durlabham ||
children.translated_text: I shall explain his mantra, hard to obtain in the three worlds.

children.text: oṃ caṇḍāya pinākine śūlahastāya oṃ diśāṃ bandhaya vidiśāṃ bandhaya ṭhaṭhaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ, to <s>Caṇḍa</s>, to <s>Pinākin</s>, to the trident-bearer: oṃ, bind the directions, bind the intermediate directions, ṭha ṭhaḥ.
Sesame seeds, rice grains, and mustard seeds, with this very mantra,
the practitioner should make seven-times consecrated and cast into the directions.
With collected mind, having taken protected water in a bitter bottle-gourd vessel,
he should carefully take that and return to his own place.

children.text: oṃ namo'mṛte'mṛtarūpiṇi amṛtaṃ me kuru kuru evaṃ rudra ājñāpayati svāhā
children.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to the deathless one, whose form is nectar; make nectar for me, make it; thus <s>Rudra</s> commands. Svāhā.
Having made that water seven-times consecrated with this mantra,
then for one day he should triturate mercury together with two māṣas of gold
with that water; the discerning man should drink that.
Then, living on milk for twenty-one nights, with effort,
he lives for ten thousand kalpas and more, able to assume any form and very strong.
Having gone a hundred yojanas, he returns again;
invulnerable to all beings, moving at will, he is a sky-goer.

children.text: kanakaṃ pāradaṃ vyoma samam ekatra yojayet
children.translated_text: Gold, mercury, and vyoma (mica) should be combined together in equal measure.
He should triturate them with that water and then heat them seven times by steaming.

children.text: sa rasaḥ sarvalohāni ṣaṣṭyaṃśena tu vedhayet ||
children.translated_text: That rasa (mercurial elixir) penetrates all metals with only a sixtieth part.

children.text: athavā taṃ rasaṃ divyaṃ madhunā saha bhakṣayet
children.translated_text: Or else he should eat that divine rasa with honey.
By using it for just one month, he lives for ten thousand days of <s>Brahmā</s>.
By his urine, feces, and sweat, copper becomes gold.
In a windless place he should take water and drink three handfuls.
As soon as it is drunk, there is fainting; after three watches, well-being arises.
For just twenty-one days in this way he should then live on milk.
The wise man has the form of an eight-year-old, can assume any form, and is very strong.
He sees the whole earth, with all its openings, together with the seven pātālas.
He becomes invulnerable to gods and daityas, and has a lifespan of a kalpa.
Or else, having taken water, mercury, and manaḥśilā (realgar),
he should triturate them on a mortar-stone; then it becomes reduced to a fine paste.

children.text: svedayet saptarātraṃ tu trilohena ca veṣṭayet ||
children.translated_text: He should steam it for seven nights and wrap it in the three metals.
In an instant he becomes invisible and becomes lord of the vidyādharas,
surrounded by a hundred siddha maidens, for as long as fourteen kalpas.
On all those days he should provide boiled śāli rice and ghee,

children.text: payasā ca samāyuktaṃ nityamevaṃ tu kārayet ||
children.translated_text: mixed also with milk; he should make this a daily practice.
I shall teach the procedure for hot water; listen with attentive mind.
Wherever he sees hot water, he should establish his residence right there.
There is the very famous <s>Godāvarī</s> by name in <s>Mahārāṣṭra</s>;
on its northern side is <s>Sahyādri</s>, the holy mountain.
There is a famous shrine named <s>Mātāpura</s>;
north of that, O <s>Devī</s>, is the excellent city called <s>Kampā</s>.
There is the god <s>Kampeśvara</s>, and there hot water certainly exists.

children.text: praṇītākhyā nadī tatra snātvā vai sādhakottamaḥ
children.translated_text: There is a river named <s>Praṇītā</s>; after bathing there, the best practitioner
should afterward perform the rite in the hot-water pool as it has been stated.
Having stayed there for the night, he becomes wealthy day by day.
If he consumes it for merely a month, he lives eight hundred years.
If he uses it for one year, he lives ten thousand years, happy,
free from wrinkles and gray hair, and an enjoyer like <s>Purandara</s>.
If he drinks the water for one year, he lives as long as the moon, sun, and stars.
By his urine and feces, copper becomes gold.
Hot water together with kāsīsa (green vitriol) and gandhapāṣāṇa (sulfur-stone),
and rasaka (zinc ore) as a fourth part, should be added in ten parts.

children.text: śulvaṃ ca mardayet sarvaṃ naṣṭapiṣṭaṃ kṣaṇena tu
children.translated_text: He should triturate all the copper; in an instant it becomes a fine paste.
By merely being smeared with it, copper becomes gold.

children.text: niṣiktaṃ tena toyena prativāpaṃ daded budhaḥ
children.translated_text: The wise man should pour it on with that water and add it at each casting.
And the copper becomes gold, shining like the young sun.
Gold sprinkled with that water and joined with seed-substance,

children.text: tāraṃ cānena mārgeṇa niṣiktaṃ hematāṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: and silver sprinkled by this same method, reaches the state of gold.
He should eat bhallāta (marking nut) and sesame paste with hot water.
By using this for two months, he lives three hundred years.
Mercury, gandhāśman, rasaka, tuttha, darada, and mākṣika,
ground for a yāma with hot water, should be smeared on sheets of silver.
It should be blown twice, O <s>Devī</s>; it becomes fourteen-varṇa gold.
By this procedure, O <s>Deveśī</s>, copper becomes sixteen-varṇa gold.
One part each of gold and silver, and separate paired portions of kānta and abhra,
triturated with hot water, become a khoṭa by blowing.
If a man holds it in his mouth for a month, he becomes diamond-bodied.
He should eat its powder, the measure of a barley grain, with honey and ghee.

children.text: yāvat palaṃ tasya malaiḥ śulvaṃ bhavati kāñcanam ||
children.translated_text: Until he has taken a pala, by his wastes copper becomes gold.
He should eat horse-gram cooked with hot water and should drink milk.
He should bathe with hot water; after a year he gains a lifespan of a hundred years.
He should cook milk, hot water, and a decoction of triphalā.

children.text: pāyasaṃ kāntapātre tanmāsam ekaṃ tu bhakṣayet
children.translated_text: He should eat that milk-rice in a kānta vessel for one month.
Having eaten it, a man lives for a hundred kalpas and has a Vaiṣṇava lifespan.
After this I shall explain the procedure for śailodaka, O beloved.
It is fourfold: muddy water, earth-born water, mountain-born water, and stone-born water.
Some penetrate in an instant, and some penetrate in a day;
on earth, some penetrate over a fortnight, a month, and up to six months.

children.text: kṣiptaṃ yadā bhavet kāṣṭhaṃ śailībhūtaṃ ca dṛśyate
children.translated_text: When wood has been thrown in and is seen to have become stone-like,
Both externally and internally, O <s>Deveśi</s>, that is called a penetrative agent.

children.text: hiṅgulaṃ haritālaṃ ca gandhakaṃ ca manaḥśilā
children.translated_text: <s>Hiṅgula</s>, <s>haritāla</s>, sulfur, and <s>manaḥśilā</s>:

children.text: eṣāṃ gandhāpahāraṃ yat kurute tacca vedhakam ||
children.translated_text: whatever removes the odor from these is also a penetrative agent.

children.text: gandhakaṃ tālakaṃ caiva toyapūrṇe ghaṭe kṣipet
children.translated_text: One should throw sulfur and <s>tālaka</s> into a pot filled with water.
When it takes on the form of bubbles, then it becomes <s>śailodaka</s> (mountain-water).
Otherwise, O <s>Devi</s>, it is a mere covering substance, unfit to be taken and useless.
At <s>Śrīśaila</s>, on the edge of <s>Śrīvana</s>, on the stone surface called <s>Paryaṅka</s>,
what is found there, on the bank of the river <s>Bhagavatī</s>, penetrates in an instant.

children.text: ekāhe vedhakaṃ tatra gokarṇe tu dinatrayam ||
children.translated_text: There it penetrates in one day; at <s>Gokarṇa</s>, however, in three days.
At <s>Bhadrāṅga</s> it is a day-penetrating agent; at the end of the three holy places, it takes three nights.
At <s>Dhāreśvara</s> it takes a fortnight; at <s>Varṣāpurī</s>, one day.

children.text: brahmeśvare māsikaṃ syāt vyāghrapuryāṃ tu vāsaram
children.translated_text: At <s>Brahmeśvara</s> it takes a month; at <s>Vyāghrapurī</s>, however, a day.

children.text: aghoreśe māsikaṃ tu siṃhadvīpe tathā punaḥ
children.translated_text: At <s>Aghoreśa</s> it takes a month, and again on <s>Siṃhadvīpa</s> likewise.
On <s>Brahmagiri</s> it takes one day, but in the <s>Vindhya</s> it penetrates in an instant.
Among the <s>Mālyavants</s> it takes a day; the <s>śilodaka</s> penetrates in an instant.
On the lovely mountain of <s>Kiṣkindhyā</s>, on the bank of the <s>Pampā</s>, there is grass-water.
Two yojanas to the west of it, O <s>Devi</s>, again,
there is <s>Bhūśaila</s>; there on that mountain it penetrates in three days.
On the <s>Sahya</s> mountain, in the city of the goddess, near the <s>Kṣīrakṣetra</s>,
the <s>śailodaka</s> penetrates ten millionfold; in the <s>Durja</s> region too, it takes a day.
It penetrates one hundred thousandfold in the city of <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, called <s>Gokula</s>.
Wherever else it may be, born from <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, or <s>Śiva</s>,
there too that nectar is excellent for making one diamond-like.
I shall explain its origin, as practitioners know it.
From the body of <s>Varāha</s>, when he had lifted up the earth,
the sweat that fell from him became the supreme <s>śailodaka</s>.

children.text: tanmukhe kṣaṇikaṃ jātaṃ kroḍadeśe tu vāsaram
children.translated_text: At his mouth it arose as instant-acting; at the region of his snout it takes a day.

children.text: bāhubhyāṃ tryahavedhi syāt māsavedhi tu pārśvayoḥ
children.translated_text: From his two arms it penetrates in three days, while from his two sides it penetrates in a month.
At the rear part it takes six months; all of it has the same result.
Having protected that field with the <s>Aghorāstra</s> mantra and offered bali to the directions,

children.text: dattvā lakṣaṃ japitvā tu gṛhṇīyādamṛtaṃ param ||
children.translated_text: and having recited the mantra one hundred thousand times, he should collect the supreme nectar.
In autumn, summer, spring, or winter, O worshiped by the gods,
in an iron vessel, a copper vessel, or else a vessel made from gourd,
he should put in eight palas of <s>śailāmbu</s> (mountain-water) and one pala of milk.
Having boiled it down until only the milk remains, a man should drink it for twenty-one days.
He lives for a thousand years, free from wrinkles and gray hair.
Or else, eight palas of milk joined with one pala of water:
he should consume it when only the milk remains, and obtains the result stated before.
He should boil water with eight times as much horse gram until one eighth remains.
With four times that amount he should cook ghee until only the ghee remains.
<s>Bṛhaspati</s> should lick it together with an equal amount of honey for twenty-one days.
Within a month, having understood the attainment of the śāstras and the measure of strength and weakness, O <s>Devi</s>,
he has the form of a sixteen-year-old and a lifespan of a thousand years; there is no doubt.
As for the remaining horse gram, a quarter portion with honey and ghee
he should eat for one year; within a month he gains a life of ten thousand years.
With the oil prepared from that, one should have an anointing and massage performed.

children.text: māsamekaṃ tato mardyaṃ dehasiddhiṃ karoti ca ||
children.translated_text: After being rubbed for one month, the body to be massaged brings about bodily perfection.
It quickly overcomes scab, eczema, ringworm, and skin diseases.
He becomes free from wrinkles and gray hair and lives a thousand years.
Whoever, rising in the morning, drinks three handfuls of <s>śailāmbu</s>,
after six months becomes thousand-lived and free from wrinkles and gray hair.

children.text: athavā sūtakaṃ devi vāriṇā saha mardayet
children.translated_text: Or else, O <s>Devi</s>, he should triturate mercury together with the water.
In one month, O <s>Deveśi</s>, it will become <s>naṣṭapiṣṭa</s> (a fully amalgamated paste).
He should eat it for one month only; he becomes free from old age and death.

children.text: athavā taṃ rasaṃ hemnā hemabhasma tato balī
children.translated_text: Or else, that <s>rasa</s> with gold becomes gold ash; then, being strong,
he should triturate it with that water and blow it with a fire of khadira wood.
The pill called <s>Sundarī</s> wards off every weapon.
Its maker and taker becomes perfected by himself and lives as long as the moon, sun, and stars.

children.text: kunaṭī cābhramākṣīkaṃ hema tāraṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Kunaṭī</s>, mica, pyrite, gold, and silver too:

children.text: tat sarvaṃ payasā kṣīrairmadyaṃ pācyaṃ dinatrayam
children.translated_text: all that should be cooked for three days with milk and other milks, or with liquor.
By using it for only one month, he is free from wrinkles and gray hair.
Then with that very water he should cook rice pudding with half milk.
By using it for only one month, wrinkles and gray hair are destroyed.

children.text: paktvā tenāmbhasā pathyāḥ ṣaṣṭiṃ trīṇi śatāni ca
children.translated_text: Having cooked three hundred and sixty <s>pathyā</s> fruits with that water,

children.text: madhu saṃyojya bhāṇḍasthaṃ bhūmau sarvaṃ nidhāpayet ||
children.translated_text: he should mix them with honey, place the whole in a vessel, and bury it in the ground.
Day by day, rising in the morning, he should eat one each in that way.
Free from wrinkles and gray hair, he lives for a thousand years.
Or he should eat horse gram made stone-like, with honey and ghee.
By eating it for six months, he lives for a thousand years.

children.text: kūṣmāṇḍaṃ māritaṃ kṛtvā yāni kāni phalāni ca
children.translated_text: Having made bottle gourd incinerated, and whatever fruits there are,
and metals thrown into the water and made stone-like, he should eat them.
Living on milk after they are digested, a man becomes diamond-bodied.
Having thoroughly triturated mica with that water, O beloved, he should decoct it.
He should eat it mixed with the three pungents and lives for a thousand years.
Or else he should triturate one karṣa of <s>rasa</s> with that water.
Placed inside an <s>iṅgudī</s> fruit and immersed in that <s>śailodaka</s>,
after just three times the period, hardness arises in it.

children.text: ṣaṇmāsaṃ tanmukhe dhāryaṃ vajrakāyaṃ karoti ca
children.translated_text: Kept in the mouth for six months, it makes the body diamond-like.
With life-force equal to ten elephants, he delights together with the gods.
Having taken <s>triphalā</s> there, he should place it in mountain water.

children.text: yadā bhavati tacchailaṃ gṛhītvā cūrṇayet tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: When it has become stone-like, he should take it and then grind it to powder.
Together with <s>rasa</s> (mercury) digested with <s>kānta</s>, soaked in ghee and honey,
he should eat it for one year; after that he should live on milk.
He becomes like the rising sun, intelligent and pleasing to behold,
with dark curling hair, and he lives as long as the moon, sun, and stars.

children.text: pāradaṃ haritālaṃ ca śilā mākṣikameva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Pārada</s> (mercury), <s>haritāla</s> (orpiment), <s>śilā</s>, and <s>mākṣika</s>,

children.text: daradaṃ ca viṣaṃ caiva sarvamekatra kārayet ||
children.translated_text: and also <s>darada</s> and poison: he should put all these together in one place.
He should triturate them on a mortar-stone with the juice of citron,
make them into a ball, and place it in water.

children.text: tena tāraṃ ca śulvaṃ ca kāñcanaṃ bhavati dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: By means of that, silver and copper certainly become gold.
One should use it for one month; free from wrinkles and gray hair,
his life lasts a thousand years, and he has great strength and valor.
With turmeric that has become stone-like, by the mere sprinkling of that powder,
lead attains the state of gold, with a brilliance like the young sun.
Having placed it in stone-water, or in earth-stone, or even in mud,
after knowing the measure of time, he should then bind the mercury.
Heated with red alkali, equalized in flow with gold,
with only a hundredth part it makes all metals into gold.
Having obtained the second <s>sāraṇā</s> (alchemical projection), he should eat it with honey and ghee.
At once the breath rises upward from the thoughts that arise in him.
He obtains knowledge of time, and he lives for fifty thousand years.
Having obtained the second <s>sāraṇā</s>, it pierces with a thousandth part.

children.text: taṃ khoṭaṃ dhārayedvaktre divyatvaṃ labhate dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: He should hold that <s>khoṭa</s> (solidified lump) in his mouth; he certainly obtains divinity.

children.text: nicule kakubhe caiva kiṃśuke madhuke'pi vā
children.translated_text: In <s>nicula</s>, <s>kakubha</s>, <s>kiṃśuka</s>, or also <s>madhuka</s>,
or inside the fruit of <s>iṅgudī</s>, for the span of two nights,
he should triturate mercury and sulfur into the form of a pill.
He should cook it for one day; wrapping it in gold, he should carry it.
Carefully coating it with a paste of <s>triphalā</s> and <s>vyoṣa</s>,

children.text: pādena kanakaṃ dattvā pāradaṃ tatra yojayet
children.translated_text: after adding a quarter part of gold, he should combine the mercury there.
He should throw it into mountain water; the pill becomes like diamond.

children.text: pūrvavat sāraṇā kāryā pūrvavat siddhidā bhavet
children.translated_text: The <s>sāraṇā</s> should be performed as before; as before, it grants accomplishment.

children.text: dhāryamāṇā mukhe sā tu sahasrāyuṣkarī bhavet ||
children.translated_text: When held in the mouth, that pill gives a lifespan of a thousand years.
Through the application of the second <s>sāraṇā</s>, it pierces ten thousand.
When held in the mouth, this pill gives a lifespan of ten thousand years.
Through the application of the third <s>sāraṇā</s>, it becomes capable of piercing a hundred thousand.
He should hold that <s>khoṭa</s> in his mouth; the man comes to have a lifespan of a hundred thousand years.

children.text: caturthīṃ sāraṇāṃ prāpya koṭivedho na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: Having obtained the fourth <s>sāraṇā</s>, it pierces ten million; there is no doubt.
His lifespan is ten million years, and aerial movement is obtained.

children.text: pañcabhir daśakoṭiḥ syāt ṣaḍbhiḥ koṭiśataṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: With five, it becomes ten crores; with six, it becomes a hundred crores.
His life lasts as long as the moon and sun, and he possesses endless strength and vigor.

children.text: dadāti saptamīṃ sāpi sāraṇāṃ guṭikā parā
children.translated_text: That supreme pill also grants the seventh <s>sāraṇā</s>.
It is famed by the name <s>khecarī</s>, taught by <s>Bhairava</s>.
But whoever eats even a mustard-seed measure of it for one month,
becomes a perfected one with a diamond body, beloved by divine women.

children.text: krīḍate khecarair bhogaiḥ svecchayā śivatāṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: He sports with aerial enjoyments as he wishes and attains the state of <s>Śiva</s>.
There are various kinds of results from its juices and from the oil of the seeds.

children.text: tadbaddhaṃ pāradaṃ caiva guṭikāṃ śṛṇu sundari ||
children.translated_text: Now listen, O beautiful one, to the mercury bound by it and to the pill.
In purified, bound <s>rasendra</s> (lord mercury), one should digest sulfur.

children.text: triguṇe gandhake jīrṇe tena hema tu kārayet ||
children.translated_text: When sulfur in triple quantity has been digested, he should make gold by means of it.

children.text: kārayedbhasma sūtaṃ tu kāñcanaṃ tatra sūtakam
children.translated_text: One should make mercury into ash; mercury should be placed there in gold.

children.text: tadbhasma sūtake jāryaṃ rasendrasya same samam ||
children.translated_text: That ash should be digested in mercury, equal part for equal part with <s>rasendra</s>.
With that digested mercury, he should digest diamond-jewel.
That diamond becomes ash, resembling red vermilion.

children.text: tadbhasma jārayate sūte triguṇe tu surārcite
children.translated_text: One digests that ash in mercury, in triple quantity, O worshiped by the gods.

children.text: hāṭake sārayettaṃ tu guṭikāṃ tena kārayet ||
children.translated_text: He should project it into gold and make a pill with it.

children.text: trilohāveṣṭitaṃ taṃ tu mukhe prakṣipya sādhakaḥ
children.translated_text: The practitioner should put that pill, enclosed in the three metals, into his mouth.
He becomes without a shadow, invisible to gods and demons.
At that very instant, O <s>Devi</s>, he turns all metals into gold.
For many thousands of years he remains without wrinkles and gray hair.
He should carry, in mouth and hand, what bears the trident, is joined with <s>śakti</s>, and is adorned with the qualities of jewels and the like,
for warding off all weapons.
<s>Vyoma</s> (mica), the essence of <s>mākṣika</s>, and <s>surāyudha</s> in a silver measure,
together with <s>vaikrānta</s>, <s>tālaka</s>, and mercury, adorned with the qualities of jewels and the like:
that pill, O fair-hipped one, joined with the three sweets,

children.text: vaktrasthā nāśayet sākṣāt palitaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: when placed in the mouth, directly removes gray hair; there is no doubt.
And <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>, O <s>Deveśi</s>, should be joined with jewels and the like, as in the <s>Śiva</s> rite.

children.text: hema tāraṃ tathā bhānuṃ samabhāgāni kārayet
children.translated_text: He should make gold, silver, and <s>bhānu</s> in equal parts.
With women's menstrual blood, placed in the midst of a tiger, he should wrap it with lotus fiber.
He should sprinkle it and, having wrapped it in that way, place it in a secret place.

children.text: raṇe rājakule dyūte divye kāmye jayo bhavet
children.translated_text: There will be victory in battle, in the royal court, in gambling, and in divine or desired matters.

children.text: yanmukhe caiva tadgolaṃ sa sarvarañjako bhavet ||
children.translated_text: And whoever has that ball in his mouth becomes one who delights everyone.
<s>Vaikrānta</s>, mica, <s>kānta</s>, <s>sasyaka</s>, and <s>surāyudha</s>
should be equal to the sour gruel produced from <s>vibhītaka</s> and the others.
Then he should add <s>rājāvarta</s> to the mercury in a quarter proportion.
Rubbed with the juice of <s>kumārī</s>, a single auspicious pill is made.
When held in the mouth, it destroys disease, death, and old age; there is no doubt about this.
O fair-hipped one, there should be five parts of silver and two of <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury),
three parts of mica, and one part each of gold and magnetite.
By the procedure with half copper, O beautiful immortal one, the pill is made.
Through it he becomes inexhaustible, free from old age, and very strong.
Freed from all diseases, he lives by holding it in the mouth.
There should be one pala of calcined mercury and likewise a pala of killed magnetite,
a pala of pyrite and again a pala of bitumen.
There should be one pala of <s>viḍaṅga</s> and likewise a pala of powdered <s>pathyā</s>.

children.text: ekīkṛtyātha tat sarvaṃ madhvājyena tu peṣayet ||
children.translated_text: Having combined all that into one, he should grind it with honey and ghee.
O <s>Devi</s>, he should make three hundred and sixty pills.
He should eat one each day, continuously for one year.
He lives for thousands of years, equal to <s>Rudra</s>, and possessed of great strength.
After this I shall teach the rasāyana of calcined <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
It should be known as requiring no regimen, the supreme divine medicine made manifest.

children.text: āmalakyādi kāntaṃ ca pāradaṃ ca manaḥśilām
children.translated_text: Take <s>āmalakī</s> and the other ingredients, magnetite, <s>pārada</s> (mercury), and realgar,
and seven parts of <s>vākucī</s>, ground with the juice of <s>kṣīriṇī</s>.
Together with the juice of <s>meghanāda</s>, it should be placed in a closed crucible and fired.

children.text: māṣaṃ trimāṣaṃ triguṇaṃ bhakṣayettu krameṇa tu
children.translated_text: He should eat it in order, first one māṣa, then three māṣas, and then three times that amount.
O <s>Devi</s>, over three years, in sequence, the measure reaches a quarter and then a half niṣka.
For six, seven, and eight years, successively, he should take it in niṣka measures.
Then he eats divine food and is free from the disfigurement of old age.
If someone eats a niṣka, or even half a niṣka, mixed with a little gold,
within three years he thoroughly conquers all diseases.
In the eighth year he has a thousand-year lifespan; in the twelfth he can pierce a lakh.

children.text: ṣoḍaśe vatsare devi divyarūpaḥ sa jāyate ||
children.translated_text: In the sixteenth year, O <s>Devi</s>, he becomes divine in form.

children.text: śatapalam abhayānām akṣadhātryos tathaiva kvathitajalaśatāṣṭau bhāgamaṣṭāvaśeṣam
children.translated_text: One hundred palas of <s>abhayā</s>, and likewise of <s>akṣa</s> and <s>dhātrī</s>, should be boiled in eight hundred palas of water until one eighth remains.

children.text: ghṛtamadhusitayāḍhyaṃ vyoṣacitraṃ daśāṃśaṃ rasaphalarasasiddhaṃ lohajīrṇaṃ mṛtaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: It is enriched with ghee, honey, and sugar, made varied with one tenth part of the three pungents, prepared with the juice of <s>rasaphala</s>, and combined with digested and killed iron.
Mica equal to mountain bitumen, magnetite, <s>bhṛṅga</s>, and <s>viḍaṅga</s>, well impregnated together with mercury and with excellent divine rice,
form this best paste, a māṣa in measure, mixed as a paste made by cool rays and thoroughly perfected over three days in an iron vessel.
If he licks it at bedtime, while attending upon a woman with beautiful eyes, he becomes like the pride of an intoxicated elephant, with a firm and compactly handsome waist.

children.text: vigatasakaladoṣaḥ sarvadigdivyacakṣuḥ madana iva sukāntiḥ kāminīnāṃ pravīraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Freed from every defect, with divine sight in all directions, he is as lovely as <s>Madana</s> and foremost among lovers of women.
Having a body like a fragment of cloud and curly blue-black hair, pure like the preceptor of the gods, he becomes a good poet and a maker of marvels.

children.text: vṛṣabhagativiceṣṭaḥ snigdhagambhīraghoṣaḥ suragaja iva loke śrāntihantāśu nityam ||
children.translated_text: With the gait and movements of a bull, and with a smooth, deep voice, he always quickly removes weariness in the world like the elephant of the gods.

children.text: prabhavati khalu loke somatārārkajīvī kamalasadanasuśrīr nyāyaśāstrādivettā
children.translated_text: Indeed he becomes powerful in the world, living as long as the moon, stars, sun, and <s>Jīva</s>; he has the fine splendor of the lotus-seated goddess and knows logic, scripture, and the rest.
He protects the custom of good people, approves the initiation of <s>dharma</s> (religious duty), is deep like <s>Hari</s> and <s>Hara</s>, and steady as the sun, moon, and ocean.
A beautiful and auspicious ball of magnetite, gold, copper, silver, and mica, placed in the fruit of <s>iṅgudī</s>,
becomes a ball perfected by mountain-water, pleasing even to the immortals.
A ball of magnetite, gold, copper, silver, mica, diamond-jewel, and <s>ahirāja</s>,
cast into the hollow of an <s>āmalaka</s> wood and set in the earth and mountain, is drawn out.
When it has become stony and is then placed in the mouth, it makes the body adamantine within a few days.
A ball made with orpiment, gold, excellent copper, and mercury, enclosed in a wooden apparatus of <s>varaṇa</s>,
and made into the beautiful elixir by mountain-water, is called the <s>khecarī</s> pill.
A <s>palāśa</s> seed thrown into mountain-water, made stony, should be eaten with honey and ghee.

children.text: triḥsaptarātraṃ dinamekamekaṃ sahasrajīvī vijayī naraḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: For three times seven nights, one each day, a man becomes a thousand-year-lived conqueror.
Mercury and mica, combined with the milk of <s>vajrī</s>,
and joined with gold, become the <s>khecarī</s> pill.
He should place mercury inside a <s>karañja</s> fruit.
Set within ghee and mountain-water, it grants a thousand-year lifespan.
In a <s>tinduka</s> fruit it gives two thousand years, and in a citron three thousand.
In a <s>mātuluṅga</s> and in an orange it gives four and five thousand years.
In a plantain fruit it gives six thousand, and in a jackfruit the number seven thousand.
And in a <s>vibhītaka</s> fruit it gives the number ten thousand.
In a coconut, O greatly fortunate one, it gives fourteen thousand years.
In a lotus it gives thirty thousand, and in an <s>āmalaka</s> a hundred thousand.
In the liquid of mica leaf, in a decoction, and in stone-water for a day and night,
the mercury drawn out from that destroys death and poverty.
By the method of the <s>sāraṇā</s> process, a new body is produced.

children.text: rase rasāyane caiva lakṣavedhī na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In mercury and in rasāyana it certainly has the power to penetrate a lakh.
A ball is made from clay and the juice of <s>kumārī</s>.
From blowing it there falls the essence; a man should hold that in his mouth.
By using it for six months, he reaches freedom from old age and death.
The essence, fused together with collyrium from a spring, is mixed with mercury.

children.text: taṃ khoṭaṃ dhārayedvaktre adṛśyo bhavati dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: He should hold that lump in his mouth; he surely becomes invisible.
Whatever procedure for water has been taught in the <s>Śivāgama</s>,

children.text: rasenaiva tu kāle tu kuryādeva rasāyanam ||
children.translated_text: he should perform that rasāyana at the proper time only with mercury.
The blessed <s>Devi</s> said:

children.text: deva tvaṃ pāradendrasya proktā me bālajāraṇā
children.translated_text: O god, you have told me the preliminary digestion of lord <s>pārada</s> (mercury).
Therefore next explain fully the <s>jāraṇā</s> (digestive processing) of that which has been properly bound.
<s>Śrībhairava</s> said:
The one described before is this inferior, childish <s>jāraṇā</s>.
The superior and rare <s>baddhajāraṇā</s> (processing of the bound substance) is to be heard.

children.text: abaddhaṃ jārayed yastu jīryamāṇaḥ kṣayaṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: Whoever causes an unbound substance to undergo <s>jāraṇā</s> goes to ruin while it is being digested.

children.text: baddhasya jīryate grāso jīrṇasya ca mukhaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: For the bound substance a <s>grāsa</s> (morsel) is digested, and when it is digested it obtains a mouth.
Whether possessing a good mouth or lacking a mouth, it bears the complete marks of the highest kind.
The ordinary one, through its capacity to endure fire, is a digester of great jewels.
The ordinary form should be made first; when furnished with a <s>grāsa</s>, it is highly approved.
O <s>Devi</s>, this ordinary form indeed becomes a maker of an excellent body.
But the bound substance that lacks a <s>grāsa</s> produces divine accomplishment.
The best is root-binding, the middling is the binding of mercury,
and the inferior is binding by cooking; thus binding is threefold.
The binding called root-binding is termed <s>vāsanābandha</s>.
Binding is made by some root from among the sixty-four roots.
Among animal parts, masūra and the like, the root-part is regarded as divine.

children.text: pāṣāṇaṃ caiva siddhānāṃ mānuṣāṇāṃ ca pūjitam ||
children.translated_text: Stone too is honored among siddhas and revered among human beings.
Binding is threefold, by pellet, by liquefaction, and by contraction.
Pure binding with divine herbs has been taught before.
Mercury is bound by <s>drutis</s> (liquefied essences); this is called momentary binding.
Mica, <s>Harabīja</s>, and gold in a sixteenth part,
when smelted in an open crucible, should be purified with glass and borax.
Smelted with rightward turning, the alloy with <s>Harabīja</s>,
after leaving the crucible, O fair-hipped one, remains like bound mercury.
With a measure of only half of a half-raktikā, it can pierce even mountains.
From eating it, O queen of gods, a man becomes equal to <s>Rudra</s>.
He sports in the seven worlds, with prowess equal to <s>Śiva</s>.
O <s>Devi</s>, listen to the mixing of the <s>drutis</s>, dependent on divine herbs.
<s>Vajrakanda</s>, <s>lāṅgalī</s>, and <s>uccāṭa</s> together

children.text: abhrakaṃ kramate śīghram anyathā nāsti saṃkramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: make mica enter quickly; otherwise there is no penetration.
With black aloe, <s>śaṅkhanābhī</s>, garlic juice, white substance, and <s>rāmaṭha</s>,
together with woman's flower and palāśa-seed oil,
all the heated and boiled <s>drutis</s> combine with the rasas.

children.text: mākṣikaṃ ca viṣaṃ guñjā ṭaṅkaṇaṃ strīrajastathā
children.translated_text: Pyrite, poison, guñjā, borax, and likewise a woman's menstrual fluid,
smeared with a woman's milk, cause all pairs of substances to combine.
A <s>krāmaṇa</s> (penetrating agent), well impregnated with <s>jīvāhi</s>, <s>vyoma</s>, stone, and <s>kroṣṭujihvā</s>,
serves for the penetration of all metals and also for the mixing of <s>drutis</s>.
Horse's saliva, garlic, fresh ginger, and neem shoots,

children.text: ṭaṅkaṇaṃ ca rasaṃ vyoma vajraṃ cāpi praveśayet ||
children.translated_text: along with borax, mercury, <s>vyoma</s>, and diamond too, should be introduced.
Mica, gold-<s>druti</s>, and mercury, the three, should be combined in one place.

children.text: krāmaṇena tu mūṣāyāṃ lepaṃ dattvā vicakṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: With the <s>krāmaṇa</s> in a crucible, the skilled man, after applying a coating,
makes them combine instantly by steaming in the ground with chaff-fire.
This becomes a hundred-piercer for iron, silver, and copper.

children.text: tasya madhye tathā deyā abhrahemadrutiḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Into its middle, again, mica-gold <s>druti</s> should then be placed.
It should be steamed with chaff-fire until only mercury remains.

children.text: sahasravedhī sa bhavet nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: It becomes a thousand-piercer; no doubt should be entertained here.
With each successive <s>saṃkala</s> in binding, the piercing power becomes ten times greater.
The great <s>rasa</s> bound with seven <s>saṃkalas</s> is a crore-piercer.
When the wise man eats it for the sake of the body, in a guñjā-measure,
combined with <s>trikaṭu</s> and <s>triphalā</s>, together with ghee and honey,

children.text: jīrṇe jīrṇe tu saṃgrāhyaṃ yāvat syādaṣṭaraktikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: it should be taken after each digestion until it amounts to eight raktikās.
The mercury struck by <s>saṃkalas</s>, from a hundred up to a crore,
makes one live according to that measure, like <s>vajravallī</s>, as does the <s>rasa</s>.
Mercury combined with the <s>drutis</s> of gold, mica, and copper
should pierce by the previous procedure and should be eaten according to every procedure.
One obtains the station of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, with prowess equal to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
The <s>drutis</s> of copper, mica, and gold, combined with mercury,
when added back to tin in a hundredth part, certainly produce <s>stambhana</s> (fixation).
Sharp iron, <s>māra</s>, and gold, combined with mercury,
when added back to lead in a hundredth part, produce <s>stambhana</s>.

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ ghoṣaṃ tathā tāraṃ pāradena samanvitam
children.translated_text: Sharp iron, bell-metal, and silver, combined with mercury,
when added back to tin, produce <s>stambhana</s> in a hundredth part.
Thus these <s>drutiyogas</s> (formulas with liquefied essences) are to be known according to rule.
By this <s>drutiyoga</s>, mercury becomes a maker of body and metals.
<s>Śrībhairava</s> said:
Again I shall teach another <s>vajrabandha</s>, O queen of gods.
A woman should eat sulphur for twenty-one days.
Her menstrual fluid is beneficial for the binding and <s>jāraṇā</s> of the king of rasas.

children.text: vajrabhasma tu bhāgaikaṃ bhāgāḥ śuddharasās trayaḥ
children.translated_text: One part diamond ash and three parts purified mercury
should be ground with a woman's menstrual fluid until it has become a paste.
With a quarter-part of gold, he should have a coating made for metal leaves.
The juice of <s>vyomavallī</s>, magnetic ore, and finely powdered borax,
with mica as an eighth part, should be placed in a mortar and ground.
That fourfold lost paste, after being sealed, should then be fired in a <s>puṭa</s>.
Placed in a closed crucible, smelted, and joined with <s>krāmaṇa</s>,
a <s>khoṭa</s> arises, O <s>Devi</s>, a hundred-piercing great <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: sauvīraṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ kācaṃ dattvā dattvā viśodhayet
children.translated_text: By repeatedly adding <s>sauvīra</s>, borax, and glass, he should purify it.
When what is undigested has combined with gold, <s>samāvarta</s> arises.
Then, in a sequence increasing by one at each step, he should advance it by the <s>saṃkalī</s> bindings.
With mercury in onefold quantity, it is called the first <s>saṃkalikā</s>.

children.text: triguṇena tu sūtena dvitīyā saṃkalī bhavet ||
children.translated_text: But with mercury in threefold quantity, it becomes the second <s>saṃkalī</s>.

children.text: ṣaḍguṇena tu sūtena tṛtīyā saṃkalī bhavet
children.translated_text: But with mercury in sixfold quantity, it becomes the third <s>saṃkalī</s>.
With mercury in tenfold quantity, it becomes the fourth <s>saṃkalī</s>.
With fifteenfold quantity, O mistress, it becomes the fifth <s>saṃkalī</s>.
With twenty-onefold quantity, O mistress, it is considered the sixth <s>saṃkalikā</s>.
With twenty-eightfold quantity, O mistress, it is remembered as the seventh <s>saṃkalī</s>.
Joined with thirty-sixfold quantity, it becomes the eighth <s>saṃkalikā</s>.
With forty-fivefold quantities, it is considered the ninth <s>saṃkalī</s>.
With fifty-fivefold quantity, it is remembered as the tenth <s>saṃkalī</s>.
Thus, by progressive increase, its binding is the tenfold <s>saṃkalī</s>.
In the first it pierces ten; in the second it pierces a hundred.
In the third it pierces a thousand, and in the fourth it pierces ten thousand.

children.text: pañcame lakṣavedhī syāt daśalakṣaṃ tu ṣaṣṭhake
children.translated_text: In the fifth it pierces a hundred thousand; in the sixth, however, a million.
In the seventh it pierces a crore, and in the eighth likewise ten crores.
In the ninth it is the sight of smoke; in the tenth it pierces by sound.
Bound by each successive <s>saṃkalī</s>, the <s>vedha</s> (piercing power) becomes tenfold.
The great mercury, bound by ten <s>saṃkalikās</s>, is sound-piercing.

children.text: yathā lohe tathā dehe kramate nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As it moves through metal, so it moves through the body; there is no doubt here.
By that measure it should pierce metals and also the body.
He should make a divine pill, the size of a jujube stone.
Having worshiped <s>Mahākālī</s>, the wise man should carry it constantly.
I shall proclaim its mantra, hard to obtain even for the thirty gods.
The praṇava, the seed-syllable of <s>Bhuvaneśī</s>, and after that the seed-syllable of <s>Lakṣmī</s>:

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ kālikā kāli mahākāli māṃsaśoṇitabhojini
children.translated_text: oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, O <s>Kālikā</s>, O <s>Kālī</s>, O <s>Mahākālī</s>, eater of flesh and blood,

children.text: hrīṃ hrīṃ huṃ raktakṛṣṇamukhe devi rasasiddhiṃ dadasva me ||
children.translated_text: hrīṃ hrīṃ huṃ, O goddess with red-black face, grant me accomplishment in mercury.

children.text: śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ ramā śaktiśca tārākhyo mantro'yaṃ sarvasiddhidaḥ ||
children.translated_text: śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ, <s>Ramā</s>, <s>Śakti</s>, and the mantra called <s>Tārā</s>: this grants every accomplishment.
Then, having worshiped the goddess, especially the accomplished circle,

children.text: tāṃ kṣiped vaktramadhye tu guṭikāṃ divyarūpiṇīm ||
children.translated_text: he should place that divine-form pill in the middle of his mouth.

children.text: śatavedhena yā baddhā rasena guṭikā priye
children.translated_text: The pill that is bound with mercury of hundredfold <s>vedha</s>, O beloved,
when it stays in the mouth for one month, one lives for the duration of a yuga.

children.text: tathā sahasravedhena yā baddhā guṭikā śubhā
children.translated_text: Likewise, the auspicious pill that is bound with thousandfold <s>vedha</s>,
when it stays in the mouth for two months, one lives as long as the moon, sun, and stars.
If the pill is bound with ten-thousandfold <s>vedha</s>,
then, after three months, its lifespan is equal to that of <s>Śakra</s>, O fair-faced one.
The divine-form pill that is bound with hundred-thousandfold <s>vedha</s>,
when it stays in the mouth for four months, grants the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>.
The divine-form pill that is bound with a millionfold <s>vedha</s>,
when it stays in the mouth for five months, obtains a lifespan equal to <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s.
The divine-form pill that is bound with crorefold <s>vedha</s>,

children.text: ṣaṇmāsaṃ saṃsthitā vaktre sākṣādvai rudratāṃ nayet ||
children.translated_text: when it remains in the mouth for six months, brings one directly to the state of <s>Rudra</s>.
The divine-form pill, by the distinction of a hundred crores,

children.text: saptamāsaṃ tu vaktrasthā sa labhedaiśvaraṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: when it stays in the mouth for seven months, causes him to obtain the lordly state.
The <s>Śiva</s>-form pill that is bound at the level of smoke-sight,

children.text: aṣṭamāsaṃ tu vaktrasthā īśānasya phalaṃ labhet ||
children.translated_text: when it stays in the mouth for eight months, obtains the fruit of <s>Īśāna</s>.
The <s>Śiva</s>-form pill that is bound with sound-piercing <s>vedha</s>,

children.text: navamāsaṃ tu vaktrasthā sa bhavedvyāpako naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: when it stays in the mouth for nine months, that man becomes all-pervading.
Bound by nine <s>saṃkalikās</s>, he is <s>Svayambhū</s> or <s>Maheśvara</s> himself.
He himself is creator, destroyer, and enjoyer, the maker of curses and blessings.
He is all-knowing and all-creating, subtle in form and stainless.
By his will he creates; by his will he withdraws the world.
Having become one who moves freely, the man becomes universal in form.
And he is worshiped by all the gods, by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>.
Again I shall proclaim another very rare <s>vajrabandha</s> (diamond binding).
He should prepare edible gold in equal part with purified mercury.
He should triturate dead diamond, in a pala portion, with the juices of two-footed beings.
The remainder, as before, born previously, should be well triturated with <s>haṃsapādī</s>.

children.text: bhāvitaṃ puṭitaṃ ratnaiḥ pūrvavat saphalaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Infused and roasted with jewels, it becomes successful as before.
One bound with diamond becomes accomplished, unconquerable by gods and demons.
He becomes the leader of the twenty-four siddhas and the giver of every accomplishment.
He should triturate mercury equal to diamond powder with <s>haṃsapādī</s>.

children.text: puṭitvā mārayettaṃ tu punastulyaṃ rasaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Having roasted it, he should kill it; then he should add an equal quantity of mercury.
When smelted, it quickly becomes a <s>khoṭa</s>; it is purified with glass and borax.
Until that mercury becomes like the rising of <s>Śakra</s>, O beloved.

children.text: vajrasattvaṃ ca gaganaṃ rasaṃ hema ca melayet
children.translated_text: He should combine diamond essence, mica, mercury, and gold.
With it held in the mouth, O lord of gods, he attains immortality.
Having digested that mercury, he should again digest it by means of that very thing.

children.text: koṭivedhī na saṃdeho vaktrasthaḥ khecaraṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: It pierces a crore, without doubt; when held in the mouth, it gives the state of a sky-goer.
By that measure it should pierce metal and also the body.
He should make a divine pill in gold by means of diamond-perfected mercury.
By this sequence of procedure he should kill it as much as possible.
That ash of mercury, O goddess, destroys all diseases.
Having first caused it to flow with gold, then he should smear it with moon and sun.
With a thirty-second part, half the gold becomes greater by the measure of the letters.
The wise man should make a pill the size of a jujube stone.

children.text: yathā lohe tathā dehe kramate nānyathā kvacit ||
children.translated_text: As it proceeds in metal, so it proceeds in the body; it is never otherwise.
Gold, paired with diamond and joined with <s>kānta</s> and copper,
should be colored seven times; that <s>khoṭa</s> should be finely powdered.
It should be impregnated, as with women's menstrual blood, and combined in the measure of five <s>guñjā</s> berries.
Then, placing it in a birch-bark sheet and tying it with cloth as a bundle,
one should steam it, O <s>Devadeveśi</s>, until it becomes a ball.
<s>Lāṅgalī</s>, <s>jīvaka</s>, and <s>indravāruṇī</s> joined with <s>mustā</s>:

children.text: eteṣāṃ nikṣipet piṇḍe vajragolaṃ tu veṣṭayet ||
children.translated_text: he should place these in a lump and wrap the diamond ball with them.
Putting it inside a crucible and carefully sealing it,

children.text: bhūmau mūṣāṃ vinikṣipya puṭaṃ mūrdhni pradāpayet ||
children.translated_text: he should set the crucible in the ground and apply a heating on its top.
By this very application, the <s>mahārasa</s> (great mercury) becomes bound.
If he holds the ball in his mouth for one year, dear one,
he lives for thousands of aeons, like a mighty serpent.
In twelve years he directly becomes of the form of <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: gātrasya tasya prasvedāt aṣṭau lohāstu kāñcanam ||
children.translated_text: From the sweat of his limbs, the eight metals become gold.
Diamond ash, and likewise <s>sūta</s> (mercury), combined with gold:
whoever keeps it in his mouth becomes free from gray hair within a year.

children.text: kṛṣṇābhrakasya sattvaṃ ca tāraṃ tāmraṃ ca hāṭakam
children.translated_text: The essence of black mica, silver, copper, and gold,
<s>mākṣika</s>, <s>kānta</s>, and <s>tīkṣṇa</s> should be made in equal parts.
When smelted in a sealed crucible, a <s>khoṭa</s> is immediately produced.

children.text: taṃ khoṭaṃ sūkṣmacūrṇaṃ tu drutasūtena golakam ||
children.translated_text: That <s>khoṭa</s>, finely powdered, should be made into a ball with molten <s>sūta</s>.
One part of dead diamond and four parts of the ball:
he should triturate it with a heated mortar; the <s>sūtaka</s> becomes ash.
He should kill it in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus by the procedure of seven sealings.

children.text: guñjāmātraṃ tu tadbhasma madhvājyena tu lehayet ||
children.translated_text: A <s>guñjā</s>-measure of that ash should be licked with honey and ghee.
Through use for a year, a man becomes one whose life is ten thousand years,
free from wrinkles and gray hair, and endowed with great strength and valor.

children.text: tadbhasmapalam ekaṃ tu palaikaṃ gandhakasya ca
children.translated_text: One <s>pala</s> of that ash and one <s>pala</s> of sulfur:
when smelted in a sealed crucible, a <s>khoṭa</s> is immediately produced.
He lives for thousands of aeons, like mighty <s>Anaṅga</s>.
By his urine and feces the eight metals become gold.
Afterward he should color that <s>khoṭa</s> with <s>vaṅga</s>, mica, and <s>kapālī</s>.
He should color it seven times; it becomes like saffron.
Having melted it together with gold and subjected it to the three <s>sāraṇā</s> operations,
he should pierce all metals with that very substance in the thousandth part.

children.text: kṛṣṇābhrakasya sattvaṃ ca tāraṃ tāmraṃ ca hāṭakam
children.translated_text: The essence of black mica, silver, copper, and gold,

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ ca baddhasūtaṃ ca mākṣikaṃ ca samanvitam ||
children.translated_text: <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, bound <s>sūta</s>, and <s>mākṣika</s> combined:
when smelted in a sealed crucible, a <s>khoṭa</s> is immediately produced.
Having melted it together with gold and subjected it to the three <s>sāraṇā</s> operations,
with that very substance, in the hundredth part, he should bring about the piercing of copper.
Divine gold is produced, fit to adorn the ornaments of the gods.
One part of bound <s>sūta</s>, one part of <s>pannaga</s>,
one part of gold, and one part each of mica and <s>kānta</s>:

children.text: ekīkṛtya tu taddhāmyaṃ rase jīrṇe tu jārayet
children.translated_text: having made them one, it should be smelted; when it is digested in mercury, he should digest it further.
With that very substance, in the hundredth part, he should bring about the piercing of copper.
One part of bound <s>sūta</s> and one part of <s>kuṭila</s>:
when smelted in a sealed crucible, a <s>khoṭa</s> is immediately produced.

children.text: tasya khoṭasya bhāgaikaṃ bhāgaikaṃ gandhakasya ca
children.translated_text: One part of that <s>khoṭa</s> and one part of sulfur:
it should be smelted in a sealed crucible until only <s>vaṅga</s> remains.
By this sequence of procedure, having quenched <s>vaṅga</s> sixfold,
by this sequence of procedure it should carry <s>nāga</s> sixfold.
Afterward he should color that mercury with <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, copper, and <s>kapālī</s>.
He should color it carefully until it becomes like saffron.
Having melted it together with gold and subjected it to the three <s>sāraṇā</s> operations,

children.text: śatāṃśe vedhayet śulvaṃ divyaṃ hema prajāyate ||
children.translated_text: he should pierce copper with a hundredth part; divine gold is produced.
Again I shall teach another excellent liquid preparation.
He should color purified gold with <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, copper, and <s>kapālī</s>.
One part of prepared seed and one part of molten <s>sūtaka</s>:
he should triturate them with a medium sour liquid; a ball is produced at once.
One part of dead diamond and four parts of the ball:
he should triturate it with a heated mortar; the <s>sūtaka</s> becomes ash.
He should kill it in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus by the procedure of seven sealings.

children.text: tadbhasma tu punaḥ paścāt madhyamāmlena mardayet ||
children.translated_text: Then afterward he should again triturate that ash with a medium sour liquid.
He should carefully give it a heating three hundred and sixty times.
That ash becomes divine, resembling red vermilion.
With that very substance, in the thousandth part, he should pierce silver into gold.
One part of dead diamond and sixteen parts of <s>sūtaka</s>:
triturated successively with the juice of <s>devadālī</s> and <s>śaṅkhapuṣpī</s>,
he should kill it in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus; it becomes ash at once.
When blown with a thousand blasts, it does not disappear while being smelted.

children.text: īdṛśaṃ bhasmasūtaṃ ca dehe lohe ca yojayet ||
children.translated_text: Such ash-mercury should be applied to the body and to metal.
One <s>pala</s> of that ash and one <s>pala</s> of <s>pannaga</s>:
when smelted in a sealed crucible, a <s>khoṭa</s> is immediately produced.
Afterward he should color that <s>khoṭa</s> according to the <s>kāpālika</s> sequence of procedure.
Through the application of the three <s>sāraṇā</s> operations, he should bring about the piercing of copper.
And one <s>pala</s> of ash-mercury and one <s>pala</s> of <s>pannaga</s>.
Through a <s>puṭa</s> (heating) it becomes an ash resembling red vermilion.

children.text: tadbhasma tu punaḥ paścād gopittena tu mardayet
children.translated_text: Then afterward he should triturate that ash with cow bile.
Having put it in a copper vessel, he should triturate it with an iron pestle.
Then it should be cooked over a gentle fire until it combines with lead.
One part of that ash, and one part a pellet of gold,
having combined them, he should then triturate them together with <s>krāmaṇa</s> (a penetrating reagent).
By that same thousandth part, gold acts upon defective silver.
By this ordered procedure, ash of tin is produced.
With that same thousandth part, he should cause <s>vedha</s> (penetration) in copper.
That copper becomes silver, resembling conch shell, jasmine, and the moon.
The essence of white mica, and iron, both magnetic and non-magnetic,

children.text: vaṅgaṃ tāraṃ tathā śvetaṃ vaikrāntaṃ ca kadambakam ||
children.translated_text: tin, silver, likewise white metal, <s>vaikrānta</s>, and <s>kadambaka</s>:
when smelted in a sealed crucible, they become a <s>khoṭa</s> (metallic lump) resembling jasmine and the moon.

children.text: taṃ khoṭaṃ sūkṣmacūrṇaṃ tu drutasūtena golakam ||
children.translated_text: That <s>khoṭa</s>, made into fine powder, is made into a pellet with liquid mercury.
One part of incinerated diamond and four parts of the pellet:
he should triturate them in a heated mortar; the mercury becomes ash.
He should incinerate it in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus by the sequence of seven <s>saṃkalikās</s>.
Then an ash is produced, resembling conch shell, jasmine, and the moon.

children.text: tadbhasma palamekaṃ tu palamekaṃ tu gandhakam
children.translated_text: One <s>pala</s> of that ash and one <s>pala</s> of sulfur
are smelted in a sealed crucible; a <s>khoṭa</s> is produced at once.
Having smelted it together with silver, and having subjected it to the three <s>sāraṇās</s>,
with that same thousandth part he should cause <s>vedha</s> in copper.
Eight <s>palas</s> of sharp mercury and eight <s>palas</s> of liquid mercury
he should triturate in a heated mortar with the juice of <s>kuṣṭha</s> bark.
At once a mass is produced, a pellet together with iron.
He should triturate it in a heated mortar; it becomes ash at once.
He should incinerate it in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus by the sequence of seven <s>saṃkalikās</s>.
With one sixteenth part of that same substance, he should cause <s>vedha</s> in tin.
One <s>pala</s> of that ash and one <s>pala</s> of sulfur
are smelted in a sealed crucible; a <s>khoṭa</s> is produced at once.

children.text: tasya khoṭasya bhāgaṃ ca tīkṣṇacūrṇaṃ ca tatsamam
children.translated_text: One part of that <s>khoṭa</s>, and an equal amount of powdered <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (iron),

children.text: dvau bhāgau drutasūtasya sarvam ekatra mardayet ||
children.translated_text: and two parts of liquid mercury: he should triturate everything together.

children.text: taptakhalle tu saṃmardya golako bhavati kṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: When triturated in a heated mortar, it becomes a pellet at once.
He should incinerate it in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus by the sequence of seven <s>saṃkalikās</s>.
All that becomes ash, resembling conch shell, jasmine, and the moon.

children.text: tadbhasma kārayet khoṭaṃ tīkṣṇena dvaṃdvitaṃ saha ||
children.translated_text: He should make that ash into a <s>khoṭa</s>, compounded together with <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (iron).
By this ordered procedure, through the sequence of seven <s>saṃkalikās</s>,
he should afterward digest that ash, after it has been subjected to the three <s>sāraṇās</s>.
With one hundred-thousandth part of that same substance, he should cause <s>vedha</s> in tin.
One <s>pala</s> of ash-mercury should be smeared onto purified tin.

children.text: mardayedāyase pātre vaṅgaṃ tu mriyate kṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: He should triturate it in an iron vessel; the tin is killed at once.
Two <s>palas</s> of killed tin, and two <s>palas</s> of silver powder,

children.text: dvipalaṃ gandhakaṃ dadyāt palaikaṃ ṭaṅkaṇasya ca
children.translated_text: he should add two <s>palas</s> of sulfur and one <s>pala</s> of borax.
Smelted in a sealed crucible, it becomes a <s>khoṭa</s> at once.
One <s>pala</s> of powdered <s>khoṭa</s> and one <s>pala</s> of liquid mercury
he should triturate with the sour juice of citron; it becomes a pellet at once.
With one sixteenth part of that same substance, he should cause <s>vedha</s> in copper.
In place of tin he should put lead, and in place of silver, gold.

children.text: pūrvavat kramayogeṇa rasaṃ khoṭaṃ tu kārayet
children.translated_text: By the ordered procedure as before, he should make the <s>rasa</s> into a <s>khoṭa</s>.

children.text: taṃ khoṭaṃ sūkṣmacūrṇaṃ tu drutasūtena golakam ||
children.translated_text: That <s>khoṭa</s>, made into fine powder, is made into a pellet with liquid mercury.
With one sixteenth part of that same substance, he should cause <s>vedha</s> in defective silver.
One <s>pala</s> of killed tin and one <s>pala</s> of mercury,
and one <s>pala</s> of powdered essence: he should mix the three together.
He should triturate them with the sour juice of citron; it becomes a pellet at once.
One part of incinerated diamond and four parts of the pellet:
he should triturate them together in a mortar, joined with the liquid of herbs.
He should incinerate it in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus with a set of seven <s>puṭas</s>.

children.text: tat sarvaṃ jāyate bhasma vajrasyaiva prabhāvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: All that becomes ash through the very power of diamond.
O <s>Devi</s>, he should put sea salt and <s>triphalā</s> into the ash.
Having combined them, he should triturate them for three days in the milk of <s>vajrī</s>.
Kept in a <s>Viśvāmitra</s> bowl, he should give it a <s>puṭa</s> in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus.
All that becomes ash, resembling conch shell, jasmine, and the moon.
With just a barley-grain measure of it, he solidifies tin at once.

children.text: vaṅgaṃ tāraṃ tathā sattvaṃ samasūtena golakam ||
children.translated_text: Tin, silver, and the essence are made into a pellet with an equal amount of mercury.
By this ordered procedure he should incinerate each separately.

children.text: tat sarvaṃ jāyate bhasma vajrasyaiva prabhāvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: All that becomes ash through the very power of diamond.
One <s>pala</s> of ash-mercury and two <s>palas</s> of tin ash,
two <s>palas</s> of killed silver, and two <s>palas</s> of essence ash,
five <s>palas</s> of conch-shell powder and eight <s>palas</s> of sea salt,
and eight <s>palas</s> of borax: he should triturate everything together.
Grinding it with the milk of <s>vajrī</s>, he should give fourteen <s>puṭas</s>.
This is truly a perfected <s>rasa</s>, difficult even for the thirty gods to obtain.

children.text: vaṅgaṃ tu drāvayet paścāt bhāṇḍe caiva tu mṛnmaye
children.translated_text: Then he should melt tin in an earthen vessel.
When the ash is perfected, he should stir it with an iron rod.
He should carefully cast it in until it becomes hard.
Smelted in a sealed crucible, it becomes beautiful silver.
Sometimes, when the silver has been heated in a <s>puṭa</s>, he should again add <s>vaṅga</s>.

children.text: pattre dāhe kaṣe chede tattāraṃ śāśvataṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: If, as a sheet, it withstands burning, testing on the touchstone, and cutting, that silver becomes permanent.
That stabilized material and the ball, furnished with a sixteenth part,
together with one part of dead diamond, he should triturate in one place.
He should triturate it with <s>devadālī</s> and <s>śaṅkhapuṣpī</s>, using their juice.
He should kill it in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus by means of seven <s>puṭa</s> heatings.

children.text: tadbhasma tu punaḥ paścāt dīpayantreṇa pācayet ||
children.translated_text: Then afterward he should cook that ash again by means of the lamp-apparatus.
One <s>pala</s> of ash-mercury, two <s>palas</s> of white mica,
one <s>pala</s> of powdered conch-shell, and one <s>pala</s> of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>:
having combined all that into one, he should grind it with the milk of <s>vajrī</s>.
Afterward he should give fourteen <s>puṭa</s> heatings with forest fuel-cakes.
This <s>rasa</s>, in the measure of a barley grain, stabilizes <s>vaṅga</s> at once.
One <s>pala</s> of black mica and two <s>palas</s> of dead <s>sūtaka</s>,
and one <s>pala</s> of sulfur: having brought them together, he should triturate them.
When it is carefully triturated, it becomes a ball at once.
One part of dead diamond and four parts of the ball:
he should triturate it for one <s>prahara</s>; the <s>sūtaka</s> becomes ash.
He should give a <s>puṭa</s> in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus with forest cow-dung fuel.
By this sequence of procedure he should make it into a sevenfold preparation.
With that very substance, in the hundredth part, he should bring about the piercing of <s>nāga</s>.
Afterward he should color that <s>khoṭa</s> with copper, mica, and <s>kapālī</s>.
Again afterward he should color it with <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, copper, and <s>kapālī</s>.
Again afterward he should color it with <s>nāga</s>, mica, and <s>kapālī</s>.
Having melted it together with gold, after it has been made to pass through the three <s>sāraṇā</s> operations,
with that very substance, in the thousandth part, he should bring about the piercing of copper.
Divine gold is produced, the finest ornament of the gods.
Diamond ash, heated in the milk of <s>snuhī</s> by ten <s>puṭas</s>,

children.text: tattulyaṃ mardayet sūtaṃ devadālyā rasaiḥ puṭet ||
children.translated_text: should be triturated with an equal amount of <s>sūta</s>; he should heat it with the juices of <s>devadālī</s>.

children.text: tattulyaṃ ca puṭettīkṣṇaṃ triphalāyā rasena tu
children.translated_text: He should heat an equal amount of <s>tīkṣṇa</s> with the juice of <s>triphalā</s>.
He should heat an equal amount of <s>nāga</s> with <s>mahimārāṭa</s> and <s>rūṣaka</s>.
When combined in a twentieth part, that indeed gives a golden color.
With this in a sixty-fourth part, he should color purified silver.
With that very substance in an eighth part, he should smear sheets of <s>nāga</s>.
He should heat and kill the <s>nāga</s> until it resembles red vermilion.
He should kill an equal amount of gold and heat it in the juice of <s>kāñcanāra</s>.
He should kill an equal amount of copper with the juice of <s>gṛhakanyā</s>.
Afterward he should heat it with a sour liquid until it resembles vermilion.
He should color <s>candrārka</s> with that and pierce it with a hundredth part.

children.text: sabījaṃ bījavarjaṃ vā vajreṇa saha sūtakam
children.translated_text: With seed or without seed, <s>sūtaka</s> together with diamond:
afterward he should triturate that ash with the essence of gold leaf.

children.text: tenaiva vedhayecchulvaṃ śulvaṃ tāre tu yojayet ||
children.translated_text: With that he should pierce copper; he should combine copper with silver.
With diamond he should combine gold, and with gold he should combine <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: rasena dvaṃdvayeddehaṃ sa deho hy ajarāmaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: With <s>rasa</s> he should combine the body; that body is indeed free from old age and death.
Plantain bulb and <s>sauvīra</s>, drenched with the juice of <s>kaṇṭakārī</s>,
are the <s>krāmaṇa</s> for all metals, the blending agent in all pairings.
The five parts of <s>timira</s>, joined with seeds of <s>mārjārī</s>,
should be brought together and triturated; with that he should pierce diamond.
Blown in a diamond crucible, it should make the pairing with gold.
Powder of magnetic stone, <s>bhūlatā</s>, <s>rāmaṭha</s>, honey,
<s>guñjā</s>, <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, glass, crab bone, and milk of <s>snuhī</s>:

children.text: etat sarvaṃ samaṃ yojyaṃ strīstanyena ca mardayet
children.translated_text: all this should be combined in equal measure and triturated with woman's breast milk.
When applied as a crucible coating at the edge, it easily causes diamond to fuse.
In a forced fire, in a diamond crucible, even hard diamonds fuse.

children.text: susūkṣmā rajakā bhūtvā hy ekībhāvaṃ vrajanti te ||
children.translated_text: Becoming extremely fine dust, they attain a single state.
When smelted with a mixture of glass and <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, it obtains purification.
And through many crucibles it becomes a mass of brilliance.
One part of dead diamond and sixteen parts of <s>hāṭaka</s>:

children.text: śvetakācasya cūrṇaṃ tu bhāgān ṣoḍaśa dāpayet ||
children.translated_text: he should add sixteen parts of powdered white glass.
Smelted in a sealed crucible, he should make the binding of diamond.
By this sequence of procedure he should apply it seven times.

children.text: milate tatkṣaṇaṃ vajraṃ hemnā tu salilaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: The diamond immediately joins with gold, like water.
He should add dead diamond to powder of a human skull.
Smelted in a sealed crucible, it mixes with gold at once.
A <s>bhṛṅga</s> wing, human hair, dead <s>kānta</s>, together with <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>,
and the dung of a young calf should be ground with woman's breast milk.

children.text: mūṣālepaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā vajre hema ca dāpayet
children.translated_text: Then, having made a crucible coating, he should place diamond and gold in it.
Smelted in a sealed crucible, diamond fuses; there is no other way.

children.text: kāntaṃ vajraṃ tathā guñjā gandhakaṃ ca catuṣṭayam
children.translated_text: <s>Kānta</s>, diamond, <s>guñjā</s>, and sulfur: these four

children.text: stanakṣīreṇa piṣṭaṃ tu mūṣālepaṃ tu kārayet ||
children.translated_text: should be ground with breast milk and made into a crucible coating.
Smelted in a sealed crucible, diamond fuses at once.
He should impregnate dead diamond with the milk of <s>uttaravāruṇī</s>.
Inside a gold paste, he should place the diamond right there.
He should wrap it with birch bark and wrap it outside with cloth.
It should be placed within grain continuously for one fortnight.

children.text: uddhṛtaṃ tat prayatnena vajrabandhaṃ tu kārayet
children.translated_text: When it has been carefully taken out, he should perform the binding of diamond.
Molten diamonds are to be fused by that very means, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.
That should be known as a fused binding, capable of a hundred-thousandfold <s>vedha</s> (penetration).

children.text: ratnānāṃ tu tathā sarvān vedhayitvā yathāvidhi
children.translated_text: And likewise, after causing <s>vedha</s> in all the gems according to rule,
it becomes hundred-thousandfold in <s>vedha</s> and bestows bodily perfection.
<s>Musalī</s>, <s>citraka</s>, barren <s>karkoṭī</s>, <s>kandapadminī</s>,
<s>kañcukī</s>, <s>nīlasindūrī</s>, <s>vāsā</s>, and likewise <s>nāgabalā</s>:
the juices of these, and also the liquefactions of the gems, should be placed in a bronze vessel.
After keeping them in the sun, he should then make a fire beneath.

children.text: oṣadhīnāṃ rasaṃ kṛtvā svacchaṃ kṛtvā punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having made the juice of the herbs and clarified it again and again,

children.text: yāmamātraṃ ca gharme tu drutirmilati vai rasam ||
children.translated_text: in heat for the measure of a <s>yāma</s>, the liquefaction indeed combines with the <s>rasa</s> (mercury).

children.text: na teṣāṃ krāmaṇaṃ śakyaṃ vaktuṃ varṣaśatairapi ||
children.translated_text: Their <s>krāmaṇa</s> (activating projection) could not be described even in a hundred years.
Rock salt, neem leaves, and <s>vākucī</s>, wrapped in a tube,
are considered the supreme mixture with the juice of melted mica.
Diamond, the pairing of substances, O mistress, and the killing of mercury by diamond,
the killing with seed, and also the binding as <s>khoṭa</s> have been taught.
Tell me that, O goddess; what else do you wish to hear?
<s>Śrīdevī</s> said:
With the great minerals, the secondary minerals, and the metals, O <s>Parameśvara</s>,
command the complete binding of the king of <s>rasa</s>.
<s>Śrībhairava</s> said:

children.text: vaikrāntasya tu bhāgaikaṃ cāṣṭabhāgaṃ tu sūtakam
children.translated_text: One part of <s>vaikrānta</s> and eight parts of mercury,
seven parts of gold, <s>dvipadīrasa</s>, and borax:

children.text: naṣṭapiṣṭaṃ ca śuṣkaṃ ca dhmātaṃ khoṭo bhavet priye
children.translated_text: when it is ground until lost, dried, and smelted, it becomes a <s>khoṭa</s>, beloved.

children.text: sauvīraṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ kācaṃ dattvā dattvā tu śodhayet ||
children.translated_text: He should purify it by repeatedly adding <s>sauvīra</s>, borax, and glass.
Then, having combined the mercury placed in a crucible with an equal quantity of gold,
he should make it consume an equal portion with purified mercury.
He should smelt <s>vaikrānta</s>, in a sixteenth part, by the preceding procedure.
Through the procedure of ten <s>saṃkalikās</s>, the <s>vedha</s> is increased tenfold.
Through the procedure of seven <s>saṃkalikās</s>, the <s>vedha</s> is increased tenfold.

children.text: vaikrānto vajravat jñeyo nātra kāryā vicāraṇā
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikrānta</s> should be understood as like diamond; there is no need for reflection here.
Again I shall teach another procedure, rare upon the earth.
O goddess, the essence of <s>vaikrānta</s>, joined with mercury,
digested with an equal amount of gold, should be deposited in a stone vessel.
After it has remained in the ground for a month, he should carefully take it up.

children.text: eṣa devi raso divyo dehadravyakaro bhavet ||
children.translated_text: This, O goddess, is a divine <s>rasa</s>; it brings about body and wealth.

children.text: vaikrāntakāstu ye kecit triphalāyā rasena ca
children.translated_text: Whatever kinds of <s>vaikrānta</s> there are, with the juice of <s>triphalā</s>,
with the essence of <s>bhūmyāmalaka</s>, and with the juice of <s>vasuhaṭṭa</s>,
each one, O goddess, when steamed for seven days and likewise triturated,
and well smelted in a sealed crucible, becomes an imperishable <s>khoṭa</s>.

children.text: kāntaṃ rūpyaṃ sakanakaṃ pāradaṃ caiva yojayet
children.translated_text: He should combine lodestone, silver, gold, and mercury,
and copper as a third part, together with <s>srotoñjana</s>.

children.text: tat dhmātaṃ khoṭatāṃ yāti dehalohakaraṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: When smelted, that goes to the state of <s>khoṭa</s> and becomes productive of body and metal.
He should triturate powdered white <s>vaikrānta</s> with horse urine.

children.text: ādau susvinnam ādāya pale palaśataṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Having first taken it after it has been well steamed, he should cast one hundred <s>palas</s> into one <s>pala</s>.
An ash of silver is produced, having the appearance of pure crystal.
The skilled man should mix that ash into mercury in an equal part.
He should make silver circulate in mercury and triturate it with horse urine.
He should heat it in a sealed crucible, gradually, with a gentle fire.
The skilled man should place it in a crucible, furnished with <s>krāmaṇa</s>.
In one day and night, or in three nights, the <s>rasa</s> becomes able to withstand fire.
By mere contact it will make all metals into silver.
When consumed in the manner to be stated, it destroys old age and poverty.
The operation for the red one will be described; it destroys old age and poverty.
He should impregnate its powder seven times with water from the tuber of <s>vyāghrī</s>.

children.text: palaṃ tasya palaṃ hemnaḥ palaṃ śuddharasasya ca
children.translated_text: One <s>pala</s> of that, one <s>pala</s> of gold, and one <s>pala</s> of purified mercury:

children.text: śuddhaṃ bhasma bhavet sarvaṃ punarhemaśataṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: all becomes purified ash; then he should add one hundred <s>palas</s> of gold.
That ash is produced quickly, with a brilliance equal to pure gold.

children.text: tadbhasma rasarāje tu punarhemnā ca melayet
children.translated_text: He should then mix that ash into the king of <s>rasa</s>, again with gold.
It becomes able to withstand fire, O goddess; then it becomes an excellent <s>rasa</s>.
The mercury becomes effective by contact, and the great <s>rasa</s> has ten-millionfold <s>vedha</s>.

children.text: raktavaikrāntasattvaṃ ca hemnā tu saha melayet
children.translated_text: He should mix the essence of red <s>vaikrānta</s> with gold.

children.text: samaṃ taṃ jārayet sūtaṃ sārayitvā samena tu
children.translated_text: He should digest that equal mercury, after causing it to flow with an equal amount.
With a thousandth part it penetrates metals; there is no doubt here.
One part of black <s>vaikrānta</s> and a <s>pala</s>-portion of purified mercury:

children.text: ekatra mardayet khalle cūrṇaṃ ca bhavati dvayam ||
children.translated_text: he should triturate them together in a mortar, and the two become powder.
One part of this powder and a thousand parts of gold

children.text: ekatra mardayet tāvad yāvadbhasma tu jāyate ||
children.translated_text: he should triturate together until ash is produced.
He should smelt that in a sealed crucible until it becomes a <s>khoṭa</s>.
He should make it consume an equal portion of purified mercury.
It penetrates all metals by mere contact, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.

children.text: taccūrṇam abhrakaṃ caiva rasena saha mardayet
children.translated_text: He should triturate that powder and mica together with mercury.

children.text: ekatra mardayet tāvad yāvad bhasma prajāyate ||
children.translated_text: He should triturate them together until ash is produced.
He should smelt that in a sealed crucible until it becomes a <s>khoṭa</s>.

children.text: samāṃśaṃ bhakṣaṇaṃ tasya piṣṭikāṃ kārayed budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The wise man should make its equal-portion consumption into a paste.
It penetrates all metals; by mere contact there is the state of gold.

children.text: taccūrṇam abhrakaṃ caiva rasena saha mardayet ||
children.translated_text: He should triturate that powder and mica together with mercury.
He should steam it and digest it; then it becomes able to withstand fire.
That <s>rasa</s>, once made to flow, penetrates all metals.
For yellow <s>vaikrānta</s> too, the procedure for the red and black kinds is accepted.
Powdered yellow <s>vaikrānta</s> should be combined with powdered gold.
Having mixed the <s>mahārasa</s> with powder of yellow <s>abhraka</s> (mica),
heated and triturated, in a month the <s>rasa</s> becomes able to withstand fire.

children.text: śvetaṃ pītaṃ tathā kṛṣṇaṃ raktavarṇaṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: White, yellow, likewise black, and also red in color:
thus, O fair-complexioned one, there are four kinds of color in <s>vaikrānta</s>.

children.text: vajrasthāne tu vaikrānto melanaṃ paramaṃ matam
children.translated_text: But in place of diamond, <s>vaikrānta</s> is considered the supreme admixture.
And the <s>pārada</s> which works upon the body and metals becomes iron-like, O beloved.
Blue-colored <s>vaikrānta</s>, combined with <s>rasa</s>, is killed.
That which is joined with black <s>abhraka</s> and mixed with honey and ghee,
if one eats it for a <s>maṇḍala</s>, O <s>Devi</s>, he lives as long as the moon, sun, and stars.

children.text: yasya yasya hi yo yogaḥ tasya tasya prayogataḥ
children.translated_text: For whatever person there is a given preparation, for him, through the use of that preparation,
having mixed in a <s>guñjā</s>-measure of <s>rasa</s>, combined with the three sweets,
the proper diet is milk, ghee, and rice; he should avoid all other food.
In seclusion, staying on a small bed, the man should remain apart from habitation.
The <s>Rasamṛtyuñjaya</s> mantra should always be recited within the heart.

children.text: paśūnāṃ vimukhastatra strīṇāṃ caiva na darśanam
children.translated_text: There he should avoid animals, and there should be no sight of women.
With all his limbs smeared with ash, intent on mantra and meditation,
the mortal proceeds for a year; his attainment is certain.
He should triturate <s>rasa</s> in citron juice together with the essence of <s>vaikrānta</s>;
he should heat it with gentle warmth and fill it with water.

children.text: sattvaṃ sūtaṃ ca saṃmiśrya dhamet syād rasabandhanam
children.translated_text: Mixing the essence and <s>sūta</s> together, he should smelt them; binding of the <s>rasa</s> will occur.

children.text: baddhaṃ rasaṃ mukhe kṣiptvā bhūmichidrāṇi paśyati ||
children.translated_text: Putting the bound <s>rasa</s> in his mouth, he sees openings in the earth.
