He should triturate one <s>niṣka</s> of <s>vaikrānta</s> with horse urine;
after triturating this for one day, O <s>Devi</s>, it becomes killed.
Having done this for four days, he should bring in an equal amount of <s>sūta</s>.
The trituration and heating are as before, with the mind purified.
Among the seven pairs each should be one; the seventh and eighth should amount to one <s>pala</s>.
He should triturate with sour citron juices and give sixty-four <s>puṭas</s>.
Resembling the red of dawn, it pierces all metals.

children.text: kṛṣṇābhrakasya sattvaṃ ca rasaṃ hemasamaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: The essence of black <s>abhraka</s> and <s>rasa</s> should be equal to gold;
placing them in a diamond crucible, he should smelt them and bring them to the state of a <s>khoṭa</s>.

children.text: baddhaṃ rasaṃ mukhe kṣiptvā hy ajarāmaratāṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: Putting the bound <s>rasa</s> in his mouth, he attains freedom from old age and death.
Having mixed that same ash, it should be equal to black <s>abhraka</s>.
He should triturate it for a day with water from the root of <s>śalyāviśalyā</s>.
Set in the <s>bhramara</s> apparatus, it should receive a <s>puṭa</s> for seven days.

children.text: tacchuddhaṃ bhasma sevyaṃ syāt guñjāmānaṃ tu maṇḍalam ||
children.translated_text: That purified ash should be consumed, a <s>guñjā</s>-measure for a <s>maṇḍala</s>.
The first, the fifth, the middle, and again the first are commended.
By binding as before, O <s>Devi</s>, the <s>mahārasa</s> effects <s>koṭi-vedha</s>.
Red-colored magnetite, with a luster like lac-dye,
when broken, resembles women's blood; its powder, combined with <s>sūta</s>,
he should triturate with goat's blood; when smelted it becomes a <s>khoṭa</s>, O beloved.

children.text: sa sūtaḥ śatavedhī tu sarvavyādhiharo bhavet
children.translated_text: That <s>sūta</s> effects hundredfold <s>vedha</s> and removes all diseases.
One should keep the pellet in the mouth; he lives for a thousand years.
Yellow-colored magnetite, when broken, has a luster like gold.
It pierces all metals by mere touch, O beautiful one.
<s>Lāṅgalī</s>, oleander, <s>citraka</s>, and <s>girikarṇikā</s>,
women's milk, borax, and <s>sauvīra</s>: he should make these into a coating for the crucible.
Twice as much <s>sūta</s> as <s>capala</s>, and twice as much gold as <s>sūta</s>,

children.text: naṣṭapiṣṭaṃ tu tat kuryāt andhamūṣāgataṃ dhamet ||
children.translated_text: he should make that into <s>naṣṭapiṣṭa</s>; placed in a sealed crucible, he should smelt it.

children.text: tatra sthito rasendro'yaṃ khoṭo bhavati śobhanaḥ
children.translated_text: The lord of <s>rasa</s> standing there becomes a beautiful <s>khoṭa</s>.
It should pierce lead by one-hundredth part, and it becomes the color of <s>guñjā</s>.
With that lead, at one-hundredth part, copper becomes red.
With that copper, at one-hundredth part, silver is pierced and becomes gold.

children.text: capalasya tu ṣaḍbhāgāḥ tārabhāgāstu sapta ca
children.translated_text: There are six parts of <s>capala</s>, and seven parts of silver,

children.text: aṣṭau kanakabhāgāstu nava bhāgā rasasya tu ||
children.translated_text: eight parts of gold, and nine parts of <s>rasa</s>.
Combined, O praised by the gods, they make thirty parts.

children.text: citrakaṃ karavīraṃ ca lāṅgalī gṛdhraviṭ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Citraka</s>, oleander, <s>lāṅgalī</s>, and vulture droppings,
triturated in sour citron juice: he should make a coating for the crucible.
Having sealed it, he should smelt it, O <s>Devi</s>; it becomes a beautiful <s>khoṭa</s>.
Pierced by one-hundredth part of that <s>khoṭa</s>, lead becomes ruddy.

children.text: tena nāgena viddhaṃ tu śulvaṃ guñjānibhaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Copper pierced by that lead becomes like <s>guñjā</s>.

children.text: tena śulvena tāraṃ tu viddhaṃ bhavati kāñcanam ||
children.translated_text: Silver pierced by that copper becomes gold.

children.text: hemābhaṃ capalaṃ devi pādārdhena tu saṃyutam
children.translated_text: Golden-looking <s>capala</s>, O <s>Devi</s>, should be combined with half a quarter-part.

children.text: pādena kanakaṃ dattvā kunaṭyā mardayet kṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: Adding gold by a quarter part, he should triturate it for a moment with <s>kunaṭī</s>.
<s>Lāṅgalī</s>, <s>citraka</s>, women's milk, and oleander,

children.text: gṛdhraviṣṭhā tathā sarvaṃ mūṣālepaṃ tu kārayet ||
children.translated_text: and vulture droppings: he should make all this into a coating for the crucible.

children.text: tanmadhye tu sthitaṃ dhmātaṃ khoṭo bhavati śobhanaḥ
children.translated_text: Smelted while placed in the middle of that, it becomes a beautiful <s>khoṭa</s>.
He should pierce the previously stated substance with this; seedless gold results.
Into a well-heated iron vessel he should cast a full <s>pala</s>.

children.text: sabījaṃ pāradaṃ kṛtvā capalasya tu vāpayet
children.translated_text: Having made seeded mercury, he should cast it upon <s>capala</s>.
The <s>sūta</s>, lac-like, is bound, as a great elephant by an elephant.
One <s>pala</s> of purified <s>sūta</s> and one <s>pala</s> of sulfur,
having combined and then triturated them with the juice of <s>dhuttūra</s>,
he should soak it by the <s>cakra</s> procedure; the <s>sūtaka</s> becomes ash.
Smelted inside a sealed crucible, it becomes a beautiful <s>khoṭa</s>.

children.text: sūtaṃ hema ca nāgaṃ ca candrārkau cāpi vedhayet ||
children.translated_text: It pierces <s>sūta</s>, gold, lead, and also silver and copper.
One <s>pala</s> of purified <s>sūta</s> and one <s>karṣa</s> of sulfur
He should grind it in a smooth mortar, soaked in the juice of <s>devadālī</s>.
He should grind it with his fingers; then a sulfur paste is produced.
He should grind it for one day with the juice of citron and fresh ginger.
Then he should grind it for three days with a decoction of <s>palāśa</s> root.
He should make a fine pellet combined with the five solvents.
He should coat that pellet with a paste of <s>palāśa</s> root.
He should smelt it; by combination with glass and borax a white <s>khoṭa</s> is produced.
He should purify it carefully until it reaches clarity.
With that <s>khoṭa</s>, O <s>Devi</s>, he should then color three times as much lead.
Afterward he should color it hundreds of times with purified mica-capsules.

children.text: śulve tāre ca khoṭo'yaṃ sahasrāṃśena vedhakaḥ
children.translated_text: In copper and in silver this <s>khoṭa</s> has <s>vedha</s> power at one-thousandth part.
With mercury killed by sulfur, he should make the killed metals flow.
Again, having combined it with gold, perform the feeding in equal measure.

children.text: jārite śulvatāre ca ghoṣaṃ vidhyati sūtakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When copper and silver have been digested, the mercury penetrates bell-metal.
Having made the <s>rasa</s> equal to gold, he should take sulfur half as much as the pellet,
mixed with <s>dvipadīrajas</s>, and grind it together with borax.

children.text: naṣṭapiṣṭaṃ ca tat śulvaṃ dhmātaṃ khoṭo bhavettataḥ
children.translated_text: When that copper has become a vanished paste, once smelted it then becomes a <s>khoṭa</s>.

children.text: sauvīraṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ kācaṃ dattvā dattvā tu śodhayet ||
children.translated_text: He should purify it again and again by adding <s>sauvīra</s>, borax, and glass.
Without loss, it joins with gold, and the combination takes place.
He should perform equal feeding into gold with purified mercury.

children.text: naṣṭapiṣṭaṃ ca tacchulvaṃ dhmātaṃ khoṭo bhavettataḥ
children.translated_text: When that copper has become a vanished paste, once smelted it then becomes a <s>khoṭa</s>.
He should grind it mixed with <s>dvipadīrajas</s> and furnished with borax.
Pierced with one sixteenth part of silver and copper, it becomes gold.
Joined with half as much gold, that substance reaches equality with the mother substance.
By employing a <s>saṃkalikā</s>, he should make the <s>vedha</s> ten times greater.
As in gold, so too in silver he should apply the initial seeds.
Bound by the third <s>saṃkalā</s>, it should penetrate with a six-hundredth part.
With that same substance in fourfold strength, gold is produced with a thousandth part.
If, by this ordered procedure, there are seven <s>saṃkalikās</s>,
O <s>Sundari</s>, it makes the eight metals into divine gold.
Then, after powdering it again, he should heat it in a <s>puṭa</s>; ash is produced.
O <s>Devi</s>, when one <s>pala</s> of it is consumed, it removes all diseases.
At two <s>palas</s> it gives the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>; at three, that of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: catuḥpale tu rudratvam īśaḥ pañcapale bhavet ||
children.translated_text: At four <s>palas</s>, one gains the state of <s>Rudra</s>; at five <s>palas</s>, one becomes <s>Īśa</s>.
When six <s>palas</s> are consumed, O <s>Devi</s>, one has the body of <s>Sadāśiva</s>.
Mercury, sulfur, and silver, together with the juice of <s>meṣavallī</s>,
he should grind vigorously for three days and mix it with one quarter part of tin.
Smelted inside a blind crucible, it solidifies tin at once.
Powdered sulfur, O <s>Devi</s>, impregnated with the juice of <s>markaṭī</s>,
he should impregnate it a hundred times; it becomes living ash.
He should kindle it in an earthen vessel, combined with mercury.
He should heat it by the sun's heat, together with the juice of <s>markaṭī</s>.

children.text: gandhakaṃ grasate sūtaḥ piṣṭikā bhavati kṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: The mercury swallows the sulfur; a pellet is produced at once.
With the juice of <s>tilaparṇī</s> alone he should impregnate sulfur, beloved,

children.text: sapta vārāṃstu deveśi chāyāśuṣkaṃ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: seven times, O <s>Deveśī</s>, drying it in the shade again and again.
A one-<s>pala</s> measure of purified and distilled mercury, beloved,
having placed it inside a crucible, together with <s>narendrarasa</s>,
he should digest it in a sand apparatus with the sulfur that has again been impregnated.

children.text: truṭitruṭi pradātavyaṃ gandhakaṃ ca punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: The sulfur should be added little by little, again and again.
By this ordered procedure a sulfur paste is produced.
Powder of sulfur-stone, with the juice of <s>kanaka</s>,
having combined them and ground them properly in a mortar,
he should place it in the sun, O <s>Devi</s>, with the juice of <s>kanaka</s>.
He should impregnate it seven times, and seven times with menstrual blood.
Then he should put one <s>pala</s> of purified mercury on a potsherd.
He should add the impregnated sulfur mixed with human bile.
He should heat and agitate it by the sun's heat; a pellet is produced at once.
Fine powder of sulfur with sour chickpea gruel, O <s>Bhairavi</s>,
he should impregnate seven times, and seven times with menstrual blood.
Into the middle of molten mercury he should add equal amounts of camphor and sulfur,
and place it in a cow pen; after seven days there is sulfur paste.
The seed of bitter <s>kośātakī</s> and the bulb of <s>caṇḍālī</s>,
having crushed them with breast milk, he should coat the pellet with that.
He should heat it in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus; it is fixed, without doubt.
Inside a gold capsule he should make the combination.
With one eighth part of that same substance he should produce <s>vedha</s> in lead.
That lead becomes divine, resembling vermilion-red color.
With that lead, at one eighth part, he should produce <s>vedha</s> in copper.
With that same substance, at one sixteenth part, he should produce <s>vedha</s> in silver.
That silver becomes gold; this is the doctrine of <s>Siddhayogeśvarī</s>.
One <s>pala</s> of sulfur paste and eight <s>palas</s> of lead paste:
he should smear them on lead leaves and then dry them in the shade.
He should coat the lead leaves with a mass of <s>āṭarūṣaka</s>.
O <s>Devi</s>, he should give three <s>puṭas</s> with wild cow-dung cakes.
That lead is killed and becomes divine, resembling vermilion-red color.
One <s>pala</s> of that lead and eight <s>palas</s> of powdered copper:
he should grind them for one watch with the juice of <s>vāsaka</s>.
He should kill it in a distillation apparatus; that copper is killed at once.
With one sixteenth part of that same substance, he should cause <s>vedha</s> in silver.
Divine gold is produced, the finest ornament for the gods.

children.text: yā kācidgandhapiṣṭī tu ādau nāgaṃ tu mārayet
children.translated_text: Whatever sulfur-paste there may be, at the beginning it should kill lead.

children.text: nāgaṃ tu vedhayecchulvaṃ śulvaṃ tāraṃ tu vedhayet
children.translated_text: He should make lead penetrate copper, and copper penetrate silver.
Divine gold is produced; this is declared to be a perfected procedure.
Sulfur, combined with honey and triturated with <s>Harabīja</s> (Hara's seed),
when placed in the earth for six months, makes silver become gold.
Rubbing with that same substance destroys <s>kuṣṭha</s> disease.
Combined together with ghee, it destroys diseases of wounds.
By using it for a year, a man becomes one whose life spans a thousand years.
One <s>pala</s> of purified mercury and one <s>pala</s> of <s>tālaka</s>,
having combined them, he should triturate them with the juice of <s>unmatta</s>.
He should kill it in the <s>cakra</s> apparatus; the mercury becomes ash.
Smelted in a sealed crucible, it becomes a fine <s>khoṭa</s>.

children.text: vaṅgaṃ tāraṃ ca śulvaṃ ca kramaśo vedhayedrasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>rasa</s> should successively penetrate tin, silver, and copper.
One <s>pala</s> of purified tin and one <s>pala</s> of mercury,
and two <s>palas</s> of <s>tālaka</s>, triturated with the juice of <s>unmatta</s>,
he should kill in the <s>pātana</s> apparatus; by blowing it, he should bring it to the state of a <s>khoṭa</s>.
One <s>pala</s> of <s>tālaka</s>-paste and one <s>pala</s> of sulfur,

children.text: dve pale śuddhasūtasya dinamekaṃ tu tena vai ||
children.translated_text: and two <s>palas</s> of purified mercury: with that, for one day,
having combined them, he should triturate them with the juice of <s>unmatta</s>.
He should kill it in the <s>pātana</s> apparatus; by blowing it, he should bring it to the state of a <s>khoṭa</s>.
One <s>pala</s> of purified lead and one <s>pala</s> of mercury,
and two <s>palas</s> of <s>kunaṭī</s>: he should triturate everything together.
He should kill it in the <s>pātana</s> apparatus; by blowing it, he should bring it to the state of a <s>khoṭa</s>.
One <s>pala</s> of gold-paste and one <s>pala</s> of sulfur,
having combined and triturated them with the juice of <s>dhuttūra</s>,
he should kill it in the <s>pātana</s> apparatus; by blowing it, he should bring it to the state of a <s>khoṭa</s>.

children.text: kṛṣṇābhrakasya sattvaṃ ca kāntaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca hāṭakam
children.translated_text: The essence of black mica, <s>kānta</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, and gold,

children.text: śuddhaśulvaṃ ca tāraṃ ca mākṣikaṃ samabhāgikam
children.translated_text: purified copper, silver, and <s>mākṣika</s>, in equal portions:
smelted in a sealed crucible, it becomes a <s>khoṭa</s> at once.
One <s>pala</s> of that <s>khoṭa</s> and one <s>pala</s> of mercury,
and two <s>palas</s> of <s>kunaṭī</s>: he should triturate everything together.
He should kill it in the <s>pātana</s> apparatus; by blowing it, he should bring it to the state of a <s>khoṭa</s>.
One <s>pala</s> of black mica, and likewise one <s>pala</s> of <s>rasaka</s>,
and one <s>pala</s> of mercury, all combined together, O dear one:
he should triturate them with the juice of <s>unmatta</s> for two <s>praharas</s>.
He should triturate them for one day, mixed with borax.
He should make a pellet, O <s>Devi</s>, and dry it in the shade.
Smelted in a great fire, the mercury becomes a <s>khoṭa</s>.
He should purify that <s>khoṭa</s> with white glass and borax.
Having fused it with gold and subjected it to three <s>sāraṇās</s>,
with one thousandth part of that same substance he should cause <s>vedha</s> in copper.
By this ordered procedure the <s>rasa</s> becomes capable of crore-fold penetration.
Two seeds of <s>palāśa</s> and one <s>pala</s> of mercury
he should triturate with the sour juice of citron and dry in the shade.

children.text: tumbī ca meghanādā ca kākajaṅghā ca cūlikā
children.translated_text: <s>Tumbī</s>, <s>Meghanādā</s>, <s>Kākajaṅghā</s>, and <s>Cūlikā</s>,
he should place in a crucible that has been smeared with woman's breast milk.
He should blow it with <s>khadira</s> charcoal; an inexhaustible <s>khoṭa</s> is produced.
He should triturate it with <s>palāśa</s> oil until it becomes a mercury-paste.
Smelted in a sealed crucible, it becomes a <s>khoṭa</s> at once.

children.text: pūrvaśuddhena sūtena saha hemnā ca pārvati
children.translated_text: With previously purified mercury and with gold, O <s>Pārvati</s>,
he should make a ball; having triturated it, he should make it molten.
The seeds of <s>brahmavṛkṣa</s>, cotton seed, and <s>vibhītaka</s>,

children.text: yavaciñcā tu vandhyā ca rājikā ca samanvitam ||
children.translated_text: together with <s>yavaciñcā</s>, <s>vandhyā</s>, and mustard seed:

children.text: sūkṣmapiṇḍīkṛtaṃ sarvaṃ tena liptvā tu golakam
children.translated_text: having made all of it into a fine powder, he should smear the ball with it.
With seven <s>puṭas</s>, O <s>Devi</s>, stabilization of the paste occurs.

children.text: bṛhatpuṭaṃ tato dattvā mūṣāyāṃ tattu bhāvayet
children.translated_text: Then, after giving it a large <s>puṭa</s>, he should process it in a crucible.

children.text: samāvartaṃ tu taṃ sūtaṃ samahemnā niyojitam
children.translated_text: He should combine that mercury with an equal amount of gold in a <s>samāvarta</s> procedure.
With one hundredth part, O you praised by the gods, he should penetrate <s>candra</s> and <s>arka</s>.
Again, by that same procedure, he should make stabilization of the paste.
Having subjected it to <s>sāraṇā</s>, he should then, with gold, make it penetrate a thousandfold.

children.text: evaṃ lakṣāṇi koṭiṃ ca vedhayet kramayogataḥ
children.translated_text: In this way, by the ordered procedure, he should make it penetrate lakhs and then a crore.

children.text: saptasaṃkalikād ūrdhvaṃ kṛtvā vaktre tu golakam
children.translated_text: After carrying out more than seven <s>saṃkalikās</s>, he should place the ball in his mouth.
In one year he becomes free from wrinkles and gray hair.
<s>Cāṇḍālī</s> and <s>Rākṣasī</s>, <s>rasa</s> arisen from <s>kuṇḍagola</s>,

children.text: bījaṃ sūtaṃ ca vaikrāntaṃ mardayet praharatrayam ||
children.translated_text: the seed, mercury, and <s>vaikrānta</s>: he should triturate them for three <s>praharas</s>.
Having made a purified ball, he should roast it in a <s>mūka</s> crucible.
A <s>khoṭa</s> is produced, O <s>Devi</s>, well smelted by a <s>khadira</s> fire.
With the juices and flowers of <s>Cāṇḍālī</s> and <s>Rākṣasī</s>, with honey, ghee, and borax,
he should also add mica, one among the eight great minerals.

children.text: nāgaṃ vaṅgaṃ samaṃ sūtaṃ hema tāramathāpi vā
children.translated_text: Lead, tin, an equal amount of mercury, or gold or silver,
or mica, <s>druti</s>, or essence: he should triturate them for two <s>praharas</s>.
Then, after drying the ball in the shade, he should heat it in a <s>mūka</s> crucible.

children.text: dattvā laghupuṭaṃ devi khoṭo bhavati śobhanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having given a light <s>puṭa</s>, O <s>Devi</s>, a fine <s>khoṭa</s> is produced.
<s>Rambhā</s>, <s>Vīrā</s>, the milk of <s>snuhī</s>, <s>Kañcukī</s>, and <s>Yavaciñcikā</s>,
and also <s>Vārāhī</s>, <s>Gorambhā</s>, <s>Mīnākṣī</s>, and <s>Kākamācikā</s>:
for mercury triturated with these, rebirth does not occur.
As before, by the ordered procedure, a fine <s>khoṭa</s> is produced.

children.text: viṣṇukrāntā ca cakrāṅkā balā ca tulasī tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇukrāntā</s>, <s>Cakrāṅkā</s>, <s>Balā</s>, and also <s>Tulasī</s>,
<s>Mahāsomāhivallī</s> and <s>Sūryāvarta</s>, O beautiful one:

children.text: ebhistu marditaḥ sūtaḥ pūrvavat khoṭatāṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: mercury triturated with these becomes a <s>khoṭa</s> as before.

children.text: mukhena grasate grāsaṃ jāraṇā tena sundari
children.translated_text: It takes in the morsel through its mouth; by that there is <s>jāraṇā</s> (digestion), O beautiful one.
Mercury triturated with the roots of <s>rasona</s> and <s>rājikā</s>, O fair-limbed one,
is to be cooked in a <s>puṭa</s> of divine herbs; this is the characteristic of a mercury-<s>khoṭa</s>.
This secret has been told to you; it should be understood by those who practice <s>rasavāda</s>.
By my grace, O queen of the gods, his success is beyond doubt.
The milk of <s>snuhī</s> with sour gruel, and the seeds of <s>kanaka</s>,
<s>Kañcukī</s>, <s>Lāṅgalī</s>, <s>Indravāruṇī</s>, and <s>Viṣamuṣṭikā</s>,
and water from the root of <s>palāśa</s>: with that he should triturate mercury.

children.text: same hemni samaṃ sūtaṃ piṣṭikāṃ kārayedbudhaḥ
children.translated_text: With an equal amount of gold and an equal amount of mercury, the wise man should make a <s>piṣṭikā</s> (paste).
For the sake of the <s>piṣṭikā</s>, he should triturate the <s>mahārasas</s> with the juices of herbs.
After triturating for three <s>yāmas</s>, the wise man should make a ball.
After binding the <s>piṣṭikā</s>, he should cook it in sulfur oil.
He should place the shade-dried ball in a sealed crucible.

children.text: tato laghupuṭaṃ dattvā khadirāgnau tu dhāmayet
children.translated_text: Then, after giving a light <s>puṭa</s>, he should blow it in a <s>khadira</s> fire.

children.text: khoṭastu jāyate hemni saha hemnā tu sārayet
children.translated_text: A <s>khoṭa</s> is produced in gold; he should carry out <s>sāraṇā</s> with gold.
Unexhausted, it combines with gold, and <s>samāvarta</s> arises.
By eating the mercury itself, a man becomes one with a divine body.
The mercury, colored and processed in sequence, penetrates all metals.
He should triturate mercury that consumes equal portions with the juices of herbs.

children.text: naṣṭapiṣṭaṃ tu taṃ kṛtvā pūrvayogena dhāmayet ||
children.translated_text: Having made it into a lost paste, he should blow it by the previous procedure.
A divine <s>khoṭa</s> is produced; with one sixteenth part it should perform <s>vedha</s> (penetration).
Bound through the <s>saṃkalikā</s> procedure, it should penetrate tenfold more.

children.text: mṛgadūrvā candravallī pakvā ciñcā tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Mṛgadūrvā</s>, <s>Candravallī</s>, and ripe tamarind as well,

children.text: kokilā karavīraṃ ca bījaṃ conmattakasya ca
children.translated_text: <s>Kokilā</s>, <s>Karavīra</s>, and the seed of <s>Unmattaka</s>,
combined with the fruit of <s>Kākāṇḍī</s>: he should triturate them, O heavenly beauty.

children.text: samahemni samaṃ sūtaṃ piṣṭikāṃ kārayed budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With equal gold and equal mercury, the wise man should make a <s>piṣṭikā</s>.

children.text: athavā sārayitvā tu samena saha sūtakam
children.translated_text: Or, after subjecting mercury to <s>sāraṇā</s> together with an equal amount,
he should triturate the <s>mahārasa</s> with herbal juices for the sake of the <s>piṣṭikā</s>.
After triturating for three <s>yāmas</s>, he should then make a ball.
He should place the ball in a sealed crucible and dry it in the shade.

children.text: tato laghupuṭaṃ dattvā dhmātaḥ khoṭo bhavet priye ||
children.translated_text: Then, after a light <s>puṭa</s> has been given, once blown, it becomes a <s>khoṭa</s>, O dear one.
The feeding of mercury is done with the juices of <s>Mṛgadūrvā</s>, <s>Tamā</s>, and <s>Soma</s>.
It is killed with the roots of the three, and with <s>Lāṅgalī</s> and <s>Rāmaṭha</s>.

children.text: samena hemnā saṃyuktāṃ piṣṭikāṃ kārayed budhaḥ
children.translated_text: The wise man should make a <s>piṣṭikā</s> joined with an equal amount of gold.
Then he should make a silver paste with an equal amount of mercury.
As before, by the ordered procedure, a fine <s>khoṭa</s> is produced.
Placed in a sealed crucible in the ground, it should be steamed with a fire of cow-dung cakes.
After a day and night, or after three nights, powder-binding then occurs.
That powder-binding produces <s>vedha</s> tenfold greater.
Mercury with the juice of <s>Śūlinī</s>, combined with <s>srotoñjana</s>,
by the previous <s>piṣṭikā</s> procedure becomes a fine <s>khoṭa</s>.
<s>Srotoñjana</s>, <s>Satagara</s>, and mercury joined with the three pastes:
he should blow it after it has been cast into the fire; the mercury accomplishes every operation.
Gold-mica, silver-mica, copper-mica, mica with iron,
tin-mica and lead-mica too: he should make <s>vedha</s> with an equal amount of mercury.
Triturated with whatever herbs are available and combined with the <s>mahārasa</s>,
with gold, silver, copper, iron, tin, and lead,

children.text: ebhir vyastaiḥ samastairvā piṣṭīṃ kṛtvā same samām
children.translated_text: with these separately or all together, he should make equal <s>piṣṭīs</s> in equal portions.
He should kill them by the previous method in a womb-apparatus with a husk fire.

children.text: samāṃśaṃ sūtakaṃ dattvā vāraṃ vāraṃ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Adding an equal portion of mercury again and again,
various <s>khoṭas</s> are produced; the <s>mahārasa</s> is bound with <s>kānta</s>.
Through the <s>saṃkalikā</s> procedure, <s>vedha</s> becomes tenfold greater.

children.text: khoṭaḥ poṭastathā bhasma dhūliḥ kalkaśca pañcamaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Khoṭa</s>, <s>poṭa</s>, ash, dust, and paste as the fifth:
these, through the <s>nigala</s> and <s>gola</s> methods, bring about all the fruits of binding.
Alkali produced from <s>śigru</s> and <s>sarja</s>, seeds of <s>brahma</s>, and <s>guggulu</s>,
and twice as much rock salt: after adding them and triturating, the expert,
with this paste, O beautiful one, should make an envelope for the <s>piṣṭikā</s>.
Having made it the size of a bilva fruit, he should prepare a fine, very firm crucible.

children.text: ūrdhvādho lavaṇaṃ dattvā mūṣāmadhye rasaṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: After placing salt above and below, he should put the mercury in the middle of the crucible.
A coating for the crucible should be applied, made of powder of burnt conch and the like.

children.text: mukhaṃ tasyā dṛḍhaṃ baddhvā loṇamṛttikayā punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having bound its mouth firmly again with salt-clay,
he should apply a coating of lime and dry it in the shade.
This <s>nigalabandha</s> has been stated; it should not be told even to one's son.
With a chaff fire in the ground he should produce a gentle steaming.
With care he should give a <s>puṭa</s> lasting a day and night.

children.text: evaṃ mūṣā maheśāni rasasya khoṭatāṃ nayet
children.translated_text: In this way the crucible, O great lady, brings the mercury to the state of a <s>khoṭa</s>.
Well blown with <s>khadira</s> charcoal, the lord of mercury becomes a <s>khoṭa</s>.

children.text: sauvīraṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ kācaṃ dattvā khoṭaṃ tu śodhayet
children.translated_text: After adding <s>sauvīra</s>, borax, and glass, he should purify the <s>khoṭa</s>.
Unexhausted, it combines with gold, and <s>samāvarta</s> arises.
He should make it consume equal portions with purified mercury.
He should blow it by the previous procedure and bring <s>rasendra</s> to the state of a <s>khoṭa</s>.
Through the <s>saṃkalikā</s> procedure, <s>vedha</s> becomes tenfold greater.
The extract of <s>palāśa</s> seeds, <s>Kokila</s>, <s>Unmatta</s>, and <s>Vāruṇī</s>...
He should triturate it, combined with the juice of <s>śūlinī</s> and mixed with rock salt.
Having made an enclosure for the <s>piṣṭikā</s> (mercurial paste), he should bind it with a <s>nigala</s> (restraining compound).
O <s>Devi</s>, the <s>nigala</s>, smeared on in a crucible according to <s>Śiva</s>'s teaching,
should remain in a great fire for the transformation of the <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
With a sheet of mica, with <s>vajrārka</s>, milks, and salts,
with <s>tāpya</s>, iron dross, and sand-clay as well:
the great mercury, belonging to quicksilver, bound with these <s>nigalas</s>,
does not overstep its boundary, just as the great ocean does not overstep the shore.
Oil, the milk of <s>arka</s>, <s>vārāhī</s>, and <s>lāṅgalī</s> form an excellent <s>nigala</s>.
Crow-dung, seeds of <s>brahma</s>, and <s>lāṅgalī</s> are a fine <s>nigala</s>.
<s>Vākucī</s>, seeds of <s>brahma</s>, and crab bones, O beautiful one,
together with sea salt and <s>sāmbara</s> salt, are an excellent <s>nigala</s>.
The milk produced from <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>, seeds of <s>brahma</s>, <s>kokilā</s>,
and the seeds of <s>karaka</s> should be triturated with one eighth part of iron.
Another <s>nigala</s> consists of the roots of <s>gojihvā</s>; another is woman's menstrual blood.
<s>Vākucī</s>, seeds of <s>brahma</s>, the milk of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>, and rock salt,
<s>jvālinī</s> and crow-dung are praised as an excellent <s>nigala</s>.
Salt, borax, alkali, realgar, orpiment, and sulfur,
as well as sour <s>vetasa</s>, <s>tāpya</s>, and cinnabar, each in equal portions,
mixed with the milks of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>: he should triturate them into an excellent <s>nigala</s>.
He should enclose the <s>piṣṭikā</s> with one of these <s>nigalas</s>,

children.text: lohamūṣāgataṃ prāgvat khoṭaṃ kṛtvā tu vedhayet ||
children.translated_text: and, placing it in an iron crucible as before, he should make it into a <s>khoṭa</s> and then perform <s>vedha</s>.
I shall explain the second ball, an excellent means for stabilizing the <s>piṣṭikā</s>.
The menstrual blood and urine of a woman, rock salt, mica, and guggul,

children.text: piṣṭīṃ saṃveṣṭya kalkena mṛdā tu punaraṣṭadhā ||
children.translated_text: having enclosed the <s>piṣṭī</s> with the paste, and again with clay eight times,
he should apply gentle steaming in the ground with a fire of husk and <s>karṣa</s> fuel.

children.text: ahorātraṃ trirātraṃ vā pūrvavat khoṭatāṃ nayet ||
children.translated_text: For one day and night or for three nights, he should bring it to the state of a <s>khoṭa</s> as before.
<s>Vākucī</s>, seeds of <s>brahma</s>, mica, <s>vimala</s>, and gem,

children.text: sauvarcalaṃ saindhavaṃ ca ṭaṅkaṇaṃ gugguluṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>sauvarcala</s> salt, rock salt, borax, and guggul as well:
he should triturate that very finely with woman's menstrual blood and urine.

children.text: piṣṭīṃ saṃveṣṭya kalkena pūrvavat khoṭatāṃ nayet ||
children.translated_text: Having enclosed the <s>piṣṭī</s> with the paste, he should bring it to the state of a <s>khoṭa</s> as before.
Seeds of <s>viṣa</s>, seeds of <s>brahma</s>, and seeds of <s>kanaka</s>,
the roots of <s>yavaciñcā</s>, together with <s>lāṅgalī</s> and <s>indravāruṇī</s>,
the milks of <s>kokilā</s>, <s>arka</s>, and <s>snuhī</s>, rock salt, mica, and guggul:

children.text: piṣṭīṃ saṃveṣṭya kalkena pūrvavat khoṭatāṃ nayet ||
children.translated_text: having enclosed the <s>piṣṭī</s> with the paste, he should bring it to the state of a <s>khoṭa</s> as before.
<s>Lāṅgalī</s>, seeds of <s>brahma</s>, crow-dung, and guggul,
the roots of white <s>aśvamāra</s> and the root of <s>kanakavāruṇī</s>,
and oil mixed with rock salt: the skilled practitioner should triturate that.

children.text: piṣṭīṃ saṃveṣṭya kalkena pūrvavat khoṭatāṃ nayet ||
children.translated_text: Having enclosed the <s>piṣṭī</s> with the paste, he should bring it to the state of a <s>khoṭa</s> as before.
<s>Vākucī</s>, seeds of <s>brahma</s>, the two kinds of cumin, and guggul,
rock salt, mica, crab bone, borax, and the juice of <s>jvālinī</s>:

children.text: piṣṭīṃ saṃveṣṭya kalkena mṛdā tu punaraṣṭadhā
children.translated_text: having enclosed the <s>piṣṭī</s> with the paste, and then with clay eight times,
he should apply gentle steaming in the ground with a fire of husk and <s>karṣa</s> fuel.

children.text: ahorātraṃ trirātraṃ vā rasendraṃ khoṭatāṃ nayet
children.translated_text: For one day and night or for three nights, he should bring <s>Rasendra</s> to the state of a <s>khoṭa</s>.
Through the procedure of ten <s>saṃkalikās</s>, the great <s>rasa</s> becomes capable of sound-penetration.

children.text: śaṃkarasya dvibhāgaṃ tu pāradasya trayaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Two parts of <s>Śaṃkara</s> and likewise three parts of mercury:
with that he should make a <s>piṣṭikā</s> in sour gruel in a heated mortar.
Provided with a <s>nigala</s> as before, he should make it into a <s>khoṭa</s> and then perform <s>vedha</s>.
Through the procedure of ten <s>saṃkalikās</s>, the great <s>rasa</s> becomes capable of sound-penetration.
With bound mercury, <s>rājendra</s>, realgar, sulfur, and pyrite,
combined with powder of lodestone and with earth-creepers,
this <s>rasa</s>, O you honored by the gods, is blown while placed in a crucible.
Then, in the womb of an open crucible, it consumes the <s>rasas</s>, subsidiary minerals, metals, jewels, and gems,
like the submarine fire.

children.text: mākṣikaṃ daradaṃ caiva gandhakaṃ ca manaḥśilā
children.translated_text: Pyrite, cinnabar, sulfur, and realgar,

children.text: rājāvartaṃ pravālaṃ ca kaṅkuṣṭhaṃ tutthakaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>rājāvarta</s>, coral, <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, and blue vitriol as well,
should be impregnated with the yellow and red groups and mixed with <s>kaṅguṇī</s> oil.

children.text: khoṭaṃ haṇḍikayā pakvaṃ drutaṃ hi nalike kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: The <s>khoṭa</s>, cooked in a small pot and melted, should be placed into a tube.

children.text: haṇḍyāṃ tu sikatāṃ dattvā trirātramapi dhāmayet ||
children.translated_text: Having put sand in the pot, he should blow it even for three nights.

children.text: āranālena tat svinnaṃ dolāyāṃ dhṛtameva ca
children.translated_text: Then it is steamed with sour gruel, placed in a <s>dolā</s> apparatus.
Mercury colored in this way becomes productive of bodily perfection and wealth.
This is taught as the supreme opening process, excellent and beneficial for all operations.

children.text: chattrī pataṃgī durdrāvī durmelī naiva jāyate
children.translated_text: It does not become umbrella-like, moth-like, difficult to melt, or difficult to combine.
It changes color and causes bursting, O fair-colored one.
Having thus quickly made the binding, it brings about the digestion of vajra.
Tell me that, O queen of gods; what else do you wish to hear?
<s>Śrīdevī</s> said:
How, O <s>Īśvara</s>, is the king of <s>rasa</s> liquefied once it has been bound,
and how is the digestion of vajra and the rest done? Command me, O lord.
<s>Śrībhairava</s> said:

children.text: taṃ khoṭaṃ sūkṣmacūrṇaṃ tu strīrajobhistu bhāvayet ||
children.translated_text: That <s>khoṭa</s>, made into a fine powder, should be impregnated with woman's menstrual blood.
<s>Punarnavā</s>, <s>Mīnākṣī</s>, plantain bulb, and woman's menstrual blood,
<s>maṇimantha</s> and mineral realgar: he should grind everything together.
Covered with this paste and combined with the juice of <s>āroṭa</s>,

children.text: taṃ rasaṃ bhūrjapattre tu baddhvā poṭalikāṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: that <s>rasa</s> should then be tied in birch bark as a small bundle.
O queen of the gods, he should steam it in a <s>dolā</s> apparatus for three days.
By this ordered procedure, the killed mercury becomes molten.

children.text: ārdrakaṃ mūlakaṃ śuṇṭhī laśunaṃ hiṅgu mākṣikam
children.translated_text: Fresh ginger, radish, dry ginger, garlic, asafoetida, and pyrite,
the three alkalis, the five salts, alum, green vitriol, and sulfur
One should make a ball combined with the acid group, O dear one.

children.text: tasya madhyagatā piṣṭī dolāyāṃ svedanena tu
children.translated_text: The paste placed in the middle of it, by steaming in the <s>dolā</s> apparatus,

children.text: dravate nātra saṃdeho drutaṃ jārayate rasam ||
children.translated_text: melts; there is no doubt here. When melted, it causes <s>rasa</s> (mercury) to undergo <s>jāraṇa</s> (digestion).
O <s>Devi</s>, one should liquefy bound <s>mahārasa</s> by the <s>pāda</s> procedure.
Then it should be placed in the molten <s>pāda</s>; after liquefying it, it melts again.
Thus, having made the bound substance molten, whether equal, double, triple, and so on,

children.text: tasmin drute jāraṇā ca kartavyā karmavedibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: in that molten substance <s>jāraṇa</s> should be performed by those who know the operation.
<s>Kukkuṭīkanda</s>, <s>Mārjārī</s>, <s>Uccaṭā</s>, and likewise <s>Pīśvarī</s>,

children.text: kṣīrakañcukayā yuktaṃ sveditaṃ ca drutaṃ rasam ||
children.translated_text: together with <s>Kṣīrakañcukā</s>: mercury should be steamed and melted with them.
The melted substance, broken down in the <s>dolā</s> and the like with <s>Kukkuṭī</s> and the others for three days,

children.text: ārdrakādyair drutaṃ caiva tatsūtaṃ svedyatāṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: and melted with ginger and the like: that mercury should be subjected to steaming.
As one causes molten diamond to be digested into mercury, O you praised by the gods,
he should be known as <s>Īśvara</s>, the god of gods, the teacher of the world.

children.text: vidhāya khoṭaṃ yat kiṃcit mṛtakotthāpite rase
children.translated_text: Having made whatever <s>khoṭa</s> in mercury that has been revived from the dead state,

children.text: ṣaḍguṇaṃ hema jāryaṃ tu sārayet sāraṇātrayam ||
children.translated_text: sixfold gold should be digested into it, and he should perform the threefold <s>sāraṇā</s>.
With one croreth part of that very substance he should produce <s>vedha</s> (penetration) in copper.
Divine gold is produced, fit to adorn the ornaments of the gods.
Again, into that lord of mercury he should digest diamonds and jewels.
In the belly of an open crucible, under a violent fire, it is digested in a moment.
With <s>Uccaṭā</s>, <s>Mīnanayanā</s>, <s>Sarpākṣī</s>, and red <s>Citraka</s>,
by these, jewels quickly melt: sapphire, ruby, and pearl.
<s>Viṣṇukrāntā</s>, <s>Cakrāṅkā</s>, <s>Kumārī</s>, and <s>Yavaciñcikā</s>,
diamonds, <s>padmarāga</s> gems, <s>rājāvarta</s>, and <s>sasyaka</s>:

children.text: oṣadhīnāṃ dravaṃ dattvā tapte sūte vinikṣipet ||
children.translated_text: after adding the liquid of the herbs, one should cast them into heated mercury.
Afterward the jewels should be added; they melt like water.
O <s>Devi</s>, one should steam it in a <s>dolā</s> and digest it with a <s>viḍa</s> compound.
In the belly of an open crucible, under a violent fire, one should digest it in a moment.
With conch and the milk of <s>arka</s>, heated or quenched a hundred times by <s>puṭa</s>,
that seed, joined with alkali, should be impregnated with the acid group.
With <s>viḍa</s>, cinnabar, <s>rājāvarta</s>, and coral,

children.text: gandhakaḥ śilayā yuktaḥ khoṭānāṃ jāraṇe hitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: sulfur joined with <s>śilā</s> is useful for the <s>jāraṇa</s> of <s>khoṭas</s>.
Through the application of crucible-smearing and the like, there is indeed <s>jāraṇa</s> of fixed gold.
By casting that in, O <s>Devi</s>, <s>jāraṇa</s> arises with the <s>viḍa</s> compound.
Afterward gold should be added, with one thirty-sixth part of liquid.
Then, for the king of mercury, a circle of rays is produced,
filled with a mass of radiance spreading sideways, upward, and downward.

children.text: itthaṃ śuddho bhavet sūtaḥ cintāmaṇiriva svayam
children.translated_text: Thus mercury becomes purified by itself, like a <s>cintāmaṇi</s> jewel.

children.text: sadevaiḥ pūjyate siddhaiḥ dvitīya iva śaṃkaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is worshiped by the gods and by the perfected ones, like a second <s>Śaṃkara</s>.
It acts for the welfare of the worlds and bestows enjoyment and liberation.
And one should digest <s>mahānīla</s> according to the sequence of the number of principles.
When it revolves clockwise, then that mercury is <s>khecara</s> (sky-going).
It will penetrate all metals in measures of <s>bhāras</s>, O <s>Pārvati</s>.
Now hear the <s>kāpālika</s> coloring of mercury that has been digested in this way.
One <s>pala</s> of copper leaf and half a <s>pala</s> of sulfur,
one <s>karṣa</s> of borax and one <s>karṣa</s> of mercury black-sulfide paste,
and one <s>karṣa</s> of <s>mākṣika</s>: one should make all of this together.
Smelted in a sealed crucible, it becomes a <s>khoṭa</s> at once.

children.text: taṃ khoṭaṃ sūkṣmacūrṇaṃ tu caṇakāmlena mardayet
children.translated_text: That <s>khoṭa</s>, as a fine powder, should be triturated with sour chickpea liquid.
One should give it fourteen <s>puṭas</s> with forest cow dung.
It becomes like an <s>indragopaka</s> insect; there is no doubt here.

children.text: taccūrṇaṃ madhunā yuktaṃ śuddhatāraṃ tu rañjayet
children.translated_text: That powder, mixed with honey, should color purified silver.

children.text: rañjayet trīṇi vārāṇi śobhanaṃ hema jāyate ||
children.translated_text: He should color it three times; fine gold is produced.
This is the <s>kāpālika</s> formula; it colors all metals.
It colors fixed mercury, and it also colors diamond-bound material.
Or one <s>pala</s> of brass powder, or one <s>pala</s> of killed lead,
or one <s>pala</s> of tin and mica, or one <s>pala</s> of <s>tīkṣṇa</s> powder,
or three parts copper, or lead and tin, furnished with one part each,
or three parts copper with one part red ocher, or else <s>tīkṣṇa</s> and <s>mākṣika</s>,

children.text: athavā tīkṣṇabhāgau dvau trayo ghoṣā navoragāḥ
children.translated_text: or else two parts <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, three parts bell-metal, and nine parts lead,
nine parts of copper, and four parts of brass,
or else, O goddess of gods, two <s>palas</s> of <s>mākṣika</s>,
one part peacock-neck <s>tuttha</s>, and likewise one <s>pala</s> of killed lead,
or else one part each of tin and lead, O you praised by the gods,
two parts <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, three parts copper, and four parts gold-pyrite,
or <s>vimalā</s>, <s>vaikrānta</s>, tin, lead, and <s>rītikā</s>,
together with copper, or else gold, <s>vimalā</s>, and <s>bhujaṃgama</s>.
Any one of these, O <s>Devi</s>, furnished with the previous procedure,
when smelted in a sealed crucible, becomes a <s>khoṭa</s> at once.
One should heat it with the previous formula and color it by the previous formula.
Lead, copper, and likewise <s>tīkṣṇa</s>: this is the excellent <s>kāpālī</s> sequence.
With that very substance one should color silver seven times, again and again.
With that very substance one should color gold seven times, again and again.
This is the best cooked seed; one should apply it in all operations.

children.text: vaṅgatīkṣṇaṃ kapālī ca śulvaṃ tāraṃ tu rañjayet
children.translated_text: Tin, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, <s>kapālī</s>, and copper color silver.
It colors all metals until they resemble saffron.
<s>Vaikrānta</s>, lead, and <s>kāpālī</s> color purified silver.

children.text: rañjayet saha hemnā tu bhavet kuṅkumasannibham ||
children.translated_text: It should color it together with gold; it becomes saffron-like.
Sprinkled with red oil, it removes the transference of base metal.
But the powder of <s>ārakāpālī</s> should color purified silver.
With <s>vimala</s> and lead, <s>Kāpālī Parameśvarī</s>
should color all metals, especially silver and gold.

children.text: rañjayet trīṇi vārāṇi jāyate hema śobhanam
children.translated_text: If he colors it three times, fine gold is produced.
With that same substance he should color gold again and again, seven times.
When it has been sprinkled with salt-water, it destroys metallic transference.

children.text: vaṅganāgaṃ tathā kāntaṃ śulvaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca mākṣikam ||
children.translated_text: Tin, lead, likewise <s>kānta</s>, copper, iron, and <s>mākṣika</s>:
the <s>kāpālī</s> made from copper and lead should color purified silver.

children.text: rañjayet trīṇi vārāṇi tārāriṣṭaṃ tu jāyate
children.translated_text: He should color it three times, and a preparation removing silver's defect is produced.
With that same substance he should color gold seven times, O <s>Pārvati</s>.
And when it has been sprinkled with the red group, it destroys metallic transference.
Tin, lead, likewise copper: this is <s>kāpālī</s>, O you praised by the gods.
With jaggery, blue glass, blue vitriol, sour salt,
and a paste of poison, bile, and sour liquid, he should destroy the defect occurring at the time of transference.
He should grind red ochre, sulfur, and mercury with sesame oil.
He should smear leaves of silver, after adding a copper <s>kāpālikā</s>.
In a sealed crucible, above and below, it becomes a white leaf of gold.
One part of orpiment and one part of red ochre,
one part of a paste of <s>mākṣika</s>, and four parts of the ball:
when placed in a sealed crucible and blown, it colors gold instantly.
By this ordered procedure he should color it four times.
This is the best ripened seed, with a radiance like the young sun.
Through it an increase of two colors arises with one sixteenth part.
And when it has been sprinkled with red oil, it destroys metallic transference.

children.text: rasakasya tu kāpālī candrārkaṃ tu śatāṃśataḥ
children.translated_text: A <s>kāpālī</s> of <s>rasaka</s>, and <s>candra</s> and <s>arka</s> in one-hundredth part:
when placed in a sealed crucible and blown, fine gold is produced.
One <s>pala</s> of purified lead and one <s>karṣa</s> of molten mercury:
he should make them flow in a <s>sāraṇā</s> apparatus; the mercury becomes a <s>khoṭa</s>.

children.text: khoṭasya palamekaṃ tu mākṣikasya palaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: One <s>pala</s> of the <s>khoṭa</s>, and likewise one <s>pala</s> of <s>mākṣika</s>:
having combined them and then triturated them with the juice of gold,
he should cook them in an earthen vessel; it becomes like saffron.
Mixed with the previous paste, he should first make the <s>khoṭa</s>.
From this <s>kāpālikā</s> procedure he should triturate the powder with sour liquid.
He should heat it with the previous procedure and color it according to the previous procedure.
Having bound mercury by whatever means, with gold, sulfur, or <s>śilā</s>,
and having wrapped it in sequence and blown it, he should make it penetrate a hundred times.

children.text: ādau tu baddhasūtaṃ ca vaṅgaṃ tāraṃ manaḥśilā
children.translated_text: First, bound mercury, tin, silver, and realgar:

children.text: krameṇa veṣṭayet dhmātaṃ śatavedhī na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he should wrap them in sequence and blow them; it is a hundredfold penetrator, without doubt.

children.text: anena kurute tāraṃ kanakena tu kāñcanam ||
children.translated_text: By this he makes silver, and with gold he makes gold.

children.text: sūto mṛto hanti samena vaṅgaṃ tenaiva hanyāddviguṇaṃ ca tāram
children.translated_text: Dead mercury kills an equal amount of tin; with that same substance he should kill twice as much silver.

children.text: tāraṃ catuḥṣaṣṭiraviṃ karoti hemāpi tadvat phaṇihemayogāt ||
children.translated_text: It makes silver into sixty-four-fold copper, and gold likewise, through union with serpent-gold.

children.text: mṛtarasapalamekaṃ pañcanāgaṃ ca dadyāt kanakapalavimiśraṃ dhmātasūtāvaśeṣam
children.translated_text: He should add one <s>pala</s> of dead mercury and five of lead, mixed with a <s>pala</s> of gold; when blown, the mercury remains.

children.text: punarapi śatavārānevameva krameṇa bhavati ca rasarājaḥ koṭivedhī krameṇa ||
children.translated_text: Again and again, a hundred times, in just this order, the king of <s>rasa</s> gradually becomes capable of crore-fold penetration.

children.text: mṛtasūtapalaikaṃ tu dve pale daradasya ca
children.translated_text: One <s>pala</s> of dead mercury and two <s>palas</s> of cinnabar,
four <s>palas</s> of sulfur, three <s>palas</s> of <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>,

children.text: śilāyāḥ pañcakaṃ caiva gopittena tu mardayet ||
children.translated_text: and five of <s>śilā</s>: he should triturate these with cow's bile.
He should smear one <s>pala</s> of lead leaves with that paste.
He should kill it by the <s>puṭa</s> procedure; this lead is killed at once.

children.text: vaṭikāṃ kārayetpaścāt ṣaṣṭiṃ trīṇi śatāni ca
children.translated_text: Afterward he should make pellets, three hundred and sixty in number.
Then he should triturate each pellet with cow's bile.

children.text: anena kramayogeṇa śataṃ dadyāt puṭāni ca
children.translated_text: By this ordered procedure he should give one hundred <s>puṭas</s>.
This lead, O <s>Devi</s>, becomes like red vermilion.

children.text: śatāṃśena ca tenaiva tāre vedhaṃ pradāpayet
children.translated_text: With one hundredth part of that very substance he should cause <s>vedha</s> in silver.
That silver, O <s>Devi</s>, becomes the finest ornament of the gods.
One <s>pala</s> of dead lead, and a gold leaf equal to it:
he should kill it by the <s>puṭa</s> procedure; the gold is killed at once.
That ash, joined with one part lead, and a gold leaf equal to it:
he should kill it by the <s>puṭa</s> procedure; the gold is killed at once.
By this ordered procedure he should perform it three times.
With one thousandth part of that very substance he should cause <s>vedha</s> in silver.
By an easily accomplished procedure that silver becomes gold.
Now I shall explain paste-penetration, easily accomplished, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>.
<s>Palāśa</s>, neem, bilva, <s>akṣa</s>, cotton, and bitter gourd,
and <s>kaṅguṇī</s> bitter oil: each one is a killer of mercury.

children.text: same hemni samaṃ sūtaṃ tāraṃ tāmramathāpi vā
children.translated_text: In an equal amount of gold, an equal amount of mercury, or silver, or else copper,
among the eight great minerals, and likewise four secondary minerals,
he should triturate them with fruit acid and sour gruel, without charcoal in the middle,
on heated iron, or with an iron pestle, over a gentle fire.
The skilled man should put oil into the sand apparatus previously described,
and triturate it for one fortnight, day and night, without weariness.
That paste becomes excellent, granting <s>dharma</s>, desire, wealth, and liberation.
It should penetrate the eight metals; it is difficult even for the gods to obtain.

children.text: nāśayet sakalān rogān palaikena na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: It destroys all diseases with one <s>pala</s>, without doubt.
One should eat it with <s>trikaṭu</s> and <s>triphalā</s>, together with honey and ghee.

children.text: hemnā tu baddhaṃ guñjaikaṃ tāreṇa dve sureśvari
children.translated_text: When bound with gold, one <s>guñjā</s>; with silver, two, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>;
with copper, three <s>guñjās</s>: within a year one becomes free from old age and death.
Moon-faced women, adorned with all ornaments, attend upon him.
Having made a nasal application at night with seeds of <s>triphalā</s>, honey, and ghee,

children.text: rasaṃ tu bhakṣayet prātarajīrṇaṃ naiva jāyate
children.translated_text: he should eat the <s>rasa</s> (mercurial preparation) in the morning; indigestion does not arise at all.
The wise man should use sulfur as a drink and an ointment, and should consume <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>.
He should consume one <s>pala</s> of <s>sūta</s> (mercury), honored by gods and demons.
His form becomes like heated gold, with a radiance like the young sun.

children.text: vedhayet sarvalohāni chede dāhe na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: It penetrates all metals in cutting and burning; there is no doubt.

children.text: baddhā tu saṃkalābandhair vaṭikā khecarī bhavet ||
children.translated_text: But when bound by <s>saṃkalā</s>-bindings, the pellet becomes <s>khecarī</s> (sky-moving).
<s>Kākajaṅghā</s>, <s>Bṛhatī</s>, <s>Śarapuṅkhā</s>, and <s>Ajaśṛṅgikā</s>,
<s>Śivā</s>, <s>Śakralatā</s>, and <s>Kanyā</s>: these seven are the great creepers.
The secret beyond secrets has been explained, combined with the oil of <s>vātāri</s>.

children.text: same hemni samaṃ sūtaṃ tāre tāmre 'thavā priye ||
children.translated_text: With equal mercury in equal gold, or in silver or copper, O dear one,
he should add one among the eight <s>mahārasas</s> (great minerals), and likewise the <s>uparasas</s> (secondary minerals).
He should triturate it on a stone mortar until it becomes inert.
He should heat it with <s>āranāla</s> and triturate it like the previous paste.
He should apply that to the respective operations for metal and for the body.
One part each of gold and mica, and likewise two parts of mercury;
one part each of silver and mica, and likewise two parts of mercury:
with that he should make a <s>piṣṭikā</s> (paste) and bind it with a <s>nigala</s> (fettering agent).
In the <s>puṭas</s> (closed heatings), the binding of the paste is done by the ball and by the <s>nigala</s>.
Again I shall explain another binding, the powder-binding, O queen of the gods.
Having added borax to the paste, he should triturate it with <s>dvipadī-rasa</s>.

children.text: naṣṭapiṣṭaṃ ca śuṣkaṃ tat dhāmayitvā puṭe pacet ||
children.translated_text: When the paste has disappeared and become dry, he should blow it and cook it in a <s>puṭa</s>.
He should wrap it, O goddess of gods, with a ball and with a <s>nigala</s>.
On the ground, with a husk-fire, he should subject it to gentle heating.

children.text: ahorātraṃ trirātraṃ vā cūrṇaṃ bhavati śobhanam
children.translated_text: For one day and night, or for three nights, it becomes a fine powder.
Because it lacks the state of a bound chain, it becomes a twofold penetrator.
Again I shall explain another binding, the very rare plate-binding.
<s>Kāsīsa</s>, borax, alkali, rock salt, sulfur, and mica,
and mercury triturated with citron for the duration of a <s>yāma</s>:
he should make a ball from tin, silver, mica, <s>rasaka</s>, and the milk of <s>snuhī</s>.
He should wrap it in birch bark and then wrap it with cloth and thread.
Having placed cow-dung above and below, he should then heat it within the ground.
He should perform trituration and heating three times in just this way.
According to local practice he should smear it, and triturate it with jaggery and sour gruel.
He should place it in a crucible smeared with <s>dhattūra</s> juice.

children.text: baddhvā mūṣāmukhaṃ devi saṃdhilepaṃ tu kārayet
children.translated_text: Having sealed the mouth of the crucible, O goddess, he should make a sealing-paste for the joint.
He should place the crucible in the midst of salt, with a large crucible outside it.

children.text: mukhaṃ tasyāśca mūṣāyā baddhvā loṇamṛdā tataḥ
children.translated_text: Then, having sealed the mouth of that crucible with salty clay,
on the ground, with a husk-fire, he should subject it to gentle heating.

children.text: ahorātraṃ trirātraṃ vā citradharmā bhavanti te
children.translated_text: For one day and night, or for three nights, they acquire variegated properties.
By this very procedure he should do it seven times.
Bound both inside and outside, they become purified in their properties.
Mercury killed with sulfur, <s>kāṅkṣī</s>, <s>kāsīsa</s>, and rock salt,
together with <s>snuhī</s>, <s>arka</s>, borax, and <s>guñjā</s>, triturated with the milk of <s>arka</s>,
quickly becomes mature and grants <s>dharma</s>, desire, wealth, and liberation.

children.text: pañcabhāgaṃ tu śulvasya dvibhāgaṃ kuñjarasya ca
children.translated_text: He should take five parts of copper and two parts of <s>kuñjara</s>,
make the leaf-like properties, and smear it according to the previous formula.

children.text: rasendro rañjati hy evaṃ kartavyaṃ sāraṇādikam
children.translated_text: In this way <s>Rasendra</s> (mercury) indeed becomes colored; <s>sāraṇa</s> and the rest should be performed.
Tell me that, O queen of the gods; what else do you wish to hear?
The blessed <s>Devī</s> said:

children.text: drāvaṇaṃ rañjanaṃ caiva pāradasya śrutaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: I have heard of the melting and coloring of mercury.
Please explain <s>sāraṇa</s> and <s>krāmaṇa</s> in order.
The blessed <s>Bhairava</s> said:
Having made a cow-teat crucible in the shape of a <s>dhattūra</s> flower,

children.text: tadardhaṃ pūrayettailaṃ rañjitaṃ ca rasaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: he should fill half of it with oil and place the colored mercury in it.
He should apply a husk-fire outside the crucible.
The <s>khoṭaka</s>, brought to <s>samāvarta</s> and combined with a twentieth part of lead,
should be inserted with long tongs; it becomes <s>sārita</s> (subjected to sāraṇa).
Then, with twice as much gold, it becomes <s>pratisārita</s>.
With three times as much gold, it becomes <s>anusārita</s>.
He should digest it with the <s>viḍa</s> compound as before, again and again.

children.text: anena vidhinā devi bhaveddvedhā tu vedhakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By this procedure, O goddess, it becomes a twofold penetrator.
<s>Bhūlatā</s>, red arsenic, poison, borax, mercury,
and <s>tāpya</s>, ground with woman's breast milk: this is <s>krāmaṇa</s> for throwing in and smearing.

children.text: indragopo viṣaṃ kāntaṃ daradaṃ rudhiraṃ tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Indragopa</s>, poison, <s>kānta</s>, <s>darada</s>, and blood,
as well as <s>rasaka</s> and sesame oil: this is <s>krāmaṇa</s> for throwing in and smearing.
<s>Bhūlatā</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, arsenic, borax, blood, and poison,
crow-dung, breast milk, and dirt from the two ears of a buffalo,
and <s>rāmaṭha</s>, O great goddess: this is <s>krāmaṇa</s> for throwing in and smearing.

children.text: bhūlatā lāṅgalī śṛṅgī kākaviṣṭhā ca śailajam
children.translated_text: <s>Bhūlatā</s>, <s>Lāṅgalī</s>, <s>Śṛṅgī</s>, crow-dung, and mineral pitch,
<s>Viṣṇukrāntā</s>, beeswax, blood, and dust from a biped,

children.text: surasā brahmasomā ca gṛdhrakarṇī ca lakṣaṇā
children.translated_text: <s>Surasā</s>, <s>Brahmasomā</s>, <s>Gṛdhrakarṇī</s>, and <s>Lakṣaṇā</s>,
and also what is found in the ear of a buffalo: this is <s>krāmaṇa</s> for throwing in and smearing.
<s>Gaṇḍola</s>, poison, frog-mouth, and the impurity from a buffalo's eye,
combined with blood, are the supreme transference of <s>rasa</s>.
Poison, <s>Surendragopa</s>, <s>rocanā</s>, and <s>guggulu</s>,

children.text: strīstanyaṃ caiva tair yukto lohe tu kramate rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and woman's breast milk: combined with these, the <s>rasa</s> advances into the metal.
With <s>śrīkhaṇḍa</s>, neem exudation, woman's breast milk, poison, and borax...

children.text: goghṛtena samāyukto lohe tu kramate rasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Joined with cow ghee, <s>rasa</s> (mercury) advances into iron.
Tin and lead, killed by the enemy-group, are both the supreme <s>krāmaṇa</s> (penetrating agent).
<s>Mātṛvāha</s>, <s>kulīra</s>, and the impurity born inside a conch,
and likewise the exudation of <s>kapittha</s>, are the supreme transference-agent for mercury.
At the time of <s>vedha</s> (penetration), one should administer <s>krāmaṇa</s> to the king of <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: krāmaṇaṃ yo na jānāti śramastasya nirarthakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For one who does not know <s>krāmaṇa</s>, his labor is fruitless.
After this I shall explain the leaves of gold and silver.
Lead and mercury, in equal amount, ground and combined with twelve parts of sulfur,
and ground in the juice of <s>dhattūra</s>, make a pellet the size of a chickpea.
There are four parts of silver and likewise three parts of copper;

children.text: samyag āvartya deveśi guṭikaikāṃ tu nikṣipet ||
children.translated_text: having melted them properly, O <s>Deveśī</s>, one should drop in a single pellet.

children.text: anena kramayogeṇa tāre tāmraṃ tu vāhayet
children.translated_text: By this ordered procedure, one should make copper enter into silver,

children.text: yāvattu jāyate raktaṃ tāraṃ caiva na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: until the silver becomes red; there is no doubt at all.
Of this, two parts should be taken, together with five parts of silver;
combined with one part of gold and melted, it becomes eightfold gold.
Copper killed with sulfur and combined with cinnabar,

children.text: ārdrakaṃ mūlakaṃ śuṇṭhī laśunaṃ hiṅgu mākṣikam ||
children.translated_text: ginger, radish, dry ginger, garlic, asafoetida, and <s>mākṣika</s>,
one should triturate with citron and smear upon lead leaves.
By a <s>puṭa</s> heating, the lead is killed, resembling red vermilion.

children.text: tattāre triguṇe vyūḍhaṃ nirbījaṃ kanakaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: When this is inserted into three times as much silver, it becomes seedless gold.
With sulfur-stone, cinnabar, iron, <s>kharpara</s>, and mercury,
in increasing parts, with equal honey and ghee, one should smear a fifth part.
Through <s>puṭa</s> heating and dry <s>puṭa</s> heating, silver becomes black in two ways.
Smeared with yellow sulfur and the exudation of <s>palāśa</s>,
silver becomes gold by the application of three <s>puṭas</s>.
The yellow, black, and red group, obtained as available and well powdered,
when impregnated with cow ghee and blown into silver, destroys its whiteness.
The red, yellow, and black group, with abundant goat's milk,
should be kept on silver for seven days; by quenching, redness increases.
When, through blowing and quenching, it has the luster of a cat's eye,
that silver is called a leaf; the union is considered supreme.

children.text: śulvasya kāṃsyakṛṣṇaṃ tu rasakena tu rañjayet
children.translated_text: Copper, blackened like bronze, one should color with <s>rasaka</s>;

children.text: dvau bhāgau tasya śulvasya tārasyaikaṃ ca melayet ||
children.translated_text: two parts of that copper and one part of silver should be combined.

children.text: tadā tasya rasendrasya melanaṃ paramaṃ matam
children.translated_text: Then, for that lord of <s>rasa</s>, the union is considered supreme.
One should cause <s>vedha</s> with pure mercury, using a hundredth part, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>.
One should grind gold-<s>mākṣika</s> and salt with honey and ghee,
until it becomes like saffron; with that, one should cook it in a lead <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: samaṃ śulvaṃ tato deyaṃ tacchulvaṃ tārapattrake
children.translated_text: Then an equal amount of copper should be added; that copper should be put into a silver leaf.
Having purified it three times after adding it, it becomes pure gold leaf.

children.text: vaṅgaṃ nāgaṃ tathā tīkṣṇaṃ śulvaṃ tāraṃ ca pañcakam
children.translated_text: Tin, lead, iron, copper, and silver: these five
having purified them three times after adding them, become pure gold leaf.
<s>Tālaka</s>, sulfur-stone, <s>mākṣika</s>, <s>kharpara</s>, and poison:
having smeared tin-metal with these, mixed with citron, one should cook it in a <s>puṭa</s>.
Cinnabar, sulfur-stone, <s>mākṣika</s>, rock salt, and poison:
having smeared sharp iron with these, mixed with citron, one should cook it in a <s>puṭa</s>.
<s>Kunaṭī</s>, sulfur-stone, <s>mākṣika</s>, rock salt, and poison:
having smeared lead-metal with these, mixed with citron, one should cook it in a <s>puṭa</s>.

children.text: sarvaṃ hemadale vāhyaṃ hema baddhena vedhayet ||
children.translated_text: Everything should be made to enter into the gold leaf; one should pierce it with bound gold.

children.text: tulyāṃśau hemakariṇau tīkṣṇaṃ dviguṇam eva ca
children.translated_text: Equal parts of the two gold-making substances, and twice as much sharp iron,

children.text: vyūḍhaṃ raktagaṇaiḥ siktaṃ tattāraṃ kanakaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: inserted and sprinkled with the red group: that silver becomes gold.

children.text: śulvaṃ tāpyahataṃ kṛtvā varanāgaṃ tu rañjayet
children.translated_text: Having made copper killed by <s>tāpya</s>, one should color excellent lead;
one should make that lead enter into silver until it becomes gold leaf.
Poison, sulfur equal to mercury, and joined with three times as much collyrium,

children.text: amlena tridinaṃ piṣṭvā tārārkau melayet samau ||
children.translated_text: having ground them with sour liquid for three days, one should combine equal silver and <s>arka</s>.
Cooked with the five clays, one should give a <s>puṭa</s> until only silver remains;
in this way, after three turns, one should color the finest silver.
Of <s>bhujaṅga</s> and copper there should be four parts each, separately,
and separately twelve parts of oil, for both <s>rītikā</s> and silver.
There should be one part of gold, with gold and silver left as the remainder;
O <s>Devi</s>, it becomes an excellent gold leaf with the luster of a cat's eye.
Eight parts silver, four parts copper, two parts lead, and one part gold:

children.text: sarvaṃ tato raktagaṇena siktaṃ tārāvaśeṣaṃ kanakaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: all of it, then sprinkled with the red group and reduced until silver remains, makes gold.

children.text: rājāvartaṃ caturthaṃ ca daradaṃ ca pravālakam
children.translated_text: <s>Rājāvarta</s>, a fourth part, cinnabar, and coral,
combined with gold-<s>mākṣika</s>, should be prepared in equal parts.
Three parts of <s>rasaka</s> should be triturated with ewe's milk;
afterward one should make a pellet and then dry it in the shade.
Joined with the five solvents, one should grind it on a stone slab;
with this perfected paste one should treat defective silver.
In the first application, with an equal amount of paste; in the second, with half of that;
in the third, with a quarter part, the silver treatment is produced.

children.text: pattre dāhe kaṣe chede hema taccākṣayaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: On the leaf, in burning, rubbing, and cutting, that gold becomes imperishable.

children.text: sūtakaṃ daradaṃ tāpyaṃ gandhakaṃ kunaṭī tathā
children.translated_text: Mercury, cinnabar, <s>tāpya</s>, sulfur, and <s>kunaṭī</s>,
taking them in progressively increasing amounts, one should smear copper leaves.
Having ground them in fresh <s>cāṅgerī</s> juice, one should apply five <s>puṭas</s>.
One should make that powder enter into silver; this is the drawing-out of gold.
One should apply it to gold, O <s>Devi</s>; from that it becomes black in color.
Having ground <s>niśā</s> with cow's urine, he should melt the copper and quench it.
Through purification a hundred times, it becomes a gold-and-silver producing substance.
Now, O beloved, copper extracted from bronze, or else <s>āroṭa</s>,

children.text: ṣaḍguṇena tu nāgena śodhayitvā tato budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the wise man should purify with six times as much lead, and then:
he should pour fifty measures of <s>sindhuvāra</s> into the mercury.

children.text: kuṣmāṇḍasya rase paścāt saptavāraṃ tu dāpayet ||
children.translated_text: Afterward he should treat it seven times in the juice of <s>kuṣmāṇḍa</s>.

children.text: tathā takre niśāyukte taptataptaṃ ca dāpayet
children.translated_text: Likewise, heated again and again, he should treat it in buttermilk mixed with <s>niśā</s>.
It is like a parrot's beak or <s>kiṃśuka</s>, red when cut, and also soft.

children.text: tāpyena vāpyaṃ kṛtsnaṃ tat śulvaṃ kālikayā gatam ||
children.translated_text: That whole copper, infused with <s>tāpya</s>, has become blackened.
Cinnabar, <s>kiṃśuka</s> juice, and red <s>citraka</s>,
and the two turmerics, O fair-hipped one, he should grind with goat's urine.
He should apply the quenching to copper seven times; there is no doubt.

children.text: śulvaṃ sindūravarṇaṃ ca varaṃ hemadalaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: The copper becomes vermilion-colored and becomes an excellent gold leaf.
He should cause twice as much sharp iron and lead, together with <s>ghoṣa</s> and black metal, to flow.
Or, from the apparatus-maker, in the order of one, two, and three <s>palas</s>,

children.text: tripañcakaṃ ca nāgasya śulvasya ca palaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: he should take fifteen <s>palas</s> of lead and one <s>pala</s> of copper likewise.
When it is blown, what remains becomes like refined gold.
<s>Lāṅgalī</s>, <s>citraka</s>, <s>śigru</s>, <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, and oleander,
together with the milks of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>, tamarind acid, and <s>vajrakanda</s>,
and combined with buffalo's milk, O <s>Devi</s>, he should prepare the liquor.
He should smear copper leaves with the milks of <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s> and with salts.
He should cook them for one day in the liquor described first.
As before, when smeared and fire-colored, he should repeatedly quench them in the liquor.
Melted many times, he should process them with cowries from a pit.
He should sprinkle with <s>sarjikā</s> and rock salt, and employ it in operations.
One <s>pala</s> of <s>rasaka</s>, combined with gold-colored <s>mākṣika</s>,
and half a <s>pala</s> of rock salt, mixed with citron acid:
then he should have it cooked; when smelted it is like saffron.
He should digest the paste, like an <s>indragopa</s> insect, by the <s>puṭa</s> procedure.
That paste, combined with honey and furnished with sugar and borax,
having been made into one mass and then thoroughly triturated, should be cooked with cow's milk.

children.text: prāg eva śodhitaṃ śulvaṃ rasakalkena rañjayet
children.translated_text: He should color previously purified copper with the mercury-paste.

children.text: rañjayet trīṇi vārāṇi jāyate hema śobhanam ||
children.translated_text: He should color it three times; excellent gold is produced.
He should impregnate <s>munipuṣpa</s>, oleander, and realgar.

children.text: tatpūrvaṃ rañjitaṃ śulvaṃ śilayā ca tathā yutam
children.translated_text: That copper, colored beforehand, and likewise joined with the realgar,
when placed in a closed crucible and blown, becomes excellent gold.
With that same mercury-paste he should make a silver paste.
He should quench it in <s>kaṅguṇī</s> oil; that becomes divine gold.
<s>Arjunī</s>, <s>lāṅgalī</s>, <s>padmacāriṇī</s>, and <s>śakravāruṇī</s>,
together with gold-making herbs and red ochre, O <s>Pārvatī</s>:

children.text: viliptaṃ śulvapattraṃ tu niṣiktaṃ kanakaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: a copper leaf smeared with these and quenched becomes gold.
Peacock-neck blue vitriol, saffron, and <s>rasaka</s>,
the dung of a young calf, poison, and <s>hālāhala</s> poison,
and powder of red <s>citraka</s>: he should make these in equal parts.
He should triturate them with a medium acid and dry them in the shade.
Having combined them with honey, he should smear lead leaves.
When blown in a sealed crucible, it colors lead in an instant.
He should quench it seven times with the juice of vegetable leaves,
or twenty-eight times in oil produced from <s>bhūnāga</s>.
That lead becomes divine, an ornament fit for adorning the gods.
Or else, powder of <s>bhūlatā</s> and powder of lead in equal portions,
blown in a closed crucible, should be heated and quenched in oil.
When this has been done seven times, it becomes of sixteenfold color.
The dung of a young calf, lac, red ochre, and sandalwood,
cinnabar called <s>haṃsapāda</s>, bilva pith, and molasses,
<s>rājāvarta</s> and <s>kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, with water from vegetable shoots:
by quenching a hundred times, he should make lead into gold.
<s>Mañjiṣṭhā</s>, the pair of turmerics, <s>kāṅkṣī</s>, and gold-colored <s>mākṣika</s>,
<s>kausumbha</s>, poison-born rock salt, cinnabar, and red sandalwood,
combined with vegetable shoots and <s>palāśa</s> flowers:
by quenching a hundred times, O beloved, it colors lead.
<s>Kaṅkuṣṭha</s>, sulfurous stone, and the two turmerics likewise
he should impregnate seven times with gold juice.
Quenched in <s>śiṃśapā</s> oil and repeatedly infused seven times,

children.text: nāgaṃ rañjati ca kṣipraṃ rañjitaṃ cākṣayaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: it colors lead quickly, and when colored it becomes imperishable.
Coral, cinnabar, and sharp iron should be repeatedly infused with this.
He should quench them in <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s> and <s>kiṃśuka</s> juice and also in vegetable juice.
Repeatedly infused and quenched, and colored by this sequence,

children.text: bhujago hematāṃ yāti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: lead reaches the state of gold; no deliberation is needed here.

children.text: uktaṃ hemadalaṃ devi varaṃ tāradalaṃ śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: The excellent gold leaf has been taught, O <s>Devi</s>; hear of the excellent silver leaf.

children.text: śvetābhraṃ kāñjike svinnaṃ trivāraṃ puṭitaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: White mica, boiled in sour gruel and then given <s>puṭa</s> three times,
together with a little borax and tin, should be infused into purified copper.

children.text: pañcamāṃśena miśraṃ tat tāraṃ tālaṃ ca vedhayet
children.translated_text: Mixed with a fifth part, that silver should pierce <s>tāla</s>.
He should mix that <s>tāla</s> into silver; when molten, he should pierce it with the quenched substance.
Mercury and rock salt, one part each, and sesame and <s>sarjī</s>, two parts each,
and one part borax: he should triturate them in gold juice for three days.
A copper leaf smeared with that should be blown after being melted again.
He should grind <s>iṅguda</s> together with <s>tālamūla</s> in sour curds.
Into the middle of that he should pour copper seven times; it becomes a leaf.
He should mix it with one third of the <s>bīja</s> (seed-agent), O <s>Parameśvarī</s>.
<s>Lāṅgalī</s>, <s>citraka</s>, <s>dantī</s>, <s>hayaghnā</s>, and <s>uttaravāruṇī</s>,
<s>godhāvatī</s>, <s>vajravallī</s>, white <s>arka</s>, and <s>śakravāruṇī</s>,
<s>viṣṇukrāntā</s>, <s>aśvagandhā</s>, <s>śigru</s>, and likewise <s>pañcāṅgulī</s>,
<s>punarnavā</s>, <s>apāmārga</s>, <s>iṅgudī</s>, and <s>cakramardaka</s>,
also <s>guḍūcī</s> and <s>hiṃsrā</s>, in measures of one, two, three, and four:
by preparing them with buffalo's milk, after a week, dear one,
when quenching is performed, the purification of copper is produced.
He should smear copper leaves with a sixteenth part of <s>tāla</s>.
Having placed them in a closed crucible, he should melt them again three times.
The white group, threefold alkali, conch, rock salt, and <s>sarjikā</s>,
teeth, cowries, conch-shell, and oyster shells are casting additives for copper.
A quarter of this, with sprinklings of liquor, becomes pale like a fingernail.
There should be three parts of lodestone and also two parts of copper-silver alloy.
There should be ten parts of tin; he should penetrate it by the <s>vedha</s> (piercing) of silver.

children.text: ārasya dviguṇaṃ tāraṃ tārāt kāntaṃ caturguṇam
children.translated_text: Silver is twice the copper, lodestone four times the silver,
and tin eight times the lodestone; he should penetrate it by the <s>vedha</s> of silver.

children.text: tālaṃ sūtaṃ samaṃ kṛtvā vajrīkṣīreṇa marditam
children.translated_text: Having made <s>tāla</s> and <s>sūta</s> (mercury) equal and triturated them with <s>vajrī</s> milk,

children.text: puṭaṃ dattvā tu yantreṇa sattvaṃ patati śobhanam ||
children.translated_text: after giving a <s>puṭa</s> (closed heating) by means of the apparatus, a fine essence falls down.
Having melted tin, O <s>Deveśī</s>, he should grind it with <s>vajrī</s> milk.
Done twenty-one times, this is the best purification of tin.

children.text: tadvaṅgaṃ jārayet sūtaṃ samaṃ vā dviguṇādikam ||
children.translated_text: He should cause that tin to be digested by mercury, in an equal amount or twice as much and more.
With the oil of <s>bhallāta</s> and mustard, with conch powder and <s>viḍa</s> salt,
lead and tin become so, through <s>sāraṇa</s> (flowing) with an equal amount of tin.
And by quenching in alkaline water, the <s>bīja</s> is made in the same way, in many forms.
I shall explain that method by which softness is produced.
Ghee, curds, milk, honey, and the juices of bilva and citron,
combined with jaggery and sesame, make it soft through quenching.
Elephant tusks, horse nails, ram's horn, and buffalo horn,
combined with the exudation of conch-shell: he should quench it seven times.
The leaf, split a thousandfold, takes on softness.
In the oil of <s>jyotiṣmatī</s> and safflower, or also in <s>kārañja</s> oil,
quenching of gold is very highly praised by the learned.

children.text: āvartyamānaṃ tāre ca yadi tannaiva nirmalam
children.translated_text: If, when it is being melted in silver, it is not clear,
with an addition of glass and borax it quickly reaches clarity.
With licorice, honey, ram's ghee, alum, jaggery, and rock salt,
and an addition of oyster shell, conch, and liquor, silver and copper become soft.
By quenching in calf's urine with honey, oil, and ghee,
even leaves of hard essences acquire softness.
With tamarind juice, sea salt, in the milk of <s>arka</s>, and by fire,
silver becomes purified, resembling conch, jasmine, and the moon.

children.text: yadi tannirmalaṃ naiva tadā tadvat punaḥ pacet
children.translated_text: If that is not pure, then he should cook it again in the same way.
This procedure, honored in the work of silver, has been explained.
<s>Kaṅguṇī</s> oil, madder, the two kinds of turmeric, and saffron,
through quenching, make gold shine like the young sun.
Having added sulfur equal to half the copper, and dead mercury half of that,
he should triturate it for three days with the juice of <s>cāṅgerī</s>.
Dipped in the juice of <s>citra</s>, he should smear pale gold with it.
Having cooked it with the five clays, O <s>Devi</s>, this is the best enhancement of gold.

children.text: hema śulvaṃ tathā tīkṣṇaṃ samabhāgāni kārayet
children.translated_text: He should make gold, copper, and sharp iron in equal parts.
Blown while placed in a closed crucible, it immediately becomes a <s>khoṭa</s>.
One part of the <s>khoṭa</s>, combined with mercury and gold,
he should cook with sour gruel until it resembles saffron.
With one hundredth part of that very substance he should penetrate pale gold.
Divine gold is produced; it becomes an enhancement by two colors.
Until it becomes pure, he should heat it in a <s>puṭa</s> with salt ash.
It should be quenched in red oil; excellent gold is produced.
Gold ochre and sulfur triturated with pungent oil,
or else <s>rājāvarta</s> and <s>mākṣika</s> in the acid of citron,
or else pigeon dung, <s>rājāvarta</s>, and rock salt:
by heating in a <s>puṭa</s>, it makes pale gold saffron-colored.
Powder of <s>rājāvarta</s>, steeped in the juices of <s>śirīṣa</s> flowers
many times and added in an eightieth part, gives color.

children.text: śataśaḥ kaṅguṇītaile tāmraṃ hemnā samaṃ drutam
children.translated_text: Copper, repeatedly treated a hundred times in <s>kaṅguṇī</s> oil and melted with an equal amount of gold,
with <s>mākṣika</s> as the additive, produces color when used in a hundredth part.
With cotton seed, realgar, blue vitriol, rock salt, and ochres,
with lac on leaves, madder, red sandalwood, and coral,
joined with jaggery, <s>bhallātaka</s> oil, calf dung, and brick,
by the addition, white gold becomes like the sun.

children.text: raktāṣṭakaṃ trayo bhāgāḥ trayo bhāgāḥ samudrajam
children.translated_text: Three parts of the red octad and three parts of what is born from the sea:
a <s>puṭa</s> with the water of white <s>arka</s> leaves grants color.

children.text: raktapītau samau kṛtvā tābhyāṃ tulyaṃ ca mākṣikam
children.translated_text: Having made the red and the yellow equal, and <s>mākṣika</s> equal to those two,
he should stir it with <s>karañja</s> oil and blow it in a sealed crucible.
Once, with a tenth part of yellow, it penetrates ten; with a hundred of yellow, ten;
with a thousand of yellow it penetrates a hundred; with half, it penetrates a crore.
Salt, steeped again hundreds of times in the juice of <s>kiṃśuka</s>,
with a <s>puṭa</s> of borax itself, becomes a giver of color-enhancement.

children.text: lohacūrṇaṃ trayo bhāgā gairikaṃ dviguṇaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Iron powder should be three parts, and likewise red ochre twice as much.
He should moisten it with waters of <s>madhuka</s> and <s>kumuda</s>, and also with urine.
He should grind it with <s>kodrava</s> alone and place it in the middle of a cowshed.
With an eightieth part, this becomes color-giving when added by casting.
He should subject gold that has an excess of copper to a <s>puṭa</s> in a sealed crucible.
