At that time quenching with the water of a marine mineral is recommended.
When smeared with marine ochre and melted, it becomes soft.
Smeared with cow-dung ash, it should be coated with an equal part of that.
Gold with excess copper becomes pure by the <s>puṭa</s> procedure.
The skilled man, after smearing the crucible with a paste of ash from <s>nāga</s> bones,
should place it in a sealed crucible; it always becomes gold leaf.
Then the skilled man should spread it out with gentle blows,
and, heated again and again, it should be quenched until it becomes soft.
The skilled man should smear it with a paste of marine mineral,
place it on a <s>palāśa</s> leaf, and burn it with a gentle fire.
The wise man should cook it again and again until it becomes pure.
Then, having made it cool, he should afterward quench it in water.
This same procedure should be done until the color has appeared.
Then he should heat it again, joined with cow-dung powder.
When it is heated by the fire, the wise man should cast it into salt.
Then he should cook the refined gold with salt and red ochres.

children.text: karṣakeṇa tu saṃśodhya bhūyo bhūyo vicakṣaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The skilled man should purify it again and again with a <s>karṣa</s> measure.
He should smear it and subject it to <s>puṭa</s>, for the production of color.
O <s>Deveśī</s>, he should cook <s>tārāriṣṭa</s> in red oil.
He should quench it hundreds of times; the protected leaf becomes dyed.
He should carry through the class of <s>rasa</s> and secondary minerals into <s>nāga</s> and <s>vaṅga</s>.

children.text: nāgavaṅgau punaḥ śulve śulvaṃ tāre tu nirvahet ||
children.translated_text: Again, he should carry <s>nāga</s> and <s>vaṅga</s> into copper, and copper into silver.

children.text: tāraṃ niṣiktaṃ deveśi raktataile punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: O <s>Deveśī</s>, silver quenched again and again in red oil
becomes fine gold, free from every defect.
The residue of <s>rasa</s>, combined with half its amount of gold, is praised.
It becomes divine gold, excellent, equal to <s>mātṛkā</s>.

children.text: vaṅgābhraṃ sitatāpyaṃ vā śailaṃ vā vāpayet site
children.translated_text: He should cast <s>vaṅgābhra</s>, white <s>tāpya</s>, or <s>śaila</s> into silver.
That, in a tenth part, gives excellence of color to silver.
There should be ninety-eight parts of <s>tārāriṣṭa</s>, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.
One part each of <s>rasa</s> and gold is remembered as the hundredfold penetrator.
By this ordered procedure it penetrates with a thousandth part.

children.text: mūṣāṃ tu gostanīṃ kṛtvā dalapūrṇāṃ tathā dṛḍhām
children.translated_text: He should make a cow-udder-shaped crucible, firm and filled with metal leaves.
He should blow the pure leaf when it is held and opened.

children.text: krāmaṇena samāyuktaṃ rasaṃ dattvā tu vedhayet
children.translated_text: Joined with <s>krāmaṇa</s>, he should add <s>rasa</s> and cause penetration.
The metal leaf, smeared with <s>rasa</s>, is placed inside a copper vessel.
It is smeared over with clay on top, and only a gentle fire is applied.
Having melted it together with the seed-substance, the intelligent man should always set it aside.

children.text: ṭaṅkaṇaṃ tilacūrṇaṃ ca śītale tu nivāpayet
children.translated_text: He should quench it, when cool, with borax and sesame powder.
He should keep the <s>rasa</s>-perfected gold in the ground for one fortnight.
Having taken it out and opened it again, it may be sold, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>.
Again I shall explain how penetration by <s>rasa</s> takes place.
He should provide two <s>palas</s> of sesame and mustard powder,

children.text: dve pale ca haridrāyā ekatraiva tu mardayet ||
children.translated_text: and two <s>palas</s> of turmeric, and grind them together.
He should grind five <s>palas</s> of <s>pannaga</s> in an earthen vessel.
He should cast it with perfected mercury and stir it with a rod.
Again he should cast it repeatedly until it becomes hard.
That <s>nāga</s> becomes divine, with a luster equal to <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold.
I shall explain the opening, and the <s>pannaga</s> penetrated by <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: ghoṣākṛṣṭaṃ tu yat śulvaṃ ṣoḍaśāṃśena yojayet
children.translated_text: He should combine copper drawn from bell-metal with a sixteenth part.
Having united and melted it, he should quench it in goat's urine.
It becomes beautiful gold, completely free from all defects.
This is known as metal penetration, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>, in its full extent.

children.text: yathā lohe tathā dehe kartavyaḥ sūtakaḥ sadā
children.translated_text: As with metal, so with the body, mercury should always be applied.
O <s>Devī</s>, entering both body and metal, it makes them the same.

children.text: pūrvaṃ lohe parīkṣeta tato dehe prayojayet
children.translated_text: First one should test it on metal; afterward one should apply it to the body.
Tell me that, O <s>Deveśī</s>; what else do you wish to hear?
<s>Śrīdevī</s> said:
O <s>Deva</s>, the metal penetrations have been described by you for a certain purpose.

children.text: taṃ dehavedham ācakṣva yena syāt khecarī gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Explain that body penetration by which sky-going motion may arise.
<s>Śrībhairava</s> said:
First one should purify the body; afterward one should perform the paste procedure.

children.text: anyathā na bhavet siddhiḥ rase caiva rasāyane ||
children.translated_text: Otherwise there is no success in <s>rasa</s> or in <s>rasāyana</s>.
At the beginning, morning after morning for three days, one should drink ghee with rock salt.

children.text: ketakyāḥ stanajaṃ kvāthaṃ tadanu tridinaṃ pibet ||
children.translated_text: After that, for three days, one should drink a decoction of the breast-born product of <s>ketakī</s>.
Having performed sweating according to rule, together with <s>yavakṣāra</s> and sugar,
one should drink a decoction of <s>varā</s> for three days, O one honored by gods and demons.
When purgation has properly arisen from a decoction of <s>kaṭukarohiṇī</s>,
one should eat barley food for three days, mixed with ghee.
By eating medicinal balls of <s>palāśa</s> seed, worm-killer, and <s>guṇa</s>,
one should bring about the expulsion of worms, and then with <s>kākeṣṭa</s> water,
from <s>vacā</s>, pepper, rock salt, turmeric, <s>kaṇa</s>, and dry ginger,
and from <s>dhātrī</s>, jaggery, and <s>viḍaṅga</s>, one should take powder for three days.
Having been purified in this way, with <s>śāli</s> rice, milk, mung-bean water, and barley preparation,
then, after becoming strong, one should undertake the <s>rasāyana</s> procedure.
With the juice of <s>dhātrī</s>, ghee, and honey, and with milks produced from celestial trees,
one should churn out the oil, O <s>Deveśī</s>, furnished with two, four, or six <s>palas</s>.
In the light, middle, and excellent measures, he should drink it every day for three months.

children.text: āroṭaṃ bhakṣayet paścāt jīrṇaṃ ca tadanantaram ||
children.translated_text: Afterwards he should eat <s>āroṭa</s>; when that has been digested, then the next step follows.

children.text: kṣetrīkṛtya tato dehaṃ tato bhakṣyaṃ tu vardhayet ||
children.translated_text: Having thus made the body into a prepared field, he should then increase the food to be eaten.
After purifying it with <s>vyoma</s> (mica) and <s>tāpya</s>, and after making it descend,
the <s>rasa</s> (mercury), ground with <s>taṇḍulīyaka</s> and what is called <s>bhṛṅga</s>, should be subjected to infusion.
He should first take this as <s>āroṭa</s> for bodily perfection.
Or else, when it has become ash through combination with paste six times,
he should make use of the <s>āroṭaka</s> until a full year has passed.
Food made of mineral pitch, honey, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, ghee, iron, <s>abhayā</s>, mercury, and <s>tāpya</s>
fills the weak constituents of the body in fifteen nights, just as the moon is filled.
With the juice of <s>bakakanyā</s>, honey, the two <s>niśās</s>, <s>triphala</s>, and jaggery,
mercury made into a paste and combined with <s>vyoma</s>, <s>kānta</s>, honey, and ghee,
when eaten, leads one to immortality; this is the best preparation of the body as a field.
Then powder of the essence of mica, or of <s>kānta</s> iron,
or of <s>tīkṣṇa</s> iron, O <s>Mahādevī</s>, should be steeped in a decoction of <s>triphala</s>.
Until it resembles collyrium, it should be screened through cloth and purified.
With the essence of <s>bhṛṅga</s> and <s>āmalaka</s>, and with the juice of turmeric,
it is heated in a covered firing, combined with mercury, and mixed with honey and ghee.
Placed inside an iron capsule, it should be set in grain for a month.
He should lick it with ghee and honey; it is the best preparation of the body as a field.
By using it for a year in this way, a man becomes one whose life lasts a thousand years.

children.text: rasasiddheḥ purā hema guñjāmātraṃ dine dine
children.translated_text: Before the perfection of mercury, he should eat gold the size of a <s>guñjā</s> day by day,
for the sake of bodily perfection; then the perfection of mercury arises.
<s>Kānta</s> and mica-essence, together with mercury and slightly digested with gold,
he should lick at the beginning with equal honey and ghee; it is the best preparation of the body as a field.

children.text: varṣaṃ varṣārdham athavā pūrvamevaṃ tu bhakṣayet ||
children.translated_text: For a year, or for half a year, he should eat it beforehand in this way.
Mercury digested with <s>vajra</s>, O <s>Devī</s>, is proclaimed to be the best.
That digested with gold is middling, and that digested with silver is inferior, O beloved.
When ash-mercury digested with gold is eaten, one reaches the state of <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: viṣṇutvaṃ tārajīrṇe tu brahmatvaṃ bhāskareṇa tu ||
children.translated_text: Through that digested with silver one reaches the state of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and through that digested with <s>Bhāskara</s>, the state of <s>Brahmā</s>.
When it is digested with <s>tīkṣṇa</s> iron, one becomes lord of wealth; in the abode of <s>capala</s>, one gains solar nature.

children.text: vājare tu śaśāṅkatvam analatvaṃ tu rohaṇe
children.translated_text: With <s>vajra</s> one gains the state of the moon, and with <s>rohaṇa</s> the state of fire.
In general, by means of <s>tīkṣṇa</s> iron, a man obtains the state of <s>Śakra</s>.
Thus whoever eats ash-mercury digested with metal

children.text: jalena jalarūpaḥ syāt sthalena sthalatāṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: becomes water-formed with water, and with earth he assumes the nature of earth.
When fire is predominant he becomes fire, and he is stronger even than wind.
He himself is directly the destroyer and creator, the maker of curses and blessings.
Wherever the practitioner lets fall his urine and feces,

children.text: pāṣāṇo mṛnmayaṃ tatra spaṣṭaṃ bhavati kāñcanam ||
children.translated_text: there stone and what is made of clay clearly become gold.
The sweat of his limbs penetrates the eight metals.

children.text: tat sarvaṃ kanakaṃ nityaṃ bhakṣite dvādaśe pale
children.translated_text: All that always becomes gold, when the twelfth <s>pala</s> has been eaten.
He becomes equal to <s>Rudra</s>, O <s>Mahādevī</s>; it makes him ageless and immortal.

children.text: bhasmasūtaṃ tathā tāraṃ bhakṣayet ṣoḍaśaṃ palam
children.translated_text: Likewise he should eat ash-mercury and silver to the measure of sixteen <s>palas</s>.
Or else he should eat ash-mercury digested with silver.

children.text: śulvaṃ ca vaṅgaghoṣaṃ ca tatsvedāt tāratāṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: Copper, tin, and bell-metal become silver through his sweat.
Or else he should eat ash-mercury digested with <s>tīkṣṇa</s> iron.

children.text: mūtreṇa tasya spṛṣṭaṃ tu vaṅgaṃ vrajati tāratām ||
children.translated_text: Tin touched by his urine becomes silver.
With each single sprinkling, lead and tin are stabilized.

children.text: guñjāmātraṃ rasaṃ devi hemajīrṇaṃ tu bhakṣayet
children.translated_text: O <s>Devī</s>, he should eat mercury digested with gold in the measure of a <s>guñjā</s>.
For silver-digested mercury the dose is two <s>guñjās</s>; for sun-digested mercury, three of them.
For <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, mica, and <s>kānta</s>, one <s>māṣa</s>; for a liquefying substance, one <s>guñjā</s>.
Mercury digested with <s>vajra</s> and <s>vaikrānta</s> should be eaten together with ghee.
Lead, tin, mercury, and ash, combined with poisons and subsidiary poisons,
and furnished with the proper dose, should then be eaten in the <s>rasāyana</s> treatment.

children.text: hema tāraṃ tathā kāntaṃ jāyate'gnisahaṃ kramāt
children.translated_text: Gold, silver, and <s>kānta</s> become fire-resistant in due order,
and this bound king of mercury grants bodily perfection.
With diamond, lodestone, <s>mākṣīka</s>, <s>vaikrānta</s>, mica, and gold,
mercury digested with these, as available, is praised in <s>rasāyana</s>.
He should also cause the six subsidiary minerals to be prepared for eating.
From eating that which is digested with <s>tīkṣṇa</s> iron, he should eat one <s>pala</s>.
He lives for up to ten thousand years, with a diamond body.

children.text: evaṃ ca dvādaśapalaṃ tīkṣṇajīrṇaṃ tu bhakṣayet
children.translated_text: In this way he should eat twelve <s>palas</s> of that digested with <s>tīkṣṇa</s> iron.
Thus he lives for a great aeon, and at the end of dissolution he reaches <s>Śiva</s>.
Of ash digested with copper, one <s>pala</s> gives a hundred thousand years of life.
Two <s>palas</s> give a crore of years; three <s>palas</s> give the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Four <s>palas</s> give the lifespan of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and the fifth <s>pala</s> the lifespan of <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: ṣaṣṭhe pale ca samprāpte mahākalpaṃ sa jīvati ||
children.translated_text: When the sixth <s>pala</s> has been reached, he lives for a great aeon.
Of ash digested with gold, one <s>pala</s> gives the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Two <s>palas</s> give the lifespan of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and three <s>palas</s> the lifespan of <s>Rudra</s>.
With four <s>palas</s>, O <s>Deveśī</s>, a man obtains the state of <s>Śiva</s>.
When three <s>palas</s> of gold-digested ash-mercury have been eaten in sequence,
eighty-eight thousand <s>yoginīs</s>, swollen with power,
stand as his servants; the man becomes able to assume any desired form.
Whatever form he visualizes, he becomes the bearer of that very form.
With measured doses amounting to eleven <s>palas</s>, he should eat the ashes of gold.
Knowing his own digestive fire, O <s>Deveśī</s>, he should take only the measure of one <s>guñjā</s> berry,
cover it with ghee and honey, take betel, and enjoy women.

children.text: eko hi doṣaḥ sūkṣmo'yaṃ bhakṣite bhasmasūtake
children.translated_text: There is this one subtle fault when ash-like <s>sūtaka</s> has been eaten:
for three times seven days, O fair-hipped one, a man becomes blinded by desire.
He could excite a thousand passionate women in the course of a day,
but through intercourse with women, O fair-hipped one, the <s>sūtaka</s> moves through the body.
Through intercourse with women, O fair-hipped one, indigestion arises in him.
When semen is stirred by sexual union, gradually up to three times seven days
danger to life arises; therefore he should avoid that sexual union.
Conversation with a young woman may be done, and massage of the limbs by a young woman,
for by her mere touch <s>rasa</s> circulates in the body.
Just as desire itself arises from beholding the form of a beautiful woman,

children.text: tathā krāmyati deveśi sūtako'sau tataḥ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: so, O <s>Deveśī</s>, that <s>sūtaka</s> then circulates in due order.
The woman whose vulva is like the leaf of an aśvattha tree, even and auspicious,

children.text: tādṛśyāḥ surataṃ devi bhājanaṃ tu rasāyane ||
children.translated_text: with such a woman, O <s>Devī</s>, sexual enjoyment is a vessel for <s>rasāyana</s>.
But a vulva that is fleshless, long, and dry-veined
should always be avoided in <s>rasāyana</s>, as causing poverty.
He should satisfy them daily with an offering and present fish and meat.
Having worshiped the lordly yogins and yoginīs with mantras, he should ask forgiveness.
He should avoid the group of eight beginning with the letter ka, and pungent, sour, and salty things.
With one <s>pala</s> of digested mica, he is not overcome by diseases.

children.text: dvitīye śukravṛddhiḥ syāt tṛtīye balavān bhavet ||
children.translated_text: At the second, there is an increase of semen; at the third, he becomes strong.

children.text: caturthe palitaṃ hanti valīṃ jayati pañcame
children.translated_text: At the fourth, it destroys grey hair; at the fifth, it conquers wrinkles.
At the sixth, he is retentive of what he has heard and eloquent; at the seventh, he conquers eye disease.
At the eighth, his sight becomes like <s>Tārkṣya</s>'s; he has the lifespan and prowess of <s>Brahmā</s>.
By using nine <s>palas</s>, he becomes one who can meet with the gods.
By the use of ten <s>palas</s>, he becomes a second <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
For the protection of the potency of <s>rasa</s>, he should give a bali offering day by day.
He should recite the <s>Mṛtyuñjaya</s> mantra; success in <s>rasa</s> is produced.

children.text: same tu vimale jīrṇe yo rasaṃ bhakṣayennaraḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>rasa</s> has been digested in an equal amount of pure <s>vimala</s>, the man who eats it
lives for ten thousand years, O <s>Parameśvarī</s>.

children.text: dviguṇe vimale jīrṇe daśalakṣaṃ sa jīvati
children.translated_text: When it has been digested in twice as much <s>vimala</s>, he lives for a hundred thousand years.

children.text: triguṇe vimale jīrṇe daśakoṭiṃ ca jīvati ||
children.translated_text: When it has been digested in three times as much <s>vimala</s>, he lives for ten crores of years.

children.text: jīrṇe caturguṇe devi rasaḥ khecaratāṃ nayet
children.translated_text: When it has been digested in four times as much, O <s>Devī</s>, <s>rasa</s> brings about sky-going motion.
Then, when digested in five times as much, the great <s>rasa</s> penetrates by touch.
Whatever result there is when it is digested in <s>vimala</s>, the same applies to gold pyrites.

children.text: tat phalaṃ labhate devi tasya vīrye sa jīvati ||
children.translated_text: That fruit he obtains, O <s>Devī</s>; by its potency he lives.
Again I shall explain another <s>rasāyana</s>, the ash of diamond.
First he should digest sulphur in mercury, O one honored by the gods.

children.text: dāpayettriguṇaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ samaṃ hema ca sūtake ||
children.translated_text: He should add three times as much sharp iron and an equal amount of gold to the mercury.
With that same gold-digested substance, he should smear the diamond jewel.
Then he should wrap that diamond with the dung of a young calf.

children.text: baddhvā poṭalikāṃ tena puṭapākaṃ tu dāpayet
children.translated_text: Having tied it into a small bundle with that, he should subject it to baking in a covered heating pit.
At once it becomes ash, resembling conch, jasmine, and the moon.
That diamond ash, O lovely one, he should make equal to a paste preparation.
He should triturate it with the powder of that mercury ball, whose body has departed.
Again, with the powder of that ball and with dung from a young calf,

children.text: mūṣālepaṃ tu tenaiva ardhārdhena tu kārayet ||
children.translated_text: he should make the coating for the crucible with that very substance, half and half.
He should blow it in a closed crucible, stupefied and digested with diamond.
By a thousand blasts of the bellows, that ash is produced at once.
Ash is obtained in halves, like cow's milk, O beloved.
The paste that is kept in fat, combined with <s>kaṅguṇī</s> oil,
brings about purification of the body after three times seven days, O fair-hipped one.
A sesame-seed measure of diamond ash, and the same amount of gold ash,
should be blown after being smeared with datura juice; it destroys wrinkles and grey hair.
Eight <s>palas</s> of purified gold, joined with dead mercury,
he should triturate with a medium sour liquid; a ball is produced at once.

children.text: ardhaṃ ca prāpyate bhasma gokṣīrasadṛśaṃ priye ||
children.translated_text: Half is obtained as ash, resembling cow's milk, O beloved.
One part of dead diamond and four parts of the ball
he should triturate in a heated mortar; the <s>sūtaka</s> becomes ash.
He should kill it in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus, according to the sequence of seven enclosures.

children.text: tadbhasma tu punaḥ paścāt madhyamāmlena mardayet ||
children.translated_text: Then afterward he should again triturate that ash with a medium sour liquid.
He should carefully give three hundred and sixty heating operations.
That ash becomes, O <s>Devī</s>, like vermilion in its red color.
He should lick one <s>pala</s> of that ash, combined with honey and ghee.
In this way he should lick it seven times, living on milk and having conquered his senses.
On the second and seventh occasions he should eat two <s>palas</s>.
By this gradual increase, he should eat seven sevens.
Through that increase a man becomes accomplished and possessed of divine splendor.
His lifespan becomes that of <s>Rudra</s>, and there is no doubt that he gains sky-going power.
By his urine and feces, the eight metals become gold.
One <s>pala</s> of that ash, endowed with <s>krāmaṇa</s>,
when applied to a mass of substance measuring twelve thousand <s>palas</s>, O serpent-like one,
becomes divine gold, adorned as ornaments for the gods.
Eight <s>palas</s> of powdered <s>kānta</s>, and eight <s>palas</s> of <s>rasa</s>...
Having combined them and then triturated them, rubbed with the sour juice of <s>bījapūra</s>,
one should grind it in a heated mortar; a pellet forms at once.
One part of calcined <s>vajra</s> and four parts of the pellet
should be combined and then triturated; the <s>sūtaka</s> becomes ash.
One should kill it in the <s>Bhūdhara</s> apparatus, by the sequence of seven links.

children.text: tadbhasmabhāgam ekaṃ tu bhāgaikaṃ gandhakasya ca
children.translated_text: One part of that ash, and one part of sulfur as well,
placed in a blind crucible and blown, becomes a <s>khoṭa</s> at once.
Thirty-two parts of the calcined <s>khoṭa</s>, and twenty parts of purified gold,
silver, copper, essence of mica, and essence of lodestone as the fourth,
should each be twelve parts; one should bring everything together.
Placed in a blind crucible and blown, it becomes a <s>khoṭa</s> at once.
One should make the thirty-two combined <s>khoṭas</s> into a fine powder.
That fine powder of <s>khoṭa</s>, combined with <s>āroṭa-rasa</s>,
should be ground with a medium acid; a pellet forms at once.

children.text: golakasya pale dve ca mṛtakāntasya tatsamam
children.translated_text: There should be two <s>palas</s> of the pellet and the same amount of calcined <s>kānta</s>.
Having combined them and then triturated them with the juice of <s>meghanāda</s>,
and also with the juice of <s>munipuṣpa</s>, one should grind for one day.
One should make three hundred and sixty pills, O <s>Devī</s>.
Of these, one pill, joined with ghee, <s>triphalā</s>, and honey,
should be eaten for one year; a man obtains the lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: sarvāstā bhakṣayet paścāt rudrāyuḥ sa bhavennaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: If afterward he eats all of them, that man obtains the lifespan of <s>Rudra</s>.
Now, if one pill is held in the mouth, O <s>Amarasundarī</s>,
it forcefully destroys all diseases and gray hairs.
I shall explain the regimen for the <s>vajra-sattva rasāyana</s>.

children.text: vajrabaddhastu yo devi raso'yaṃ vajratāṃ nayet
children.translated_text: This <s>rasa</s>, bound by <s>vajra</s>, O <s>Devī</s>, brings about a diamond-like state.

children.text: tena baddhāstu ye dehāste dehā vajrarūpiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Bodies bound by it are bodies of diamond-like form.

children.text: tilamātraṃ rasaṃ devi brahmāyur daśa jīvati
children.translated_text: A sesame-grain measure of <s>rasa</s>, O <s>Devī</s>, makes one live for ten lifespans of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: yavamātraṃ rasaṃ devi viṣṇukoṭiṃ sa jīvati ||
children.translated_text: A barley-grain measure of <s>rasa</s>, O <s>Devī</s>, makes him live for a crore of lifespans of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
A <s>guñjā</s>-seed measure, O <s>Deveśī</s>, makes him one whose life lasts a great aeon.
A <s>māṣa</s> measure, O fair-hipped one, makes him equal to me in qualities.

children.text: mantrahīnena subhage na sa gamyo bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Without mantra, O lovely one, it will not be attainable by him.
Nor will the practice for his attainment succeed, even in hundreds of crores of births.
This foolish-minded man wanders about, deprived of the teaching of the <s>kula</s>.
Thousands of obstacles are made for him by gods and <s>dānavas</s>,
and by goddesses who move in the sky and those who move on the earth, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>.

children.text: svapne taṃ bhajayitvā tu retorakte haranti tāḥ
children.translated_text: Having enjoyed him in a dream, they take away his semen and blood.
Through that very channel of semen they take away the <s>rasa</s> he has eaten.
The planets beginning with <s>Bhāskara</s>, O <s>Devī</s>, roar in their own form.

children.text: kṣatriyasya tu rūpeṇa devā vai garjayanti ca ||
children.translated_text: And the gods roar in the form of a <s>kṣatriya</s>.
<s>Piśācas</s> take the form of <s>vaiśyas</s>, and <s>rākṣasas</s> the form of <s>śūdras</s>.
Others, in human form, approach him in the midst of dreams.
They eat his bones and flesh in dreams, O <s>Surasundarī</s>.

children.text: svapnānte prāpyate bhrāntiḥ prāyaḥ paśyati mānavaḥ
children.translated_text: At the end of the dream, delusion arises; a man often sees this.
They carry off the <s>vajra</s>-ash and disturb him at the end of dreams.
When pure, spotless gold has been consumed, they flee to the ten directions,
<s>bhūtas</s>, <s>pretas</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, <s>śākinīs</s>, <s>guhyakas</s>, and the rest.

children.text: vajrāṇāṃ māraṇe ye tu lohānāṃ vā rasasya tu
children.translated_text: In the killing of diamonds, or of metals, or of <s>rasa</s>,
those things must be carefully avoided; hear of them as they are employed, dear one.
The forms of their procedures, as employed by those who provide the methods,

children.text: evaṃ vadanti bhūtādyā bhīṣayanti sma taṃ naram ||
children.translated_text: are thus described by the <s>bhūtas</s> and others, who terrify that man.

children.text: rañjako rāgakārī syāt krāmaṇaḥ krāmaṇe hitaḥ
children.translated_text: A colorant should be a producer of color; a penetrator is useful for penetration.
Binders are strengtheners, and similarly they are remembered as nourishers.
He may consume it in various ways with semen, blood, feces, and urine.
But that, if tainted with lead and tin, produces <s>kuṣṭha</s> disease.
<s>Triphalā</s>, <s>jātī</s>, and <s>kaṅkola</s>, mixed with camphor and <s>rasa</s>,
and <s>khadira</s>, ground with an equal amount of water: he should consume the <s>rasa</s>.
Having rubbed <s>kaṭuka</s> with milk, it is a wholesome and excellent <s>krāmaṇa</s>.
This should not be eaten with breast milk rubbed with gold, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>.
From eating <s>alambuṣā</s>, lodestone, and <s>tālaka</s>,

children.text: dehe krāmati sūtendro nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: the lord of <s>sūta</s> penetrates the body; no doubt is to be entertained here.

children.text: avaśyaṃ kramate sūtaḥ strīyoge krāmaṇaṃ param
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s> necessarily penetrates; union with a woman is the supreme <s>krāmaṇa</s>.

children.text: brahmacaryeṇa vā yogī sadā seveta sūtakam ||
children.translated_text: Or, with celibacy, the yogin should always consume <s>sūtaka</s>.

children.text: samādhiḥ kāraṇaṃ tacca krāmaṇaṃ paramaṃ matam ||
children.translated_text: Absorption is its cause, and is regarded as the supreme <s>krāmaṇa</s>.
In the morning he should consume <s>sūta</s>; the proper food is after more than two <s>yāmas</s>.

children.text: no laṅghayet triyāmaṃ tu madhyāhne na tu bhojayet ||
children.translated_text: He should not let three <s>yāmas</s> pass, and he should not eat at midday.
He should avoid excessive drinking, excessive eating, excessive sleep, and excessive wakefulness,
excessive attachment to women and excessive travel.
He should avoid excessive anger, excessive joy, excessive restlessness, and excessive desire,
dry disputation, playing in water, and excessive worry.
Pumpkin, cucumber, watermelon, and bitter gourd,
<s>kusumbhaka</s>, <s>karkoṭa</s>, plantain, and <s>kākamācikā</s>:
one who consumes <s>rasa</s> should avoid this set of eight beginning with the sound ka.

children.text: pātakaṃ ca na kartavyaṃ paśusaṅgaṃ vivarjayet
children.translated_text: No sinful act should be done, and contact with animals should be avoided.

children.text: liṅgacchāyāṃ na laṅgheta nārīchāyāṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: He should not step across the shadow of a <s>liṅga</s>, nor likewise the shadow of a woman.

children.text: catuḥpathe na gantavyaṃ viṇmūtraṃ na ca laṅghayet
children.translated_text: He should not go to a crossroads, and he should not step across feces or urine.

children.text: surāṇāṃ nindanaṃ devi strīṇāṃ nindāṃ ca varjayet ||
children.translated_text: He should avoid censuring the gods, O <s>Devī</s>, and censuring women.

children.text: satyaṃ ca vacanaṃ brūyādapriyaṃ na vadedvacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He should speak a truthful word; he should not speak an unpleasant word.
He should avoid horse gram, linseed oil, sesame seeds, black gram, and lentils,
as well as <s>kapotaka</s>, sour-gruel food, and rice mixed with buttermilk.
Whatever is bitter, sour, sharp, salty, slimy, or productive of bile,
sesame oil, curds, milk, grapes, jujube, and <s>parūṣaka</s>,
badara, <s>cirabilva</s>, mango, and <s>suvarcala</s>,
orange, <s>kāñcanāra</s>, and even <s>śobhāñjana</s>, he should abandon.

children.text: kṣudhārto naiva tiṣṭheta ajīrṇaṃ naiva kārayet
children.translated_text: He should not remain afflicted by hunger, nor should he bring on indigestion.

children.text: na vādajalpanaṃ kuryāt divāsvāpaṃ na kārayet ||
children.translated_text: He should not engage in debate or idle talk, and he should not sleep by day.

children.text: naivedyaṃ naiva bhuñjīta karpūraṃ varjayet sadā
children.translated_text: He should not eat food offered as <s>naivedya</s>, and he should always avoid camphor.
Anointing with saffron is to be avoided; he should also avoid dancing on the ground.

children.text: nāgniṃ spṛśettu pādena na gā vā brāhmaṇānna ca
children.translated_text: He should not touch fire with his foot, nor a cow or a brahmin.

children.text: na hanyāt kumārīṃ ca vātulānapi varjayet ||
children.translated_text: He should not strike a maiden, and he should also avoid deranged people.

children.text: divārātraṃ japenmantraṃ snātavyaṃ ca dine dine ||
children.translated_text: Day and night he should recite the mantra, and he should bathe every day.

children.text: hitaṃ ca mudgā dugdhānnaṃ śālyannaṃ ca samāhitam
children.translated_text: Beneficial are mung beans, milk-rice, and carefully prepared <s>śāli</s> rice.

children.text: śākaṃ paunarnavaṃ devi meghanādaṃ ca vāstukam
children.translated_text: Vegetables such as <s>paunarnava</s>, O <s>Devī</s>, <s>meghanāda</s>, and <s>vāstuka</s>,
rock salt, dry ginger, <s>mustā</s>, and lotus roots he may eat.
A dark-hued, beautiful, fortunate, auspicious woman with developed nipples,
endowed with divine radiance and with her erotic power increased,
should be kept nearby, and should be protected by elders.
He should never consort with one who is dark or pale, whose body is over-aged, or who is of bad conduct.

children.text: tilakaṃ kuṅkumaṃ gandhaṃ kastūryā ca manoharam
children.translated_text: A tilaka, saffron, fragrance, and charming musk,
fragrant flowers, a pleasant bed, and desired food,
comfortable dwelling itself is taught as the <s>krāmaṇa</s> of <s>sūta</s> (mercury).
So too are discourse on self-knowledge and especially the worship of <s>Śiva</s>.
These observances, O <s>Bhadre</s>, he should not transgress while consuming <s>rasa</s>.
From transgression various signs are observed; his symptoms are now described.

children.text: rasarāje tvajīrṇe tu pratyayo'yaṃ bhavet priye
children.translated_text: When the king of <s>rasa</s> is undigested, this sign appears, O beloved:

children.text: mūrcchā śoko bhramaḥ kampaḥ chardirmoho jvarastathā ||
children.translated_text: fainting, grief, dizziness, trembling, vomiting, stupefaction, and fever,
hiccup, shaking, pains, sleepiness, lassitude, and loss of appetite,
stiffness of the penis, diarrhea, cough, difficult breathing, and yawning,
and in the ears, mouth, eyes, belly, testicles, abdomen, and head,
burning in the penis, weakness of digestion, and disorder arising throughout the whole body.
Other great diseases too should be recognized when <s>rasa</s> is undigested.
Sour gruel, alkali of <s>sarjikā</s>, soaked in bitter-gourd juice,
mixed with cow urine and rock salt: he should drink that as its <s>saṃkrāmaṇa</s> remedy.
O <s>Devī</s>, the juice of <s>mokṣaka</s> and the juice of royal <s>koṣātakī</s>,
<s>sindhuka</s>, black cow urine, soaked in bitter-gourd juice,
and combined with <s>sauvarcala</s> salt should be drunk by a man when <s>rasa</s> is undigested.

children.text: rasājīrṇe na jīvettu mriyate nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>rasa</s> is undigested he does not live; he dies, without doubt.

children.text: rasāyane sujīrṇe tu tena sarvaṃ vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: But when the <s>rasāyana</s> is well digested, everything is accomplished by it.

children.text: yadā suptastadaṅgaṃ ca strī stanenaiva gharṣayet
children.translated_text: When he is asleep, a woman should rub his body with her breast,
and should massage him with the left hand; thus <s>sūta</s> moves on without pain.
In a windless, solitary place, in an underground chamber free from disturbance,
free from cold and heat, eating wholesome food and taking light meals,
he obtains success in the stated number of days; there is no doubt about this.
With all foods, he obtains success in twice as many days.
Through exposure to cold and wind, success comes in three times as many days, in sequence,
and through the conditions of excessive wandering, in four times as many days.
There I shall explain <s>vedha</s> (penetration), preceded by bodily perfection.
Out of affection for you, O <s>Deveśī</s>, the <s>rasāyana</s> has already been taught.
Skin-penetration, O <s>Devī</s>, is first; flesh-penetration is second.
The third is blood-penetration, and the fourth is bone-penetration.
The fifth is marrow-penetration; channel-penetration is the sixth.
The seventh is metal-penetration, and the eighth is that of the <s>kavaca</s>.
Through skin-penetration, O <s>Deveśī</s>, <s>pannaga</s> becomes <s>kuṭila</s>.
Through flesh-penetration, O fair one, <s>kuṭila</s> becomes gold.
Through bone-penetration, O <s>Deveśī</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s> reaches the state of gold.
Marrow-penetration, O lovely-waisted one, penetrates all eight metals.

children.text: kavacasya tu vedhena mṛnmaye kāñcanaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Through penetration of the <s>kavaca</s>, what is earthen becomes gold.

children.text: vedhe tu hemavimale majjño hema prajāyate ||
children.translated_text: And when there is penetration in stainless gold, gold is produced from marrow.
In silver, O <s>Sureśānī</s>, digested <s>sūta</s> penetrates the flesh,

children.text: alake vimale tāpye tīkṣṇe tāre ca bhāskare ||
children.translated_text: in <s>alaka</s>, <s>vimala</s>, <s>tāpya</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, silver, and copper.

children.text: krāmaṇe tu bhavettakraṃ śarkarā mākṣikaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: For <s>krāmaṇa</s> there should be buttermilk, sugar, and honey as well.
That buttermilk of tawny and black cows, O <s>Devī</s>, is for the <s>rasāyana</s>.
Cow buttermilk is sattvic; that born of <s>sārasa</s> is rajasic.

children.text: tāmasaṃ māhiṣaṃ takraṃ deyaṃ naiva rasāyane ||
children.translated_text: Buffalo buttermilk is tamasic and should never be given in <s>rasāyana</s>.

children.text: ārdrakasya raso devi tathā pūgaphalāni ca
children.translated_text: The juice of fresh ginger, O <s>Devī</s>, and betel nuts too,
together with rubbing by means of fresh butter, are the supreme <s>krāmaṇa</s> of <s>rasa</s>.
That arising from vegetable roots is inferior; that produced from fruit roots is middling.
The highest, O goddess of gods, is <s>rasaka</s> in <s>rasāyana</s>.
By <s>tīkṣṇa</s>-penetration it is bluish; by copper it has a reddish brilliance.
By silver it is moon-like; by gold it resembles gold.
The smoke-seeing one, held in the mouth, leads to sky-going within a month.
The touch-penetrating one, held in the mouth, grants accomplishment within two months.
The hundred-crore type acts in three months; the ten-crore type in four months.
The five-crore type acts in five months, and the crore-penetrating type in six.
In this way, step by step, it makes the body unaging and deathless.
Sovereignty endowed with powers beginning with minuteness, and perfection in command, arise.
With seven months it becomes a penetrator of a hundred thousand; with eight, again, of ten thousand.
With nine months it penetrates a thousand, and with ten months, again, a hundred.
By his urine and feces, and also by his phlegm and bodily impurities,
through smearing, stones and the like on the earth become gold.
From a sixty-fourth part there is penetration; after one month it penetrates tenfold.
But as a penetrator by a thirty-second part, after a year it penetrates the body.
A young woman whose hair has curled tips, who is dark and lotus-eyed,

children.text: vistīrṇaṃ jaghanaṃ yasyāḥ saṃkīrṇaṃ hṛdayaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: whose hips are broad and whose chest is narrow,
and whose menstruation appears in the dark fortnight,

children.text: kāminī sā samākhyātā uttamā ca rasāyane ||
children.translated_text: she is called a beloved woman, and is excellent for <s>rasāyana</s>.
In embracing and touching, and also in intercourse and conversation,
he is freed from every disease and is without wrinkles or gray hair.

children.text: nāsau chidyeta śastraiśca pāvakena na dahyate
children.translated_text: He is not cut by weapons, nor is he burned by fire.
He has the speed of wind and great brilliance, like another <s>Kāmadeva</s>.
At will he becomes visible, and he also becomes invisible.
By the mere touch of him, all metals become gold.
In that terrible single ocean, when stationary and moving beings have perished,
where the gods dissolve, the perfected one dissolves there alone.

children.text: idaṃ rahasyaṃ paramaṃ mayā proktaṃ sureśvari ||
children.translated_text: This supreme secret has been told by me, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>.
Those good and noble people who know the essence and are devoted to the practices of digested <s>rasa</s>
are called speakers of <s>rasa</s>; the others are speakers of hostility.
Again I shall teach another pill, hard to obtain through <s>rasa</s>.
Mercury is prepared by alchemists with tin, lead, copper, mica, gold, and silver,
and joined with diamond, iron, and the like.
Having put all those together in one place and set them inside a crucible, he should blow them.
A divine pill arises, called <s>Vajrāṅgasundarī</s>.
Held in the mouth, it is said to grant perfection and to destroy old age and death.
In battle he is victorious, heroic, diamond-bodied, and very strong.
He is always dear to all people and fortunate among women.

children.text: vajravyomajasattvakaṃ sakanakaṃ candraṃ raviṃ kāntakaṃ nāgaṃ vaṅgamathāyasaṃ dṛḍhataraṃ sūtaṃ kṛtaṃ tatsamam
children.translated_text: Diamond, mica-essence, together with gold, silver, copper, magnetic iron, lead, tin, and then iron, and very firm mercury, are made in equal measure.

children.text: vaktrasthaṃ rasagolakaṃ ratikaraṃ sarvārthadaṃ tāpahaṃ varṣaikena nihanti doṣanicayaṃ kalpāyuṣo jāyate ||
children.translated_text: The ball of <s>rasa</s> held in the mouth brings sexual pleasure, grants every aim, removes heat, destroys the mass of disorders within one year, and gives a lifespan of a cosmic age.
O <s>Devī</s>, into previously perfected <s>rasa</s> one should add gold in a quarter portion.
One should use mica-essence with a pala portion of dead diamond.
With the liquid of the milk-sheath and with the juice of <s>suradālī</s>,

children.text: vidhinā mardayitvā tu naṣṭapiṣṭaṃ tu kārayet ||
children.translated_text: having ground it according to rule, one should make it into a vanished paste.
After adding a tiny measure of magnetic powder, he should place it in a sealed crucible and blow it.
A divine pill arises; held in the mouth, it grants all perfections.
<s>Subhaga</s>, <s>mākṣika</s>, diamond, and mica,

children.text: hema śulvaṃ tathā tāraṃ samabhāgāni kārayet
children.translated_text: as well as gold, copper, and silver, should be made in equal parts.
The pill, bound with diamond, held in the mouth, grants all perfections.
<s>Bhrāmaka</s> and <s>mākṣika</s>, joined with the three metals,
combined with the seed of power and with the three seed-substances,
and mercury rubbed with <s>tridaṇḍī</s> should be united into a ball.
Heated in a blind crucible, it should be brought to complete fusion.

children.text: pūjāṃ kṛtvā kṣipedvaktre ṣaṇmāsāt sa bhavet priye
children.translated_text: Having performed worship, he should put it in his mouth; after six months, O dear one, he becomes
fearless before all enemies, diamond-bodied, and very strong.
Those such as <s>Nandikeśa</s> and <s>Kumāra</s> who carry off what is being consumed

children.text: naṣṭachāyā na dṛśyante haste dadati bhasma ca ||
children.translated_text: are shadowless and are not seen; they place ashes in the hand.
A foolish-minded man does not see the <s>rasa</s> being carried off by them.
He tells all beings, "I have no success in <s>rasāyana</s>."

children.text: manasā rasasiddhistu tathā kleśo mayā kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: "Perfection in <s>rasa</s> was only in my mind; hardship was undertaken by me.
Loss of materials was caused by me, foolish and dull-minded as I was."

children.text: īdṛśaṃ naiva jānāti vidhihīnaṃ mayā kṛtam
children.translated_text: He does not understand, "Such a thing was done by me without proper rule."
The sinful man blames the scripture; such people do not know their own action.
O <s>Devī</s>, <s>rasa</s> without proper rule never succeeds at any time.
For one without scripture, O <s>Deveśī</s>, there is no perfection, O fair-faced one.

children.text: aśubhaiḥ karmabhiḥ sarvaiḥ sampradāyo na sidhyati
children.translated_text: Through all inauspicious actions, the lineage-tradition does not succeed.

children.text: na sidhyedrasaśāstre tu na sidhyettādṛśo guruḥ ||
children.translated_text: It does not succeed in <s>rasaśāstra</s>, and such a guru does not succeed.

children.text: na prāpettādṛśīmājñāṃ naiva jñānaṃ ca tādṛśam
children.translated_text: He does not obtain such a command, nor such knowledge,
nor does he obtain such a single-minded woman, O fair-faced one.

children.text: na prāpedrasavantaṃ ca tāṃ ca devīṃ rasāṅkuśīm
children.translated_text: Nor does he obtain one possessed of <s>rasa</s>, nor that goddess <s>Rasāṅkuśī</s>.

children.text: yasya tuṣṭaḥ śivaḥ sākṣāttasya siddhī rasāyane ||
children.translated_text: For the one with whom <s>Śiva</s> himself is pleased, there is perfection in <s>rasāyana</s>.
Again I shall teach another excellent binding of a ball,
by the mere eating of which one becomes free from old age and death.
Sulfur, mica, magnetic iron, <s>bhānu</s>, potsherd-substance, and gold,

children.text: samaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ rasendrasya baddhaṃ kṛtvā tu golakam ||
children.translated_text: with an equal amount of sharp iron, are made into a bound ball of <s>rasendra</s>.
He should mix five <s>palas</s> of <s>rasendra</s> in equal proportion.
He should grind the ball with the juice of seven citrons.

children.text: chāyāviśuṣkaṃ golaṃ tu śaśibhāvaṃ karoti tat
children.translated_text: When the ball is dried in the shade, it produces a moon-like state.

children.text: etat sarvaṃ vimardyaṃ tu sūtakaṃ golakasya ca ||
children.translated_text: All this, together with the mercury of the ball, should be thoroughly ground.

children.text: tat karīṣāgninā bhūmau mṛdusvedaṃ tu kārayet
children.translated_text: He should give it gentle heating in the earth with a cow-dung fire.
This ball, held in the mouth, grants immortality.
The fruit of the mercury-ball cannot be expressed.
In <s>rasāyana</s> it improves complexion and grants perfection in <s>rasa</s>.
Fragrant ointment, betel, musk, saffron, and aloe wood...
He should provide <s>śrīkhaṇḍa</s> sandalwood, musk, <s>kaṅkola</s>, and nutmeg,

children.text: anyāni ca sugandhīni snāne pāne pradāpayet ||
children.translated_text: and other fragrant substances for bathing and drinking.
A young woman whose hair has curled tips, who is dark and lotus-eyed,

children.text: vistīrṇaṃ jaghanaṃ yasyāḥ saṃkīrṇaṃ hṛdayaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: whose hips are broad and whose chest is narrow,
and whose menstruation appears in the dark fortnight,

children.text: kāminī sā samākhyātā uttamā ca rasāyane ||
children.translated_text: is called a <s>kāminī</s>; she is excellent for <s>rasāyana</s>.
In embracing, touching, sexual union, and conversation too,
he becomes free from every disease and devoid of wrinkles and grey hair.
A hundred diseases are destroyed when these are held in the mouth,
in measures equal to a barley grain; he lives for three hundred years.
Now, O <s>Sureśvarī</s>, I shall speak of the qualities of the sixteen preparations,

children.text: ghṛtāni mukhamadhye tu teṣu vakṣyāmi ye guṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: which are kept in the mouth for sixteen years.

children.text: nāsau chidyeta śastraiśca pāvakena na dahyate
children.translated_text: He cannot be cut by weapons, nor is he burned by fire.
He has the speed of the wind and great splendor, like another <s>Kāmadeva</s>.
At will he becomes visible, and he also becomes invisible.
By his mere touch, all metals become gold.
Again I shall teach another <s>vajrabandha</s>, O you who are worshipped by the gods.
A man deficient in limbs, excessive in limbs, diseased, hunchbacked, bent,
with bent feet, without hands, or with the senses obstructed by old age,
even if dull, stammering, mute, and likewise unable to move,
casts off his shell-like skin and remains alive.
By the power of this bound preparation, when transformation has occurred,
one should take <s>rasa</s> that penetrates a crore-fold, joined with six lumps.
The wise man should make a pill placed in the middle of each one.

children.text: guṭikāḥ pañcasaṃkhyātāḥ ṣaṣṭhī caiva tu pañcamī
children.translated_text: The pills are five in number, and the sixth is again a fifth part.
The mass should be multiplied sixfold; the copper vessel should be handsome.

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ puruṣamātraṃ tu puruṣārdhaṃ ca maṇḍalam
children.translated_text: Above it should be a man's height, and the circular enclosure half a man in measure.
He should place over it a four-mouthed wooden structure.
He should smear it equally with ghee and great oil,
and, after worshipping the cauldron, he should also worship the guardians of the directions.

children.text: kumārīṃ pūjayet paścād dadyāddikṣu baliṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Afterward he should worship a virgin girl and likewise give a <s>bali</s> offering in the directions.

children.text: dhamanaṃ tatra kurvīta caturdikṣu śanaiḥ śanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: There he should perform the blowing from the four directions, slowly, slowly.

children.text: sutaptaṃ ca vidhātavyaṃ nirdhūmaṃ ca yadā bhavet
children.translated_text: When it has been well heated and has become smokeless,
then, after bowing to the guru, the deity, and also the moon, sun, and other planets,

children.text: nakṣatrāṇi ca sampūjya ātmānaṃ tatra nikṣipet ||
children.translated_text: and after worshipping the constellations, he should place himself there.
Earth, water, fire, wind, and ether
should be understood as exceedingly difficult to obtain; he should apply them as the form of accomplishment.

children.text: kalalaṃ ca bhavet sarvaṃ puraś cāpo vinikṣipet
children.translated_text: Everything becomes an embryonic mass, and then he should cast water before it.
He should know it to be red in color, and should join fire to fire.
A lump of flesh arises there; he should cast the wind into that very place.

children.text: kāntavarṇaṃ tadā kāryaṃ nikṣipet khaṃ kapālake ||
children.translated_text: Then he should make it the color of <s>kānta</s>; he should place ether in the skull-vessel.

children.text: dhamantaṃ hemasaṃkāśaṃ kṣāratvaṃ taṃ tu pādayet ||
children.translated_text: While it is being blown and is like gold, he should bring it to an alkaline state.
Having made a great roar there and the <s>huṃkāra</s> honored by the gods,

children.text: uttiṣṭhati na sandehaḥ puṣṭāṅgo bhāskaro yathā
children.translated_text: it rises up, without doubt, with well-nourished limbs like the sun.
It has divine splendor, a great body, divine sight, and great strength.
Its bell-sound extends over a hundred <s>yojanas</s>, and it is greatly honored.
It is divine, made of blazing gold, and adorned with jewels and rubies.
It is rich with flower garlands and banners, and decorated with networks of small bells.
Mounted on the finest celestial vehicle, amid the sounds of conches and trumpets,
with the singing and instruments of apsarases and with charming dances,
filled with divine ornaments and adorned with divine garlands,
beautiful, endowed with sidelong passion, and bewildered with intoxication,
a divine maiden comes, without doubt, to summon him.
Taking the chief practitioner, she then dwells with him in the world of the perfected ones.
He has divine baths and drinks, and divine ornaments.
He enjoys himself for a hundred thousand years with love-stricken perfected maidens.
In that terrible single ocean, when the stationary and moving world has perished,
where the gods dissolve, the perfected one dissolves there alone.
This fierce rite called <s>Bhūtakālāntaka</s> has been described.

children.text: tattvato'yaṃ mahādevi yadā kartuṃ na śakyate
children.translated_text: O great <s>Devī</s>, when this cannot truly be performed,
then success will arise by means of this very body.
